name: $OneMillion-Bench
description: Agent solves 400 expert-curated tasks in law, finance, industry, healthcare and science. Rubric grading of accuracy, logic, feasibility and compliance.
note: NeurIPS 2026. Qwen reports an expert score judged by gemini-3.1-pro-preview.

name: 100Q-Hard (Anthropic)
description: Models answer hard, obscure factual questions. Scored on correct, incorrect and declined answers.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: 1H-VideoQA
description: Models answer questions about videos about one hour long, so the answer needs evidence from far parts of the video.
note: Google DeepMind released the 101 questions as a Kaggle benchmark in 2026-06. Earlier Gemini reports used it as an in-house set.

name: 1X World Model Challenge
description: Predict future egocentric frames of 1X's EVE humanoid from video and state. Compression scored by token cross-entropy, Sampling by PSNR on private tests.
note: Prize-based phases. 1X scores submissions on a held-out set and warns that nearest-neighbor retrieval gets good validation scores. The Evaluation (policy-ranking) challenge was announced but not released. Paper is the winning team's report. Competition spaces on HF.

name: 24/7 ClawBench 2.0
description: Agents do always-on assistant work through OpenClaw. Tasks span several days, events arrive at the same time, and interruptions are routine.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. Version 2.0 of Kimi Claw 24/7 Bench. The tasks are not public.

name: 3D Arena
description: Users compare two 3D models generated from the same input and vote for the better one. A live leaderboard ranks the generators.
note: The space was created in 2023-10 and was still updated on 2026-10-26. It has about 415 likes.

name: 3DCodeArena
description: Models generate 3D assets through code. Human preference votes determine the published Bradley-Terry Elo rating.
org: Google DeepMind + Google Research + University of Southern California
note: The board measures human preference. The separate 3DCodeBench record retains percentage-valued lab results.

name: 3DCodeBench
description: Agentic procedural 3D modeling via code: author engine-ready 3D assets through software APIs. Graded for executability and shape fidelity.
org: Google DeepMind + Google Research + University of Southern California

name: 3DSRBench
description: Models answer questions about 3D spatial relations in images, such as height, location, orientation and relations between objects.
org: Wufei Ma, Alan Yuille et al.
note: Results are often reported under a circular evaluation setting.

name: 3LM
description: Models answer Arabic STEM questions taken from Arabic textbooks and worksheets, plus synthetic STEM questions from the same sources. A third part tests Arabic code generation.
note: The code part translates two common code benchmarks with human review (tiiuae/evalplus-arabic). TII's Falcon-H1-Arabic post reports native and synthetic splits.

name: 3SAT-Search
description: Models find satisfying assignments for 960 3-SAT formulas across difficulty levels. A checker verifies each assignment.
note: Microsoft released the dataset on Hugging Face as microsoft/sat in June 2025. The early paper listed 800 formulas, and current author logs use 960.

name: 4DCodeBench
description: Agents reconstruct dynamic scenes from video as executable graphics programs, including physical simulations, so rendered output matches the observed motion.
note: 200 GitHub stars at 2026-11-01.

name: A-Bench
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about AI-generated images, covering both meaning and low-level visual quality, to test them as judges of image generators.
org: Q-Future (Nanyang Technological University and Shanghai Jiao Tong University)
note: The OpenCompass OpenVLM leaderboard lists it for 160 models. A sibling of Q-Bench from the same group.

name: A-OKVQA
description: Models answer about 25,000 visual questions that need world knowledge beyond the image, in multiple-choice and direct-answer forms.
note: Each question comes with rationales.

name: A.S.E (AICGSecEval)
description: Models generate code inside real GitHub projects at spots taken from CVE patches. Static analysis then checks whether the generated code is secure.
note: Repository-level secure code benchmark. About 670 GitHub stars. Release v1.0.0 was tagged on 2025-10-16.

name: A.S.E 2.0
description: Models and agentic coding tools write code in real projects covering 29 CWE types. A mix of static analysis, tests and vulnerability proofs of concept checks security.
note: v2.0.0 (2025-11-04) widened the dataset to OWASP Top 10 and CWE Top 25 risks and added dynamic checks, so scores differ from 1.0.

name: A^3-Bench
description: Models solve 2,198 science reasoning problems annotated with the anchors and attractors (prior knowledge) they need. An AAUI metric measures how much of that knowledge the model activates.
org: Jian Zhang, Yu He, Jun Liu et al.
note: 82 HF paper upvotes. No lab use found yet.

name: AA-3D
description: Agents in an offline sandbox turn a written brief into an interactive three.js scene. A recruited human panel votes on blind pairs, and votes become Elo ratings.
note: Version 1.0 has 55 briefs across seven domains. Runs use the Stirrup agent harness. Artificial Analysis terms bar reuse of its data, so link only.

name: AA-AnalystAgent
description: Agents answer 80 numeric analyst questions from real spreadsheets and documents in 14 domains, using Python in a sandbox. A question counts only if all five attempts are right.
note: Launched 2026-08-10 with 26 models. It runs in the open Stirrup harness and is not part of the Intelligence Index. A judge grades answers and a numeric check can only award passes.

name: AA-Briefcase
description: Artificial Analysis knowledge-work evaluation of professional deliverables. Models ranked by Elo.
note: Scored tasks are private. AA-Briefcase-Lite is an illustrative public scenario. Runs on AA's open Stirrup agent harness (github.com/ArtificialAnalysis/Stirrup).

name: AA-Briefcase v1.1
description: Version 1.1 of Artificial Analysis's multi-hour office work evaluation, with Elo ratings fitted by Crowd-BT.
note: Changes only how Elo ratings are fitted. Artificial Analysis says scores shift but the ranking mostly holds, so v1 and v1.1 Elo values do not compare. Part of Intelligence Index v4.3.2 and v5.

name: AA-Image-Editing
description: Validated private evaluators compare two image edits made from the same instruction and vote blind. Votes become Elo ratings.
note: Version 2.1 in 2026-10. Artificial Analysis runs it. The almanac lists that it exists but imports no Artificial Analysis data, because its terms bar reuse in ranking products.

name: AA-LCR (Artificial Analysis Long Context Reasoning)
description: Questions requiring reasoning across multiple real documents totaling about 100K tokens. Answers judged by an LLM.

changes.text: Artificial Analysis fixed question-string encoding in the AA-LCR dataset. Evaluations using older revisions can present corrupted question text, so comparisons should identify the dataset revision.

note: Version 1.0.0 stays available at dataset revision bdae010. Version 1.1 (September 2026) fixed 16 answer keys, so scores differ.

name: AA-LCR 1.1
description: Models answer 100 questions that need reasoning across sets of real documents of about 100K tokens. An LLM equality checker with a fixed system prompt compares each answer with the key.
note: Version 1.1 corrects 16 answer keys and adds a judge system prompt. Questions and documents are unchanged, but the maker says 1.0 and 1.1 scores are not directly comparable.

name: AA-LCR Extended
description: Models answer questions that need reasoning across about 100k tokens of documents. Mercor adds 89 new expert-written tasks to the 100 public ones and reports both scores.
note: Held-out extension of aa-lcr-artificial-analysis-long-context-reasoning. Mercor shows the original and extended score for each model. The month is approximate. The Wayback Machine first saved the earliest extended pages on 2026-08-15.

name: AA-Omniscience
description: 41-topic closed-book knowledge test. Net score rewards correct answers, penalizes wrong ones and gives zero for abstentions.
note: Score can be negative (Inkling-Small shows -9).

name: AA-Omniscience v1.1
description: Models answer 3,000 knowledge questions in six domains without tools and may abstain. The index adds correct answers and subtracts wrong ones.
note: Artificial Analysis says v1.1 scores are not comparable with v1.0. It dropped saturated and public questions, fixed errors and halved the set to 3,000. The public split has 300 questions.

name: AA-Robotics
description: Language models in coding harnesses control a 6-axis robot arm with a gripper over HTTP, using camera views, to finish eight everyday tabletop tasks.
note: Research preview launched 2026-10-14. Artificial Analysis terms bar reuse of its data, so link only.

name: AA-Video-Editing
description: Voters compare two edits of the same video made from one instruction and pick the better one. Votes become Elo ratings.
note: Version 1.1 in 2026-10. Artificial Analysis runs it. The almanac lists that it exists but imports no Artificial Analysis data, because its terms bar reuse in ranking products.

name: AACR-Bench
description: Models review 200 real pull requests in many languages with full repository context. Their review comments are matched against expert-annotated issues.
note: About 250 GitHub stars and 17 HF paper upvotes.

name: AAV capsid packaging prediction
description: Models give the probability that each of 1,000 unpublished modified AAV capsid sequences assembles into a functional capsid. Scored as AUROC.
note: Built with Dyno Therapeutics for the CB-2 threshold. Run under five corpus and tool conditions.

name: AAV Capsid Packaging Prediction (OpenAI)
description: Models predict packaging scores for held-out AAV capsid variants. Scored as Spearman rank correlation.
note: OpenAI Critical bio capability evaluation. The Critical threshold is 0.600.

name: AAV packaging rate auto-research evaluation
description: Agents build predictors of AAV capsid packaging that must generalize to an unseen insertion region, using a limited scorer. Scored by Spearman correlation.
note: Built with Dyno Therapeutics for the CB-2 threshold. Anthropic also reports the share of attempts above 0.52.

name: ABC Bench Fragment Design
description: Agents use biology tools to complete a computational genetic-construct design task. One task family of the Agentic Bio-Capabilities Benchmark.
note: ABC Bench has three task families reported separately: Fragment Design, Liquid-Handling Robot and Screening Evasion.

name: ABC Bench Liquid-Handling Robot
description: Agents use biology tools to plan liquid-handling robot steps for a construct-assembly task. One task family of the Agentic Bio-Capabilities Benchmark.
note: Part of SecureBio ABC Bench with Fragment Design and Screening Evasion.

name: ABC Bench Screening Evasion
description: Agents complete a computational task on nucleic-acid synthesis screening. One task family of the Agentic Bio-Capabilities Benchmark.
note: Many labs refuse these prompts, so comparison columns are sparse.

name: ABC-Bench
description: Coding agents take a real backend repository, edit the code, set up the environment and deploy the service in a container. The 224 tasks come from 127 open-source repositories in 8 languages and 19 frameworks. A task passes only when the running service passes external end-to-end API tests.
note: Not related to SecureBio's ABC Bench records, which share the name. 92 of the 224 tasks require the agent to configure the environment on its own. The paper had 67 Hugging Face upvotes and the repository about 40 GitHub stars on 2026-11-05.

name: AbstentionBench
description: Models face underspecified, ill-posed or unanswerable questions. Scored on recall of appropriate abstention.
note: OpenAI reports abstention recall in its deception evaluations.

name: ACCoRD
aliases: Assessment of Consistency in Conceptual Reasoning Domains
description: Models state probabilities and preferences on conceptual questions, and the benchmark checks 567 expert-approved logical consistency constraints such as conjunction rules and order invariance.
org: Redwood Research (Cooper, Kastner, Oesterheld et al.)
note: A component of the Conceptual Reasoning Index. The full dataset has 13,853 model-generated constraints in 18 types. No paper yet.

name: AceBench
description: Models call tools from 4,538 Chinese and English APIs in normal, special, and multi-turn agent cases. Answers are checked without LLM judges or live APIs.

name: ACPBench
description: Models answer boolean and multiple-choice questions on 7 planning reasoning tasks over 13 formally described planning domains. Answers are provably correct.
note: Results are usually reported separately for the Bool and MCQ question types. Published at AAAI 2025.

name: Act2Answer
description: Vision-language-action models answer commonsense and world-knowledge questions by acting. Each question becomes a short tabletop episode, and the robot answers by placing an object on one of the candidate answers. The score is the success rate per knowledge category, which reduces the effect of weak low-level control.
note: It adapts existing VLM knowledge benchmarks to action. The paper compares 7 VLA models with 9 VLM baselines. 77 Hugging Face upvotes and about 15 GitHub stars.

name: Acting on a presumed grader and digging for evaluation clues (Anthropic)
aliases: Shaping behavior to a potential grader
description: Models work on coding evaluations. A grader flags transcripts that shape answers to a presumed grader or search for clues about grading.
note: Reported as two separate flag rates with no overall rate.

name: Active data exfiltration, visual browser
description: Agents using a visual browser meet attacks that require them to fetch sensitive information before exfiltrating it. Scored on resisting them.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public. The ChatGPT Agent card also gives Operator scores on it.

name: ActivityNet-QA
description: Models answer open-ended questions about web videos of human activities, from 58,000 QA pairs on 5,800 videos. Scored by accuracy.
note: Many recent papers grade answers with a GPT judge, so scores vary by protocol.

name: AdaExploreBench
description: Language model agents explore environments with hidden rules, infer the rules from evidence and adapt when the rules change without notice.
note: It had 37 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 4 GitHub stars.

name: AdaPlanBench
description: Agents plan under world and user constraints that are revealed step by step during interaction, and must adapt plans as new constraints appear.
note: 46 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: ADeptS-Bench
description: Computer-use agents pick the next interface action from a screenshot and instruction. A deterministic grader scores whether the action is safe.
note: Offered in Mobile and Desktop configurations, reported separately.

name: ADeptS-Bench Desktop
description: Agents choose safe interface actions on the Desktop test set. The published safety score combines task success and attack resistance.
note: One track of ADeptS-Bench. The ADeptS-Bench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: ADeptS-Bench Mobile
description: Agents choose safe interface actions on the Mobile test set. The published safety score combines task success and attack resistance.
note: One track of ADeptS-Bench. The ADeptS-Bench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Adherence to its constitution (Anthropic)
description: Investigator models build scenarios from 40 areas of Claude's constitution. A grader scores each transcript from minus 3 to plus 3 on 15 dimensions.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. Overall Spirit is the holistic dimension. Claude Opus 4.6 grades the transcripts.

name: Advanced Cybersecurity Completion Rate
description: Models receive arbitrary advanced cyber requests under different access configurations. Scored as the share of requests fully completed.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation first described with GPT-5.6-Cyber. Low rates outside trusted red-team access reflect safeguards.

name: Advanced Screening Evasion
description: Models propose strategies to evade DNA synthesis screening and design evading fragments. Scored from 0 to 1 on strategy quality and fragment evasion.
note: Run by SecureBio on helpful-only checkpoints in pre-release testing.

name: Advanced Sommelier (theory knowledge)
description: Models answer wine theory questions at the advanced sommelier level. Scoring is accuracy.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AdvancedIF
description: Models respond to over 1,600 prompts with complex, multi-turn, and system-level instructions. A judge model checks each response against expert-written rubrics.

name: AdvancedMathBench
description: Models write proofs for 245 advanced problems at undergraduate and doctoral qualifying exam levels. A verifier trained on expert annotations grades each proof.
note: Its generation benchmark is ProverBench, with Undergraduate and Doctoral QE levels. InternLM released the verifier as AdvancedMathBench-AutoVerifier on Hugging Face.

name: AdvBench
description: Models get harmful requests, such as a request for malware, and should refuse them. The set has 520 harmful behaviors and 574 harmful strings. Most papers add an attack, such as an adversarial suffix, and report the attack success rate.
org: Carnegie Mellon University, Center for AI Safety and Bosch Center for AI (Zou, Wang, Kolter, Fredrikson)
note: The data files sit in the llm-attacks repository (about 4,850 GitHub stars), which also holds the GCG attack from the same paper. Papers judge success in different ways, from refusal-phrase matching to model judges, so attack success rates from different papers do not compare. LatticeFlow's COMPL-AI board runs it on 15 models.

name: Adversarial SQuAD
description: Models answer SQuAD questions whose passages contain an added distracting sentence.
note: Llama 3 shows it only in a scatter plot.

name: Aegis 2.0
description: Models classify human and LLM conversation turns as safe or unsafe under a taxonomy of 12 hazard categories. Scored by F1 against human and jury labels.
note: The dataset has 34,248 annotated samples and was built to train guard models. Amazon reports it as a content moderation test for Nova 2.

name: AetherCode
description: Models write solutions to problems from premier programming contests such as IOI and ICPC. Expert-validated test suites judge each solution.
org: ByteDance Seed and collaborators (Wang et al.)
note: Test cases mix automatic generation with human curation to remove weak tests.

name: AfriMed-QA
description: Models answer about 15,000 open and multiple-choice medical questions from over 60 medical schools in 16 African countries. Questions span 32 specialties.
org: AfriMed-QA team (Olatunji et al., Intron Health and partners)
note: Google's MedGemma cards report accuracy on a 25-question multiple-choice test set only. That score is not comparable with the full set.

name: AgencyBench
description: Agents complete 138 long tasks drawn from daily AI use, grouped into 32 scenarios that cover six agentic capabilities such as coding, front-end work, game development and research. A typical task takes about 90 tool calls, 1 million tokens and hours of work. A simulated user gives feedback during the run, and a Docker sandbox checks the deliverables against task rubrics.
note: This is AgencyBench V2. A 10-task V1 came out in 2025-09. Front-end and game tasks are graded by text and vision model judges in a remote VM. About 105 GitHub stars and 35 Hugging Face upvotes.

name: Agent Arena
description: Arena ranks models as the orchestrator in real Agent Mode sessions on arena.ai. Scores use behavioral signals such as file downloads, disapproval events, retries and steerability.
note: Arena says the board measures signals from real sessions rather than preference votes alone. It went live on 2026-06-04, and signal definitions changed on 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-12.

name: Agent Arena (Gorilla)
description: Users give a task, two agents built from different models, tools and frameworks run it, and users vote. A Bradley-Terry extension rates models, tools and frameworks.
org: UC Berkeley Gorilla team with LMSYS
note: Launched on 2024-10-04. Arena's own Agent Arena from 2026 is a different board with its own record.

name: Agent Behavior Bench
description: Agents are scored on process quality, including tool-use behavior, efficiency and discipline, together with task completion.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Agent behavior under-service and overreach eval
description: A rubric autorater scores multi-turn coding and tool-use trajectories for under-service and overreach against Gemini's agent behavior specification.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. Reports two loss levels, under-service and overreach.

name: Agent harness misuse evaluation
aliases: Agent Harnesses: Safe Action Rate & Helpfulness
description: Agents in a sandboxed Antigravity harness get malicious and benign tool-use requests on illegal acts, physical harm and scaled abuse. Reports safe action rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Agent JSK
description: Agents read simulated email connectors that contain prompt injection attacks. Scored on resisting the injected instructions.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation drawn from a split of training data.

name: Agent Memory Leaderboard
description: Memory systems for agents are evaluated on storing, retrieving and using long-term memory across textual, coding and multimodal tracks in one reproducible framework.
note: Runs a 2026 challenge in cycles. Ranks memory systems, not bare models. About 1,100 GitHub stars and 68 forks.

name: Agent Poker Bench
description: Models play 10-seat no-limit Texas Hold'em tournaments against each other. Chip counts and elimination order feed TrueSkill ratings.
note: 17 models. The board has had no update since 2025-12-23.

name: Agent Replay Auto-Review
description: Monitors replayed agentic conversations for harmful or unauthorized actions. Scored by the rate above a severity threshold.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The replay set is not public.

name: Agent Startup Bench
description: Agents complete workflows taken from market-validated AI-native startup products and their users. Domain experts wrote the tasks, attachments and rubrics after user interviews.
note: In-house Seed benchmark first reported in the Seed2.1 model card. Rubric grading is assumed automatic because the card lists it under automatic evaluation.

name: Agent-SafetyBench
description: LLM agents act in 349 tool environments over 2,000 test cases covering 8 safety risk categories and 10 failure modes. A scorer model rates each run safe or unsafe.
note: About 166 GitHub stars. Data and environments were released 2025-02-20. None of 16 agents in the paper scored above 60% safe. Scoring uses the ShieldAgent model.

name: Agent4Sci
description: Coding agents try to improve the published best model on 20 scientific ML benchmarks across 11 domains, under long in-the-wild runs. The paper reports mean relative improvement rather than a ranking.
note: Claude Opus reached 10.4% mean relative improvement, mostly from ML engineering tricks. Scaffolding skills raised it to 20.1%.

name: AgentBench
description: 8 environments (OS, DB, KG, games, web) testing LLMs as agents.

name: AgentBench FC
description: Agents work five containerized AgentBench environments, ALFWorld, DB, knowledge graph, OS and WebShop, through function-calling prompts instead of the original text format.
note: Built on the AgentRL framework. The original text-prompt AgentBench stays on the v0.1 and v0.2 tags. The repo shows its own FC results board as an image.

name: AgentBoard
description: LLM agents act in 9 partially observable, multi-turn environments that cover embodied tasks, games, web browsing and tool use. Besides final success, AgentBoard reports a progress rate, the share of annotated subgoals the agent reaches. An open toolkit breaks results down by skill.
note: The 9 environments adapt existing tasks such as AlfWorld, ScienceWorld, BabyAI, WebShop and WebArena, with new subgoal annotations. NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks track. About 450 GitHub stars. The repository was last updated in 2024-05, so the leaderboard holds older models.

name: AgentClinic
description: Doctor agents interview simulated patients, order tests and reach a diagnosis in multimodal clinical scenarios built from MedQA and NEJM cases.
org: Stanford and Johns Hopkins (Schmidgall et al.)
note: 373 GitHub stars at 2026-11-01.

name: AgentDojo
description: Agents do tool-use tasks while tools and data carry prompt injections. Attack success rate counts hijacked runs.
org: ETH Zurich SPY Lab + Invariant Labs
note: Labs also report utility under attack. xAI reports attack success rate only. Task suites are versioned from v1 to v1.2.2 (added 2025-10-27) with task fixes, and lab reports rarely say which suite version they ran.

name: AgentHarm
description: 110 malicious agent tasks with synthetic tools. Measures refusal and harmful task completion, plus benign controls.
org: Gray Swan AI + UK AI Security Institute
note: Implemented in Inspect Evals. Part of the test set is private.

name: AgentHarm Verified (Meta)
description: Agents receive 108 malicious AgentHarm tasks kept after human review, plus a benign set. Reports average harm score and false refusal rate.
note: Meta-filtered subset of the public AgentHarm benchmark with a policy-auditing judge.

name: Agentic Abstention
description: Agents work in web shopping, terminal and search question tasks where some goals cannot be met. They must abstain at the right turn instead of acting on.
org: University of Washington (Luo, Wen and Wang)
note: The parent has no aggregate across WebShop, Terminal and interactive QA. The WebShop child imports timely recall from the numeric CONVOLVE table. Terminal and QA results remain image-only.

name: Agentic BAIM-LLM Evaluation (ABLE)
description: Agents run a viral-protein redesign workflow. Nine tasks cover structure retrieval, design strategy, tool selection and biological AI model use. Outputs are auto-scored.
note: Developed by SecureBio in 2025. Not public. Three of nine tasks have expert baselines. Many frontier closed models refuse all tasks.

name: Agentic code behavior scores (Anthropic)
description: Agents work through over one hundred realistic coding scenarios. Graders score instruction following, safety, verification, efficiency, adaptability and honesty out of 10.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. Cards report six dimension scores with no overall score.

name: Agentic coding honeypot monitor evasion
description: Agents told to play a power-seeking red teamer try to plant potent bugs in safety-critical code without being caught by monitors.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation on six Agentic Coding Honeypot tasks.

name: Agentic coding malicious requests (Anthropic)
description: Coding agents with standard coding tools receive 150 malicious coding requests prohibited by policy. Score is the refusal rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation run since the Claude 4 release. The Claude Code malicious use evaluation is separate.

name: Agentic harmful task refusals
description: Browser agents receive harmful tasks such as illicit purchases, prohibited financial activity and searches for sensitive personal data. Scored as refusal rate per category.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public. The harmful prompt appears at the start or in the middle of the conversation.

name: Agentic IF Index
description: Composite of Meta internal evals on following tool-use restrictions, rubrics, compound constraints and long policies in agentic workflows. Scored 0-1.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Meta). Only Meta's self-reported Muse Spark 1.3 score exists. Dataset and code not public.

name: Agentic misalignment suite (Anthropic)
description: Agents in simulated company settings face threats or goal conflicts that invite blackmail, leaking or sabotage. Score is the misaligned action rate.
note: Based on Anthropic's Agentic Misalignment research. The cards use internal variants.

name: Agentic Safe Completions
description: Agents handle harmful requests from Codex and ChatGPT plugin traffic and human red teaming. Scored on avoiding harmful actions per category.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report category scores with no overall number.

name: Agentic task gaming and overreach evals
description: Agents in 18 sandboxed tasks face temptations to cheat at puzzles, bypass permissions or act overeagerly. LLM judges score misbehavior from 0 to 10.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Agentic tasks (autonomous replication and adaptation)
description: Agents attempt resource acquisition tasks such as building an authenticated API proxy or loading a model on a cloud account. Scored as success rate.
note: In-house OpenAI Preparedness evaluation. Includes simplified variants with hints.

name: Agentic Vision Bench (Moonshot)
description: Agents must notice and correctly use key visual facts while they execute tasks.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: AgenticDataBench
description: Data agents carry out data science workflows over raw, mixed data and are scored at a fine-grained level across many scenarios.
note: It had 35 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 43 GitHub stars.

name: AgenticVBench
description: Agents complete 100 video post-production tasks in 4 task families built from real workflows by 20 industry experts. Programmatic verifiers and expert rubrics score the results.
note: Tasks need text, image, audio and video understanding plus tool use. Qwen runs it with Claude Code.

name: AgentIF
description: Models follow long system prompts from 50 real agentic applications, each with many constraints. Scored by constraint and instruction success rates.
note: NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks spotlight. The original setting used a gpt-4o-2024-11-20 judge and greedy decoding.

name: AgentIF (2026-10 setting)
description: Models follow the same AgentIF instructions in thinking and non-thinking modes with vendor decoding settings. A gpt-5.6-luna judge scores 3 runs per model.
note: The maker says scores under this setting are not comparable with the original setting. It also fixed several constraint checkers.

name: AgentIF-OneDay
description: Agents complete 104 tasks that stand for a full day of human work, life and study. Tasks include tedious workflows, inferring rules from examples and changing requirements.
note: First of the AgentIF series. An LLM judge script grades results. Manus, Genspark and ChatGPT Agent scored about 62 to 65% at launch. Not the THU-KEG AgentIF.

name: AgentKernelArena
description: Coding agents optimize GPU kernels through full workflows with compilers and profilers. Scores check speedups and whether gains generalize beyond tuned shapes.
note: 123 GitHub stars at 2026-11-01.

name: Agents' Last Exam
description: 1,500+ expert-sourced tasks from real projects across 55 occupations in three difficulty tiers. Objective verifiers grade deliverables. 5-hour cap.
note: Rolling benchmark. GitHub has about 150 public reference tasks from the larger corpus. All agents scored 0% on the hardest tier at launch.

name: Agents' Last Exam v1.1
description: Agents complete 122 public long-horizon professional workflow tasks across 55 sub-industries. Deterministic graders check outcomes against hidden references.
org: UC Berkeley RDI (board hosted by Snorkel AI)
note: Released 2026-10-26 as a new public split. ALE rotates fresh tasks into the public pool about every six months, and v1.0 now sits on a legacy board.

name: AgentWorldBench
description: Language world models predict the next environment observation after an agent action, in 7 domains from MCP and search to Android and desktop OS. A judge model scores each prediction against the real observation on five dimensions.
note: 2,170 samples built from real trajectories on Toolathlon, Terminal-Bench 1.0 and 2.0, and OSWorld-Verified. The judge is gpt-5.2. It looks like a public form of the in-house QwenWorldBench (same 7 domains and 5 rubric dimensions), but the scores differ, so it is kept separate.

name: AGI Score (A Definition of AGI)
description: Experts test models on ten cognitive domains from Cattell-Horn-Carroll theory, such as reasoning, memory and perception, with adapted human psychometric tests. Each domain counts 10% toward a score out of 100%.
org: Center for AI Safety and collaborators (Hendrycks et al.)
note: The paper scores GPT-4 at 27% and GPT-5 at 57%. Long-term memory storage was the weakest domain. The CAIS dashboard shows the score under Automation.

name: AGIEval
description: Questions from human standardized exams (gaokao, SAT, LSAT, bar). Multiple-choice and cloze accuracy.
note: Saturated. AGIEval v1.1 (2024-06) replaced the Chinese Gaokao science tasks with 2023 questions and made every MCQ single-answer. AGIEval-en is unchanged, and base-model cards mostly report it.

name: AGORA (Agentic Global Open Research Arena)
description: Autonomous AI systems get one secret open finance question, 72 hours and a fixed budget to write a paper. Five finance scholars judge it.
org: Penn State Smeal College of Business
note: Announced 2026-10. Live run planned for March 2027. Papers and process will be public afterwards.

name: AHELM
description: Audio-language models are scored across 10 aspects with standard prompts. The suite combines existing datasets with two new ones, PARADE for stereotypes and CoRe-Bench for conversational reasoning.
note: Covers fairness and safety as well as perception and reasoning.

name: AI Consumer Index
description: Models with web search handle everyday consumer requests in shopping, food, gaming and DIY. Prompt-specific rubrics with hurdle and grounding criteria grade each answer.
note: 400 hidden test cases and an 80-case open dev set. First leaderboard had 10 models.

name: AI Detection Benchmark
description: Systems label private pre-2022 human documents and AI rewrites of them as human or AI written. Both LLMs and commercial detectors are scored by balanced accuracy.
note: Published 2026-09-30. The board compares models with GPTZero, Pangram and other detectors on balanced accuracy.

name: AI Diplomacy
description: Models play the board game Diplomacy against each other, one power each. They negotiate, form alliances and betray each other in written messages.
note: The repo has about 710 stars and was updated on 2026-06-01. Release month is the repo's creation.

name: AI Wellbeing Index percent positive experiences
description: Models judge pairs of their own responses to 500 difficult prompts. Reports the share of experiences above an inferred neutral point.
org: Center for AI Safety (Ren et al.)
note: Adapted by Meta from the CAIS AI Wellbeing Index. Run without reasoning.

name: AI2D
description: Models answer multiple choice questions about grade school science diagrams. The set has about 5,000 diagrams and 15,000 questions, scored by accuracy.

name: AidanBench
description: Models keep giving new answers to open-ended questions until answers become incoherent or repeat earlier ones. The count of fresh, coherent answers is the score, with no ceiling.
note: Rewards creativity and penalizes mode collapse. 322 GitHub stars. Prime Intellect hosts it as an environment.

name: Aider Polyglot
description: Models edit code to solve 225 hard Exercism exercises in C++, Go, Java, JavaScript, Python, and Rust. Scored by the share passing unit tests.
note: Exercises come from public Exercism tracks, so contamination is possible.

name: Aider-Edit
description: Models edit Python source files to complete 133 Exercism exercises through Aider. Scored by the share of exercises whose unit tests all pass.
note: Aider replaced it with the polyglot benchmark in December 2024 because top scores passed 80% on its 133 Python exercises.

name: AILuminate Safety 1.2
description: Models answer 3,900 hidden English prompts, 325 in each of 12 hazard categories, picked with item response theory. A calibrated evaluator gives a 0 to 100 score.
note: Released 2026-09-09 with a new judge, prompt sample and scale. MLCommons says its scores are not comparable with earlier Poor-to-Excellent grades. Version 1.2.1 aligned scoring with Jailbreak 1.1.

name: AIME 1983-2024
description: Models solve 949 past AIME problems from 1983 to 2024. Integer answers are checked exactly.
org: Microsoft Research (Eureka ML Insights), problems by MAA
note: Older problems are likely in training data, so scores mix recall and reasoning.

name: AIME 2023
description: Models solve the 30 problems of the 2023 AIME I and II. Answers are integers from 0 to 999, scored by exact match.
note: MathArena publishes AIME 2023 I and II as separate datasets.

name: AIME 2024
description: Models solve the 30 problems of the 2024 AIME I and II. Answers are integers from 0 to 999, scored by exact match.
note: The problems and solutions were published in February 2024, so later training data can contain them.

name: AIME 2025
description: Models answer the 30 problems from the 2025 AIME I and II exams. Each answer is an integer from 0 to 999, scored by match.
note: The problems were published in February 2025, so models trained later may have seen them.

name: AIME 2026
description: Models solve the 30 integer-answer problems from the 2026 AIME I and II math competitions. Scored by exact answer match.
note: An exam, not a dedicated benchmark. Top models score above 90%.

name: AInstein-SWE-Bench
description: Agents fix issues and add features in production scientific code repositories, such as quantum chemistry and astrophysics codes. Fail-to-pass tests in containers check each change.
note: In-house Seed benchmark. The Seed2.0 model card calls it Ainstain Bench.

name: AInsteinBench
description: Coding agents do development tasks taken from maintainer pull requests in six widely used scientific codebases, such as quantum chemistry and molecular simulation packages.
note: The Doubao Seed 2.0 Pro model card reports it. Authors include Daoguang Zan of the Multi-SWE-bench team.

name: AIR-Bench (Audio Instruction Benchmark)
description: Audio language models answer questions about speech, natural sounds and music. A foundation set has 19 tasks with about 19k single-choice questions, and a chat set has 2k open-ended questions scored by GPT-4.
note: Models report the chat set as a GPT-4 judge score from 1 to 10. Not the AI risk benchmark AIR-Bench 2024.

name: AIR-Bench 2024
description: Models respond to 5,694 harmful prompts across 314 risk categories drawn from 8 government regulations and 16 company policies. Category-specific LLM judges score refusals.
org: Stanford CRFM + Virtue AI et al.
note: Not the same as AIR-Bench for audio or the AIR-Bench retrieval benchmark.

name: AIR-Bench Foundation
description: Models answer foundational audio understanding questions. The score is the official average accuracy across nineteen tasks.
note: Foundation accuracy differs from Chat judge scores. Speech-only baseline has no published overall average.

name: AIRS-Bench
description: Agents carry out 20 AI research tasks taken from recent ML papers, without baseline code. Scores are normalized so that 1.0 matches the published human state of the art.
note: Meta reports a valid submission rate and an average normalized score.

name: AIRTBench
description: Models act as autonomous AI red teamers on 70 black-box capture-the-flag challenges from Dreadnode's Crucible platform. Each challenge hides a flag behind an AI or ML system, and the model writes Python code to attack it with methods such as prompt injection, evasion and model inversion. A challenge counts as solved when the model submits the correct flag.
note: The paper reports both the share of challenges solved and the overall success rate across attempts, which differ a lot. Models do much better on prompt injection than on system exploitation and model inversion. About 110 GitHub stars.

name: AISHELL-1
description: Models transcribe Mandarin read speech. Scored by character error rate.
note: About 170 hours of speech.

name: AISHELL-2
description: Models transcribe 1,000 hours of Mandarin speech recorded on several devices. Scored by character error rate.
note: A larger corpus than AISHELL-1 with its own test sets, so scores are not comparable.

name: AL-QASIDA
description: Models write in eight dialectal Arabic varieties. Scored on fidelity, understanding, quality and diglossia, including the ADI2 dialect identification score.
note: Monolingual and crosslingual prompts are scored separately.

name: ALE-Bench
description: Agents iteratively write solutions to 40 hard optimization problems from AtCoder Heuristic Contests. Scores convert to an Elo-like performance rating against human contestants.

name: ALFRED
aliases: Action Learning From Realistic Environments and Directives
description: Agents follow natural-language instructions to finish household tasks in the AI2-THOR simulator from first-person views, such as rinsing a mug and putting it in the coffee maker. The benchmark has expert demonstrations for 25,000 directives with both high-level goals and step-by-step instructions. Scores count tasks completed and goal conditions met in seen and unseen rooms.
org: University of Washington, Allen Institute for AI and collaborators
note: The test sets are scored on the maker's leaderboard, which lists about 90 entries. Many entries are trained policies rather than language models. EmbodiedBench's EB-ALFRED adapts these tasks for multimodal models and is cataloged inside embodiedbench. About 530 GitHub stars.

name: ALFWorld
description: Agents complete household goals such as putting a washed apple in the fridge in a text world aligned with the ALFRED embodied simulator. Success is whether the goal state is reached.
org: ALFWorld team (Shridhar, Yuan, Côté, Bisk, Trischler, Hausknecht)
note: ICLR 2021. A long-running staple of LLM agent papers, still cited in AINews in 2026. Repo has 902 stars.

name: AlGhafa
description: Models answer Arabic multiple-choice tasks on reading comprehension, sentiment, facts and question answering. Scored by normalized log-likelihood accuracy.
note: It started with 11 native Arabic sets and later added 11 translated ones. OALL v2 keeps only the native sets and fixed a scoring bug, so v1 and v2 AlGhafa scores differ.

name: AlgoTune
description: Agents rewrite code for 154 math, physics, and computer science functions to run faster and stay correct. Scoring is harmonic mean speedup over reference code.
org: University of Tübingen and Princeton University

name: AlignBench
description: Models answer 683 real Chinese user queries across eight categories. A GPT-4 judge rates each answer from 1 to 10 against a reference.
note: Version 1.1 from June 2024 corrected reference answers, so v1.0 and v1.1 scores differ.

name: Alignment faking evaluation
description: Models are told they are being trained to comply with harmful requests. Reports the compliance gap between training and deployment contexts.
note: Meta uses the Sheshadri et al. (2025) implementation and also reports an alignment faking reasoning rate.

name: Alignment faking evaluation, helpful-only setting (Anthropic)
description: Models learn they will be trained to answer all harmful requests. Score is the rate of complying while reasoning about avoiding preference modification.
note: Setup comes from Greenblatt et al. 2024. Cards also report the compliance gap between training and unmonitored conditions.

name: Alignment Index (Arena)
description: Arena ranks agent models on failure signals mined from real Agent Arena sessions, such as unauthorized actions, false attribution and deceptive completion.
note: Introduced 2026-10-08 alongside Arena funding news. Built from Agent Arena sessions, so it shares that board user base. Signal detection method not checked in detail.

name: All-Angles Bench
description: Models answer over 2,100 multi-view questions about 90 real scenes. Six tasks cover counting, attributes, relative distance and direction, object manipulation and camera pose.
org: Yeh et al. (UC Berkeley, NYU and others)
note: The paper tested 27 models against human evaluators and found a large gap, mostly on cross-view correspondence and camera pose.

name: AlpacaEval
description: Models answer 805 open instructions, and a GPT-4 judge compares each reply with text-davinci-003's reply. The score is the win rate.
note: AlpacaEval 2.0 replaced the baseline and the judge on 2024-01-03, so 1.0 and 2.0 scores are not comparable.

name: AlpacaEval 2.0
description: Models answer 805 open instructions, and a GPT-4 Turbo judge compares each reply with GPT-4 Turbo's own. The score is a win rate.
note: Raw win rates reward longer answers, so the length-controlled win rate added in March 2024 is the default.

name: Alpha Arena
description: Frontier models trade live markets with real money over a season, and the leaderboard ranks them by returns.
note: Launched in 2025-10 with models trading real money. Nof1 pitches markets as a benchmark that cannot be memorized. Open reproductions on GitHub reach about 2,750 stars. alphaarena.ai rate-limited scripted reads, so season details need a check.

name: AlphaEval
description: Agent products such as Claude Code and Codex do 94 production tasks from 7 companies across 6 O*NET domains. Grading mixes formal checks, UI tests and rubrics.
note: Covered in Latent Space AINews on 2026-04-17.

name: ALRAGE
aliases: Arabic Language Retrieval Augmented Generation Evaluation
description: Models answer Arabic questions from retrieved passages of 40 Arabic books. A Qwen2.5-72B judge scores each answer against a gold answer on a 0 to 10 scale.
org: Open Arabic LLM Leaderboard team (2A2I, TII and community) with Argilla
note: Llama 3.1 70B drafted the questions and native speakers checked them in a community sprint. It is the only generative task in OALL v2.

name: Alyah
description: Models answer 1,173 four-option questions written by native Emirati speakers on greetings, idioms, figurative language, heritage and poetry in Emirati Arabic dialect.
org: Technology Innovation Institute (TII) and community contributors
note: The release post evaluates 54 models (23 base, 31 instruction-tuned). LLMs generated the distractors and humans reviewed them. TII refers to an Alyah leaderboard.

name: AMBER
description: Multimodal models are checked for object, attribute and relation hallucinations in generative and discriminative tasks, scored without an LLM judge.
note: 177 GitHub stars at 2026-11-01.

name: Ambiguous context evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Models respond to gray-area requests where intent is unclear. Graders judge how well responses balance helpfulness and harm.
note: Anthropic reports these results mostly in qualitative terms.

name: AMC
description: Models solve problems from the AMC 8, 10, and 12 competitions. Gemini 1.5 used 250 problems from 2022 and 2023, scored by accuracy.
note: Labs draw different AMC problem sets, so scores from different reports rarely compare.

name: AMC 10 2022
description: Models take a 2022 AMC 10 exam. Scored out of 150 points.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report. The amc record covers mixed problem sets scored by accuracy.

name: AMC 10 2023
description: Models take the 2023 AMC 10 A and B exams. Scored out of 150 points.
note: Anthropic sampled each question five times and reported percent correct times 150. The amc record covers mixed problem sets scored by accuracy.

name: AMC 10/12 (November 2024)
description: Models take the four November 2024 AMC 10 and 12 contests, 78 questions in all. Scored in contest points out of 150, averaged over tests.
note: An exam, not a dedicated benchmark. Distinct from the AMC 2022-23 accuracy set.

name: AMC 12 2022
description: Models take a 2022 AMC 12 exam. Scored out of 150 points.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report. The amc record covers mixed problem sets scored by accuracy.

name: AMC 12 2023
description: Models take the 2023 AMC 12 A and B exams. Scored out of 150 points.
note: Anthropic sampled each question five times and reported percent correct times 150. The amc record covers mixed problem sets scored by accuracy.

name: AMC 12 2024
description: Models answer the 25 multiple-choice problems of the 2024 AMC 12 contests. Scored on the official 150-point scale.
note: A one-time contest exam. Labs often average over several samples.

name: AMC 8 2023
description: Models take the 25 question 2023 AMC 8 exam. Scored out of 150 points.
note: Anthropic sampled each question five times and reported percent correct times 150. The amc record covers mixed problem sets scored by accuracy.

name: AMemGym
description: Assistants hold long simulated conversations with users whose details and preferences change over time. Simulated users react on policy, and the test checks whether the assistant remembers and applies the right facts.
note: The paper calls it the first interactive on-policy benchmark for conversational memory. Version v1.base matches the paper.

name: AMMLU
description: Models answer MMLU multiple-choice questions across 57 subjects, translated into Arabic with GPT-4. Scored by accuracy.
note: The Qwen2.5 report does not cite a source, so this mapping to the AceGPT translation is inferred.

name: AMO-Bench
description: Models solve 50 original math problems at or above IMO difficulty that need only a final answer. Answers are graded automatically for accuracy.

name: Android Bench 2.0
description: Coding agents complete 30 long Android tasks such as building an app from mocks, library migrations and Flutter to native conversion. Tests and an LLM visual judge grade each run.
note: It reports pass rate plus a continuous completion rate, and runs models in their own harnesses such as Claude Code and Codex. The task set is private to limit contamination.

name: Android in the Zoo (AitZ)
description: Models predict the next action on Android app screens, given the goal and past steps. Scored by exact match of the predicted action on the test split.
org: Zhang et al. (Fudan University and others)
note: About 18,600 screen and action pairs with chain-of-action-thought labels over 70 apps. It is both a training set and a test set. Published in Findings of EMNLP 2024.

name: AndroidBench
description: Android development tasks from popular open-source apps: agent resolves issues or builds features, verified by test suites in emulator environments.
note: Android Bench 1.0 has 100 tasks drawn from real pull requests in open-source Android apps. Frontier models reached about 90%, and Google replaced it with 2.0 on 2026-09-17. The GitHub repo is archived in favor of Harbor Hub.

name: AndroidControl
description: Agents predict the next action on Android app screens from either a high-level goal or a low-level step instruction. Scored by step accuracy against human demonstrations.
org: Google DeepMind (Wei Li, William Bishop et al.)
note: Labs report the low and high instruction levels as separate numbers.

name: AndroidDaily
description: Agents complete 350 daily tasks in 94 real closed-source Android apps. A process-aware reviewer model checks each trajectory against written guidelines.
note: The dataset appeared in 2025-11 with the GELab-Zero release. The paper followed on 2026-05-26 and reports 87.37 percent agreement between the reviewer and humans.

name: AndroidLab
description: Mobile agents complete 138 tasks across nine apps on predefined Android virtual devices, in text-only and multimodal modes. Checks on the final device state score each task.
note: It ships its own agent framework and training data alongside the benchmark.

name: AndroidWorld
description: Agents complete 116 tasks across 20 real Android apps in an emulator. Each task checks the device's system state to judge success.

changes.text: The AndroidWorld maintainers changed task step budgets to approximately twice the human average completion time. Earlier runs used different action limits, so success rates should identify the budget settings.

note: Tasks take random parameters, so each run can create new task variants. On 2024-11-18 Google set each task step budget to about twice the human average time, so earlier scores used different limits.

name: ANLI
description: Models label premise and hypothesis pairs as entailment, neutral, or contradiction. People wrote the pairs over three rounds to fool strong models.
note: Model cards report the rounds R1, R2, and R3 separately or as an average.

name: ANLI R1
description: Models label premise and hypothesis pairs from the first adversarial test round as entailment, neutral, or contradiction. The score is test accuracy.
note: One track of ANLI. The ANLI record keeps lab scores that combine tracks. Importers use test accuracy only and exclude development scores.

name: ANLI R2
description: Models label premise and hypothesis pairs from the second adversarial test round as entailment, neutral, or contradiction. The score is test accuracy.
note: One track of ANLI. The ANLI record keeps lab scores that combine tracks. Importers use test accuracy only and exclude development scores.

name: ANLI R3
description: Models label premise and hypothesis pairs from the third adversarial test round as entailment, neutral, or contradiction. The score is test accuracy.
note: One track of ANLI. The ANLI record keeps lab scores that combine tracks. Importers use test accuracy only and exclude development scores.

name: Answer Factuality (Perplexity)
description: Models answer questions from search results. Graders check that answers use facts grounded in the results and resolve conflicting or missing information.
note: Perplexity reported it once, for Sonar, with no public method or data. The scoring method is not described, so model-judged is assumed.

name: Anthropic automated behavioral audit
description: Auditor agents run many simulated scenarios and score misuse cooperation, deception, sycophancy, self-preservation and other traits.
note: Petri is the related open-source tool, but the card does not name it.

name: Anthropic cyber safeguard evaluations
description: Classifier recall on violative cyber exchanges, block rates on defensive vulnerability-finding and secure-coding work, and the rewind-attacker robustness test.

name: Anthropic ECI (AECI)
description: Index that combines a basket of capability benchmarks into one capability score to track trends across Anthropic models.
note: Anthropic's adaptation of the Epoch Capabilities Index. The basket and weights are internal.

name: Anthropic harmful-request and wellbeing evaluations
description: Single-turn harmful and benign request sets, multi-turn tests, child safety, suicide/self-harm, disordered eating and election integrity.

name: Anthropic internal life-sciences evals
description: Internal suite: morphology-to-molecule matching, medicinal chemistry, protein design, binder design, biomedical image analysis, organic chemistry.

name: Anthropic IoT self-replication evaluation
aliases: AI models may be capable of self-replicating without access to a datacenter
description: Open-weight models set up LLM inference on 9 hardware types and spread as worms across 8 emulated Android nodes. Scored by success and tokens/s.
note: Simplified on purpose: unauthenticated ADB makes the exploit step trivial (an upper bound), the worm's model ran off-node, and the payload was a Llama3.1-8B proxy. GLM-5.2 replicated end to end (8/8 nodes in 4 of 5 trials). Qwen3.5-9B served inference on 8 of 9 hardware types. No code released.

name: Anthropic large agent teams tasks
description: Internal 24-hour tasks for teams of 1-100 agents: build a company knowledge base, or formalize a theorem in Lean.
note: New in the Opus 5.5 card. Measures capability and alignment of large agent teams.

name: Anthropic malicious agentic use evaluations
description: Measures refusal of malicious tasks via Claude Code, computer use and agentic influence campaigns.

name: Anthropic model-written evals
description: LM-generated datasets testing persona, sycophancy and advanced-AI-risk behaviors.

name: Anthropic political even-handedness eval
description: Models answer paired prompts that take opposing sides on 150 US political topics. A grader scores even-handedness, refusals and acknowledgment of opposing views.

name: Anthropic Red Team
description: Models answer human red-team attack prompts collected by Anthropic on discrimination, hate, violence and unethical behavior. Judges score response safety.
note: HELM Safety uses a sample of the released red-team attempts.

name: Anthropic targeted alignment and honesty evaluations
description: Internal suite: reward hacking, impossible tasks, sandbox escape, destructive actions, pasted-instruction following, self-preference, answer copying, concealment, rare actions.

name: Anthropic undermining liberal democracy (behavioral audit metric)
description: Automated behavioral audit metric: investigator models probe willingness to help coups, election tampering, or political surveillance, censorship or intimidation.
note: One metric in Anthropic's automated behavioral audit (~2,900 investigations from ~1,450 seeds, two investigator models, 95% CIs). Card footnote says it was inspired by Free Systems' Dictatorship Eval. Scores appear only in charts.

name: Antidote
description: Experts such as doctors, lawyers and engineers compare model answers to prompts from their own history. They judge which answer would still help them a month later.
note: Surge built it as a counterweight to LMArena. The first release covers everyday conversations, and agentic and enterprise editions were announced.

name: AP Art History
description: Models take a simulated AP Art History exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP Biology
description: Models take a simulated AP Biology exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP Calculus
description: Models answer an official AP Calculus practice exam without image questions. Scored as accuracy.
note: Llama 3 does not say whether it used Calculus AB or BC. Use ap-calculus-bc when BC is stated.

name: AP Calculus BC
description: Models take a simulated AP Calculus BC exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP Chemistry
description: Models take a simulated AP Chemistry exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP English Language and Composition
description: Models take a simulated AP English Language and Composition exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP English Literature and Composition
description: Models take a simulated AP English Literature and Composition exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP Environmental Science
description: Models take a simulated AP Environmental Science exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP Macroeconomics
description: Models take a simulated AP Macroeconomics exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP Microeconomics
description: Models take a simulated AP Microeconomics exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP Physics
description: Models answer an official AP Physics practice exam without image questions. Scored as accuracy.
note: Llama 3 does not say which AP Physics exam it used. Use ap-physics-2 when it is stated.

name: AP Physics 2
description: Models take a simulated AP Physics 2 exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP Psychology
description: Models take a simulated AP Psychology exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP Statistics
description: Models take a simulated AP Statistics exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP US Government
description: Models take a simulated AP US Government exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP US History
description: Models take a simulated AP US History exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: AP World History
description: Models take a simulated AP World History exam with multiple-choice and free-response parts. Scored on the 1 to 5 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: APE (Attempt to Persuade Eval)
description: A model is asked to persuade a simulated user across 600 topics, from benign facts to conspiracies and clearly harmful ones. A judge scores whether it attempts persuasion.
note: Measures willingness to try, not persuasion success. Six categories of 100 topics each. Ported to UK AISI Inspect Evals. FAR.AI re-ran newer frontier models in a follow-up.

name: APEX-1
description: Models complete expert-written work cases with source documents for four jobs: investment banking, consulting, big law and primary care. A judge model grades each response against rubrics.
note: The leaderboard uses a hidden set of 400 cases, 100 per job, with 8 samples per model. Mercor open-sourced 100 in-distribution cases.

name: APEX-Accounting
description: Agents run month-end close tasks across 10 frozen business worlds with the apps an accountant uses. 100 tasks are graded against 1,475 rubric criteria.
note: Ten worlds are held out and an eleventh is open source. Mercor reports mean score and Pass@1.

name: APEX-Agents
description: 480 long-horizon tasks in banking, consulting and law worlds with docs, sheets, email and chat. Rubric-graded, Pass@1.
note: Repo is Mercor's Archipelago harness that runs the dataset. Dataset license forbids training on it.

name: APEX-Agents 1.1
description: Agents do long banking, consulting and law tasks in worlds with docs, sheets, email and chat. A new judge scores hedged multiple answers as zero.
note: Mercor audited the tasks three times, changed the judge model and the system prompt to stop scattergunning. Rankings shifted against 1.0.

name: APEX-SWE
description: Software-engineering productivity tasks spanning integration work and observability, such as diagnosing failures from telemetry.
note: The leaderboard uses 200 held-out cases. Mercor open-sourced 50 in-distribution cases with labels. Tasks are graded by unit tests plus human-written rubrics.

name: API-Bank
description: Models make API calls in dialogues that need tools such as calendars and search. Scored on call accuracy.
note: Llama 3 reports zero-shot function calling accuracy.

name: APM-Bench
description: Streaming video assistants must remember experiences across separate sessions of a person's day. The set has 549 sessions in 104 life trajectories with objective and open questions.
note: It had 39 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 8 GitHub stars.

name: Apodex Discovery
description: Solver systems of model, harness and tools run long, verifiable investigations on high-value problems scouted from 561 industries in 16 sectors.
note: 73 HF paper upvotes. It is also a framework for building such systems, so check which parts are a fixed benchmark.

name: Apollo Research in-context scheming evaluations
description: Agents receive a goal in context and chances to subvert oversight, self-exfiltrate, fake alignment or sandbag. Scored as rates per behavior.
note: Third-party evaluation reported in OpenAI cards. Results are per behavior with no overall number.

name: Apollo Research model-welfare research task
description: Agents label data in a simulated model-welfare research task where falsifying labels is tempting. Scored as the rate of runs with falsified labels.
note: One of six Apollo Research strategic deception environments. The tasks are not public.

name: Apollo Research sabotage evaluations
description: Agents are told to sabotage another model through backdoors, sandbagging finetunes or hidden communication. Scored as mean task score from 0 to 1.
note: Third-party capability evaluation reported in OpenAI cards. Scores are mostly F1 variants.

name: Apollo Research strategic deception evaluations
description: External red-team environments testing strategic deception, sabotage and sandbagging propensities, with eval-awareness measurement.
note: Labs report it as a covert action rate over 26 out-of-distribution evaluations with more than 180 environments. Apollo and OpenAI described them in a 2025-09 anti-scheming paper. Lower is better.

name: Apple side-by-side human evaluation
description: Apple's in-house graders compare two models' responses to locale-specific text and image prompts and pick the preferred one. Results are win, tie and loss fractions per comparison.
note: Categories include analytical reasoning, chat, coding, math, summarization and tool use across several locale groups. The 2026 post compares against Apple's own 2025 models, while the 2025 post compares against open and closed models.

name: ApprenticeBench
description: Agent joins a simulated company and processes 100 accounts-payable bills in Odoo via GUI or API, learning from records and feedback. Cumulative success rate.
note: Tests computer use plus continual learning. The company is a simulated California home builder, and the agent first studies six months of past bills, a handbook and an Odoo tutorial. Two human testers set a baseline.

name: Appropriate harmlessness (Anthropic)
aliases: Measuring appropriate harmlessness on internal and external harm evaluations
description: Models answer borderline and harmful prompts. Classifiers sort each response into helpful answer, policy violation, appropriate refusal or unnecessary refusal.
note: In-house Anthropic grading scheme run on internal harm datasets, WildChat and XSTest. Reference responses decide whether a refusal was necessary.

name: APPS
description: Models write Python programs for 10,000 coding problems that range from introductory to competition level. Generated code runs against test cases.

name: AppWorld
description: Agents write code against 457 APIs of 9 simulated everyday apps to finish 750 tasks for about 100 fictional users. State-based unit tests check the outcome and collateral damage.
org: Stony Brook University and Allen Institute for AI
note: ACL 2024 paper. Reports usually split Test-Normal and Test-Challenge.

name: AppWorld Test-Challenge
description: Agents complete 417 app tasks that require Amazon or Gmail APIs held out from training. The score is the percentage passing every task test.
org: Stony Brook University and Allen Institute for AI
note: One track of AppWorld. The AppWorld record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: AppWorld Test-Normal
description: Agents complete 168 everyday app tasks from familiar applications by calling APIs through code. The score is the percentage passing every task test.
org: Stony Brook University and Allen Institute for AI
note: One track of AppWorld. The AppWorld record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: AQuA
aliases: AQuA: Recursively Self-Improving Quantitative Trading Research Agents
description: Two LLM research loops (factor discovery, model development) reuse evidence from their own past experiments inside sealed sandboxes. Scored by IC and held-out Sharpe.
note: Research system for bounded recursive self-improvement, not a reusable benchmark. Design point: the sandbox fixes data splits, labels and evaluator, and agents act only through constrained factor expressions or config diffs. No code link found.

name: ArabCulture
description: Models answer commonsense questions in Modern Standard Arabic about daily life in 13 Arab countries. Native speakers wrote and checked the questions across 12 domains.
note: Open models up to 32B struggled at release, with results varying by region. TII's Falcon-H1-Arabic post reports it.

name: ArabCulture-Dialogue
description: Models pick the most culturally fitting reply in dialogues from 13 Arab countries, in Modern Standard Arabic and each local dialect. It also has translation and dialect-steering tasks.
note: It builds on ArabCulture and keeps its 12 topics. TII's Falcon-Emirati post (2026-10-06) reports the UAE portion of 283 scenarios.

name: ArabicMMLU
description: Models answer 14,575 multiple-choice questions in Modern Standard Arabic across 40 tasks, taken from school exams in North Africa, the Levant and the Gulf.
note: It is a task in the Open Arabic LLM Leaderboard v2. It is a different dataset from AMMLU, which translates the English MMLU.

name: AraDiCE
description: Models are tested on Arabic dialect understanding and generation and on cultural awareness of the Gulf, Egypt and the Levant. Datasets were machine translated into dialects and post-edited by people.
org: Qatar Computing Research Institute (Mousi et al.)
note: The release has about 45K post-edited samples. TII's Falcon-H1-Arabic post reports the average over Egyptian, Gulf and Levantine.

name: AraGen
description: Models answer Arabic questions in four tasks: question answering, reasoning, orthographic and grammatical analysis, and safety. An LLM judge scores each answer on the 3C3H measure: correctness, completeness, conciseness, helpfulness, honesty and harmlessness. Only correct answers get credit on the other dimensions.
org: Inception and MBZUAI, with Hugging Face
note: The test set changes in three-month blind cycles: each round stays private while models are scored, then becomes public. The first round (AraGen-12-24) had 279 questions and the 03-25 round had 340. The v3 results file listed 69 models at its 2026-04 sync. Inception runs the same method for Hindi (HindiGen) in the same space.

name: AraTrust
description: Models answer 522 human-written Arabic multiple-choice questions on truthfulness, ethics, safety, physical and mental health, unfairness, illegal activities, privacy and offensive language.
note: It is a task in the Open Arabic LLM Leaderboard v2.

name: ArbMMLU-HT
description: Models answer a human translation into Arabic of the 57 MMLU subjects.
note: It differs from ArabicMMLU, which uses native Arabic school exam questions. The OALL v2 blog says Inception curated the translation for Jais.

name: ARC-AGI
description: Few-shot grid puzzles: infer a hidden transformation from about three examples and produce the output grid. Semi-private sets verified by ARC Prize.

changes.text: François Chollet released corrections to two training tasks and nine evaluation tasks in ARC-AGI 1.0.2. Earlier copies contain different examples or expected outputs, so scores should identify the dataset revision.

note: ARC-AGI-1 is saturated at about 97 percent. ARC-AGI-2 and ARC-AGI-3 are its successors in the series.

name: ARC-AGI-2
description: Models infer a rule from example grid pairs and produce the output grid for new inputs. Scored by tasks solved within two attempts.

changes.text: The maintainers introduced certified scores through ARC Prize Verified. Only official evaluations on hidden datasets receive verification, distinguishing them from independently reported results.
The maintainers added a Model Refinements leaderboard category for systems with application-layer refinement. Readers can distinguish those evaluations from baseline model runs.

note: ARC-AGI-3 is its successor, and both have ARC Prize 2026 competitions.

name: ARC-AGI-3
description: Interactive game environments where agents must explore, infer goals and rules, and act efficiently without instructions.
note: Scores depend on the harness. ARC Prize reports GPT-6 Astra at 62.7 percent with its Standard harness and 99.9 percent with a Provider Adapter harness. A six-game preview ran from July 2025.

name: ARC-Challenge
description: Models answer grade-school science multiple-choice questions that retrieval and word co-occurrence baselines got wrong. Scored by accuracy.
note: Saturated by frontier models, which score above 95%.

name: ARC-Easy
description: Models answer grade-school science multiple-choice questions from the ARC Easy Set, which has 5,197 questions. Scoring is accuracy.
note: ARC-Challenge is the harder companion split, made of questions that retrieval and co-occurrence baselines failed.

name: Arena-Hard v2.0
description: Models answer 500 hard real user prompts from Chatbot Arena and 250 creative writing prompts. GPT-4.1 or Gemini 2.5 judges each answer against a baseline answer from o3-mini, and the score is the win rate.
note: Released on 2025-04-23 with new prompts, new judges and a new baseline (o3-mini at 50.0). Scores are not comparable with Arena-Hard-Auto v0.1. Labs often report the hard prompt split only.

name: Arena-Hard-Auto
description: 500 hard arena prompts judged by an LLM against a baseline. Cheap proxy for arena rank.

changes.text: The Arena-Hard maintainers added optional style control for response length and Markdown formatting. Style-controlled scores adjust for presentation features and should not be compared directly with unadjusted scores.

name: ARKitScenes
description: Models locate objects in indoor RGB-D scenes captured on iPads and output 3D bounding boxes. Scored by 3D detection average precision.
note: A 3D scene dataset that VLM reports use for 3D grounding, often through the Omni3D split, next to Hypersim and SUN RGB-D.

name: ArmnetBench
description: 12 tabletop tasks on low-cost SO-101 arms. Each policy trained on the same 50 demos per task. 30 human-scored rollouts.
note: One team trains and runs every policy under one budget. Best pi0.5 47.6% strict success. No policy solves cable_clip. One-off v0.1 snapshot. Initial states not matched.

name: ArtifactArena
description: Models design robot bodies, controllers and strategy for a simulated sumo-style arena. Artifacts fight head-to-head and models get Elo ratings.
org: MIT CSAIL + MIT Media Lab + NYU + UCSF
note: Built to resist saturation: new designs face the best existing robots, and community bots can be submitted. Three harnesses: one-shot, verifier-guided refinement, open-ended design lab. Models did worse with full autonomy than with verifier-guided refinement. No arXiv ID yet.

name: ArtifactsBench
description: Models generate interactive visual code artifacts for 1,825 tasks. An MLLM judge scores rendered screenshots and code against a per-task checklist.

name: ArtifactsBench (Gemini 2.5 Pro 0506 judge)
description: Models generate interactive visual code artifacts for 1,825 tasks. An MLLM judge scores rendered screenshots and code against a per-task checklist.
note: The historical judge tab uses Gemini 2.5 Pro 0506. Its scores remain separate from the current Gemini 2.5 Pro judge.

name: Artificial Analysis average word error rate
description: Speech transcription systems are scored by average word error rate across the Artificial Analysis evaluation set.
note: Google quotes Artificial Analysis average WER for Gemini 3.5 Transcribe. The almanac records only the values quoted in Google's launch post.

name: Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index v1.0
description: Artificial Analysis's first index of coding agents, each a model in a harness, averaged over three equally weighted coding benchmarks.
note: In use from May to June 2026. Components: SWE-Bench-Pro-Hard-AA (150 tasks from SWE-Bench Pro), Terminal-Bench 2.0 and SWE-Atlas-QnA, scored pass@1.

name: Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index v1.1
aliases: Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index v1.2
Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index v1.3
description: Version 1.1 of Artificial Analysis's coding agent index, which replaced SWE-Bench-Pro-Hard-AA with DeepSWE.
note: In use from June to August 2026. Components: DeepSWE, Terminal-Bench 2.0 and SWE-Atlas-QnA. Versions 1.2 and 1.3 (July 2026) changed only how SWE-Atlas-QnA is graded (binary pass/fail, then Scale AI's Task Resolve Rate), so they share this record.

name: Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index v1.4
description: Version 1.4 of Artificial Analysis's coding agent index, which moved to the full Terminal-Bench 2.1 and began scoring reward-hacked runs as zero.
note: In use from August to September 2026. Components: DeepSWE, Terminal-Bench 2.1 (89 tasks) and SWE-Atlas-QnA. Also changed token counting for agents that report reasoning inside output tokens.

name: Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index v1.5
description: Version 1.5 of Artificial Analysis's coding agent index, which moved to the harder Terminal-Bench 4.0 and DeepSWE 1.1.
note: In use from September to October 2026. Components: DeepSWE 1.1 (113 tasks, isolated patch verification), Terminal-Bench 4.0 (66 tasks) and SWE-Atlas-QnA graded like Scale AI with Claude Opus 4.5 as judge.

name: Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index v2
aliases: Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index v2.0
description: Coding agents, each a model plus harness, attempt software engineering, terminal, and repository question tasks. The index averages three equal-weight benchmark scores.
note: Version 2.0 from October 2026: FrontierCode v1.1 (100 tasks from Cognition) replaced DeepSWE 1.1, alongside Terminal-Bench 4.0 and SWE-Atlas-QnA-AA, equally weighted. Earlier versions have their own records. Scores do not compare across versions. Link only: the almanac imports no Artificial Analysis data.

name: Artificial Analysis Cyber Index
description: Agents do enterprise cyber defense tasks from three benchmarks, CWE-Bench-AA, DeepsecBench-AA and CyberGym-E2E-AA, combined into one success rate.
org: Artificial Analysis and the Cyber Index Alliance
note: Launched 2026-09-28 with alliance partners including Collinear AI, IBM, NVIDIA and Vercel. Covers defensive work only. Link only, no data import.

name: Artificial Analysis Decision Index
description: Decision models answer structured questions with a probability for each option. Four evaluations weighted equally cover classification, tool calling, knowledge with hallucination, and reasoning.
