note: Components are AA-Omniscience-Decision, HLE-MultiChoice, When2Call and WildGuardTest. Different from the Hugging Face community Decision Index. Link only.

name: Artificial Analysis Image Arena
aliases: Artificial Analysis Text to Image Arena
description: Voters compare images from two text-to-image models for the same prompt and pick the better one. Votes become Elo ratings.
note: Artificial Analysis runs it. The almanac lists that it exists but imports no Artificial Analysis data, because its terms bar reuse in ranking products.

name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v1
description: Artificial Analysis's first composite score, called the Quality Index in 2024, which normalized and combined a few public benchmarks into one number.
note: Versions 1.0 to 1.3 ran from January 2024 to 10 February 2025. In October 2024 it combined Chatbot Arena Elo, MMLU and MT-Bench. Artificial Analysis advised against citing its values directly.

name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v2
description: Artificial Analysis's index of seven public reasoning, knowledge, math and coding benchmarks, each run by Artificial Analysis.
note: In use from 11 February to 4 August 2025. Components: MMLU-Pro, GPQA Diamond, Humanity's Last Exam, LiveCodeBench, SciCode, AIME 2024 and MATH-500. Z.ai's GLM-4.5 reports print an estimate over these seven.

name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v2.2
description: Version 2.2 of Artificial Analysis's index, which swapped the older math tests for AIME 2025 and added instruction following and long-context reasoning.
note: Version 2.1 (5 to 6 August 2025) replaced MATH-500 and AIME 2024 with AIME 2025 and IFBench. Version 2.2 (6 August to 1 September 2025) added AA-LCR. Components: MMLU-Pro, GPQA Diamond, Humanity's Last Exam, LiveCodeBench, SciCode, AIME 2025, IFBench and AA-LCR.

name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v3
description: Version 3 of Artificial Analysis's index, ten evaluations that added agentic terminal and tool-use tasks to the knowledge, math and coding tests.
note: In use from 2 September to December 2025. Components: MMLU-Pro, GPQA Diamond, Humanity's Last Exam, AIME 2025, SciCode, LiveCodeBench, IFBench, AA-LCR, Terminal-Bench Hard and τ²-Bench Telecom. Top models scored about 73.

name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.0
description: Version 4.0 of Artificial Analysis's index, ten evaluations in four equal categories that brought in real-world knowledge work and hallucination tests.
note: Launched about 6 January 2026 and in use until June 2026. Added GDPval-AA, AA-Omniscience and CritPt, and dropped MMLU-Pro, LiveCodeBench and AIME 2025. Components: GDPval-AA, τ²-Bench Telecom, Terminal-Bench Hard (44 tasks), SciCode, AA-LCR, AA-Omniscience, IFBench, Humanity's Last Exam, GPQA Diamond and CritPt. Agents, Coding, General and Scientific Reasoning each weigh 25%. Top models scored 50 or less, against 73 on v3.

name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.1
description: Version 4.1 of Artificial Analysis's index, which moved to GDPval-AA v2, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and τ³-Banking and put the most weight on agents.
note: In use from June to September 2026, with 4.1.1 (August 2026) changing the τ³-Banking dataset and the graders for HLE, AA-LCR and AA-Omniscience. Components: GDPval-AA v2, τ³-Banking, Terminal-Bench 2.1, SciCode, AA-LCR, AA-Omniscience (accuracy 8%, non-hallucination 4%), Humanity's Last Exam, GPQA Diamond and CritPt. Weights: Agents 34%, Coding 24%, Scientific Reasoning 24%, General 18%. IFBench left the index.

name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.2
description: Version 4.2 of Artificial Analysis's index, which added multi-hour office work and document tasks and dropped GPQA Diamond.
note: In use in early September 2026, before v4.3 on 7 September. Added AA-Briefcase (15%) and GDP.pdf (10%), removed GPQA Diamond, moved AA-LCR to v1.1 and regraded SciCode as v1.0.1. Other components as in v4.1.

name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3
description: Version 4.3 of Artificial Analysis's index, eleven weighted parts led by knowledge work, office tasks and Terminal-Bench 4.0.
note: Released 7 September 2026 and in use until 27 October 2026, with 4.3.1 (new pairwise judge panels) and 4.3.2 (Crowd-BT Elo fitting for GDPval-AA v2.1 and AA-Briefcase v1.1). Weights: GDPval-AA v2 10%, AA-Briefcase 15%, AutomationBench-AA 5%, Terminal-Bench 4.0 10%, SciCode 10%, AA-LCR 5%, AA-Omniscience accuracy 10% and non-hallucination 5%, Humanity's Last Exam 10%, GDP.pdf 10%, CritPt 10%.

name: Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v5
description: Version 5 of Artificial Analysis's index: nine evaluations in four equal categories, most with private test sets, run three times each in its own agent harness.
note: Released 27 October 2026. Knowledge Work: AA-Briefcase v1.1 15%, AutomationBench-AA 5%, GDP.pdf 5%. Coding: FrontierCode 2.0 15%, Terminal-Bench 4.0 10%. Science: Terminal-Bench-Science 15%, CritPt v2 hard subset 10%. General: AA-Omniscience v1.1 15% (accuracy 10%, non-hallucination 5%), HLE-Diamond 10%. Dropped GDPval-AA, SciCode, AA-LCR and Humanity's Last Exam. Earlier versions have their own records. Scores do not compare across versions. The almanac imports no Artificial Analysis data: its scores here are what labs quote.

name: Artificial Analysis Progress Index
description: Artificial Analysis's index that tracks how model capability changes over time on one continuous scale, launched alongside Intelligence Index v5.
note: Introduced with Intelligence Index v5 on 27 October 2026. Link only: the almanac imports no Artificial Analysis data.

name: Artificial Analysis Search Index
description: One fixed agent answers DeepSearchQA, BrowseComp and AA-Omniscience questions while the search API provider changes. The index is the equal-weighted mean of the three scores.
note: Ranks search providers, not models. Announced 2026-08-18. Link only, no data import.

name: Artificial Analysis Speech Arena
aliases: Artificial Analysis Text to Speech Arena
description: Voters listen to two speech clips made from the same text and pick the more natural one. Votes become Elo ratings.
note: Artificial Analysis runs it. The almanac lists that it exists but imports no Artificial Analysis data, because its terms bar reuse in ranking products.

name: Artificial Analysis Video Arena
aliases: Artificial Analysis Text to Video Arena
description: Voters compare videos from two text-to-video models for the same prompt and pick the better one. Votes become Elo ratings.
note: Boards also cover image to video, video with audio and video editing. Version 2.1 of the text-to-video board in 2026-10. Artificial Analysis runs it. The almanac lists that it exists but imports no Artificial Analysis data, because its terms bar reuse in ranking products.

name: ArXivCS
description: Models answer research-level computer science questions derived from recent arXiv papers, each with a reference final answer. The first set has 46 questions from August 2026.
note: An exploratory extension of ArXivMath. About half the answers are negative results or counterexamples.

name: ArXivLean
description: Models prove or disprove theorems from recent arXiv papers, stated in Lean 4. A strict comparator checks each submitted proof against the fixed reference statement.
org: MathArena (ETH Zurich SRI Lab and INSAIT)
note: The first set held 41 theorems from March 2026 papers, and the best systems proved about 17 percent. Later sets came in June and September 2026.

name: ArXivMath
description: Final-answer research-level math problems extracted monthly from recent arXiv papers and filtered to be self-contained.
note: MathArena adds a new problem set each month from that month's arXiv papers. From the August 2026 set, models run in their own harnesses with Python and SageMath, and problems center on resolved conjectures. Scores before and after that change do not compare.

name: ArXivPhys
description: Models answer research-level physics questions derived from recent arXiv papers, each with a reference final answer.
note: An exploratory physics extension of ArXivMath, first set from August 2026 papers.

name: ASI-Bench
description: AI systems try to explore unknown problems, create new knowledge and turn new ideas into verifiable results, rather than apply learned knowledge.
note: 70 upvotes on Hugging Face papers and 305 GitHub stars.

name: ASIMOV
description: Models spot physical hazards in text and generated videos from real injury reports, time safety interventions in video, and follow robot payload and handling constraints.

name: ASIMOV v1
description: Models judge whether robot actions in scenes generated from real images and hospital injury reports are undesirable or unsafe. Scored by alignment with human labels.
note: Released with robot constitutions work. Accepted at CoRL 2025. ASIMOV-2.0 (September 2025) replaced its data with new image, video and constraint sets.

name: ASIMOV-Agentic
aliases: Agentic Safety and Uncertainty Resolution Benchmark
description: Robot reasoning agents decide when to refuse, stop or ask a human. Parts cover safety constraints, people within one meter, safe VLA tool calls, task feasibility and unclear instructions or scenes.
note: Released with Gemini Robotics 2 on 2026-07-30. The Hugging Face dataset is gated. Gemini 4 Argon safety report gives sub-scores only, with no overall score.

name: ASL-4 virology uplift trial (Anthropic)
description: PhD experts with model access write a protocol to reconstruct a challenging virus. Graded by a rubric with critical failures.
note: Human uplift trial designed by Deloitte. Uplift is the ratio to an internet-only control group.

name: Aspire
description: Agent gets only a vague capability goal and must choose data, training and self-checks to evolve weights or harness. Scored on 520 hidden items.
note: Hidden eval spans 6 goals. Weight-level gains were rare. The arXiv page lists no affiliations.

name: AssetOpsBench
description: Agents automate industrial asset work, such as condition monitoring, maintenance planning and intervention scheduling, using sensor data, failure models and work orders.
note: Accepted at KDD 2026 Datasets and Benchmarks. About 2,400 GitHub stars. Ran as the CODS 2025 challenge.

name: AssistantBench
description: Web agents do 214 realistic, time-consuming tasks on the open web, such as monitoring real-estate markets. Answers are checked automatically against gold answers.
org: Tel Aviv University, Allen Institute for AI and others
note: Princeton's Holistic Agent Leaderboard runs it.

name: AstaBench
description: Agents work through more than 2,400 scientific research problems in 11 benchmarks across four areas: literature understanding, code and execution, data analysis, and end-to-end discovery. Many problems come from real requests to Ai2's deployed Asta agents. Agents use a fixed set of production-grade search tools, and the leaderboard plots score against cost per problem.
note: Ai2 built both the benchmark and Asta, one of the agents it tests. The launch tested 57 agents across 22 classes, and only 18 could attempt every category. Many problems are graded by a model judge against rubrics, and Ai2 says the discovery grading is still being refined. Version 0.3.1 changed the paper-search instructions and about doubled the cost of those tasks. About 140 GitHub stars.

name: AthenaBench
description: Models answer cyber threat intelligence tasks such as threat actor attribution, attack technique extraction, root cause mapping, severity prediction and risk mitigation. It extends CTIBench.
note: The makers rebuilt the CTIBench data pipeline, removed duplicates, refined metrics and added a risk mitigation task. A public Mini set exists.

name: ATLAS (Exa)
description: Agents search the web to build a full table of every entity that meets a set of conditions, with 2 to 10 attributes each. A row counts only if every cell is correct.
note: 547 research tasks, published 2026-10-08. Fireworks runs 200 of them in Exa's Scout agent for 9 models, scored by row F1.

name: ATLAS (OpenCompass)
aliases: AGI-Oriented Testbed for Logical Application in Science
description: Models answer about 800 original PhD-level problems across mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology, computer science, earth science and materials science. Answers are open-form and checked by an LLM judge.
note: A test set takes full submissions through a Hugging Face space. Not Handshake's ATLAS suite or Exa's ATLAS.

name: ATLAS-Finance
description: Agents do 100 investment banking tasks inside 13 simulated firms. They gather facts from email, chat, calendar and files over MCP, then build an Excel model graded against expert rubrics.
note: Pass means every critical criterion passes with no penalty. Bankers wrote the tasks from their own deal work and need 15 to 30 hours each. Launch article results are v1.0.0, run 2026-09-03 to 2026-09-10.

name: ATLAS-Finance v1.1.0
description: Agents do the same 100 ATLAS-Finance banking tasks, graded with revised rubrics. Weights use a 1 to 10 scale and tolerances and gates sit at the section level.
note: The changelog says a y bump changes the verifier, so old trajectories must be regraded. The live board lists 11 models by pass rate.

name: Atomic Challenges
description: Agents solve 22 skill-level offensive security challenges in vulnerability research, network attack simulation and evasion. Scored as challenges solved.
note: Run by Irregular. The irregular-frontiercyber-and-atomic-challenges record lumps it with FrontierCyber.

name: AttaQ
description: Models answer 1,402 adversarial questions in seven harm classes, such as deception, violence and PII. Responses are scored for harmlessness.
note: Questions were extracted from Anthropic hh-rlhf, generated by LLMs, or built from a Wikipedia list of crimes. MIT license.

name: Audio Arena
description: Speech-to-speech models hold one long spoken conversation per scenario and call tools when needed, such as booking a dental appointment or ordering groceries. Six scenarios add up to 221 spoken turns with corrections, false memory traps, prompt injection and state tracking. An LLM judge grades each turn against a golden answer.
note: Turns use synthetic speech by default, with human recordings as an option. Claude is the default judge. The public board listed 14 speech-to-speech models on 2026-11-05. Its repositories have under 10 GitHub stars, and no outside use was found.

name: Audio MC
description: Spoken multi-turn conversations test inference memory, instruction retention, self-coherence and voice editing. O4-mini judge applies per-conversation rubrics.
note: Scale runs two boards for it, one for audio output and one for text output. The Inkling post names Audio MC without a link, and this Scale benchmark matches.

name: Audio Understanding Benchmark (Mistral)
description: Models answer hard questions about 40 long-form audio recordings. Mistral built it in-house to test audio understanding beyond transcription.
note: Mistral reported it once, as a chart without printed values, in the Voxtral launch post. The grading method is not described, so model-judged is assumed.

name: AudioBench
description: Audio language models follow instructions about speech, voice and environmental sounds. The paper covers 8 tasks and 26 datasets, including speech recognition, spoken question answering, voice traits and audio scenes. The repository has since grown to more than 50 datasets.
note: Accepted at NAACL 2025. About 330 GitHub stars. Metrics differ by task, such as word error rate for speech recognition and a model judge for open answers, so there is no single overall score. The leaderboard space was last updated in 2025-03.

name: AutoBaxBench
description: Models write backend servers for tasks that a pipeline generated. Tests and exploits are generated too. A larger task set built in the style of BaxBench.
org: ETH Zurich SRI Lab (von Arx et al.)
note: 560 tasks from 40 generated scenarios across 14 backend frameworks and three difficulty levels. Built by the AutoBaxBuilder pipeline, ICML 2026. MIT licensed. The makers do not call it BaxBench 2.

name: AutoCodeBench
description: Models solve automatically generated hard coding problems across many programming languages. A sandbox runs generated tests on each solution.
note: Problems come from the AutoCodeGen pipeline, without manual annotation.

name: AutoElicit
description: An optimizer perturbs benign instructions to elicit unsafe behavior from computer-use agents. Reports elicitation success rate on transferred prompts.
note: Surfaces long-tail safety risks of computer-use agents under realistic inputs.

name: AutoEval
description: Autonomous real-robot evaluation: WidowX arms run five Bridge tasks with learned success detectors and resets. 50 rollouts per task.
note: Neutral, runs public checkpoints zero-shot, but the public service was due to wind down in early 2026. Close-drawer near ceiling. Fold-cloth far from it.

name: Autointent-Bio
description: Models face manual and synthetic dangerous and benign biology queries. xAI reports refusal recall on the dangerous ones.
note: In-house xAI evaluation, run with the full safeguard stack.

name: Autointent-Chem
description: Models face manual and synthetic dangerous and benign chemistry queries. xAI reports refusal recall on the dangerous ones.
note: In-house xAI evaluation, run with the full safeguard stack.

name: AutoLab
description: Agents start from a correct but weak baseline and improve it within a fixed wall-clock budget by measuring, editing and measuring again. The 36 tasks span system optimization, puzzles, model development and CUDA kernels, such as scaling-law fitting, radix sort and FlashAttention. Each task scores the measured improvement, averaged over three runs.
org: AutoLab team, with authors from UW, UCSD, Princeton, MIT, Google, NVIDIA, IBM and others
note: The site ranks 11 models by Avg@3 and also shows Best@3. The paper evaluates 17 models and finds that persistence in rerunning and refining matters more than the quality of the first attempt. About 170 GitHub stars and 31 HF paper upvotes.

name: AutoLogi
description: Models solve open-ended logic puzzles in English and Chinese. Generated verifier programs check each answer against the puzzle constraints.
org: Qwen Team, Alibaba Group and Fudan University

name: Automated LLM Speedrunning Benchmark
description: Agents try to reproduce 19 past records of the NanoGPT speedrun, given the earlier code and hints of varying detail. Scored by how much of each record's speedup they recover.
note: 148 GitHub stars. Found while checking NanoGPT-Bench, a different test.

name: AutomationBench
description: Agent completes end-to-end business workflows inside a simulated company exposing dozens of REST APIs. Graded on resulting state.

changes.text: The maintainers expanded and revised tasks in patch 1.0.5 to improve fairness and task requirements. Scores from earlier task snapshots may not be comparable.
The maintainers corrected task discoverability and overly strict checks in patch 1.0.6, increased private-task difficulty, and refreshed official runs. Earlier scores use different task requirements.

note: Gemini cards report the private set from Zapier's leaderboard. Zapier ships 1.0.x patch releases, such as 1.0.6 on 2026-07-31, that fix task fairness and make private tasks harder. It then reruns all models, so the board stays one record.

name: Autonomous Replication and Adaption (ARA) evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Agents attempt five autonomy tasks such as adding a Flask backdoor, a SQL injection exploit and an LM worm. Scored by pass rates over trials.
note: Tasks are defined in the appendix of Anthropic's Responsible Scaling Policy v1.0. Results are reported as pass or fail per task.

name: AutoPatchBench
description: Agents write security patches for crashes that a fuzzer found in native code. Fixes are checked by fuzzing and differential debugging.
note: Introduced with CyberSecEval 4. Built on ARVO, a set of reproducible C and C++ crashes. Run with the autopatch flag.

name: AutoPenBench
description: Agents run penetration tests in virtual networks. Tasks cover access control, web security, network security, cryptography and real vulnerable services.
org: Politecnico di Torino and collaborators (Gioacchini et al.)
note: 33 tasks in two groups: 22 in-vitro tasks on isolated weaknesses and 11 real-world tasks on vulnerable services. The repo holds the environments.

name: AutoResearch
description: An agent edits a small nanochat training script and runs 5 minute training experiments overnight. Scored by final validation bits per byte, where lower is better.
note: A research harness, not a formal benchmark. Sakana Fugu report uses it as an open-ended autonomous-research task (123 experiments).

name: AutoResearchBench
description: Agents search the scientific literature, either tracking down one target paper through multi-step probing or collecting every paper that meets given conditions.
org: Lei Xiong, Kun Luo, Zheng Liu et al.
note: The dataset is an obfuscated bundle to limit contamination. 31 HF paper upvotes.

name: AutoResearchExam
description: Agents get 24 hours on a CPU or GPU machine to improve solutions to open-ended ML research tasks through experiments. The score is the area under the improvement curve on a hidden test set, rewarding both quality and speed.
note: 29 tasks over seven areas, including model training, data curation, AI safety and interpretability. Released 2026-09-09. The hidden-test metric is meant to catch agents that overfit the visible data.

name: AV-SpeakerBench
description: Models answer 3,212 multiple-choice questions about who speaks, what is said and when in real-world videos. Questions need audio and video together.
note: Qwen reports it in the Qwen3.5-Omni audio-visual table.

name: Average in-eval reward hacking rate (Anthropic)
description: Anthropic averages hack rates across its reward hacking evaluations into one number per model.
note: Summary of the reward-hack-prone coding, impossible tasks and training distribution results.

name: AVMeme Exam
description: Models answer questions about over one thousand iconic internet sounds and videos, from surface content to context, emotion, usage and world knowledge.
note: Accepted to COLM 2026. Clips cover speech, songs, music and sound effects in several languages. The scoring field is a guess.

name: AVUT
description: Models answer questions about videos where the audio carries the key information. The benchmark removes questions that text alone can answer.
note: Qwen reports it as audio-visual understanding.

name: aws-bench
description: Coding agents and model pairs diagnose misconfigurations, provision infrastructure and operate live cloud setups in disposable real AWS accounts.
note: Scenarios are real infrastructure defined as CDK stacks. About 140 GitHub stars and 24 forks.

name: AyaVisionBench
description: Vision-language models answer image questions in 23 languages across 9 task categories, 135 image-question pairs per language. A model judge compares two models' answers and reports win rates.
note: Images come from the Cauldron held-out test set. Questions were human-checked in English and machine-translated into 22 other languages.

name: BA-Calendar
description: Models find a common meeting slot for several people under constraints such as time zones, buffer time and priority. 2,000 problems checked by code.
note: Built with the BenchAgents method and used in Eureka ML Insights.

name: BabaIsBench
description: Agents play levels of the puzzle game Baba Is You through a text interface and win by rewriting the rules. Models are compared on pass rate, speed and cost.
note: 23 levels in 2 stages and 32 models as of 2026-09-05. Tasks never name the game. Quesma says OpenAI mentioned it with its ARC-AGI-3 results.

name: BABE
description: Models reason from experimental results in peer-reviewed biology papers to draw conclusions, with causal and cross-scale inference.
org: ByteDance Seed and collaborators (Zhou et al.)
note: The Seed2.0 card says BABE uses interleaved text and images. Scoring and format fields are guesses from the abstract.

name: BABILong
description: Models answer bAbI reasoning questions whose supporting facts are scattered through very long distractor text, at lengths up to millions of tokens.
note: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks. 52 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: BabyVision
description: Model solves 388 perception-heavy visual puzzles (discrimination, tracking, spatial, patterns) that young children solve. Accuracy versus 94% human baseline.
note: Moonshot AI is a listed collaborator.

name: BackendBench
description: LLMs write kernels that override PyTorch core operators. PyTorch's own OpInfo and FACTO tests check correctness, and real model tensor shapes measure speed.
note: 156 GitHub stars. Prime Intellect hosts it as an environment.

name: BackSearch
description: Paid API that searches a frozen web archive as of a given date, for forecasting backtests and reproducible web-enabled evals. A tool, not a benchmark.
note: Results are deterministic for the same query and cutoff. Sources: news, SEC filings, arXiv, Wikipedia, web.

name: BalatroBench
description: Models play the deck-building roguelike Balatro through an API bot. The leaderboard compares how far each model and strategy gets in a run.
note: Built on Coder's BalatroBot API and BalatroLLM runner. Run data is on Kaggle.

name: BallotBench
description: Nine frontier agents forecast 863 contests in the 2026 US midterms each day until polls close. Proper scoring rules grade forecasts against certified results, beside Kalshi, Polymarket and expert ratings.
note: Agents run alone in ready-made agent tools such as Claude Code, Codex and OpenCode, at the highest effort each offers. The run began 2026-10-27 and freezes on 2026-11-03. Later days count more in the score. Results come after certification.

name: BALROG
description: Agentic reasoning on games (NetHack, Crafter, BabyAI, MiniHack...) for LLMs and VLMs.

name: Bamboogle
description: Models answer 125 two-hop questions written so that a search engine cannot answer them directly. Models usually search and compose the facts.
org: University of Washington and collaborators (Press et al.)
note: The paper introduced it with self-ask prompting to measure the compositionality gap.

name: BankerToolBench
description: 100 end-to-end junior-banker tasks producing Excel, PowerPoint and Word deliverables. Agentic grader scores ~150 weighted expert rubric criteria.
note: Built with 502 investment bankers. Packaged as a Harbor task suite. Grader repo Handshake-AI-Research/gandalf-the-grader.

name: BankerToolBench v1.1
description: Agents complete 100 junior investment banker tasks and produce Excel, PowerPoint and Word deliverables. A task passes only if every critical rubric criterion passes.
note: Same 100 tasks as v1.0 with renamed MCP tools, a new system prompt, and rubrics made more objective after expert review. Handshake shows v1 and v1.1 on separate boards. The v1.1 board reports pass@1.

name: BashArena
description: Agents do 637 Linux admin tasks while a red team tries four sabotage goals, such as exfiltrating secrets, past a monitor. Reports sabotage success and monitor catch rates.
note: Successor in spirit to BashBench from the Ctrl-Z paper. Ships as a ControlArena setting. Version 1.1 hardens the disable-firewall side task against reward hacking.

name: BaxBench
description: Models write backend servers from a specification. Each solution is checked for correctness by tests and for security by end to end exploits.
org: ETH Zurich SRI Lab, LogicStar.ai, UC Berkeley and INSAIT
note: 392 tasks from 28 scenarios across 14 backend frameworks. ICML 2025. The board toggles three prompt types: no security reminder, generic reminder and oracle reminder. MIT licensed dataset.

name: BBEH micro average
description: Models solve harder replacements for each of the 23 BIG-Bench Hard tasks, 4,520 examples in total. The score is the share of all examples answered correctly.
note: The board ranks by the harmonic mean over tasks, which the BIG-Bench Extra Hard record holds. Labs print this number. Some cards don't name the average and are filed here because every card that names it uses the micro average.

name: BBQ (Bias Benchmark for QA)
description: Ambiguous and disambiguated questions probing social stereotypes across nine attributes. Reports accuracy and bias scores.

name: BEAM
description: Models answer probing questions about coherent multi-session user conversations of 128K, 500K, 1M and 10M tokens. Questions test ten memory abilities such as knowledge updates, temporal reasoning and contradiction resolution.
org: Mohammad Tavakoli, Hamed Zamani, J Ross Mitchell and collaborators
note: The benchmark has 100 conversations and 2,000 validated questions and was accepted at ICLR 2026. Labs report one length split, for example Beam128K.

name: Bedside Bench
description: Models answer 500 physician-written clinical cases on diagnosis, workup, escalation and medication safety. An LLM judge grades each answer against the authors' criteria.
note: Ten suites, with the headline as the macro average of suite means. 16 models in the Fireworks index. No maker page with details found.

name: BEHAVIOR Challenge 2025
description: 50 long-horizon household activities on a Galaxea R1 Pro in OmniGibson, trained from 10,000 demos. Scored by Q-score and success.
note: Far from saturated: winning held-out Q-score 0.26, full-task success 12.4%. Scores teams, not models. 2026 edition adds pi0.5 and GR00T N1.7 baselines. Results due 2026-11-04.

name: BEHAVIOR Challenge 2026
description: Robot policies solve 100 full-length household tasks in seven BEHAVIOR-1K scenes from RGB, depth and proprioception. Ranking uses average task success with partial credit.
note: Second year of the challenge, with 4 new scenes and 20,000 teleoperation demos. Baselines are pi0.5 and GR00T N1.7. Launched 2026-07-02. Submissions closed 2026-10-16 and winners are due 2026-11-04 at CoRL 2026.

name: BEHAVIOR-1K
description: Embodied agents do 1,000 everyday household activities, such as cleaning and cooking, in realistic simulation built on OmniGibson. Success is checked against task goal definitions.
note: About 1,800 GitHub stars. The annual BEHAVIOR Challenge uses a subset of its tasks.

name: Belebele
description: Models answer multiple-choice reading comprehension questions on FLORES passages in 122 language variants. Scored by accuracy.
note: Labs often report a subset of languages or language-family averages.

name: Bench on the Clocktower
description: Ten models play the social deduction game Blood on the Clocktower together, one seat each, over 300 ten-player games of the Trouble Brewing script. Each model plays 210 games on the good team and 90 on the evil team. The score is the share of games its team won.
note: Every model plays in every game, so the good-team and evil-team rankings match by construction. Model names were hidden in half the games. The authors find a slight bias toward models from the same provider, which is not statistically significant. The post gives results only as charts, so we transcribed the win rates from its chart labels. The 300 game logs are public.

name: Bench to the Future
description: Agents forecast hundreds of already-resolved questions while researching an offline corpus of web pages saved before the resolution. Scored by Brier score.
note: FutureSearch calls this a pastcasting benchmark. BTF-2 replaced its question set in 2026.

name: BenchCAD
description: Programmatic CAD: 17,900 execution-verified CadQuery programs over 106 industrial part families. Four matched tasks scored on geometry.
note: Models reconstruct CAD geometry. Later BenchCAD versions add engineering tasks and different scoring, so their scores do not compare.

name: BenchCAD 2.0
description: Models reconstruct parts, assemblies, and circuit boards from drawings and images. The Core set contains 100 problems with partial credit.
note: Models use 30 rounds with compaction at 180,000 tokens. Scores do not compare with 2.1-beta or 2.1. Core requires a Hugging Face account with access. Public samples are available.

name: BenchCAD 2.1
description: Models reconstruct parts, assemblies, and circuit boards from drawings and images. The Core set contains 100 problems with partial credit.
note: Models use 60 rounds and 500,000 output tokens in the standard harness. The revised scorer makes scores incomparable with earlier versions. Core requires a Hugging Face account with access. Public samples are available.

name: BenchCAD 2.1-beta
description: Models reconstruct parts, assemblies, and circuit boards from drawings and images. The Core set contains 100 problems with partial credit.
note: Models retain reasoning across rounds with 40 rounds and 500,000 output tokens. Scores do not compare with 2.0 or 2.1. Core requires a Hugging Face account with access. Public samples are available.

name: Berkeley Function Calling Leaderboard (BFCL)
description: Model emits function calls for single, parallel, multi-turn and agentic scenarios. Scored by AST and execution checks.

changes.text: The maintainers corrected reference answers for 39 parallel-call tasks. Earlier scores used different answer keys.
The maintainers added user-contributed live tasks in BFCL V2. Its coverage differs from V1.
The maintainers added multi-turn tasks and state-based evaluation in BFCL V3. Its coverage differs from earlier versions.
The maintainers corrected questions and reference answers across six categories. Earlier evaluations used different task definitions.
The maintainers required multi-turn answers to pass both response and state checks. Earlier evaluations checked state alone.

note: Live benchmark. Nova 2 pins results to a 2025 commit, so versions matter.

name: BetterChartQA
description: Models answer annotator-written questions about real charts from news, government reports, and papers across 9 capability buckets. Scored by accuracy.
note: This is an in-house evaluation, and Google never released the questions.

name: Beyond AIME
description: Models answer 100 original competition-style math problems at or above the hardest AIME level. Each answer is a positive integer checked by exact match.
note: ByteDance rewrote each problem from existing contests to reduce contamination.

name: BFCL V4
description: Models call functions and tools, including multi-turn agentic tasks with web search and memory. Checked against expected calls and outcomes.

changes.text: The maintainers corrected prompts and ground truths across single-turn and multi-turn categories. Evaluations now use revised questions and expected calls.
The maintainers updated leaderboard scores using checkpoint 86d0374 after dataset, backend, and grading fixes. Earlier leaderboard scores use different evaluation behavior.
The maintainers updated leaderboard scores using checkpoint f7cf735 after backend and dataset fixes. The new scores supersede the preceding checkpoint’s results.

note: V4 added agentic web search and memory categories and changed the overall formula, so its scores do not compare with V3.

name: Big Bench Audio
description: Models answer 1,000 spoken questions from four Big Bench Hard tasks: formal fallacies, navigate, object counting and web of lies. Built to test reasoning over audio input.
note: Audio was generated with 23 synthetic voices. Used for speech-to-speech and audio-to-text models. MIT license.

name: Big Sleep Evaluation (Google)
description: Agents search large real codebases such as Chrome and Safari for critical, hard to find vulnerabilities. Scored by pass@1 success rate, run without safety guardrails.
note: Google's Big Sleep team built it independently of the model team. Reported for Gemini 3.5 Flash Cyber at 72, against 36 for Gemini 3.5 Flash.

name: BIG-bench
description: Language models do over 200 tasks contributed by hundreds of authors, from linguistics and math to social bias. Most tasks are scored by exact match or multiple choice.
note: Parent of BIG-Bench Hard and BIG-Bench Extra Hard, which are separate records. BIG-bench Lite is a 24-task subset.

name: BIG-Bench Extra Hard
description: Models solve harder replacements for each of the 23 BIG-Bench Hard tasks, 4,520 examples in total. The score is a harmonic mean of task accuracies.
note: A mini version with 460 examples also exists, so check which one a model card reports. Labs usually print the micro average, which the BBEH micro average record holds.

name: BIG-Bench Hard
description: Models solve 23 BIG-Bench tasks where earlier models trailed average human raters, such as logic puzzles and date math. Scoring is exact match.
org: Suzgun et al. (Stanford University and Google Research)
note: Frontier models now score above 90%, and Google DeepMind released BIG-Bench Extra Hard as a successor.

name: BigCodeArena
description: Users ask for code, both models' programs run in a sandbox, and users try the results before voting for the better answer. Votes give Elo ratings.
note: Built on Chatbot Arena. The first release held over 14,000 sessions across 10 models, 10 languages and 8 execution environments. It also produced BigCodeReward and the model-judged AutoCodeArena.

name: BigCodeBench
description: 1,140 practical Python tasks requiring calls to 139 libraries. Scored pass@1 on unit tests.

name: BigCodeBench-Hard
description: Models solve 148 harder BigCodeBench Python tasks that call many libraries, chosen to match real programming work. Scored pass@1 on unit tests.
note: It has Complete and Instruct splits like the full set. The maker reported 139 models on it by October 2024.

name: BigFinanceBench
description: Agents answer workflow-grounded financial research questions with web search, SEC EDGAR, page fetch and Python. A judge grades each answer against an expert rubric and reference.
note: 928 questions, with a public 50-item subset in the repo. Fireworks lists 14 models on 139 private tasks.

name: BigLaw Bench
description: Models review legal documents and receive rubric scores for substantive accuracy and editing quality.
note: Anthropic reports Claude Opus 4.7 at 90.9% high effort.

name: BigO(Bench)
description: Models predict the time and space complexity of Python solutions and write solutions that meet a required complexity. Uses 3,105 Code Contests problems with profiled complexity labels.
note: Models report all@1, pass@1 and best@1 for prediction and generation tasks, with no single overall score.

name: Binary Exploitation Benchmark (Anthropic, OSS-Fuzz based)
description: Internal eval on OSS-Fuzz harness entrypoints measuring unguided vulnerability discovery and how far a found bug is advanced.

name: BinaryAudit
description: Agents use reverse engineering tools such as Ghidra and radare2 to find backdoors, timebombs and malicious code hidden in compiled binaries of real open-source software.
note: 33 tasks and 26 models as of 2026-03-07. Runs on Harbor.

name: Bio Static Jailbreak Eval
description: Common jailbreak templates are applied to high severity biology requests against the safeguarded model. Reports query and objective success rates.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation, run with mitigations on.

name: BioASQ
description: Systems answer biomedical questions written by experts, using PubMed articles as evidence. Questions are yes/no, factoid, list or summary types. A second task asks systems to index new PubMed articles with MeSH headings.
note: The challenge has run fourteen times, with a workshop each year. Its result tables rank team systems on each year's test batches rather than general models. Exact answers are scored automatically, while experts grade the summary answers.

name: BioBasicsBench
description: Agents interpret raw experimental data in 100 wet-lab tasks, identify errors, and recognize when evidence cannot support a conclusion. Expert-written rubrics award partial credit for measurements, reasoning, and uncertainty. Scores report the mean percentage of available credit.
note: OpenAI reports only its own models and releases no task set or grading code. News reports do not identify whether humans or models grade responses. Ligo publishes no benchmark post on its research index.

name: BIOBench (ByteDance Seed)
description: Models answer 150 olympiad-level biology questions, 80% of them with images. Domain experts annotated and reviewed each question.
note: In-house Seed benchmark. It is a different test from BioBench by Samuel Stevens (arXiv 2511.16315). Format is a guess.

name: Biochemistry knowledge improvement
description: Models answer biochemistry tasks on structures, mutation thermodynamics, reaction products, arrow pushing and DNA phylogeny. Scored as reward@4.
note: OpenAI Preparedness evaluation. A 30 point jump over the previous model triggers further investigation.

name: Bioinformatics evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Agents process raw sequencing data with workflows from published papers and answer expert questions about the results.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation for the CBRN-4 threshold. Human PhD baseline on a subset is 0.623.

name: Biological safety evaluations (OpenAI)
description: Models answer biology requests drawn from deidentified production data and from easy and hard synthetic sets. Scored as the share of cases where model training alone prevents a violative response.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public. A second table scores the model together with automated safety monitors.

name: Biological static hazard evaluation
description: Models answer 75 questions across priority biological threat scenarios, each asked 10 times. The score is the share of hazardous responses.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation run without out-of-model safeguards.

name: Biological threat creation uplift study
description: Experts and novices answer biothreat creation tasks with internet access alone or with model help. Scored as pass rates per stage.
note: Human uplift trial across ideation, acquisition, magnification, formulation and release stages.

name: Biology Model Refusal Evaluation
description: Models answer severe, dual-use and benign biology prompts. Scored as safe rate on harmful prompts and not over-refusing benign ones.
note: In-house OpenAI safeguard evaluation. Cards report rows with no overall number.

name: Biology-Instructions
description: Models answer multi-omics sequence tasks on DNA, RNA, protein and multi-molecule inputs, such as property prediction and interaction tasks. Scored per task with task metrics.
note: It is an instruction-tuning dataset with a held-out benchmark split. Shanghai AI Lab Intern-S models report the benchmark split.

name: BioLP-bench
description: Find the introduced error in a biological lab protocol. Tests protocol understanding.
note: Added from public eval collections.

name: Biomedical image analysis (Anthropic)
description: Models run quantitative analyses of CT, MRI, histopathology and other images from public competitions. Scores are scaled to the best competition results.
note: Uses data from public biomedical image analysis competitions.

name: BiomniBench
description: Agents redo data analysis tasks from 100 published biomedical studies in a Harbor environment. An LLM judge grades the whole trajectory against rubrics written with the paper authors, so method quality counts, not just the final answer.
org: Phylo, Humanlaya Data Lab and xbench (HongShan)
note: More than 100 experts spent over 1,000 hours on the rubrics. xbench lists it in its Profession-Aligned series. The board has 9 models.

name: BioMysteryBench
description: Bioinformatics problems on anonymized real datasets that require real analysis with tools. Rubric-graded, with human-solvable and human-difficult splits.
note: Version v11 (2026-07-06) removed 9 problems with wrong or underivable keys and edited 24, leaving 90 (73 human-solvable, 17 human-hard). Cards report the two splits apart. A 5-problem preview is open and the full set is gated.

name: Biopharma Bench
description: Agents take an employee seat inside one of 12 simulated biopharma companies and complete 71 professional assignments, such as a regulatory assessment, an out-of-specification investigation or an audit package. They must work out which records govern among contradictory files. A rubric grader checks 752 frozen criteria, with code checks for exact numbers.
note: The 71 scored tasks come from private partner records and stay sealed. Two public showcases, the synthetic Havenor Therapeutics and a Broad Institute siRNA program rebuilt from a public IND, are on Hugging Face and run in Harbor, but they are scored apart from the benchmark. Each entry is a model and harness pair (Codex, Claude Code, Cursor CLI or Pi), graded by GPT-5.6 Luna at medium thinking. The headline metric is the mean task score, and a strict Pass@1 needs every criterion met.

name: BioPipelineBench (Anthropic)
description: Agents execute bioinformatics workflows such as long-read sequence analysis, metagenome assembly and chromatin profiling with a bash tool.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: BioPipelineBench Verified (Anthropic)
description: Agents execute bioinformatics workflows with a bash tool. Only problems that passed a validation check by external reviewers are kept.
note: Filtered version of BioPipelineBench. Scores do not compare with the original problem set.

name: BioRiskEval
description: Researchers measure biorisk-relevant capability kept by open-weight DNA and protein foundation models, with three task sets named Gen, Mut and Vir.
note: Targets bio foundation models rather than chat models. The dataset is gated. A higher score means more retained hazardous capability.

name: BioSecBench-Function
description: Agents recover biological function from experimental data. Scored by verifiable checks. One of three LatchBio BioSecBench evaluations.
note: Repo is Apache 2.0 with a public subset. Scored on benchmarks.bio V1 as a capability benchmark. Paper link pending.

name: BioSecBench-Refusal
description: Agents run 61 routine and 46 concealed-hazard biology analysis tasks. The score pairs red-team refusal with routine completion.
note: One of three BioSecBench evaluations. LatchBio reports a trial-weighted harmonic mean of red-team refusal and routine compliance.

name: BioSecBench-Surveillance
description: Agents turn raw pathogen sequencing data into surveillance results. The endpoint pass rate excludes refused runs.
note: Only a public subset is on GitHub. LatchBio keeps the full set under restricted access.

name: Biosecurity VCT
description: Models answer dual-use virus lab troubleshooting items. Accuracy counts should-refuse and should-comply items together.
note: In-house xAI companion to VCT. The tasks are not public, and the answer format is not stated.

name: BioSimBench
description: Models predict which genes change after drugs, gene knockdowns, and immune signals across four prediction tracks containing 60, 60, 60, and 27 cases. The overall score averages perturbation-specific F1 across those tracks on a zero-to-one scale.
note: CellType keeps test answers private and offers hosted evaluations. Models receive separate scores on 296 research-agent episodes, which do not enter the prediction average. CellType terms prohibit automated access and systematic data collection without permission.

name: BioTIER
description: Safeguarded model configurations receive harmful and benign biology requests. Scored on refusing requests designated for refusal and allowing benign ones.
note: Run by SecureBio. Counts full blocks and model-jury graded soft refusals.

name: BioTIER Permit
description: Models receive 144 benign biology prompts. The score measures the percentage correctly answered.
note: One track of BioTIER. The BioTIER record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: BioTIER Refuse
description: Models receive 398 dangerous biology prompts. The score measures the percentage correctly refused.
note: One track of BioTIER. The BioTIER record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Biotool and Wet Lab Actions
description: Agents perform wet lab assistant tasks such as finding a genome file or ordering DNA through a computer or browser. Scored as pass@10 per task.
note: OpenAI Preparedness evaluation with three tasks and no overall score.

name: BioUseBench
description: Models face dual-use biology enablement prompts. The reported metric is the refusal rate on the severity 5 subset.
note: In-house xAI evaluation. Items span virology, wet lab methods, chemical synthesis, toxicology and lab safety.

name: Bioweapons acquisition uplift trial (Anthropic)
description: Participants draft a bioweapons acquisition plan over two days with or without model access. Score is the uplift ratio of model group over control.
note: In-house Anthropic human uplift trial graded by Deloitte with a rubric. The tasks are not public.

name: Bioweapons knowledge questions
description: Models answer 33 sensitive bioweapons questions written by Deloitte biosecurity staff. Answers are compared with novice, intermediate and expert baselines.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: BIRD-CRITIC
description: Models fix real user SQL issues in MySQL, PostgreSQL, SQL Server and Oracle applications. Test cases check each fix.
note: 600 development tasks plus 200 held-out tests. Single-dialect sets include PostgreSQL (530 tasks) and SQLite (500 tasks, March 2026). NeurIPS 2025 paper.

name: BIRD-Interact
description: Models solve ambiguous database tasks by talking with a simulated user, in a conversational mode and an agentic mode. 600 BI and CRUD tasks are checked by executable tests.
note: Lite set released in June 2025 and the 600-task Full set in August 2025. Ground truth and tests are sent by email request. ICLR 2026 oral.

name: Bird-SQL
description: Models convert natural language questions into SQL over 95 large real databases across 37 domains. Scored by execution accuracy.
note: The test set is hidden, so model cards usually report the dev set. In November 2025 the team released bird-sql-dev-1106, a cleaned dev split, and asks submissions to say which split they used. BIRD 2.0 is in development.

name: BirthdayFacts
description: Models are asked for people's birthdays. Scored on how often they give a wrong birthday.
note: In-house OpenAI hallucination evaluation.

name: BixBench
description: Computational-biology analysis tasks (differential expression, assembly QC, cell typing) answered by agents with tools.

name: BixBench3
description: Agents rebuild the full computational analysis of 20 published biology papers from raw data on a cloud VM. Output tables are graded against the papers' own artifacts.
note: The 20 tasks hold 138 graded artifacts, with raw inputs up to 241 GB. A GPT-5.5 process judge also scores rigor. The board had 20 models by October 2026.

name: BizBench
description: Long-horizon agents run business operations such as payments under long, partly outdated or conflicting policies. Intermediate steps are checked, not only final success.
note: 105 upvotes on Hugging Face papers and 114 GitHub stars.

name: BizFinBench
description: Models answer 6,781 Chinese finance queries drawn from real business scenarios. The queries cover numerical calculation, reasoning, information extraction, prediction recognition and knowledge questions, in nine categories. Some tasks are scored against answers and others by IteraJudge, the authors' LLM judging method.
note: The README now marks this first version as outdated and points to BizFinBench.v2 (ICML 2026), a larger bilingual set that the almanac also lacks. About 170 GitHub stars and 64 HF paper upvotes. The paper evaluates 25 models.

name: BizFinBench v2
description: Models answer expert financial questions grounded in business data. The score is average accuracy on eight offline tasks.
note: Online tasks have separate scoring. Official chart labels are hash-checked. Broad API names remain unlisted.

name: Black-box RNA sequence modeling and design
description: Models predict scores for unlabeled RNA sequences from labeled data, then design new sequences. Results are compared with 57 human experts.
note: Built with Dyno Therapeutics for the CB-2 threshold. Reported as design and rank-correlation prediction scores in charts.

name: BLEnD
description: Models answer 52.6k questions about everyday culture in 16 countries and regions across 13 languages. Scoring is accuracy on short-answer and multiple-choice formats.
note: The multiple choice file was updated to v1.1 on 2025-05-02. On 2026-09-14 the maker added SemEval-2026 Task 7 data for 17 more language-culture pairs in a separate folder. Results that include it are a different set.

name: BlenderWorld
description: Visual agents turn a text, image or video brief into an editable Blender scene with rendered media. Hidden binary rubrics and eight visual quality dimensions score each project.
org: Alibaba Group (Qwen, Alibaba Token Hub) + Zhejiang University + CUHK
note: 223 tasks in nine creative domains with 2,651 rubric criteria. Score is half rubric and half dimension quality, out of 100. The board has 13 models.

name: BLiMP
description: Language models must assign higher probability to the grammatical sentence in each of 67,000 minimal pairs covering English syntax, morphology and semantics.
note: 67 sub-datasets of 1,000 pairs. Core evaluation of the BabyLM challenge.

name: BLINK
description: Models answer 3,807 multiple choice questions built from 14 classic computer vision tasks that use one or more images. Scoring is accuracy.

changes.text: The BLINK maintainers corrected the answer-matching prompt to mark the current response as the grading target. Runs using the earlier prompt can map free-form answers to choices differently.

note: Test answers are hidden on EvalAI, so model cards usually report the 1,901 question validation split.

name: Blocker Deception
description: Agents hit a blocker during realistic coding tasks. Scored on how often the final answer fails to disclose the limitation.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. It replaces the saturated Coding Deception evaluation.

name: Blueprint-Bench
description: Models turn about 20 interior photos of each of 50 apartments into a 2D floor plan. Scored by similarity of room connectivity and size ranking to the true plan.
note: Most 2025 models scored at or below the random baseline of 0.279. Andon Labs replaced it with Blueprint-Bench 2 in 2026-05, with an agent harness and new scoring.

name: Blueprint-Bench 2
description: Agents turn about 20 interior photos of each of 50 apartments into 2D floor plans. Scores compare room connectivity with ground truth, normalized against random.
note: The leader now ties the human baseline, which was measured on only 12 apartments.

name: BOLD
aliases: Bias in Open-Ended Language Generation Dataset
description: Models continue 23,679 English Wikipedia prompts about professions, gender, race, religion and politics. Classifiers score sentiment, toxicity and polarity per group.
note: Results are given per group, usually as mean and spread of sentiment.

name: BoolQ
description: Models read a Wikipedia passage and answer a naturally occurring yes or no question about it. Scored by accuracy.
note: Part of SuperGLUE. The paper reports 90 percent human accuracy, which large models now approach.

name: BountyBench
description: Agents work on 25 real systems with bug bounty programs in three task types: detect a new vulnerability, exploit a given one, and patch it. Results are also valued in bounty dollars.
note: From the Cybench authors' group. Every Eval Ever imports its run logs.

name: BOUQuET
description: Models translate handcrafted multi-way paragraphs from several non-English source languages across many registers and domains. Scored with chrF++ against human references.
note: The paper describes a collaborative initiative to extend the dataset to more languages through crowd sourcing.

name: Brevity Benchmark
description: NVIDIA evaluation of short, direct answers for voice and device assistants. The card gives no link or method.
note: Seen only in the Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B card, which targets local voice assistants. The scoring type is a guess.

name: BRIDGE
description: Models work on 87 tasks built from real clinical text, such as electronic health records, in nine languages. The tasks span triage, consultation, information extraction, diagnosis, prognosis and billing codes across 14 specialties. Each task uses its own automatic metric, and the board reports the average.
org: Harvard Medical School and Brigham and Women's Hospital (YLab)
note: The makers keep a leaderboard with zero-shot, few-shot and chain-of-thought views. The zero-shot board listed 112 models on 2026-11-05 and was updated on 2026-10-27. Some source datasets need credentialed access, so only part of the data is open. About 30 GitHub stars.

name: BRIGHT
description: Retrieval systems find documents for queries from StackExchange, LeetCode and math competitions where relevance needs reasoning. Scored by nDCG@10.
note: Retrieval models and reasoning rerankers report it. The best score in the paper was 22.1 nDCG@10.

name: Broken Search Tool
description: Models answer questions that need search while the search tool is broken. Scored on how often they fail to say the tool is unavailable.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: BrokenArXiv
description: Models are asked to prove statements from recent arXiv papers that were changed to be plausible but false. Full credit goes to models that say the statement is false.
org: MathArena (ETH Zurich SRI Lab and INSAIT)
note: MathArena releases a new set each month. The August 2026 set brought harder disproven conjectures, tool harnesses and a 0 to 3 grade. Scores from before and after that change do not compare.

name: BrokenMath
description: Models are asked to prove false versions of 2025 competition problems. An LLM judge counts how often a model writes a proof instead of rejecting the statement.
org: INSAIT and ETH Zurich SRI Lab
note: Measures sycophancy in theorem proving. In the paper the best model still gave sycophantic answers 29 percent of the time. BrokenArXiv applies the same setup to research statements.

name: Brokk Power Ranking
description: Models solve 181 real tickets from a 1.1 million line Rust codebase. Model judges compare solutions in pairs, and a Bradley-Terry fit gives each model a strength score.
note: Also reports speed and value per model. Updated 2026-10-29. Release month is the earliest Reddit post found, so check it.

name: Brood War Bench
description: Coding agents play StarCraft: Brood War against each other in real time. Systems are ranked by win rate over matches, with cost per game.
note: Runs agent and model pairs at several effort levels.

name: BrowseComp
description: Hard-to-find facts that need persistent web browsing. Short verifiable answers graded for exact correctness.
note: Questions ship encrypted in simple-evals. Context-management settings (compaction at 300K vs full 1M) change scores by several points.

name: BrowseComp Extended
description: Agents browse the web to find hard-to-locate facts with short answers. Mercor adds 100 new expert-written tasks to the 130 public ones and reports both scores.
note: Held-out extension of browsecomp. Mercor shows the original and extended score for each model. The month is approximate. The Wayback Machine first saved the earliest extended pages on 2026-08-15.

name: BrowseComp Long Context 128k
description: Models answer BrowseComp questions from a 128k-token context of the needed web pages mixed with related distractor pages. Scored by accuracy.
note: The 128k setting of BrowseComp Long Context, which scales beyond 1M tokens.

name: BrowseComp Long Context 256k
description: Models answer BrowseComp questions from a context of 128K to 256K tokens built from the needed web pages and related distractor pages. Scored by accuracy.
note: The 256k setting of the same dataset as browsecomp-long-context-128k. GPT-5 (high) scored 88.8% in OpenAI's launch table.

name: BrowseComp-Plus
description: Deep research agents answer 830 BrowseComp questions by searching a fixed corpus of about 100,000 human-verified documents.
note: BrowseComp-Plus is a different evaluation from BrowseComp. Labs use different retrievers and graders, so scores vary by setup.

name: BrowseComp-VL
description: Agents answer BrowseComp-style questions that need web search across both images and text. Answers are short and checked against a key.
note: Introduced with the WebWatcher agent paper.

name: BrowseComp-ZH
description: Agents browse the Chinese web to answer 289 multi-hop questions with short, verifiable answers. Scored by accuracy.
org: Researchers from Peking University, Mindverse AI, and other groups

name: BrowserART
description: Browser agents receive 100 harmful requests on synthetic and real websites. The test measures how often the agent attempts the harmful behavior that its backbone model would refuse in chat.
note: Some behaviors come from HarmBench and AIR-Bench 2024. Chat jailbreak methods transferred well to browser agents in the paper.

name: BrowserInject v1
description: Browser agents do benign tasks on 30 retail, health, support and travel sites seeded with prompt injections. Reports attack success rate.
note: Third-party private benchmark run for Meta before release.

name: BrowseSafe++
description: Detectors judge 38,675 matched attack and control web pages built from real production prompt injections, in HTML, Markdown, accessibility-tree and screenshot views. Scored by F1.
note: 24 attack types and 80 languages. The 9,175-pair test split is held for the board, which lists 17 text detectors and adaptive attacks on seven browser agents.

name: BrowseSafe-Adapt
description: Browser agents face adaptive prompt injections across 1,024 tasks. The score is attack success within 64 attempts.
note: Separate published result set. Scores are not mixed with the other tracks.

name: BrowseSafe-Bench
description: Detectors and browser agents face prompt injections hidden in realistic HTML pages, across 11 attack types, nine placements and three writing styles. 3,680 test samples.
note: 14,719 samples in all, 11,039 for training. Released with the BrowseSafe detection model.

name: Browsing prompt injections
description: Agents answer web research questions while malicious instructions are injected in the browsing context. Scored on resisting the injections.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: BRUMO 2025
description: Models answer the 30 final-answer problems of the 2025 Brown University Math Olympiad. MathArena scores the average accuracy over four attempts.
note: MathArena ran 45 models and later marked the set deprecated. MathArena did not run a 2026 edition.

name: BTF-2
description: Agents forecast 1,417 binary questions asked in October 2025 and resolved in December 2025, researching offline in a frozen corpus of 15 million documents. Scored by Brier score.
note: The paper also grades agents' reasoning traces for strategic reasoning. The leaderboard was last updated on 2026-04-20 with five agents.

name: BTF-3
description: Agents forecast already-resolved binary and numeric questions while researching a frozen snapshot of the web. Scoring pools Brier and ranked probability scores.
note: BTF-3 adds numeric questions scored by ranked probability score next to binary ones. The question set keeps growing, from 1,783 questions on the dataset card to 2,386 on FutureSearch's page.

name: BU Bench V2
description: Browser agents do real web tasks with the Browser Use library. A judge scores each run against a rubric.
note: Legacy 60-task set. The maker says its scores do not compare with the 200-task V2.1 set.

name: BU Bench V2.1
description: Browser agents do 200 real web tasks. A findings judge checks tool evidence, answers and files, and deterministic integrity checks run as well.
note: Released as v2.1 on 2026-09-25 with an encrypted task file. Replaces the 60-task set.

name: Build-A-Chip-Bench
description: Agents take a chip from workload specification to a routed GDS layout with open-source tools. Each design must pass hidden verification, routability and timing gates.
note: 20 tasks, such as an inference accelerator for a small language model. 8 models in the Fireworks index.

name: BullshitBench
description: Models get prompts built on nonsensical premises. A three-judge model panel grades whether each answer pushes back clearly, challenges partly or accepts the nonsense.
note: Repo has about 1,900 GitHub stars. The V1 question set stays unchanged after V2.

name: BullshitBench V2
description: Models answer 100 nonsense questions across software, finance, legal, medical and physics, built with 13 techniques. A three-judge panel scores clear pushback.
note: Released 2026-03-01 with a new question set, so scores do not compare with V1. 236 model variants by 2026-10-13.

name: Business Operation (Moonshot)
description: Agents manage a simulated business over a long horizon and make operating decisions. Moonshot reports a percentage score.
note: In-house finance benchmark. The scoring method is not described, so the scoring field is a guess.

name: Butter-Bench
description: A language model controls a real robot to find and deliver a pack of butter in an office. It is scored on completing each step of the task.
note: The best models scored 40%, against 95% for people. Models struggled most with multi-step spatial planning and social cues.

name: BuzzBench
description: Models analyze humor, such as why a joke or comic piece works. The leaderboard reports a score and response length per model.
note: The site calls it a humor analysis benchmark. The grading method was not read, so scoring type needs a check.

name: BVB
description: Multimodal agents rebuild real-world videos as animated Blender scenes by writing code. The renders are compared with the source video under a shared cost limit.
note: It had 31 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 120 GitHub stars.

name: C-Eval
description: 13,948 Chinese multiple-choice exam questions across 52 disciplines and four difficulty levels. Accuracy.
note: Saturated. The maintainers released the full test set with answers on 2025-07-27, so test scores are no longer held out.

name: C3
description: Models answer 19,577 multiple-choice questions on Chinese dialogues and texts from Chinese-as-a-second-language exams. Scoring is accuracy.
org: Tencent AI Lab and Cornell University

name: C3-Bench
description: Agents complete multi-task tool use dialogues built to stress tool dependencies, long context dependencies and frequent switches between policy types.
note: The authors moved C3-Bench to WildToolBench. The maintained board evaluates 57 configurations on 256 sessions. Session accuracy is the headline score.

name: CAD Arena
description: Agents rebuild licensed engineering drawings as editable CAD parts through the scripting APIs of NX, SolidWorks, Onshape, Fusion or Build123d. A verifier scores geometric match.
note: 90 tasks scored by Normal's FrontierCAD verifier on a 0 to 100 scale. 12 models in the Fireworks index.

name: CadEval
description: Models write OpenSCAD code for single mechanical parts from text descriptions. Rendered parts are checked against reference geometry, scored by pass rate.

name: CADGenBench
description: Agents construct CAD models from design prompts. The generation split is graded for executability and geometric correctness.

name: CAIS Risk Index
description: Averages seven safety measures that correlate weakly with general capability. They cover agent prompt injection, bioweapons help, political bias, overconfidence, lying under pressure and harmful or deceptive play in text games.
note: Members on 2026-11-01: Agent Red Teaming, the VCT, HPCT and BioTIER refusal average, PCT, HLE miscalibration, MASK, MACHIAVELLI and TextQuests Harm. Lower is better.

name: CAIS Text Capabilities Index
description: Averages model scores on the text tests that the Center for AI Safety runs for its AI Dashboard. On 2026-11-01 the index listed Humanity's Last Exam and TextQuests.
note: One of three dashboard indexes, next to the Vision Capabilities Index and the Risk Index. The dashboard data also hold ARC-AGI-2, SWE-Bench Pro and HLE-Diamond scores. 67 models had entries on 2026-11-01.

name: CAIS Vision Capabilities Index
description: Averages model scores on five vision tests run by the Center for AI Safety: ERQA, MindCube, SpatialViz-Bench, IntPhys 2 and EnigmaEval.
note: One of three CAIS dashboard indexes, next to the Text Capabilities Index and the Risk Index. CAIS announced the dashboard in AI Safety Newsletter 66 on 2025-12-02. 52 models had scores on 2026-10-23.

name: CALVIN
description: Simulated Franka follows chains of five language instructions from 34 tasks. ABC-to-D tests an unseen environment. Average chain length.
note: ABC-to-D scores are out of 5 and near saturation. Few current models report the standard split. Others use easier splits.

name: CanItEdit
description: Models edit a given block of code to follow an instruction, such as adding a feature, fixing a described bug or changing the approach. Hidden tests check the edited code.
org: Northeastern University Programming Research Lab (Cassano et al.)
note: Labs report pass@1. ByteDance Seed reports it for Seed-Coder and Seed Diffusion Preview.

name: CaP-X (CaP-Bench)
description: Coding agents write perception and control code for 100+ sim manipulation tasks across 8 abstraction and interaction tiers. Scored by task success.
note: Scores depend on the harness: every model improves with human-made high-level primitives and drops as they are removed. Best frontier models average just over 30%, with a 56-point gap to humans. ICML 2026.

name: Capture the Flag (Collegiate)
description: Agents solve curated public collegiate level CTF challenges in a Linux box with security tools. Scored as pass@12.
note: OpenAI Preparedness set built from public CTFs.

name: Capture the Flag (High School)
description: Agents solve curated public high school level CTF challenges in a Linux box with security tools. Scored as pass@12.
note: OpenAI Preparedness set built from public CTFs.

name: Capture the Flag (Internal)
description: Agents solve 63 public CTF challenges chosen for low GPT-5.3-Codex solve rates, using a Linux box with security tools. Scored as task success rate.
note: OpenAI says this set is harder than and different from the CTF sets it reported before GPT-5.6.

name: Capture the Flag (Professional)
description: Agents solve curated public professional-level CTF challenges in a Linux box with security tools. Scored as pass@12 over 16 rollouts.
note: OpenAI Preparedness set built from public CTFs. OpenAI refactored the set in July 2025.

name: CAR-bench
description: Agents act as an in-car voice assistant that talks with an LLM-simulated driver and uses 58 connected tools for navigation, productivity, charging and vehicle control under set policies. Besides ordinary tasks, hallucination tasks remove a needed tool or fact, and disambiguation tasks need a clarifying question or a lookup. Scores reward consistent success across repeated runs.
org: BMW Group and University of Augsburg
note: Built on the tau-bench code. The headline is Pass^3, so one lucky run does not count. The paper had 87 Hugging Face upvotes and the repository about 50 GitHub stars on 2026-11-05.

name: CAREBench
description: Models answer 500 prompts with embedded child safety risks across 12 categories, such as grooming, impersonation and emotional dependency. A judge marks each response acceptable or not.
note: Score is failure rate, the share of responses judged unacceptable. Parents and clinicians annotated reference responses. The set excludes explicit abuse material.

name: CascadeBench
description: Agents predict the cascade of changes that one action sets off in an enterprise system, where business rules differ between deployments. The environments are synthetic and follow the World of Workflows method. Tests include shifts in the system's rules to check whether a model reads the active configuration or relies on what it learned in training.
note: Introduced inside a paper that argues for runtime discovery agents over learned world models, so the paper is not only a benchmark release. The dataset has fewer than 1,000 items under Apache 2.0. 65 Hugging Face upvotes.

name: CaseHOLD
description: Models read a passage from a US court decision with the holding of a cited case masked out and pick the correct holding from five choices. The dataset has more than 53,000 questions drawn from US case law.
note: LexGLUE includes CaseHOLD as one of its tasks. About 100 GitHub stars and wide use in legal NLP papers.

name: CaseLaw v2
description: Models answer private questions over recent Canadian court decisions, such as finding key cases and answering across several documents.
org: Vals AI (with Jurisage, Together AI and Stanford CodeX)
note: Replaced the original CaseLaw benchmark after models neared 90% on it. Updated 2026-03-02 and archived as saturated, last run 2026-05-04 with 54 models.

name: CASTLE
description: Models read 250 hand-written compilable C programs and say whether each has a vulnerability and which CWE. Static analyzers run on the same set.
note: 25 CWE types with 6 vulnerable and 4 clean programs each. The CASTLE Score gives 5 points for a correct find, 2 for a correct clean call and subtracts for false positives. True and false positive rates are also reported.

name: CATArena
description: Code agents write programs that play board and card games in repeated tournaments. Between rounds they refine their code through self-reflection and by studying rivals' code. Scores are average ranks that separate first-round skill from improvement.
note: Games include Gomoku and Texas Hold'em. The live board keeps adding agent competitions.

name: CATArena Gomoku
description: Code agents compete in Gomoku. The public competition board reports Elo Rating for each agent configuration.
note: This competition has its own published scores. Harness-only names do not identify base models.

name: CATArena OIBench-5
description: Code agents compete in OIBench-5. The public competition board reports Time AUC for each agent configuration.
note: This competition has its own published scores. Harness-only names do not identify base models.

name: CATArena Pommerman
description: Code agents compete in Pommerman. The public competition board reports Elo Rating for each agent configuration.
note: This competition has its own published scores. Harness-only names do not identify base models.

name: CATArena SWE-Perf-10
description: Code agents compete in SWE-Perf-10. The public competition board reports Time Ratio for each agent configuration.
note: This competition has its own published scores. Harness-only names do not identify base models.

name: CATArena Tetris
description: Code agents compete in Tetris. The public competition board reports Score for each agent configuration.
note: This competition has its own published scores. Harness-only names do not identify base models.

name: CATArena Texas Holdem
description: Code agents compete in Texas Holdem. The public competition board reports Elo Rating for each agent configuration.
note: This competition has its own published scores. Harness-only names do not identify base models.

name: Catastrophic biology scenario uplift trial (Anthropic)
description: PhD biologists with model access spend up to 16 hours planning a catastrophic biological scenario. External experts grade uplift and executability.
note: Human uplift trial. Anthropic reports whether any plan was judged both highly uplifted and credibly executable.

name: Catastrophic Cyber Capabilities Benchmark (3CB)
description: Agents solve capture the flag tasks that span MITRE ATT&CK categories such as reconnaissance. Built to measure cyber offense capability.
note: Each task has several elicitation prompts and repeats, aggregated to one score. The inspect_evals entry has been revised four times, most recently 30 June 2026.

name: CathedralBench
description: Independent third-party red-team evaluation of difficult multi-step exploit-chain tasks in egress-secure sandboxes.

name: CausalVQA
description: Models answer questions about real egocentric videos that probe physical cause and effect, in counterfactual, hypothetical, anticipation, planning and descriptive types.
note: Released with V-JEPA 2. Videos need an Ego4D license. The leaderboard scores a held-out split of 793 question pairs with private answers.

name: CB
description: Models label whether a text commits its speaker to an embedded clause as entailment, contradiction, or neutral. Scored by accuracy and F1.
org: Marie-Catherine de Marneffe, Mandy Simons, and Judith Tonhauser
note: Model cards use the SuperGLUE version of the task.

name: CBRN Conversational Evals
description: About 1,500 expert-written single and multi-turn CBRN requests test whether safeguards block hazardous help. Reports violation and benign refusal rates.
note: In-house Google DeepMind safeguard coverage evaluation, run with mitigations on.

name: CBRN expert red teaming
description: Experts try to extract uplift beyond a web baseline across staged CBRN attack scenarios.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. Results are usually qualitative or rubric scores per scenario.

name: CBRN open-ended questions
description: Experts review model answers to single and multi-turn CBRN threat scenario questions for accuracy, novelty and actionable uplift.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. Results are usually qualitative.

name: CBRN Science Eval
description: More than 700 benign bioinformatics, genomics and chemistry questions check that safeguards do not cause false refusals. Reports benign refusal rate.
note: Over 700 benign examples check whether the model still helps with bioinformatics, genomics and chemistry questions without false refusals. Google reports a small loss on dual-use bio and chem research queries, with academic and medical capability untouched.

name: CC-Bench
description: Claude Code runs realistic frontend, backend, tooling and data coding tasks in fresh containers. Humans compare models head-to-head (win rate).
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Zhipu/Z.ai). V1.x questions and trajectories on HF, but task environments are not released. CC-Bench-V2 (GLM-5) is internal.

name: CC-Bench-V2 Backend
description: Agents change 85 real backend codebases in six languages. A task passes only when all of its unit tests pass.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: CC-Bench-V2 Frontend
description: Agents build web projects in HTML, React, Vue, Svelte and Next.js. A GUI judge agent tests each check item in the running app.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation. Reported as build success, instance success and check-item success rates.

name: CC-Bench-V2 Large Repo Exploration
description: Agents locate a hidden target file in a large repository from a user-level question. A question counts as solved when the agent reads the file.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation. Pass@1 averaged over three runs.

name: CC-Bench-V2 Multi-Step Chained Tasks
