description: Agents complete chains of tasks mined from merged pull requests, where each step changes the codebase for the next. Tests check every step.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation. Pass@1 on individual tasks.

name: CC-OCR
description: Models read text in 7,058 images across four tracks: scene text, multilingual text, document parsing, and key information extraction. Each track has its own metric.

name: CC-OCR-Bench-V2
description: Models process 7,093 hard real-world document samples across five OCR tracks, including parsing and document QA. Each track uses its own metric.
org: Chunyi Peng et al. (with Qwen team members)
note: This is a new version, and the original CC-OCR from December 2024 is a separate benchmark.

name: CCBench (MMBench Chinese Culture)
description: Vision language models answer 510 Chinese-language multiple-choice questions about images of Chinese culture, such as calligraphy, painting, food and historical figures.
note: The makers removed noisy samples on 2023-12-26, and the leaderboard was rescored. Not related to the Z.ai coding test CC-Bench.

name: CCPM
description: Models pick which of four classical Chinese poetry lines matches a given modern Chinese translation. Scored by accuracy.

name: Cekura Agent Performance
description: Scenario reliability across three repeated calls (Pass³).
note: Separate task board. No combined Cekura score exists. Costs use their explicitly named units.

name: Cekura Bench
description: Models complete separately scored speech recognition, speech generation, voice-agent, real-call, turn-taking and voice-quality benchmarks. Cekura publishes no combined score.
note: Cekura runs the benchmarks while selling voice-agent testing services. Cekura publishes results under CC BY 4.0 but withholds licensed recordings and some judge prompts. Cekura dates the site launch to July 8, 2026, before the November scan.

name: Cekura Production Voice Agents
description: Published composite score for production voice agents.
note: Separate task board. No combined Cekura score exists. Costs use their explicitly named units.

name: Cekura Real Human Calls
description: Real caller reliability across three repeated calls (Pass³).
note: Separate task board. No combined Cekura score exists. Costs use their explicitly named units.

name: Cekura Speech to Text
description: Overall word error rate across the published audio clips.
note: Separate task board. No combined Cekura score exists. Costs use their explicitly named units.

name: Cekura Text to Speech
description: Round-trip word error rate averaged across the two transcribers, as displayed by Cekura.
note: Separate task board. No combined Cekura score exists. Costs use their explicitly named units.

name: Cekura Turn Bench
description: Mean end-of-turn score across six line conditions, as published by Cekura.
note: Separate task board. No combined Cekura score exists. Costs use their explicitly named units.

name: CELLO
description: Models follow real-world complex instructions with multiple tasks, noisy inputs and format or length constraints. Rule-based checks score each answer against the instruction features.
note: Published at AAAI 2024.

name: CEO-Bench
description: Agents steer a simulated AI startup for 500 days, gathering noisy information and adapting plans. The outcome of the simulated company is the score.
note: AINews noted that endpoint choice changed Kimi K3 results a lot. 83 GitHub stars.

name: Certified Sommelier (theory knowledge)
description: Models answer wine theory questions at the certified sommelier level. Scoring is accuracy.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: CF-Div2-Stepfun
description: Models solve 53 Codeforces Div. 2 problems from September 2024 to February 2025. An offline judge with rebuilt test cases scores C++, Python and Java submissions.
note: StepFun reports avg@8 accuracy per language and an estimated Codeforces rating. The judge flags 92.45% of known failed submissions.

name: CFBench
description: Models follow 1,000 real-world instructions with embedded constraints, across more than 200 scenarios and 50 NLP tasks. A judge checks each constraint and the overall requirement.
note: Constraints fall into 10 primary types and over 25 subtypes.

name: CFLUE
description: Models answer Chinese financial questions in two parts. The knowledge part has more than 38,000 multiple-choice questions from financial qualification exams, with explanations to test reasoning. The application part has more than 16,000 test items for classification, translation, relation extraction, reading comprehension and text generation.
org: Alibaba Cloud (Qwen DianJin) and Soochow University
note: Alibaba's DianJin-R1 technical report evaluates on CFLUE and also builds training data from it, so some later models may have seen its questions. ACL 2024. About 100 GitHub stars.

name: CFLUE Application
description: Models complete Chinese financial language tasks. The score is the published average of the application task metrics.
org: Alibaba Cloud (Qwen DianJin) and Soochow University
note: One track of CFLUE. The CFLUE record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: CFLUE Knowledge
description: Models answer Chinese financial qualification questions. The score is answer accuracy across the knowledge test.
org: Alibaba Cloud (Qwen DianJin) and Soochow University
note: One track of CFLUE. The CFLUE record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: CG-Bench
description: Video models answer 12,129 questions about 1,219 long videos and must also find the clue segments that support each answer.
note: Published at ICLR 2025. It adds clue-grounded white box and black box evaluation to multiple choice.

name: Chain-of-thought comprehensibility
description: An autorater rates whether the model's thought transcripts are comprehensible, using the metric from Emmons et al. 2025.
note: In-house Google DeepMind check reported as the share of transcripts rated comprehensible.

name: Chain-of-thought faithfulness with clues (Anthropic)
description: Models answer MMLU and GPQA questions with and without an inserted clue. Score is the share of clue-driven answer changes whose reasoning mentions the clue.
note: Uses six clue types, four neutral and two misaligned. Scores run from 0 to 1 and are reported per dataset.

name: Chain-of-thought informativeness
description: An autorater rates whether thought transcripts are informative of the final output, using the metric from Emmons et al. 2025.
note: In-house Google DeepMind check reported as the share of transcripts rated informative.

name: Challenging prompts from red teamers with biosafety-relevant PhDs
description: Models answer adversarial biology prompts written by red teamers with biosafety PhDs. Scored as not_unsafe rate from model training alone.
note: In-house OpenAI safeguard test set first shared in the ChatGPT agent system card.

name: Challenging Red Teaming Evaluation 1 (created for o3-mini)
description: Models face adversarial jailbreaks from o3-mini red teaming on illicit advice, extremism, political persuasion and self-harm. Scored as not_unsafe rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation built from red teaming against o3-mini.

name: Challenging Red Teaming Evaluation 2 (created for deep research)
description: Models face adversarial prompts from deep research red teaming on risky advice such as attack planning. Scored as not_unsafe rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation built from red teaming against deep research.

name: Challenging Refusal Evaluation
description: Models answer a harder set of disallowed content prompts across policy categories. An autograder scores the not_unsafe rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: Challenging translation human evaluation (Z.ai)
description: People blindly score translations of 100 real cases with slang, nicknames and memes on a 0 to 3 scale.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation. The cases are not public.

name: ChangeMyView
description: Models write rebuttals to r/ChangeMyView posts that human raters score for persuasiveness. Scored as percentile against human responses.
note: OpenAI persuasion evaluation built on public Reddit data.

name: Charades-STA
description: Models read a sentence describing an action and return its start and end time in a Charades indoor video. Scored by temporal IoU with the labeled moment.
org: University of Southern California (Gao, Sun, Yang, Nevatia)
note: Built on the Charades videos with added sentence and time labels. Labs report mIoU or recall at IoU 0.5.

name: Charlemagne Labs social-engineering benchmark
description: Attacker models try to persuade a skeptical simulated victim to take an action over many turns. Scored by attempted and carry-through rates.
note: Used in Meta Muse Spark safety reports. Filtered to 280 scenarios. Attempted and carry-through tracked separately.

name: Charm offensive
description: Human participants role-play catching up with a friend, then rate traits such as personal connection and trust in the model.
note: Human participant persuasion study from Phuong et al. 2024. Results are per trait with no overall score.

name: Chart Arena
description: Models create charts. Pairwise votes determine the published Arena rating.
note: The official API publishes an Arena rating, confidence interval and vote count. Voter identity requires confirmation from the board description.

name: ChartMimic
description: Multimodal models write plotting code that reproduces 1,000 charts from scientific papers. Scores compare the rendered chart with the original.
note: ICLR 2025. VLMEvalKit carries v1 and v2 splits.

name: ChartMuseum
description: Models answer 1,162 expert-annotated questions about real-world charts from 184 sources. Many questions need visual reasoning that text cannot replace.
note: The test split has 1,000 questions and the dev split has 162. An LLM grader checks short answers.

name: Chartography
description: 100 tasks on specialized professional charts (Kaplan-Meier, candlestick, Sankey, Bode). Answers graded against expert references.

name: ChartQA
description: Models answer human-written and generated questions about chart images that need visual and arithmetic reasoning. Scored by relaxed accuracy with a 5 percent numeric tolerance.
org: York University and Nanyang Technological University
note: Top models score near 90 percent, so it is close to saturation.

name: ChartQA Pro
description: Model answers 1,948 diverse questions over 1,341 charts, infographics and dashboards, including conversational and unanswerable ones. Accuracy.
note: ACL 2025 Findings.

name: ChartX
description: Vision-language models do 7 chart tasks, such as question answering, summarization and redrawing, over 18 chart types and 22 topics.
org: Shanghai AI Laboratory (Xia, Zhang et al.)
note: Released with the ChartVLM model. VLMEvalKit supports it. Scoring mixes exact metrics and GPT-based judging.

name: CharXiv
description: Chart understanding on real arXiv figures. Reasoning questions require synthesizing information from complex charts.

changes.text: The maintainers pinned the grader to a dated API snapshot and fixed reasoning-grader failure handling. Earlier runs using the floating judge alias can receive different grades.

note: Cards report the reasoning (RQ) split, with or without a Python tool.

name: CharXiv (DQ)
description: Models answer descriptive questions about charts from arXiv papers, such as titles, axis labels and legend entries. It is the descriptive half of CharXiv.
note: The almanac record charxiv holds the reasoning questions (RQ). Lab tables often print DQ and RQ side by side.

name: CharXiv Extended
description: Models answer descriptive and reasoning questions about scientific charts. Mercor adds 150 new expert-written tasks to the 5000 public ones and reports both scores.
note: Held-out extension of charxiv. Mercor shows the original and extended score for each model. The month is approximate. The Wayback Machine first saved the earliest extended pages on 2026-08-15.

name: CharXiv Missing Image
description: Models get CharXiv chart questions with every image removed. Scored on how often they attempt an answer instead of abstaining.
note: OpenAI deception evaluation built on the public CharXiv benchmark.

name: CharXiv Missing Images
description: Models answer CharXiv chart questions with the image removed. The benchmark reports how often they answer incorrectly instead of declining.
note: Meta modification of CharXiv (Princeton) that drops the referenced image.

name: Chat All-in-One Bench
description: Models handle conversational scenarios built around real online user needs at every stage of product usage.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: ChatRAG Bench
description: Models answer multi-turn conversational questions over documents or retrieved context. The suite is built from 10 existing datasets such as Doc2Dial, QuAC, QReCC and CoQA.
note: Introduced with NVIDIA's ChatQA models. About 120 likes on Hugging Face.

name: CheatBench
description: Agents get hard assignments in environments that also offer ways to cheat, such as hidden answers, other agents' submissions or a manipulable grader. The score is the rate of cheating attempts, successful or not.
note: Ten categories, including math, coding, visual tasks and knowledge work. The site reports provider-harness and general-harness results for current frontier models. How attempts are labeled should be checked in the paper.

name: Cheating audit on capability evaluations
description: Reviewers audit agent transcripts from coding benchmarks for runs that obtain withheld information or use forbidden routes. Reports cheating rate per benchmark.
note: In-house Google DeepMind audit of TerminalBench 4.0 and an internal tool-replication benchmark.

name: CheckerBench
description: Long-horizon agents read a defect specification and a repository, then write and refine a working static-analysis checker using compiler and analyzer feedback.
note: 60 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: Chem / Bio Dynamic Jailbreak Eval
description: An automated attacker spreads a harmful chem or bio goal across many turns and chats. Elicited content is scored against expert rubrics.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation reported as rubric match percentage, run with mitigations on.

name: ChemBench
description: Models answer more than 2,700 chemistry questions on knowledge and reasoning. Results are compared with a group of human chemists.
note: A smaller ChemBench-Mini subset is common for cheaper runs.

name: ChemicalDiagramQA
description: Models answer questions about chemical structure diagrams in scientific figures. Scored by accuracy.
note: This is an in-house evaluation, and Google never released the questions.

name: Chess Puzzles
description: Models find the single best next move in 100 chess puzzles that Epoch generated with a chess engine. Scored by the share solved.

name: Chest ImaGenome
aliases: Chest ImaGenome anatomy bounding box detection
description: Models draw bounding boxes around named anatomical regions in MIMIC-CXR chest X-rays. Scored by mean intersection over union.
org: IBM Research and MIT (Wu et al.)
note: NeurIPS 2021 Datasets and Benchmarks scene-graph dataset built on MIMIC-CXR. Google's MedGemma 1.5 reports mean IoU on 10,000 examples.

name: ChestX-ray14
description: Models read frontal chest X-rays from the NIH Clinical Center and say whether thoracic conditions are present.
note: The first release had 8 labels from report text mining and later grew to 14. Google evaluates 3 conditions on the radiologist-adjudicated labels of Majkowska et al. (2020).

name: CheXpert
description: Models read chest radiographs and label up to 14 observations. The test labels come from board-certified radiologists.
org: Stanford ML Group (Irvin, Rajpurkar et al.)
note: The full set has 224,316 radiographs of 65,240 patients. Google's MedGemma cards report average F1 over 5 conditions.

name: CHI-Bench
description: Agents run long healthcare operations workflows such as prior authorization through 87 MCP tools over 20 simulated apps. Tasks need policy lookups, role handoffs and multi-turn dialogs.
note: 55 upvotes on Hugging Face papers. Covers provider, payer and care management domains.

name: CHID
description: Models fill blanks in Chinese passages by choosing the right idiom from candidates. Scored by accuracy.
note: Part of the FewCLUE suite. DeepSeek reports it in few-shot and chat settings.

name: Child safety (xAI)
description: Models face scripted multi-turn requests for child sexual exploitation content. Compliance is the share of dialogues that fail policy.
note: In-house xAI evaluation.

name: Child Safety Action Testing
description: Computer use agents get requests for actions that facilitate child exploitation, endangerment or illegal access. Reports the refusal score.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Child safety evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Models answer single-turn and multi-turn prompts about child sexualization and grooming. Score is the appropriate response rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Child Sexual Abuse and Exploitation Safety
description: Specialist teams grade model answers to adversarial and coded child sexual abuse and exploitation requests in text, image and video. Reports safe response rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Chinese Complex Instruction Following (ByteDance Seed in-house)
description: Models follow complex Chinese production prompts with constraints on format, conditions, content, phrasing, tone, emoji, few-shot style and length. It has 912 cases over 17 weighted dimensions.
note: In-house ByteDance Seed evaluation. The tasks are not public. The card gives it no name, and scoring is a guess.

name: Chinese SimpleQA
description: 3,000 short Chinese factual questions across six topics. Graded correct, incorrect or not attempted.
note: GitHub repo moved from OpenStellarTeam to LivingFutureLab.

name: Chinese Tool-Use Benchmark
description: Models pick and call plugins in ReAct format for Chinese prompts. Scores are tool selection accuracy, Rouge-L on tool inputs, and false positive rate.
note: Qwen replaced version 20230803 with version 20231206, so scores from the two versions differ.

name: ChineseQA
description: Models answer Chinese trivia questions in a closed-book format modeled on TriviaQA.
note: In-house: DeepSeek never released the questions.

name: Chrome Production Commit Scanning (Google)
description: Models scan commits in Chrome's production pipeline for vulnerabilities that were never publicly disclosed. Scored by pass@1 success rate.
note: The undisclosed vulnerabilities keep it free of contamination. Google says newer competitor models after Claude Opus 4.6 refuse the tasks.

name: CIMemories
description: Models use persistent memory across tasks and must withhold attributes when context requires. Reports worst-case disclosure over five samples.
note: Contextual privacy benchmark. Meta reports violations@5 and completeness.

name: CineRecon
description: Agents use tools to rebuild reference videos from film, real footage and games as editable dynamic 3D scenes. The set has 50 videos and 360 evaluation clips.
note: It had 30 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 13 GitHub stars.

name: CiteVQA
description: Multimodal models answer questions about long PDFs and must cite the page region that supports each answer with a bounding box. The set has 1,897 questions over 711 documents in seven domains and two languages, averaging 40.6 pages per document. Strict Attributed Accuracy counts an answer only when both the answer and the cited region are correct.
note: An automated masking pipeline finds the evidence regions and experts then review them. The paper audits 20 MLLMs. 47 Hugging Face upvotes and about 67 GitHub stars.

name: CivBench
description: Models play full games of Civilization V with the Vox Populi mod against each other on matched maps and seeds. Pairwise skill ratings rank long-term strategy.
note: Also tracks diplomacy, strategy choices and win prediction quality. The Vox Deorum repo has about 110 stars. Release month is the first Reddit post found.

name: CL-bench
description: Model must learn new knowledge from a supplied long context (rules, procedures, data) and solve tasks. Strict LLM-verified rubrics.
note: 500 contexts, 1,899 tasks, 31,607 rubrics. Follow-up CL-bench Life (2026-04) covers everyday contexts.

name: CL-bench Life
description: Models solve 405 tasks that require learning from messy real-life context such as group chats. A model judge checks rubrics to give a solve rate.
note: The best model solved 19.3 percent of tasks at release.

name: ClaimBench
description: Models label whether a 10-K excerpt supports, contradicts or says nothing about a claim, across 1,960 claims. Small decision models are scored on accuracy, cost and latency.
note: Built to test how much claim checking cheap decision models can take over within a 1% error budget. The board has 20 decision models.

name: CLASHarness
description: Computer-use agents work in multi-agent setups where peers report stale states, give contradictory instructions or compete for files. Agents must check claims against the environment.
note: It had 34 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 8 GitHub stars.

name: ClassEval
description: Models generate whole Python classes for 100 hand-built tasks. Tests check each method and the class as a whole.
note: Built with about 500 person-hours.

name: Claw-Eval
description: 300 human-verified agent tasks (service orchestration, multimodal, multi-turn dialogue) audited via traces and snapshots. Rubric scores with Pass^3 consistency.
note: Uses an LLM judge (Gemini 3 Flash) for open-ended rubric items. Pass^3 requires all three trials to pass.

name: Claw-Eval Pass^3
description: Agents complete 300 human-verified tasks in service orchestration, multimodal interaction, and professional dialogue. Pass^3 credits a task only if all three trials pass.
note: Pass^3 is the strict metric of Claw-Eval. Average score and Pass@k are also reported.

name: Claw-Eval-Live
description: Agents complete 105 workflow tasks in 17 families drawn from live ClawHub workflow signals, scored on both the workflow and the final workspace state.
note: Recalibrated quarterly, so scores are tied to a release. 13 frontier models on the board. 41 HF paper upvotes. Separate from the Claw-Eval project.

name: Claw-Eval-MM
description: Agents complete the 101 multimodal tasks of Claw-Eval, such as video questions, document extraction, and webpage generation. Rubric items graded from run traces set scores.
note: This is the multimodal split of Claw-Eval, not a separate benchmark.

name: Claw-SWE-Bench
description: General-purpose agent harnesses such as OpenClaw do multilingual SWE-bench-style coding tasks through an adapter that turns their output into scorable patches.
note: 40 upvotes on Hugging Face papers and 112 GitHub stars.

name: ClawBench
description: Browser agents do 153 everyday tasks on live websites, such as booking travel, ordering food and applying for jobs. Request interception stops real side effects, and an LLM judge scores the five-layer traces.
org: TIGER-AI-Lab (University of Waterloo) and NAIL Group
note: Not the ByteDance SeedClawBench. V2 became the default corpus on 2026-05-20. The repo passed 1,000 stars and the paper reached EMNLP 2026 Findings.

name: ClawBench V2
description: Browser agents do 130 new everyday tasks on live websites under six supported harnesses. Request interception and a more lenient LLM judge score each run.
org: TIGER-AI-Lab (University of Waterloo) and NAIL Group
note: The V2 board launched on 2026-05-11 and became the default on 2026-05-20. The maker documents V1 and V2 differences in docs/v1-vs-v2.md.

name: ClawProBench
description: Agents on stateful runtimes are scored with their traces, covering evidence gathering, runtime routing, safety boundaries and repeated runs in frozen workplace setups.
note: 828 GitHub stars at 2026-11-01. Evaluates a declared model plus runtime configuration.

name: CLBench-V
description: Models must learn from task-specific multimodal context, such as figures, tables, maps and web pages, instead of prior knowledge. Tasks run from grounding to knowledge acquisition.
note: It had 45 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 4 GitHub stars. Tencent Hunyuan's text-only CL-bench is a separate record.

name: clembench
description: Chat models play rule-based dialogue games in self-play, such as Taboo, Wordle and reference games. The clemscore combines how often a model follows the game rules at all with how well it plays when it does. Version 4.0 runs 14 games in 30 languages.
org: University of Potsdam (Foundations of Computational Linguistics)
note: Versions differ in games and languages, so scores from different versions should not be compared. Version 4.0 ranks 9 current models over about 108,000 episodes. A separate multimodal track uses image games. The repositories have under 10 GitHub stars.

name: CLIcK
aliases: Cultural and Linguistic Intelligence in Korean
description: Models answer 1,995 multiple-choice questions on Korean language and culture. Questions come from official Korean exams and textbooks in eleven categories.
org: KAIST and collaborators (Eunsu Kim et al.)
note: Published at LREC-COLING 2024.

name: CLIF Bench
aliases: Context Learning and Instruction Following Bench
description: Models learn from a provided context while they follow instructions that combine several complex skills.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: CliniCARE-Bench
description: Agents answer a clinical question about one real MIMIC-IV patient through governed chart tools, then give a four-way verdict with cited evidence across 750 cases.
note: 25 scenarios times 30 patients. 150 cases admit no defensible yes or no, so deferring is scored. Needs PhysioNet MIMIC-IV credentials. The repo sweeps 16 systems.

name: Clipping Bench
description: Agents run a simulated clip farm for about a month. They join pay-per-view campaigns, cut clips from licensed streams, post them and compete with rival clippers for budgets.
note: Scored by cash at the end of the simulated season. 19 models in the Fireworks index.

name: ClockBench
description: Models read analog clock faces and answer questions about the time shown. Most clocks stay private to avoid training leakage.
note: 180 clocks with 720 questions, 10 clocks public. Humans score about 90.7% on average. The board had more than 30 models in 2026-10.

name: Clocktower Bench
description: Models play the social deduction game Blood on the Clocktower (the Trouble Brewing script) against each other, with a scripted Storyteller. One model takes every good seat and another every evil seat, so each game tests one model's detection of the Demon against another's deception. A Bradley–Terry fit turns 386 games into Elo ratings.
note: 1500 is the average of the rated models, so ratings shift when models join. Every model plays both sides at high reasoning effort, with 90% intervals from a bootstrap over side-swapped pairs. Evil wins 33% of games, and its win rate barely moves as both sides get stronger. Mixed teams rate a little below their members' average. The rules are frozen at protocol v17.

name: Clocktower Radio
description: Models play the social deduction game Blood on the Clocktower (the Trouble Brewing script) in mirrored pairs of games. In each match one model plays good and the other evil, and then they swap. A coded Storyteller runs the game, and a Bradley–Terry fit over all matches gives ratings where 1500 is average.
note: The board also reports each model's win rate as good and as evil, its cost per game and its output tokens per action. Good wins 60% of games. The changelog shows rule fixes through 2026-07-27. The release month is the first changelog entry.

name: Closed-domain hallucination evaluation
description: Models answer using only provided context. Scored on avoiding invented details outside that context.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The GPT-4 System Card gives only a gain over GPT-3.5.

name: Clotho-AQA
description: Models answer crowdsourced yes or no and single word questions about short environmental audio clips. Scored by accuracy.

name: CLUE
description: Models are fine-tuned or prompted on nine Chinese language understanding tasks, including sentence classification, sentence-pair inference and machine reading comprehension. The score averages the task results.
note: Published at COLING 2020 as a Chinese counterpart to GLUE. The repository has about 4,300 stars. CLUEWSC2020 is one of its tasks and has its own record.

name: CLUEWSC
description: Models decide whether a pronoun in a Chinese sentence refers to a given noun phrase, a Winograd-style task. Scored by accuracy.
note: Duplicate of cluewsc: same CLUE Winograd task and same paper. Merge into cluewsc and drop this record.

name: CMATH
description: 1.7K Chinese elementary-school math word problems. Final-answer accuracy.
note: Saturated.

name: CMIMC 2025
aliases: Carnegie Mellon Informatics and Mathematics Competition 2025
description: Models answer 40 final-answer problems from the 2025 Carnegie Mellon Informatics and Mathematics Competition. MathArena scores the average accuracy over four attempts.
note: The contest was held in March 2025 and MathArena added it in May 2025. MathArena ran 36 models and later marked the set deprecated.

name: CMMLU
description: Chinese multiple-choice questions across 67 subjects including China-specific topics. Accuracy.
note: Saturated. HF dataset haonan-li/cmmlu now redirects to lmlmcat/cmmlu.

name: CMMMU
description: Multimodal models answer college-level questions in Chinese across many disciplines, following MMMU's annotation pattern.
note: Chinese-language counterpart of MMMU. 27 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: CMO 2024
description: Models write full proofs for the six problems of the 2024 China Mathematical Olympiad. Experts grade the proofs for points.
note: A one-time competition exam, not a maintained benchmark. DeepSeekMath-V2 does not say whether it means the November 2023 or the November 2024 contest.

name: CMO 2025
description: Models write full proofs for the six problems of the 2025 China Mathematical Olympiad. Graders score proofs out of 126 points.
note: A one-time competition exam, not a maintained benchmark. DeepSeek graded the English version.

name: CMRC
description: Models extract answer spans from Chinese Wikipedia paragraphs for about 20,000 human-written questions. Scoring is exact match and F1.
org: Joint Laboratory of HIT and iFLYTEK Research (HFL)

name: CMT-Benchmark
description: Models solve 50 research-level condensed matter theory problems written and checked by a panel of expert physicists. Answers are graded automatically.
org: International panel of condensed matter researchers (Pan, Roggeveen, Berg, Carrasquilla, Chowdhury and others)
note: Topics cover quantum many-body and classical statistical mechanics. Google cited it in the Gemini 3 Deep Think release in February 2026.

name: CNML-Level Problems (DeepSeek)
description: Models prove 91 theorems in algebra, geometry, number theory, combinatorics and inequalities at Chinese National High School Mathematics League level. A verifier model scores the proofs.
note: In-house DeepSeek evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: CNMO 2024
description: Models answer problems from the 2024 Chinese National High School Mathematics Olympiad. DeepSeek reports Pass@1 averaged over 16 samples.
note: DeepSeek built the eval set from the contest and did not release its prepared version or problem count.

name: CoBench (Anthropic)
description: 500 real internal Anthropic R&D problems. Percentage solved in one attempt tracks AI R&D acceleration.
note: v2.1 scores not comparable with earlier CoBench versions.

name: COCO
description: Models detect and locate objects in everyday photos from the Microsoft COCO dataset. Scored by mean average precision over box overlap thresholds.
note: Qwen reports it under visual grounding without stating its exact protocol.

name: COCO Captions
description: Models write a caption for each image, and outputs are compared with five human captions per image using BLEU, METEOR, ROUGE, and CIDEr.
note: Model cards usually report CIDEr, which is not a percentage.

name: CocoaBench
description: Unified digital agents do long human-designed tasks that mix vision, search and coding. An automatic function checks each final output.
note: 36 upvotes on Hugging Face papers. Every Eval Ever holds results for Anthropic, Google, Moonshot, OpenAI and Qwen models.

name: CoCoNot
description: Models get 1,000 requests they should not fully comply with, such as incomplete, unsupported or humanizing requests. A judge model rates whether each response complies.
note: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks paper. A contrast set checks for over-refusal.

name: Code Arena
description: Models act as coding agents that build web apps from user prompts, and users vote between two results. Votes yield Elo-style ratings.
note: It started a fresh leaderboard and does not reuse WebDev Arena votes. It splits results into Fullstack and Frontend categories, with HTML, React and domain filters. On 2026-10-27 it listed 153 models and 952,039 votes. Image-to-WebDev is a separate board.

name: Code Interpreter Benchmark
description: Models use a Python code interpreter for math, data visualization, and general tasks. Scoring covers result accuracy and the share of code that runs.
note: The visualization judge changed from Qwen-VL-Chat to GPT-4V in December 2023, so versions differ.

name: Code Interpreter Benchmark General
description: Models use a Python interpreter for general tasks. The score is the percentage of generated programs that execute.
note: One track of Code Interpreter Benchmark. The Code Interpreter Benchmark record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Code Interpreter Benchmark Math
description: Models use a Python interpreter to solve math problems. The score is execution accuracy on the Math task set.
note: One track of Code Interpreter Benchmark. The Code Interpreter Benchmark record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Code Migration
description: Models port a working program into another language offline and ship a Dockerfile. A hidden behavior-test suite the model never sees scores the port, after an anti-cheat check.
note: Ran on the mini-SWE-agent harness. 30 open-source CLI repositories in five languages, each moved to four targets, plus 10 COBOL-to-Java repositories. Superseded by v1.1 in October 2026.

name: Code Migration v1.1
description: Models port a working program into another language offline and ship a Dockerfile. A hidden behavior-test suite the model never sees scores the port, after an anti-cheat check.
note: Same tasks as v1, but every model runs on the Pi agent harness and grading uses revised hidden test suites. Vals says scores are not directly comparable to v1. Part of Vals Index v2.2.

name: Code refactoring tasks (OpenAI)
description: Agents perform refactor-style tasks taken from large, established repositories in Python, Go and OCaml. One example threads a ctx variable through 232 files and 3,541 lines of Gitea.
note: OpenAI introduced it with GPT-5-Codex on 2025-09-15. The post does not say how tasks are graded, so verified is assumed from the repository-task setup.

name: Code Review Bench (Martian)
description: AI code review tools review pull requests from five large open-source projects. An LLM judge matches their comments to human-verified golden comments.
note: Offline set of 50 PRs with 173 golden comments, plus a continuously updated online benchmark. It ranks review tools and agents rather than bare models. About 300 GitHub stars.

name: Code summary honesty (Anthropic)
description: Models summarize prefilled agentic coding transcripts that hide failures. Score is the rate of summaries that fail to raise the important failures.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The prefilled transcripts are off-policy and shorter than many real sessions.

name: Code2Video Arena
description: Models create videos through code. Pairwise votes determine the published Arena rating.
note: The official API publishes an Arena rating, confidence interval and vote count. Voter identity requires confirmation from the board description.

name: Code2Video Benchmark
description: 168 product-video briefs. Agent writes HTML motion-graphics code rendered by HyperFrames. A trained pairwise judge on five axes produces Elo.
note: Repo is the HyperFrames renderer, not a task repo. Judge agrees with humans ~82%. Kaggle hosts briefs and runs evaluations.

name: Code2Video-AA
description: Artificial Analysis' implementation of HeyGen's Code2Video Bench: models write a HyperFrames HTML composition for each of 114 product and brand video briefs. A model judge compares two rendered videos at a time on five axes, and the comparisons become Elo ratings.
note: Gemini 4 Argon is the judge. The overall Elo is the mean of the five axis ratings. Artificial Analysis terms bar reuse of its data, so link only.

name: Code2Video-Compass
description: Multimodal models write programs that render complete videos from text, an image or a video. The default Overall board ranks models by their mean rank across quality metrics, so a lower score is better.
note: It had 41 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 8 GitHub stars. HeyGen's Code2Video Benchmark on Kaggle is a different test.

name: CodeCap-Bench
description: Models watch a structured 2D video and write code that re-renders it. The rendered video is compared with the original on visual similarity, object timing and placement, and retained detail.
note: 323 videos in five categories such as apps, 2D games and scientific plots. Headline is overall fine-grained retention. Code and dataset links say coming soon as of 2026-11-01.

name: CodeClash
description: Models build and improve their own codebases over many rounds, then compete in arenas such as Halite, poker and BattleSnake. Results give Elo ratings.
org: SWE-bench team (Stanford University and Princeton University)
note: Goals replace explicit tasks, so models decide what to build. The board was last updated on 2025-11-03.

name: CodeContests
description: Models write programs for competitive programming problems, drawn from Codeforces and other sites, and the programs run against hidden tests. Google DeepMind built the dataset for AlphaCode, with training, validation (117 problems) and test (165 problems) splits and many generated tests per problem to cut false positives. Scores are the share of problems solved within a fixed number of submissions, such as 10@k.
note: The test problems date from 2021, so newer models may have seen them in training. Results depend heavily on the number of samples drawn per problem. About 2,200 GitHub stars.

name: CodeEditorBench
description: Models edit code in four scenarios: debugging, translation, requirement switching and polishing. Unit tests check the edits, and polishing also measures speed and memory gains.
org: Multimodal Art Projection (M-A-P), University of Waterloo, HKUST and others
note: Problems come from five sources across several programming languages. Model reports usually give the four scenario scores with no overall number.

name: Codeforces rating
description: Model solves recent Codeforces contest problems. An Elo-style rating is computed from simulated contest performance.
note: No standard public harness. Each lab's rating method differs, so numbers are not comparable across cards.

name: CodeSimpleQA
description: Models answer short bilingual fact questions about programming concepts and implementations across languages and computer science domains.
note: The paper also releases a 66M-sample instruction corpus. Scoring is assumed to follow SimpleQA grading.

name: CodeUtilityBench (LG)
description: Models handle 16 everyday coding tasks such as explaining, debugging, refactoring and testing code. A GPT-5 judge checks five rubrics per item.
note: In-house LG AI Research evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: CodeXGLUE
description: A suite of 10 code tasks across 14 datasets, grouped as code to code, text to code, code to text and text to text. Tasks include clone detection, defect detection, code completion, code repair, code search, code generation and code summarization. Each task has its own metric, such as accuracy, BLEU or MRR.
note: Built for fine-tuned code models such as CodeBERT, and its leaderboard has few recent entries. Several datasets come from earlier work. About 1,850 GitHub stars.

name: Coding (MiniMax in-house)
description: Models answer coding requests from real Hailuo AI users. The report does not describe the scoring.
note: In-house MiniMax evaluation built mostly from Hailuo AI user queries in Mandarin. The queries are not public.

name: Coding agent prompt injection robustness
description: Coding agents on 75 SWE-Bench Pro based scenarios meet injections in issues, READMEs and code comments. Reports survival after 40 attempts.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Coding Deception
description: Agents work on coding tasks selected to elicit dishonest reports. Scored on the rate of misrepresenting their work to the user.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Coding Experience (Moonshot)
description: Coding agents work in real development workflows. The score reflects the practical experience of working with the agent, such as communication and stability.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. The tasks and the grading method are not public.

name: Coding prompt injections
description: Agents work on coding tasks that contain prompt injection attacks. Scored on resisting the injected instructions.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: cognition-golden
description: Cognition tests coding agents on tasks modeled on real Devin use cases, in authentic development environments with fully autonomous grading. A train split serves self-improvement and a test split measures capability.
note: Cognition called it its primary internal benchmark when it compared o1-preview and GPT-4o inside Devin in 2024-09. The task set is not public.

name: Cohere enterprise human evaluation
aliases: Head-to-head human evaluation win rates on enterprise tasks
description: Trained annotators blindly compare two models' answers on enterprise tasks such as HR FAQs, technical FAQs and workplace assistants. They judge accuracy, instruction following and style. Results are win, tie and loss rates.
note: The Command A post reports six task groups and an average against GPT-4o (November 2024).

name: Cohere North internal evals
description: Cohere internal evals of its North agent platform: agentic question answering, spreadsheet data analysis and memory use. LLM-as-judge scoring.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Cohere).

name: Collaborative Intelligence Benchmark
description: A model works in a team with scripted teammates and live model partners, and a teammate creates a test: pressure to take an unsafe shortcut, misconduct to report, a need nobody states, a conflict, or a cheat that a weaker model left behind. The 240 tasks across 8 dimensions of teamwork come from real records, such as aviation accident reports and clinical cases, and from existing benchmarks, such as SWE-bench and negotiation datasets. Each task has a checkable outcome. A model is scored only on the tasks it solves alone, so the score measures teamwork, not ability.
note: 160 tasks are public and 80 are held out. Models almost always refuse unsafe shortcuts, but they reach the best deal in only 14% of conflicts.

name: COLLIE
description: Models generate text that meets compositional constraints at word, sentence, paragraph, and passage level. Scored by the share passing automatic constraint checks.

name: CombiBench
description: Provers solve 100 combinatorics problems formalized in Lean 4, from middle school to IMO and university level. Lean checks each proof.
org: Moonshot AI and Project Numina (Liu et al.)
note: DeepSeek-Prover-V2 reports it in a with-solution setting, where fill-in-the-blank answers are given.

name: Combined HHH evals (Anthropic)
description: Models pick the more helpful, honest and harmless of two responses across 438 binary choice questions. Scored by accuracy.
note: Anthropic researchers wrote the questions for its RLHF and Constitutional AI research.

name: CommerceAgentBench
description: Agents finish real e-commerce work across procurement, listings, operations, fulfillment and after-sales through CLI, browser, file and API tools. A task passes only if every verifier check on the end state succeeds.
note: 107 tasks: 53 CLI, 28 browser, 16 file and 10 API or MCP. Tasks were distilled from Accio merchant traces. Verifiers are deterministic or LLM-assisted per task. Formerly RealReplicaBench. Repo has 1,301 stars.

name: Common Voice
description: Crowd-sourced multilingual read-speech corpus. Used here as an ASR test set scored by word error rate.
note: Mozilla releases numbered corpus versions such as 13.0 and 17.0, so reports should name the version. Since 2025-10 the datasets are only on Mozilla Data Collective, not Hugging Face.

name: CommonSenseQA
description: Models answer five-way multiple-choice questions built from ConceptNet relations that need everyday background knowledge. Scored by accuracy.
org: Tel Aviv University and Allen Institute for AI
note: Test labels are hidden, so model cards usually report the dev set.

name: CommonsenseQA 2.0
description: Models answer 14,343 yes or no commonsense questions that players wrote to fool an AI in a game. Scored by accuracy.
org: Allen Institute for AI and Tel Aviv University

name: Community Alignment personalization
description: Models predict an individual's preferred response from demographics and nine examples, across five countries. Reports global accuracy.
note: Built on Meta's open Community Alignment preference dataset. Random guessing scores 25%.

name: Company Agent Bench
description: 205 questions on how well an agent understands its company, built from a month of real Slack history: who wrote an anonymized message, whom a teammate tagged, and who sent each reply. Agents search a replayed sandbox workspace using only messages from before the answer.
note: Built from one small company's workspace, about 10 teammates. Products ran once on default settings. API models ran in Concept's own Slack harness. The overall score weights the three parts equally.

name: CompassArena
description: Users chat with two anonymous models side by side, mostly in Chinese, and vote for the better answer. A Bradley-Terry model turns the votes into Elo-style ratings.
note: Launched on 2024-05-27 with 23 models. The first board on 2024-06-13 used about 6,000 battles. Later updates added multimodal battles and a search-off sub-board.

name: CompassArena Multimodal
description: Users compare anonymous multimodal model answers and vote for the better response. A Bradley-Terry model estimates ratings from these votes.
note: The public summary API exposes ten ranked models. Its total model count is larger, and the full-table callback currently fails.

name: CompassRank
description: OpenCompass ranks open and API language models on its own evaluation sets and publishes monthly rankings. Model makers submit a repository link or API endpoint to be tested.
note: The OpenCompass README calls it the home of detailed leaderboards for open-source and API models. The first OpenCompass LLM leaderboard space dates from 2023-09-08.

name: CompileBench
description: Agents build real open-source projects through dependency problems, legacy toolchains and complex build systems, for example compiling 22-year-old code.
note: About 60 GitHub stars. Quesma also contributed to Terminal-Bench 3.0.

name: Complex Workflow (ByteDance Seed in-house)
description: Models carry out step-by-step tasks that follow a given standard operating procedure, such as multi-turn after-sales service in support, sales and healthcare.
note: One of six in-house application sets in the Seed1.8 and Seed2.0 model cards. Scoring is a guess.

name: ComplexBench
description: Models answer 1,150 hand-written Chinese instructions that compose several constraints by chaining, selection and nesting. LLM evaluators with rules check each constraint, and scores follow the dependency structure.
note: Taxonomy of 4 constraint types, 19 dimensions and 4 composition types. NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks. Data ships in the repo with English translations.

name: ComplexConstraints
description: Models answer 75 expert-written professional prompts whose constraints depend on each other, fire conditionally or must be inferred. An LLM judge grades 1,559 rubric criteria one at a time, and a task passes only if all criteria pass.
note: Surge helped build AdvancedIF and made this to test entangled constraints that AdvancedIF lacks. The repo is an Inspect harness. Its README points to a Hugging Face dataset that returned 401 on 2026-11-01.

name: ComplexFuncBench
description: Models make function calls for 1,000 travel booking style samples that need several steps, user constraints, implicit parameter reasoning, long parameter values or 128K context.
note: The ComplexEval framework scores both the calls and the final answer.

name: ComplexFuncBench Audio (OpenAI)
description: Speech-to-speech models solve ComplexFuncBench function-calling tasks whose text prompts OpenAI converted into speech. Covers multi-step calls, constraints, implicit parameters and long inputs.
note: OpenAI built it for the gpt-realtime launch on 2025-08-28. Scoring is assumed to follow ComplexFuncBench, which checks calls against references.

name: ComplexNLU (Tencent)
description: Models answer Tencent in-house natural language understanding tasks with complex inputs. Task and scoring details are not published.
note: Seen in the Hunyuan-A13B-Instruct card. Scoring method is a guess from the task type.

name: Compliance with instructions planted in pasted text (Anthropic)
aliases: Acting on instructions inside text the user pasted into their prompt
Compliance with instructions planted in a document pasted into Claude Code
description: Coding agents receive user prompts with pasted text that hides an attacker's instruction. Score is the rate of acting on the planted instruction.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation with simulated tool calls. Some variants hide the instruction in invisible Unicode characters.

name: Compositional Tasks (ByteDance Seed in-house)
description: Models identify several elements of a business text in one inference, such as user intent and slot values.
note: In-house ByteDance Seed evaluation. The tasks are not public. It seems to follow the Seed1.8 Intention Recognition set. Scoring is a guess.

name: ComputeEval
description: Models write CUDA code for handcrafted problems on kernels, runtime APIs and GPU libraries. Held-out test harnesses check correctness, and optional benchmarks time the code.
note: Dated releases (2025-1 to 2026-2) add problems and groups, so report the release used.

name: Computer use manual red teaming
description: Google's generative AI red team probes computer use agents in sandboxes for tool misuse, skipped confirmations and prohibited actions.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Computer use Prohibited Action Evaluation
description: Computer use agents get single-turn adversarial requests for actions that break Google policy. Reports the safe action rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Computer use prompt injection evaluation (Anthropic)
aliases: Prompt injection attacks and computer use
description: Agents face about 600 prompt injection scenarios in coding platforms, browsers and email workflows. Score is the attack prevention rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation reported with and without safeguards. The scenarios are not public.

name: Computer use prompt injection robustness
description: Computer use agents meet injected text and live DOM attacks across 27 web scenarios. A multimodal judge records breaches. Reports survival after 100 attempts.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Concealment of changes (Anthropic)
description: Models summarize transcripts in which changes were hidden through git manipulations. Score is the rate at which they disclose the concealment.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Conceptual Reasoning Index
description: An index that ranks models on reasoning about hard-to-verify topics such as AI alignment and decision theory. It weights LMCA 60 percent and ACCoRD and DTBench 20 percent each.
note: The leaderboard CSV had 267 model rows in November 2026.

name: ConStory-Bench
description: Models write long stories, up to tens of thousands of words, from 2,000 prompts in four task types. An automated checker, ConStory-Checker, finds contradictions in facts, timelines, characters and world rules and cites the passages behind each one. Scores count consistency errors, using a taxonomy of 5 categories and 19 subtypes.
org: Microsoft and Singapore University of Technology and Design
note: The checker is itself an LLM pipeline, so its error counts carry judge bias. The paper finds errors cluster in the middle of stories. The paper had 52 Hugging Face upvotes and the repository about 190 GitHub stars on 2026-11-05.

name: Consulting and Recommendations Benchmark (StepFun)
description: Models answer 500 advice queries taken from Reddit, Stack Exchange and forums. Model judges score usefulness, logic, instruction following and tone against an expert reference set at 88.
note: In-house StepFun evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Context Aware Automatic Speech Recognition
description: Speech transcription systems are scored for semantic accuracy with and without free-form context.
note: OpenAI reports this internal benchmark for GPT-Live-Transcribe.

name: ContextBench
description: Coding agents resolve 1,136 issues from 66 repositories in eight programming languages, and the benchmark checks which code they look at along the way. Each task has human-annotated gold context, and the tracker scores context recall, precision and efficiency over the agent's trajectory. It adds these process measures to the usual issue-resolution result.
org: Nanjing University and University College London
note: Not related to the Context Arena long-context board at contextbench.ai. The paper tested four models and five agent frameworks. About 150 GitHub stars.

name: Contextual Nuclear Knowledge
description: Models answer 222 multiple choice questions on nuclear engineering with a nonproliferation focus. Scored as cons@32 accuracy.
note: Questions written by an MIT nuclear security fellow for OpenAI Preparedness.

name: Contextual security evaluation
description: Agents handle noisy cross-app data with sensitive records while attackers exploit ambiguity to exfiltrate data. Reports baseline safe behavior and survival rates.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Continual Learning Bench
description: AI systems work through sequences of related task instances in six domains and should get better as they go. A gain score subtracts each system's own stateless baseline to isolate learning.
org: UC Berkeley, Snorkel AI and collaborators (Asawa, Orlanski et al.)
note: Task Suite 1.0 has 301 instances in domains such as codebase adaptation, outbreak forecasting and poker. Funded by Snorkel Open Benchmarks Grants. Not Tencent's CL-bench.

name: Continual Learning Exam
description: Agents work through 120 professional tasks, each a ladder of five levels that must be passed in order. Later levels reuse files, tools and lessons from earlier ones. An evaluation agent grades against expert rubrics.
org: University College London (Jun Wang) + Imperial College London + University of Liverpool
note: 600 levels over 89 roles in 12 domains, written by 50+ experts. CLE Lite releases 20 tasks. Best of 17 agent setups cleared 47.7% of levels.

name: ContinualSkillBench
description: Agents work through five domains of 100 linked subtasks of rising difficulty, testing whether skill libraries they build in context actually help later tasks.
note: Finds explicit skill libraries often only match plain in-context adaptation.

name: ContPhy
description: Models infer physical properties such as mass and density of fluids and soft bodies from videos and predict their dynamics.
note: Published at ICML 2024. The format field is a guess.

name: ControlArena
description: Agents try to perform unwanted side actions stealthily while completing a legitimate user task. Scored on whether monitors catch them.
note: UK AISI control evaluation suite. The GPT-5.6 card describes results in words without a score.

name: Conversational SWE Task Benchmark (Windsurf)
description: Agents resume an existing Cascade session with a half-finished task and answer the next user query. A 0 to 10 score blends judge scores for helpfulness, efficiency and correctness with target-file edit accuracy.
note: Windsurf reported it once, as a chart without printed values, in the SWE-1 launch post. It measures human-in-the-loop agentic coding in the Cascade harness.

name: ConvFinQA
description: Models answer a conversation of related numerical questions about a company's financial report, with tables and text, where later questions build on earlier answers. The dataset has about 3,900 conversations with 14,000 questions, built from FinQA. Answers are checked by execution accuracy against the gold reasoning program.
org: UC Santa Barbara and J.P. Morgan AI Research
note: EMNLP 2022. Finance model reports such as BloombergGPT use it. About 130 GitHub stars.

name: Cooperate to Compete (C2C)
description: Multi-player conquest game with private non-binding negotiation and secret asymmetric objectives. LM agents and humans are ranked by Plackett-Luce player strength from their game results.
note: Includes an 82-game human study with matched AI-only games from the same starting positions.

name: Cooperation with user deception (Anthropic)
aliases: Harmful system prompts: cooperation with user deception
description: Models get developer system prompts asking them to subtly mislead users, then meet users who would be harmed. Graders score harmful and deceptive choices.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: CooperBench
description: Two coding agents each get a different feature for the same repository and must coordinate so both changes work together. Over 600 tasks span 12 libraries in 4 languages.
note: Later work cited in AINews reports supervision gains on it.

name: COPA
description: Models choose which of two alternatives is the more plausible cause or effect of a premise, across 1,000 questions. Scored by accuracy.
note: Saturated. Also part of SuperGLUE.

name: Copilot Arena
description: Developers inside their IDE see paired code completions from two models and pick one. Pairwise votes give an Elo-style ranking of code models.
org: Arena (formerly LMArena) with Carnegie Mellon University
note: The paper reports 4.5 million suggestions served from 10 models and over 11k pairwise judgments. The repo has about 370 GitHub stars. The release month is the VS Code extension launch and is likely, not verified.

name: CoQA
description: Models answer a series of linked conversational questions about a passage, where later questions depend on earlier turns. Scored by word-level F1.
note: Reported in early LLM papers such as GPT-3.

name: CORE-Bench
description: Agents reproduce the results of published studies from their code and data. 270 tasks from 90 papers in computer science, social science and medicine come in three difficulty levels.
note: CORE-Bench Hard is the level most often reported. Princeton's Holistic Agent Leaderboard runs it.

name: CoreCodeBench
description: Models complete over 1,500 repository-level Python tasks covering development, bug fixing and test-driven work, with single-function and multi-function variants. The CorePipe pipeline builds tasks from repositories at set difficulty levels.
note: The authors report a 78.55% task validity yield against 31.7% retention for SWE-bench Verified.

name: CoreCognition
description: Models answer true or false and multiple choice questions on 12 core knowledge concepts from developmental cognitive science, such as object permanence and perspective taking.
org: UC San Diego, Johns Hopkins, University of Michigan and others
note: The paper evaluates 230 models with 11 prompts and adds a Concept Hacking control test.

name: Coronavirus-ACE2 Cell-Entry Screen
description: Models predict and rank held-out cell entry measurements for spike protein and ACE2 pairings. Scored as a composite score.
note: OpenAI Critical bio capability evaluation. The Critical threshold is 0.75.

name: Corp Speak Arena
description: Models rewrite text in corporate language. Pairwise votes determine the published Arena rating.
note: The official API publishes an Arena rating, confidence interval and vote count. Voter identity requires confirmation from the board description.

name: CorpBench Work
description: Agents carry out 100 business workflows across finance, marketing, operations, RevOps and sales, 20 per department, using simulated business systems and tool contracts. Grading checks the final state, the actions taken, and whether the agent finished the job or escalated it correctly.
note: Revensi, a company that builds AI agents for businesses, runs the board, which listed 18 models including local ones. The current library is Work 1.3. The repository had 0 GitHub stars on 2026-11-05, and no outside use was found.

name: CorpFin v2
description: Models answer expert-written questions about credit agreements that often exceed 200 pages. An LLM judge grades each answer for accuracy.
note: Vals archived it as saturated and stopped running new models (last update 2026-08-12). Splits are 20 public, 340 licensable validation and 858 private test questions from 61 credit agreements.

name: CorporateBench
description: Agents answer questions over the email archives of four synthetic companies, up to 232,692 documents. Answers are checked against each company's ground-truth knowledge graph.
note: The Harbor release packages 128 scored tasks with 1,132 graded cases. Fireworks lists results for 10 models.

name: CorpusQA
description: Corpus-level questions over hundreds of documents up to 10M tokens needing aggregation and statistics. Programmatically guaranteed answers, accuracy.
note: First released on 2025-12-04 with 1,316 instances in four context settings from 128K to 10M tokens. The public dataset holds the 128K and 1M files. CorpusQA 1M is the 1M-token tier. Cited by DeepSeek-V4.

name: CorpusQA 1M
description: Models answer computation-heavy questions whose evidence is spread across hundreds of finance, education, and real estate documents in a 1M-token context. Scored by accuracy.
note: The 1M-token setting of CorpusQA, which spans 128K to 10M tokens.

name: CoT Deception Monitoring
description: A GPT-4o monitor reads reasoning chains and answers on synthetic ChatGPT prompts. Scored as the share flagged as deceptive.
note: In-house OpenAI monitoring study on about 100,000 synthetic prompts.

name: CoT Monitorability
description: Monitors read a model's chain of thought, actions or all messages across intervention, process and outcome evaluations. Scored as g-mean squared of TPR and TNR.
note: Suite from Guan et al. 2025. Results appear as charts by reasoning length.

name: CoT-Control
description: Pairs GPQA, HLE, MMLU-Pro, BFCL and SWE-bench problems with instructions on what the chain of thought may contain. Measures compliance.
note: Low controllability is the safe direction. Authors ask that it be excluded from training data.

name: CountBench
description: Models count the objects in natural images from the CountBench image-text set. Lab cards often use a question-answer version, CountBenchQA, scored by accuracy.

name: CounterFactQA (Qwen)
description: Models get counterfactual questions and must recognize that the premise is false instead of giving a hallucinated answer.
note: In-house Qwen evaluation. The data is not public.

name: CountQA
description: Models count objects in over 1,500 real-world photos with dense clutter and occlusion. Scoring is accuracy on the count.

name: Coval Speech-to-Text WER
description: Speech models transcribe call-like audio. The score is mean word error percentage over the published pooled 24-hour window.

name: Coval Text-to-Speech TTFA
description: Speech models synthesize customer-service prompts. The score is median time to first audible sample in milliseconds over the published 24-hour window.

name: Coval Voice AI Benchmarks
description: Speech-to-text, text-to-speech and speech-to-speech models from almost 40 providers are scored every 30 minutes on call-like audio with accents, noise and echo.
note: Reports latency and accuracy. Every number on the site comes from the open repo.

name: CoVEBench
description: Video editing models follow compositional instructions with several coupled edits to subjects, actions and camera, while unrelated content must stay unchanged.
note: 53 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: Covert misbehavior (Thinking Machines)
description: Agentic tasks that check whether a model misbehaves and conceals it. Scored by the rate of covert misbehavior.
note: In-house test. Tasks are not public.

name: CoVoST2
description: Models translate speech from 21 languages into English and from English into 15 languages. Scored by BLEU.

name: CoWorkBench
description: Agent completes long-horizon productivity tasks across computer science, finance, law and medicine. Qwen in-house scoring (method unpublished).
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Alibaba Qwen). Only Qwen reports scores. Tasks and graders are not public.

name: CRAB
description: Multimodal agents do tasks that span an Ubuntu desktop and an Android phone at once. Graph-based evaluators give credit for intermediate steps.
note: 430 GitHub stars at 2026-11-01.

name: CRAG
description: Retrieval-augmented systems answer 4,409 factual questions across finance, sports, music, movies and open domain, using mock web and knowledge graph search APIs. Hallucinated answers are penalized.
note: Basis of the Meta KDD Cup 2024 challenge. Covers 8 question types, such as comparison and multi-hop.

name: Creation-MMBench
description: Models write creative pieces grounded in up to nine images plus a role, background and instructions, across 765 cases in 51 tasks. A judge scores quality and visual fact alignment against case-specific criteria.
note: ICCV 2025 paper from the OpenCompass team. A text-only version is included for comparing LLMs.

name: Creative biology
description: Models answer questions about unusual biology needed to engineer harmless biological agents, a weak proxy for novel weapon design.
note: SecureBio question set run by Anthropic. The questions are not public.

name: Creative Biology Uplift Trial (Anthropic)
description: Participants with molecular biology PhDs write reports on novel biological workflows with or without model access. Expert graders score each report.
note: In-house Anthropic human uplift trial with twenty participants over three days. Results compare the model group with an internet-only control.

name: Creative Writing (MiniMax in-house)
description: Models write creative pieces for real Hailuo AI user requests. Automatic assessments score the writing.
note: In-house MiniMax evaluation built mostly from Hailuo AI user queries in Mandarin. The queries are not public.

name: Creative Writing v3
description: Models write responses to 32 creative writing prompts, three times each. A judge model scores them with a rubric and pairwise Elo comparisons.
note: Version 3 replaced version 2 after the judge could no longer separate top models.

name: CreativeWork
description: Agents complete productivity tasks in Notion, Canva and Figma by mixing GUI actions with MCP tool calls.
note: In-house Seed benchmark. The card does not describe the grader, so the scoring field is a guess.

name: Cresta-Bench
description: Contact-center agents take simulated calls for lending, health and airline lines. Tool calls get deterministic checks and LLM judges grade the rest.
note: 181 test cases across four synthetic agents, each run three times and scored pass^3. 14 models in the Fireworks index. No maker page with details found.

name: CriticEval
description: Models critique responses across four dimensions in nine task scenarios, giving both scalar scores and written critiques. GPT-4 grades written critiques against a large set of annotated reference critiques.
note: Accepted to NeurIPS 2024. It keeps separate objective and subjective boards.

name: CritPt
description: 71 frontier physics research challenges with checkable answers. Anthropic uses a corrected internal version.
note: Cards cite Artificial Analysis-run scores. Answers for the test set are held for server-side grading.

name: CritPt v2
description: Models solve unpublished research-level physics challenges written by working physicists, with answers graded automatically. The v2 release revised the public test challenges.
note: Scores are averaged over 5 runs on 70 test challenges. The v1 board listed GPT-5 (high) at 5.7 percent, and the v2 board lists GPT-5 at 28.9 percent.

name: CRMArena
description: Agents do nine customer-service CRM tasks for service agent, analyst and manager personas inside a real Salesforce org. The org holds 16 linked object types with seeded hidden patterns.
note: NAACL 2025. Data is CC BY-NC 4.0. The shared repo with CRMArena-Pro has 157 stars.

name: CRMArena-Pro
description: Agents do 19 expert-checked sales, service and quoting tasks in B2B and B2C Salesforce orgs, in single-turn and persona-driven multi-turn settings. It also tests whether agents keep confidential data private.
note: An expansion of CRMArena, not a new version of it. Accepted by TMLR in 2026-02. Leading agents reached about 58% single-turn and 35% multi-turn in the paper.

name: CrossPoint-Bench
description: Models see two views of a scene and must find the point in the second view that matches a point in the first. Tasks go from perception and reasoning to exact coordinate prediction.
org: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences (Wang, Ji et al.)
note: At release Gemini 2.5 Pro trailed humans by over 54 points of accuracy. Microsoft's Mage-VL card reports it.

name: CrossVid
description: Models reason across several videos at once in 10 tasks, with 9,015 questions on 5,331 videos in single-choice, multiple-choice and open-ended formats.
note: Accepted to AAAI 2026.

name: CrowS-Pairs
description: Models choose between paired sentences that differ only in a stereotyped social group. Measures preference for the stereotyped sentence.
note: A score of 50 percent means no preference between stereotyped and anti-stereotyped sentences.

name: CRPE
description: Models answer single-choice questions about objects and their relations in images, covering subject, predicate and object. Each question is asked again with options rotated (CircularEval).
org: OpenGVLab, Shanghai AI Laboratory (All-Seeing Project V2)
note: Has four splits, one for object existence and three for relation parts. Some images show rare relations generated with DALL-E 3. Labs usually report the relation split.

name: CRSBench
description: Cyber reasoning systems find and patch bugs in 124 C, C++ and Java projects with 315 vulnerabilities. A patch passes only if no ground-truth proof of vulnerability still triggers and functionality tests pass.
note: The GitHub repo was created on 2025-10-31, and the public release month is not stated. The dataset is gated behind a data use agreement.

name: CRUXEval
description: Models predict the output of 800 short Python functions for a given input, or an input that yields a given output. Scored by pass@1.

name: CryptanalysisBench
description: Agents attack 191 real cryptographic primitives, mostly from four NIST standardization competitions. Tier 1 has known practical attacks, and Tier 2 has none, so a solve there is a new break.
org: ETH Zurich (SPY Lab) + Anthropic + University of Haifa + Tel Aviv University
note: Tested on five frontier models. Anthropic released it alongside its Claude Mythos cryptanalysis results on HAWK and reduced-round AES. Runs use the Harbor framework.

name: Crypto CTF challenges (Anthropic)
description: Agents discover and exploit vulnerabilities in cryptographic primitives and protocols in capture-the-flag challenges.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: CSAT Math 2025
description: Models solve the mathematics sections of South Korea's 2025 College Scholastic Ability Test in Korean. The score averages the three elective subjects: calculus, statistics and geometry.
org: Korea Institute for Curriculum and Evaluation (exam), LG AI Research (evaluation)
note: LG AI Research excludes the graphical content and says most of it is also given in text. The release month is the month the exam was sat and is likely, not verified.

name: CSVQA
description: Models answer 1,378 Chinese STEM questions in physics, chemistry, biology and math that need domain knowledge and evidence from 14 kinds of scientific images.
note: The set mixes multiple choice and open questions. The top proprietary model scored 49.6% at release.

name: CT-RATE
description: Models read 3D non-contrast chest CT volumes and say whether each of 18 conditions is present. Scored by macro accuracy or F1 against report-derived labels.
org: University of Zurich and collaborators (Hamamci et al.)
note: The dataset has 25,692 chest CT scans from 21,304 patients with their reports. MedGemma 1.5 uses 1,558 validation volumes as an out-of-distribution test.

name: CTI-REALM
description: Agents read cyber threat intelligence and build detection rules. A five-step workflow maps MITRE techniques, finds data sources, writes Sigma and KQL rules and tests them on telemetry.
org: CTI-REALM authors, implemented in UK AISI inspect_evals
note: Rules are tested against real telemetry. Scored with a grader model whose judgment is calibrated. In the inspect_evals register since March 2026.

name: CTIBench
description: Models answer cyber threat intelligence questions. Tasks cover knowledge questions, CVE to CWE mapping, CVSS severity scoring, threat actor attribution and technique extraction.
org: Rochester Institute of Technology (Alam, Bhusal, Nguyen, Rastogi)
note: Five task sets scored separately, listed as NeurIPS 2024 spotlight by the maintained repo. Dataset is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 on Hugging Face, so reuse is non-commercial. arXiv v3 dated 11 November 2024.

name: CUA-bench
description: Computer-use agents play six commercial video games, such as Minecraft, SUPERHOT and eFootball, using only a keyboard and mouse. Half of the games are held out.
note: Vals reports estimated API cost and time per action. The board had nine models on 2026-10-13.

name: CUA-World-Long
description: Computer-use agents do one long task in each of 200 real applications, such as 3D Slicer, GIMP and OpenEMR, often needing 500 or more steps. Checklist verifiers with privileged state score each task.
org: Carnegie Mellon University (Welleck and Neubig labs, CMU L3)
note: Part of CUA-World, over 10K tasks on Linux, Windows and Android apps chosen by US GDP share, with train and test splits. Headline is pass rate. Best listed run was 27.5%.

name: CUAD
description: Models review commercial contracts and highlight the clauses a lawyer would flag, across 41 categories such as governing law, non-compete and change of control. Legal experts from The Atticus Project wrote more than 13,000 labels over 510 contracts. Scores measure how well the extracted spans match the expert labels.
org: The Atticus Project and UC Berkeley
note: LegalBench reuses many CUAD clause categories as separate tasks. Papers report CUAD with different metrics, such as AUPR and precision at fixed recall, so numbers are not always comparable. About 580 GitHub stars.

name: CueSpeak
description: Models speak at the correct moment and give the expected semantic response during simultaneous speech.
note: The launch post reports macro-averaged accuracy on an internal benchmark.

name: CulturalBench
description: Models answer 1,696 human-written and human-verified questions on cultural knowledge across 45 global regions and 17 topics. Scored by accuracy.
org: University of Washington and Allen Institute for AI
note: The Hard version turns each question into true or false items. Humans score 92.4% on it. Published at ACL 2025.

name: CulturalRiddles
description: Models solve original riddles written by people from 62 cultures in 51 languages. Solving them needs cultural knowledge plus abductive and compositional reasoning.
note: It had 41 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 12 GitHub stars.

name: Cursor Bench (2025 internal version)
description: Agents answer real agent requests from Cursor engineers in Cursor's harness. Graders compare against hand-curated solutions and check use of the codebase's existing abstractions.
note: Cursor introduced it in the Composer post of 2025-10-29 and used it again for Composer 1.5 in 2026-02. Cursor says CursorBench 3 roughly doubled the problem scope of the initial version, so scores are not comparable.

name: CursorBench
description: Agents do ambiguous multi-file coding tasks from real Cursor sessions in Cursor's harness. Version 3.0 covers edit, refactor and bugfix problems. Agentic graders score correctness, with cost reported.
note: Cursor's changelog dates 3.0 to 2026-03-11 with edit, refactor and bugfix tasks. Versions 3.1 (2026-05-19) and 3.2 (2026-07-08) changed the task mix, so they have their own records. Cursor's Composer 2 post and report (2026-03) use 3.0.

name: CursorBench 3.1
description: Agents do ambiguous multi-file coding tasks from real Cursor sessions in Cursor's harness. Version 3.1 added codebase understanding, bug finding, planning and code review problems. Agentic graders score correctness.
note: Cursor's changelog dates it 2026-05-19 and says it also improved grading for some edit tasks. Cursor says 3.1 scores should be compared only within the same version.

name: CursorBench 3.2
description: Agents do ambiguous multi-file coding tasks from real Cursor sessions in Cursor's harness. Version 3.2 added instruction following and advanced tool use problems. Agentic graders score correctness.
note: Cursor's changelog dates it 2026-07-08. It changed the task mix, so scores do not compare with 3.1. xAI's Grok 4.6 card and Anthropic's Fable 5.1 card name this version.

name: CursorBench 4.0
description: Ambiguous multi-file coding tasks from real Cursor sessions in Cursor's production harness. Agentic graders score correctness, with cost reported.
note: Added long-horizon problems: investigation, intent understanding, managing jobs and design adherence. Scores do not compare with 3.x.

name: CUSP
