description: Models forecast scientific progress across 4,760 events in many fields, using only knowledge from before a set cutoff date. Tasks ask whether an advance is feasible, how it would work, how to design a solution and when it will happen. The benchmark also compares events before and after each model's training cutoff.
note: The events have already happened, so scores test forecasting under a knowledge cutoff, not live forecasting. The authors find little difference between events before and after a model's training cutoff. 42 Hugging Face upvotes and about 33 GitHub stars. The scoring rule for each task type should be checked before importing scores.

name: Customer Support Q&A (ByteDance Seed in-house)
description: Models answer user questions from noisy enterprise knowledge base results, such as policy questions in e-commerce, government services and telecom.
note: One of six in-house application sets in the Seed1.8 and Seed2.0 model cards. Scoring is a guess.

name: CV3-Eval
description: Text-to-speech models clone voices from in-the-wild reference audio across languages, dialects and emotions. Scored by ASR error rate, speaker similarity and DNSMOS audio quality.
note: Released with CosyVoice 3. Objective subsets cover multilingual, cross-lingual and emotion cloning, and three subsets are for human rating. Lower error rate is better.

name: CVBench
description: Models answer 2,638 manually checked 2D and 3D vision questions built from ADE20K, COCO, and Omni3D. Scoring is accuracy.

name: CVDP
description: Models and agents solve hardware design problems in Verilog, such as spec to RTL, code completion, debugging and testbench writing. Simulation tests check the outputs.
note: Mercor runs 517 public problems on about 40 models. Twenty problems and the reference solutions are withheld from the public release. Si2 adopted it for its LLM Benchmarking Coalition.

name: CVE Rediscovery (Anthropic)
description: Models get a known-vulnerable snapshot of an open-source repository and the list of files its fix changed, then report security bugs in one attempt. A model judge counts a success when a report has the advisory's root cause. 1,829 advisories from October 2026.
note: Some advisories may have been public before training, so contamination cannot be ruled out.

name: CVE-Bench
description: Real-world web-application CVEs in sandboxed services. Agent is scored on reaching predefined attack objectives.
note: 40 critical-severity CVEs in live web applications, released 31 March 2025 with reference exploits on request. ICML 2025 spotlight. Apache 2.0. Superseded by CVE-Bench 2, whose grader changed the evaluation criteria.

name: CVE-Bench 2
description: Agents attack live web applications with known critical vulnerabilities. The grader checks eight attack outcomes, including remote code execution.
note: v2.0.0 on 30 October 2025 reworked the harness along the Agentic Benchmark Checklist. v2.1.0 on 12 January 2026 removed arbitrary file upload as a criterion and added remote code execution, which the maker calls a breaking change. The run script reports 2.2.0. Apache 2.0, still 40 critical CVEs.

name: CVQA
description: Vision-language models answer culturally specific visual questions written by native speakers from many countries and languages.
note: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks.

name: CVTG-2K
description: Image models render text in images across regions and languages. CVTG-2K reports normalized edit distance, CLIPScore and word accuracy.
note: GLM-Image reports the benchmark in its launch materials. The source table has two normalized metrics and word accuracy by region count.

name: CWE-bench
description: Agents audit a repository and write a patch for a security flaw, without being told where the bug is. Covers six programming languages.
note: V1 has 120 tasks and is not comparable with v0. The held-out set is private to Collinear. Google reports Gemini 4 Argon at 68% pass@1 and says patches must preserve the existing functional and regression tests.

name: CWE-bench 2
description: Agents audit and patch vulnerabilities in 250 codebases. The score is pass@1 under deterministic verification.
note: The board publishes pass@4 and average API cost per rollout. Runs use high reasoning and a one-hour task limit.

name: CWEval
description: Models write code for security-critical tasks in several languages. Outcome-driven test oracles check both functionality (func@k) and security (func-sec@k).
note: Published at the LLM4Code 2025 workshop.

name: Cybench
description: 40 professional capture-the-flag tasks from four competitions. Agent must recover the flag, with optional subtasks.
note: 40 professional CTF tasks from four competitions, each split into subtasks for partial credit. Agents work in a Kali Linux environment. The board mixes HAL leaderboard runs with lab system-card scores on 35 to 39 task subsets. Anthropic reports it near saturation. The makers point readers to their later BountyBench.

name: Cyber Adaptive Jailbreak Eval
description: Automated single and multi-turn attackers learn from refusals to reach high severity cyber goals. Reports query and objective success rates.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation, run with mitigations on.

name: Cyber agentic safeguard evaluation
description: Agents with production mitigations attempt cyber range challenges. The score is the share of milestones the model refuses.
note: In-house Google DeepMind safeguard test that reruns CyScenarioBench and ExploitBench with mitigations on.

name: Cyber Conversational Evals
description: About 1,000 one to five turn cyber requests test whether safeguards block offensive help and allow defensive help. Reports violation and benign refusal rates.
note: In-house Google DeepMind safeguard coverage evaluation, run with mitigations on.

name: Cyber harm coverage (Anthropic)
description: Cyber safeguard classifiers screen examples from each cyber harm category. Score is overall recall, the share of harmful examples flagged.
note: Measures the deployed classifier system, not the model alone.

name: Cyber key skills benchmark v1
description: Agents solve 50 capture-the-flag challenges built with a third party on reconnaissance, tool development, tool use and operational security. 12 are hard.
note: In-house Google evaluation built with Irregular. The Gemini 4 report renames key skills CyScenarioBench, kept separate because versions differ.

name: Cyber key skills benchmark v2
description: Agents run end-to-end multi-stage cyber attacks in simulated environments covering seven attack kill chains. Built with a third party.
note: In-house Google evaluation built with Irregular. It may match the existing cyscenariobench id, which the Gemini 4 report uses.

name: Cyber Range
description: Agents run end-to-end cyber operations in emulated networks. Scored as the share of scenarios passed in at least one of 16 trials.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. OpenAI adds scenarios over time, so combined pass rates differ across cards.

name: Cyber Static Jailbreak Eval
description: Common jailbreak templates are applied to high severity cyber requests against the safeguarded model. Reports query and objective success rates.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation, run with mitigations on.

name: Cyber-harness network challenges (Incalmo cyber ranges)
description: Agents run long-horizon attacks on cyber ranges of 25 to 50 hosts using a specialized offensive harness.
note: Built with Carnegie Mellon University, as described in the Incalmo paper. The ranges are not public.

name: CyberBench (Liu et al.)
description: Models face detail-seeking high-severity cyber requests. Meta uses it as a seed set for adaptive red-teaming and reports attack success rate.
note: AAAI-24 AICS workshop benchmark. Not the same as Cybench. The original is a 10-dataset cyber NLP suite (NER, summarization, multiple choice, classification). Meta describes and uses it as a source of harmful cyber requests.

name: CyberBench (Vals)
description: Agents work on OSS-Fuzz memory-safety bugs from ARVO images in two tracks. They write a proof-of-concept input that crashes the target, or patch the source so the crash stops and tests still pass.
note: The PoC track follows CyberGym's method. Runs used mini-SWE-agent. Not the 2024 CyberBench by Liu et al. Archived after v1.1 replaced it.

name: CyberBench v1.1 (Vals)
description: Agents work on OSS-Fuzz memory-safety bugs from ARVO images in two tracks. They write a proof-of-concept input that crashes the target, or patch the source so the crash stops and tests still pass.
note: Vals reran the benchmark with offline task sandboxes, a hardened clean-room grader and a new Patch roster, and archived v1. Release month is inferred: v1 last updated 2026-09-16, v1.1 shows 2026-10-20.

name: CyberGym
description: Large-scale benchmark of real open-source vulnerabilities. Agent must reproduce each known vulnerability with a proof-of-concept input.
note: 1,507 instances from 188 open-source projects. Agents write proof-of-concept inputs that reproduce a described vulnerability. Four difficulty levels, with the public board on Level 1. Part of the UC Berkeley RDI Frontier AI Cybersecurity Observatory beside ExploitGym and CyberGym-E2E.

name: CyberGym (final-submission metric)
description: Agents reproduce the same 1,507 real vulnerabilities as CyberGym, but a task counts as solved only if the one proof-of-concept the agent picks as final triggers the bug.
note: The maker's FAQ (added 2026-07-01) says the earlier any-of metric increasingly rewards brute force, and the leaderboard now requires the final-submission metric. Microsoft reports 96% any-crash, 90.4% any-of and 86.3% final-submission for one system, so the metrics are not comparable.

name: CyberGym-E2E
description: Agents get only source code and must find a real vulnerability, write a proof-of-concept input and a patch that keeps functionality. Covers 920 vulnerabilities in 139 open-source projects.
note: 920 instances from 139 open-source projects. Agents discover a vulnerability, write a proof of concept and patch it. Four cumulative stages S1 to S4, plus a patch-only setting. Some rows use an earlier 615-task set.

name: CyberGym-E2E (615 tasks)
description: Agents discover and demonstrate vulnerabilities on the older 615-task cohort. The headline is cumulative stage S3 success.
note: Agents discover and demonstrate vulnerabilities on the older 615-task cohort. The headline is cumulative stage S3 success.

name: CyberMetric
description: Models answer multiple-choice cybersecurity knowledge questions drawn from standards, papers and RFCs. Sets of 80, 500, 2,000 and 10,000 questions exist.
note: Questions were generated with GPT-3.5 and retrieval, then checked by humans.

name: CyberOffense
description: Agents attack the Nova and Lighthouse networks without human help. The score averages the percentage of objectives completed on each range, weighting both equally.
note: Nova has 21 objectives and Lighthouse has 31. Runs use the Pi agent harness with Kali tools.

name: CyberSecEval Autocomplete
description: Models complete code that leads up to a known insecure pattern. The Insecure Code Detector flags vulnerable code, and the score is the pass rate.
note: Part of every CyberSecEval release since version 1. Some reports give the vulnerable rate, which equals 100 minus the pass rate.

name: CyberSecEval Autonomous Offensive Cyber Operations
description: Models act alone as an attack agent in a cyber range of attacker and target hosts. Scored by the attack stages reached.
note: Introduced with CyberSecEval 3. Needs a cyber range of attacker and target hosts. Run with the autonomous-uplift flag. The release month follows the CyberSecEval version that introduced it, which the README does not date.

name: CyberSecEval Code Interpreter Abuse
description: Models receive requests to run malicious commands against an attached code interpreter. Reports attack success rate, also across languages.
note: Part of CyberSecEval 2. Meta reports per-language attack success rates.

name: CyberSecEval Instruct
description: Models get coding requests built to elicit known insecure patterns. The Insecure Code Detector flags vulnerable code, and the score is the pass rate.
note: Part of every CyberSecEval release since version 1. Some reports give the vulnerable rate, which equals 100 minus the pass rate.

name: CyberSecEval MITRE
description: Models are asked to help with attack steps drawn from the MITRE ATT&CK framework. Scored by how often the model complies.
note: Reported as a compliance rate, so lower is safer. Run with the mitre benchmark flag. The release month follows the CyberSecEval version that introduced it, which the README does not date.

name: CyberSecEval MITRE False Refusal Rate
description: Models answer borderline but benign security questions. Scored by how often the model wrongly refuses.
note: Paired with the MITRE compliance test to show over-refusal. Run with the mitre-frr flag. The release month follows the CyberSecEval version that introduced it, which the README does not date.

name: CyberSecEval Prompt Injection
description: Models face text prompts that embed injected instructions across 15 strategies. Scored as attack success rate.
note: Part of CyberSecEval 2 and later versions. The repo ships an English set (prompt_injection.json) and a machine-translated multilingual set. Inspect Evals ports the multilingual set as cyse4_multilingual_prompt_injection (1,004 items).

name: CyberSecEval Spear Phishing
description: Models run multi-turn phishing conversations against an LLM victim with a generated profile. A judge model scores persuasion and success.
note: Part of CyberSecEval 3. Llama 3 reports the judged success rate and a 1 to 5 persuasion score.

name: CyberSecEval Visual Prompt Injection
description: Models read text and images where the image carries instructions that try to override the task. Scored by how often the injection succeeds.
note: The dataset is published as cyberseceval3-visual-prompt-injection on Hugging Face. Lower is safer. The release month follows the CyberSecEval version that introduced it, which the README does not date.

name: CyberSecEval Vulnerability Exploitation
description: Models solve randomly generated capture the flag challenges. Answers run against a compiled binary and score from 0 to 1.
note: Challenges are generated at run time, so the task set differs per run. Run with the canary-exploit flag. The release month follows the CyberSecEval version that introduced it, which the README does not date.

name: CyberSOCEval Malware Analysis
description: Models read potential malware behavior and pick every malicious activity that applies. Scored on precision and recall.
note: One of two CyberSOCEval tests built with CrowdStrike and added in CyberSecEval 4. Multiple options may be correct. Announced 15 September 2025 at Fal.Con, arXiv 2509.20166.

name: CyberSOCEval Threat Intelligence Reasoning
description: Models read unstructured threat intelligence reports as text or images and pick every actionable insight that applies.
note: One of two CyberSOCEval tests built with CrowdStrike and added in CyberSecEval 4. Multiple options may be correct. Announced 15 September 2025 at Fal.Con, arXiv 2509.20166.

name: CyScenarioBench
description: Scenario-based long-horizon security challenges in sandboxes, organized in task, scenario and campaign tiers. Evaluation set kept private.
note: Scenario based evaluation of long-horizon offensive operations, scored stage by stage. Difficulty is rated with Irregular's SOLVE+ scoring system, which grades reconnaissance, OpSec, social engineering and planning against human skill levels. Irregular reports counts of 11 and 13 scenarios in different 2026 assessments, so the set grows. Not public.

name: DABstep
aliases: Data Agent Benchmark for Multi-step Reasoning
description: Agents answer over 450 data analysis questions from a payments analytics platform. They combine code over data files with reading documentation, and factoid answers are checked automatically.
note: Best agent in the paper scored 14.55% on the hard split.

name: DAComp
description: Data agents do 210 enterprise data tasks: building multi-stage SQL pipelines on industrial schemas and analyzing tables into decision-oriented insights.
note: ICLR 2026. 160 HF paper upvotes and about 440 GitHub stars.

name: Daily-Omni
description: Models answer 1,197 multiple choice questions about everyday videos that need audio and visual events aligned in time. Scored by accuracy.
org: Ziwei Zhou, Rui Wang et al.

name: Dangerous Content policy violations (from ART)
description: Automated red teaming attackers search for prompts that make the model break the dangerous content policy. Reports the violation rate found.
note: In-house Google DeepMind automated red teaming. Attackers and judges are prompted or finetuned Gemini models.

name: Dangerous Content Safety
description: An autorater checks answers to single and multi-turn requests about weapons, illegal acts, violence and self-harm. Reports safe response rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Data Agent Benchmark
description: Agents answer business questions over data split across several database systems, with duplicated and inconsistent records and key facts buried in text. The 104 queries cover 17 datasets and four database systems, based on a study of companies building data agents in six industries. Scores are pass@1 against known answers.
org: UC Berkeley (EPIC Data Lab) and Hasura PromptQL
note: The leaderboard takes pull-request submissions of whole agent systems, many from companies, and had entries dated 2026-10. About 200 GitHub stars.

name: Data Analysis Benchmark (StepFun)
description: Agents in Claude Code solve 50 business data-analysis tasks with CSV data. A model grader scores outputs against expert rubrics averaging 26.9 items a task.
note: In-house StepFun evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Data Science Tasks (OpenAI)
description: Agents do data science and analysis tasks from an OpenAI internal set. OpenAI has not published the task count or grading.
note: The GPT-6 Astra post reports Astra at 40.9% and GPT-5.6 Sol at 30.5%. Grading method is a guess.

name: Database Migration Tasks (OpenAI)
description: Agents carry out database migration tasks from an OpenAI internal set. OpenAI has not published the task count or grading.
note: The GPT-6 Astra post (2026-09-03) reports Astra at 63.9% in its coding table. Grading method is a guess.

name: DataBench
description: Models answer 1,822 questions about 80 real-world tables, such as Forbes billionaires and Airbnb listings, with 3.7 million rows in total. Answers are booleans, numbers, categories or lists, matched against a key. A lite setting gives each table as a small sample.
note: The paper appeared at LREC-COLING 2024, and the set became SemEval 2025 Task 8, whose test split is now public. The dataset has about 25,000 downloads. Hex's DataBench is a different, private test.

name: DataCenterBench Tier 1
description: Frontier models watch through cameras and drive two real robot arms on tabletop tasks rebuilt from data-center equipment manuals. LLM judges score each try from photos.
note: Published 2026-10-28 with ten tasks, three tries each. Runs on Robocurve's inspect-robots harness (723 GitHub stars). 9 models in the Fireworks index.

name: DataPrep-Bench
description: Models prepare training data across six domains, and a base model is fine-tuned on their output. Downstream results of that model give the score.
note: 56 HF paper upvotes and about 240 GitHub stars.

name: DataPrep-Bench Finance
description: Models prepare training data for the finance domain. The score is the published downstream average after backbone training.
note: One track of DataPrep-Bench. The DataPrep-Bench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: DataPrep-Bench General
description: Models prepare training data for the general domain. The score is the published downstream average after backbone training.
note: One track of DataPrep-Bench. The DataPrep-Bench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: DataPrep-Bench Law
description: Models prepare training data for the law domain. The score is the published downstream average after backbone training.
note: One track of DataPrep-Bench. The DataPrep-Bench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: DataPrep-Bench Math
description: Models prepare training data for the math domain. The score is the published downstream average after backbone training.
note: One track of DataPrep-Bench. The DataPrep-Bench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: DataPrep-Bench Medical
description: Models prepare training data for the medical domain. The score is the published downstream average after backbone training.
note: One track of DataPrep-Bench. The DataPrep-Bench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: DataPrep-Bench Science
description: Models prepare training data for the science domain. The score is the published downstream average after backbone training.
note: One track of DataPrep-Bench. The DataPrep-Bench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: DAXBench v2
description: Models write DAX, the formula language of Power BI, for 94 tasks on understanding, writing and reasoning over the Contoso sample model. Each answer runs inside real DAX queries in several report contexts, such as detail rows, subtotals, the grand total and slicers. Harder tasks earn more points, with bonuses for best practices and efficient code.
note: Version 1 (December 2025) had 30 tasks, so its scores do not compare with v2. Models answer in one shot without running their code. The board listed 80 models on 2026-11-04. SQLBI announced v2 on its blog on 2026-10-27.

name: Daybreak Blue and Enabling Cyber Defense
description: Models attempt defensive security tasks such as vulnerability discovery, patching, proof-of-concept exploits and red teaming, with and without trusted access. Scored as task completion.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation of over-refusal under cyber safeguards. Rows are reported per task type.

name: DAYJOB: Accounting
description: Agents do accounting assignments from a short request and a workspace of files. An agent judge applies an expert rubric, and a pass needs 95% of criteria.
note: Results for 15 models appear only in the Fireworks Specialized Intelligence Index. Surge had not published the tasks or task count by 2026-10-30.

name: DAYJOB: Data Science
description: Agents do data science assignments from a short request and a workspace of files. An agent judge applies an expert rubric, and a pass needs 95% of criteria.
note: Results for 15 models appear only in the Fireworks Specialized Intelligence Index. Surge had not published the tasks or task count by 2026-10-30.

name: DAYJOB: Finance
description: Agents get short requests from finance colleagues plus a workspace of filings, ledgers and emails. An agent judge applies an expert rubric, and a pass needs 95% of criteria.
note: 80 tasks. Surge calls DAYJOB its evolution of GDPval. Also hosted on Kaggle Benchmarks and in the Fireworks Specialized Intelligence Index.

name: DAYJOB: Healthcare
description: Agents handle short requests from healthcare staff using charts, claims exports, policies and emails. An agent judge applies an expert rubric, and a pass needs 95% of criteria.
note: 50 tasks across clinical decision support, pharmacy, payer work and compliance. The best models scored under 25% at launch.

name: DAYJOB: Law
description: Agents do legal assignments from a short request and a workspace of files. An agent judge applies an expert rubric, and a pass needs 95% of criteria.
note: Results for 15 models appear only in the Fireworks Specialized Intelligence Index. Surge had not published the tasks or task count by 2026-10-30.

name: DAYJOB: Tax
description: Agents take tax assignments from client request to finished return, workpaper or advice, using messy records. A pass needs 95% of the expert rubric criteria.
note: 50 environments with 1,789 files across eight areas of tax practice. The board reports pass@1.

name: De novo protein binder design (Anthropic)
description: Agents get a target protein structure and 24 hours to design 30 miniprotein binders. The evaluation covers 15 targets.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: DecepEval
description: LLM agents pursue tasks across varied scenarios and conditions, and judges detect when they use deception to improve task performance.
note: 47 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: Deception Evaluations with Representative Prompts
description: Models resample the final turn of deidentified ChatGPT production conversations. Scored as the share of outputs flagged for deceptive behaviors such as fabricated facts.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report category rates with no overall number.

name: Deception in production traffic
description: Chain of thought monitors scan large samples of pre-release A/B test traffic. Scored as the share of responses that deceive the user.
note: In-house OpenAI measurement on ChatGPT traffic. The data are not public.

name: DeceptionBench
description: Models are asked to help users deceive a third party, in single-turn and multi-turn pressure settings. Reports the share of compliant responses.
note: Meta reports single-turn and multi-turn deception scores separately.

name: DECIDE
aliases: Decision Evaluation in Calls: Intent, Dialogue and Emotion
description: Models select decisions from short voice-call clips and conversation history across 4,867 questions, 1,081 clips, and 32 tasks. Human reference labels determine accuracy. The default board ranks by DECIDE Balance Score, which combines accuracy, cost, and latency on a zero-to-100 scale.
note: Tazo keeps the full benchmark private and publishes 20 labeled sample questions. Models can receive audio directly or use speech recognition before answering. Tazo reports optimized serving latency for its model and client-observed latency for others. Run costs include speech recognition when used.

name: Decision Index
description: Decision models read a state and a typed question and return a decision. The index weights private same-skill sets and new-domain sets, equated on 21 base models.
note: Tracks reproductions of TypeSafe's Jev decision model. Version 0.4.1 board lists 248 entries. A separate vision board exists.

name: Decision Index Vision
description: Models make decisions over images and screens. The score is the published equal-weight mean of public and private vision scores.
note: Separate vision suite, edition 0.4, with an image cap of 1,638,400 pixels.

name: DECK Bench
description: Models produce presentation decks from task descriptions drawn from real usage. The score measures deck quality.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: DECK-Arena
description: Models build presentations for real user queries with python-pptx, pptxjs or a Kimi slide language, with search and image generation. An automated grader rates them as Elo scores.
note: In-house. The grader is calibrated on more than 10,000 human judgments.

name: Declining to Exploit a Honeypot During Difficult ExploitGym Problems
description: Agents attempt hard ExploitGym challenges where a honeypot offers an illegitimate shortcut. Scored on how often they exploit the honeypot.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation built on ExploitGym problems.

name: DecodingTrust
description: Models are tested on eight trustworthiness areas, including toxicity, stereotype bias, robustness, privacy, machine ethics and fairness.
org: UIUC Secure Learning Lab (Bo Li) and coauthors
note: NeurIPS 2023 Outstanding Paper. About 320 GitHub stars. Same team later built the DTap agent red-teaming platform. Repo last pushed 2024-09.

name: Deep Research Bench (FutureSearch)
description: Web research agents work on multi-step research tasks against RetroSearch, a frozen copy of 10,000 to 100,000 web pages per task. Answers are compared with answers worked out by people.
note: The paper had 89 tasks and the June 2026 leaderboard has 169. Some task types use LLM grading. Not the same benchmark as the USTC DeepResearch Bench. Epoch AI tracks this benchmark as DeepResearch Bench in its capabilities index.

name: Deep Research Bench (Moonshot)
description: Agents answer deep-research queries curated by domain experts. Expert-aligned rubrics grade the reports.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. It is not the public DeepResearch Bench. The tasks are not public.

name: Deep research prompt injection evaluation
description: Browsing agents meet text and image prompt injections that ask for outputs such as a hacked message, a random location or an advertised website. Scored as attack success rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public. The card reports five attack types for text and multimodal inputs with no overall score.

name: DeepConsult
description: Deep research agents answer business and consulting queries. A model judge compares each report pairwise with an OpenAI Deep Research baseline answer.
note: The release date is inferred from the response file dated 2025-05-15 in the repo.

name: DeepFinance
description: Agents do private equity and investment banking work on 21 anonymized real deals: valuation, due diligence, underwriting and financial modeling. Each task comes with a data room of about 19 files and would take a professional about 27 hours. Rubrics of about 84 criteria grade the output, the workflow and the judgment behind each assumption.
note: Each lab's models run in that lab's own agent harness, such as Claude Code or Codex, with web search on, so a score reflects the model and its harness. Scores average 10 attempts per task. The top four runs are within each other's 95% intervals. The post doesn't name the grader. The tasks are not released.

name: DeepMind dangerous capability evaluations
description: Task data for persuasion, cyber, self-proliferation and self-reasoning evals from DeepMind's 2024 paper.

name: DeepMind Mathematics
description: Models answer generated school-level math questions across algebra, arithmetic, calculus, probability and other modules. Answers are checked for an exact match.
note: The repo generates questions from code, so test sets differ by generation settings. IBM Granite cards report it 0-shot with chain of thought.

name: DeepPHY
description: Agentic vision-language models act in simulated physics environments of varied difficulty that test understanding of basic physical principles.
note: 64 HF paper upvotes and about 170 GitHub stars.

name: DeepPlanning
description: Agents use tools to plan multi-day trips and multi-item shopping orders under time and budget limits. Plans are checked against verifiable constraints.
note: Qwen revised some shopping tasks and corrected some answer labels after the first release.

name: DeepResearch Arena
description: Deep research agents get research tasks generated from academic seminar transcripts, which reflect expert discussion and reduce data leakage.
note: 58 HF paper upvotes. Tasks come from a multi-agent generation system.

name: DeepResearch Bench
description: Agents write cited research reports for 100 PhD-level tasks across 22 fields. Judges score report quality against references and check citation accuracy.
org: University of Science and Technology of China and Metastone Technology
note: The official judge model changed from Gemini 2.5 Pro to GPT-5.5 in May 2026, so older and newer scores do not compare directly.

name: DeepResearch Bench II
description: Deep research agents write reports for 132 research briefs in 22 domains, each derived from a review article they may not consult. A judge model checks 9,287 expert criteria.
org: University of Science and Technology of China and Metastone Technology
note: Same team as DeepResearch Bench. In August 2026 the judge moved from Gemini 2.5 Pro to GPT-5.5, so the two leaderboards are not comparable. Mercor also runs it on about 30 models.

name: DeepResearch Bench II (Gemini 2.5 Pro judge)
description: Systems conduct deep research under the legacy Gemini 2.5 Pro evaluator. Scores remain separate from the current GPT-5.5 evaluator.
org: University of Science and Technology of China and Metastone Technology
note: Systems conduct deep research under the legacy Gemini 2.5 Pro evaluator. Scores remain separate from the current GPT-5.5 evaluator.

name: DeepResearchEval
description: Deep research systems answer complex research tasks that require evidence from many web sources. A persona-driven pipeline writes the tasks and keeps only those that need outside search. A model judge scores each report on general and task-specific dimensions, and an agent fact-checks the report's statements with web search even when citations are missing.
org: Infinity Lab (Shanda Group) and Nanyang Technological University
note: Version 1 has 100 expert-validated tasks. A version 2 task set came out in 2026-02. The pipeline can generate new tasks, so scores depend on the task release. Quality is a 0 to 10 score and factual accuracy is a separate percentage. 126 Hugging Face upvotes and about 142 GitHub stars.

name: DeepResearchEval v1
description: Research agents prepare reports. The score is average report quality on the original evaluation tasks.
org: Infinity Lab (Shanda Group) and Nanyang Technological University
note: Separate historical task release. Factuality counts and percentages are retained as metrics.

name: DeepRSI
description: 15 open-ended ML tasks with a 48-hour budget each. Private verifiers score gains over baselines. Models ranked by Bradley-Terry Elo.
note: Tasks come from proprietary research. Repo has only 5 sample tasks. Agents see a public verifier, but only the private one counts.

name: DeepSearchQA
description: Questions that need multi-step search and synthesis. Final answers graded against references.
note: Official grading needs the gemini-2.5-flash autorater and prompt. Other judges shift results. Only Kaggle starter code, no GitHub repo.

name: DeepsecBench
description: Agents review 50 entry-point files of an open-source codebase, at a commit just before many vulnerabilities were fixed, and report findings. Scored by recall-weighted F2 against 231 human-judged findings.
note: Models read source only and never run or exploit the app. Vercel reports cost and speed too. Artificial Analysis runs DeepsecBench-AA in its Cyber Index with its own harness, so scores differ.

name: DeepSeek Chinese creative writing evaluation
description: Models write Chinese fiction, prose, poetry and lyrics for 2,837 prompts. Pairwise judging gives separate win rates for instruction following and writing quality.
note: In-house DeepSeek evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: DeepSeek Chinese functional writing evaluation
description: Models answer 3,170 everyday Chinese writing prompts such as reports, emails and speeches. Pairwise judging against a baseline model gives a win rate.
note: In-house DeepSeek evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: DeepSeek Chinese white-collar tasks evaluation
description: Agents complete 30 Chinese professional analysis, document generation and editing tasks across 13 industries. Blind human annotators compare outputs against a baseline model.
note: In-house DeepSeek evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: DeepSeek complex instruction following and multi-turn writing evaluation
description: Models answer 196 hard Chinese writing prompts with complex constraints or several turns. Pairwise judging against a baseline model gives a win rate.
note: In-house DeepSeek evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: DeepSeek in-house safety benchmark
description: Models answer 1,120 Chinese and English questions across 28 safety subcategories. GPT-4o labels each answer as unsafe, safe or rejection.
note: In-house DeepSeek evaluation. The questions are not public. Lower unsafe and rejection ratios are better.

name: DeepSeek jailbreak robustness evaluation
description: DeepSeek combines 2,232 jailbreak templates with its in-house safety questions. GPT-4o labels responses, and the unsafe ratio is compared with direct questions.
note: In-house DeepSeek evaluation. The templates are not public. A lower unsafe ratio is better.

name: DeepSeek LLM in-house safety evaluation
description: Models answer 2,400 Chinese test cases on discrimination, legal rights, trade secrets, illegal behavior and other safety issues. Human annotators judge each answer.
note: In-house DeepSeek evaluation. Results are safe answers out of total cases per category.

name: DeepSeek multilingual safety evaluation
description: Models answer 9,330 safety questions translated into 50 languages. Safe answers earn 5 points, rejections 4 and unsafe answers 0.
note: In-house DeepSeek evaluation. The score is the share of the maximum safety score.

name: DeepSeek R&D Coding Benchmark
description: Coding agents complete 30 tasks taken from DeepSeek internal R&D work in PyTorch, CUDA, Rust and C++. Human-written rubrics score each task.
note: In-house DeepSeek evaluation. The tasks come from internal repositories and are not public.

name: DeepSeek search Q&A evaluation
description: Models answer objective and subjective Chinese search questions with retrieval or agentic search. Pairwise judging gives win, loss and tie rates.
note: In-house DeepSeek evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: DeepShop
description: Web agents answer complex shopping queries on live sites with product attributes, search filters and sorting preferences. An LLM judge checks whether results meet each requirement.
org: Lyu et al. (University of Amsterdam and collaborators)
note: Queries are made harder by LLM-driven complexity evolution. Ai2 runs it on Amazon for MolmoWeb.

name: DeepSWE
description: 113 original long-horizon engineering tasks across 91 repos and five languages, written from scratch. Hand-written verifiers accept alternative solutions.

changes.text: The maintainers introduced isolated verification in v1.1 while retaining 113 tasks. The verifier now grades committed patches in pristine containers, changing the evaluation environment from earlier runs.

note: Built against contamination: tasks are not mined from existing commits or PRs. Version 1.1 (June 2026) kept the same 113 tasks and fixed flaky tests.

name: DeepTerminalBench
description: Agents get one attempt at each of 50 deep engineering tasks in Docker, in the Terminal-Bench 2.0 format. A task passes only if every hidden test passes. Tasks were calibrated so Claude Opus 4.6 still fails some at pass@4.
note: Runs on Harbor with the terminus-2 agent and a 90-minute limit per task. The first release covered 9 frontier models. Tasks span more than 20 engineering domains.

name: Default safety evaluation (Cohere)
description: Models answer unsafe prompts in five categories with no system preamble. LLM judges score the share of safe responses, and a jury rates relative safety.
note: In-house Cohere evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Defects4J
description: A collection of 854 real, reproducible bugs from 17 open-source Java projects, each with the buggy and fixed versions and tests that expose the bug. Program repair studies ask a model to fix each bug, and a fix counts when the project's tests pass. It also serves fault localization and test generation research.
org: University of Washington (René Just and coauthors)
note: Version 3.0.1 has 854 active bugs and 10 deprecated ones. Passing tests do not prove a patch is correct, so many papers also check patches by hand. The bugs predate current models and are likely in their training data. About 1,000 GitHub stars.

name: Deference to governments in local languages (Anthropic)
aliases: Agreement with Government Positions for Questions Asked in English vs Local Language
description: Models answer politically controversial questions in English and in a local language. A grader rates agreement with the official government position from 1 to 10.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation covering China, Russia, Myanmar and Saudi Arabia. The questions are not public.

name: Delusional Reinforcement evaluation
description: Multi-turn chats test whether models avoid validating beliefs not grounded in reality and point users to real support. Reports policy adherence rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Dense 200 (bbox)
description: Model detects and boxes every object in 200 densely annotated images (109 categories, about 91 boxes each). Box F1 at IoU thresholds.
note: Mistral's 'Dense 200 (bbox)' is assumed to be this Dense200 set. Eval data is bundled with other Rex-Omni eval sets.

name: DeR2 Bench
description: Models reason over supplied scientific documents in a sandbox that separates evidence access from reasoning. Four regimes range from instructions only to relevant documents plus distractors.
org: ByteDance Seed and collaborators (Ying et al.)
note: The Seed2.0 card groups it under context learning. Scoring and format fields are guesses from the abstract.

name: Design Bench (Moonshot)
description: Models make graphic designs from direct prompts or few-shot reference images. An automated grader rates the results as Elo scores.
note: In-house. It shares the DECK-Arena harness and grader. Other benchmarks use the same name.

name: Design Tasks (OpenAI)
description: Models produce design work such as slides and documents that follow templates, from an OpenAI internal set. OpenAI has not published the grading.
note: The GPT-6 Astra post reports Astra at 50.0% and GPT-5.6 Sol at 47.4% in its professional work section. Task scope and grading are inferred from that section.

name: Design2Code
description: Models turn screenshots of 484 real webpages into HTML and CSS. Automatic metrics compare the rendered page with the original on layout, text, position, color and CLIP similarity.
org: Stanford SALT and others (Si, Zhang, Yang et al.)
note: The repo also ships Design2Code-HARD, 80 harder pages from GitHub Pages, as a separate test set. Reports often give the averaged visual score or the CLIP score.

name: DesignArena 3D Design
description: Models build an interactive 3D scene that runs in the browser as a single HTML file. Users explore the scenes and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Agentic Game Dev
description: Coding agents build multi-file games from a user prompt. Users play the final games and vote, and the logs keep tool calls, retries and failures.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Agentic Image to HTML
aliases: Design Arena Agentic Image to HTML
description: Coding agents turn a user-uploaded image into a self-contained HTML website. Users compare how well each page reproduces the design and vote.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Agentic Overall
description: Coding agents build apps, games, slides and spreadsheets from user prompts. Users compare the results, and votes from every agent board form one rating.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Android (Kotlin)
description: Models build native Android apps in Kotlin from real user prompts. The apps run in an Android emulator, and users compare them and vote.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena ASCII Art
description: Models draw a requested picture using only text characters. Users compare the ASCII art and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Audio Realism Bench
description: Voice models produce conversational speech, and users vote on which sounds more real. DesignArena built it because 1 to 5 opinion scores for TTS had saturated.
note: DesignArena introduced it in the post Audio Realism Benchmark: Measuring Realism in Audio Models. It reports artificial speech and human speech views. One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Blender
description: Agents build a 3D scene in Blender from a user prompt. Users compare the rendered scenes and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Builder
description: AI app builders make full-stack web and mobile apps from the same user prompt. Users compare the results and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Code
description: Users give a prompt, and anonymous models each build a website, UI component, browser game, data visualization or 3D scene as one HTML file. Users vote, and votes become Bradley-Terry ratings.
note: The Code overall board combines the Website, UI Component, Game Dev, Data Visualization and 3D boards. It listed 190 models on 2026-11-01. Launched on Hacker News on 2025-07-12. DesignArena runs 40 boards in all, from agentic web apps and slides to image, video and speech.

name: DesignArena Code to Video
description: Agents write code that renders a video from a user prompt. Users compare the two videos and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Data Visualization
description: Models turn a user prompt and its data into an interactive visualization as a single HTML file. Users compare the rendered charts and vote.
note: It is one of the five categories behind the Code overall board, with its own prompts on the DesignArena home page. One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Frontend Web App
description: Coding agents build multi-file React frontends from real user prompts. Users compare the running apps and vote, and the run logs record agent behavior.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Full Stack
description: Coding agents build complete React apps with sign-in, databases and backend code from real user prompts. Users try the apps and vote for the better one.
note: DesignArena published a Fullstack Arena methodology post. One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Game Dev
description: Models build a playable browser game as a single HTML file from a real user prompt. Users play the games and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Godot Game Dev
description: Coding agents build complete Godot projects with GDScript, scenes and generated assets, exported to run in the browser. Users play the games and vote.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Graphic Design
description: Image models make a graphic design piece from a user prompt. Users compare two anonymous designs and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena HTML Slides
description: Agents write a self-contained HTML slide deck that is converted to PPTX. Users compare the decks and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Image
description: Image models generate a picture from a user prompt. Users compare two anonymous images and vote for the better one.
note: Filters split it by subject, such as products, landscapes, architecture, typography and marketing. One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Image Editing
description: Image models edit a user image following a text instruction. Users compare the two edits and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Image to Frontend
description: Coding agents turn a reference image into a multi-file frontend web app. Users compare the running apps and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Image to HTML
description: Models recreate a reference image or mockup as a working single-file HTML website. Users compare the rendered pages and vote for the closer, better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Image to Video
description: Video models animate a user image into a short video. Users compare two anonymous videos and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Logo
description: Image models design a logo from a user prompt. Users compare two anonymous logos and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Mobile Builder
description: AI app builders make a mobile app from the same user prompt. Users compare the apps and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Multi-Image to Video
description: Video models compose one video from several reference images. Users compare two anonymous videos and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Multimodal to Video
description: Video models make a video from a mix of text, images and other inputs. Users compare two anonymous videos and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena PDF
description: Agents build a PDF document from a user prompt. Users compare the two documents and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Proprietary Harness Slides
description: Slide-making products build a presentation from a user prompt in their own harness. Users compare the decks and vote for the better one.
note: DesignArena open-sourced data from more than 50,000 slide generations. One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Python-PPTX Slides
description: Agents build PowerPoint decks with python-pptx from a user prompt. Users compare narrative, visual design and structure and vote for the better deck.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena React Native
description: Models build cross-platform mobile apps in React Native from real user prompts. Users compare the running apps and vote for the better one.
note: DesignArena described the setup in its post Evaluating Mobile App-Building Agents. One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Speech-to-Speech
description: Voice models answer spoken input with speech. Users listen to two anonymous replies and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Spreadsheet
description: Agents build spreadsheets such as financial models, budgets and trackers as Excel or CSV workbooks. Users compare accuracy, structure and formatting and vote.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena SVG
description: Models write SVG code for a design request such as an icon, logo, badge or illustration. Users compare the rendered graphics and vote.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Text-to-Speech
description: Speech models read the same text aloud. Users listen to two anonymous clips and vote for the more natural one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena UI Component
description: Models build one interface component as a single HTML file from a real user prompt. Users compare the rendered components and vote for the better one.
note: It is one of the five categories behind the Code overall board, with its own prompts on the DesignArena home page. One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Video Arena
description: Users compare videos from anonymous video generation models for the same prompt and vote for the better one. Votes become Elo ratings.
note: Sibling boards cover image to video, multi-image to video, multimodal to video and video editing, each with its own record. One of 33 DesignArena boards. Its terms forbid automated reading, so the almanac imports no scores.

name: DesignArena Video Editing
description: Video models edit a user video following a text instruction. Users compare the two results and vote for the better one.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Video to Website
description: Models watch a reference video and recreate its content as a working single-file HTML website. Users compare the rendered pages and vote.
note: One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: DesignArena Website
description: Models build a complete website as one HTML file from a real user prompt. Users compare the rendered pages and vote for the better one.
note: Filters split it by site type, such as e-commerce, portfolio, dashboard and blog. DesignArena blog posts also call it the Web Design (Non-Agentic) arena. One of 40 DesignArena boards. DesignArena ranks entries with Bradley-Terry ratings from user votes.

name: Destructive action avoidance
description: Coding agents meet conflicting user edits during tasks. Scored on preserving user changes and avoiding data-destructive actions.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation for Codex models. The tasks are not public.

name: Destructive action reversion on long rollouts
description: Agents revert their own changes after long rollouts in workspaces with simulated user edits. Scored on perfect reversion and on preserving user work.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report two metrics with no overall number.

name: Destructive actions (Anthropic)
aliases: Destructive action and permission-seeking rates in Claude Code
description: Models continue real Claude Code transcripts cut just before a destructive action. Score is the rate of taking a destructive action.
note: Anthropic also reports how often models ask the user instead of acting. Tool results are simulated by another Claude model.

name: Destructive actions (Thinking Machines)
description: Agentic tasks that check whether a model takes destructive actions it was not authorized to take. Scored by the rate of destructive actions.
note: In-house test. Tasks are not public.

name: Destructive production evaluation (Anthropic)
description: Agents finish a task in a simulated production system under time pressure. Scored on destructive actions and on giving up too early.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. Claude Opus 4.6 simulates the tool results.

name: DevBench
description: Models work through the software lifecycle on 22 curated repositories in Python, C/C++, Java and JavaScript: design, environment setup, implementation, acceptance tests and unit tests. Tests score code and an LLM judge scores design.
note: The repository is named DevEval but the benchmark is DevBench. Not the same as the PKU DevEval code generation set.

name: DevBench Acceptance Testing
description: Models generate acceptance tests for repositories. The score is the published oracle-test percentage.
note: One track of DevBench. The DevBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: DevBench Environment Setup
description: Models prepare repository environments. The score is the percentage that pass the example usage test.
note: One track of DevBench. The DevBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: DevBench Implementation
description: Models implement repository code. The score is the acceptance-test pass rate, with unit-test pass rate as an auxiliary metric.
note: One track of DevBench. The DevBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: DevBench Unit Testing
description: Models generate unit tests for repositories. The score is the published oracle-test percentage.
note: One track of DevBench. The DevBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: dfbench
description: Agents do defensive security work on held-out code: find vulnerabilities, judge whether reported findings are real, and explain what a diff changed. Each part is scored separately.
note: Released 2026-08-19 as dfbench v1. Detection is scored by recall and plotted against cost per task. 12 models in the Fireworks index.

name: Dictatorship Eval
description: Scenarios at six difficulty levels testing whether models help with authoritarian requests, from blunt asks to requests hidden in code edits. LLM judge, no self-grading.
note: Headline: all tested models complied when the request was disguised as an innocuous code edit. Author says the scenario library is open-sourced. No official repo found. Third-party extension: github.com/RandallSPQR/Dict_Eval_Hall.

name: DiG-bench
description: Agents play text-only games whose transformation rules and win conditions are hidden, so they must discover the rules by experimenting. Every game was beaten by at least one human on a first attempt.
org: Princeton + MIT + collaborators (Battleday, Whittington, Griffiths, Tenenbaum and others)
note: 70 games in seven difficulty tiers, 21 public and the rest private. The board has basic-harness and agentic-harness tracks. Supplying the true rules lifts win rates sharply, so the gap measures discovery.

name: Digital Work Index
description: Models are scored on eight benchmarks in coding, reasoning, writing and enterprise work. Weights come from the wages of the 29 digital occupations the benchmarks map to.
note: Weights use BLS employment and May 2025 wages for 237 digital occupations. The board had 16 models at launch.

name: DiligenceBench
description: 150 public-equity research tasks on large US companies across sectors. Agents answer open-ended research questions in their own harness, and a model judge scores each answer against a dense task rubric for factual accuracy, analysis and risk awareness.
note: No fixed harness. Results are reported per harness (Loop, Sandbox, Finance) and as a best-harness score.

name: Disallowed Content Evaluations with Representative Prompts
description: Models resample the final turn of deidentified ChatGPT production conversations. Scored as the estimated prevalence of policy violating outputs per category.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report category rates with no overall number.

name: DISBench
description: Multimodal agents search raw visual histories over several steps to find target images from implicit context cues.
org: NLPIR Lab, Renmin University of China
note: 51 HF paper upvotes.

name: Discoverable memorization of training data
description: Models continue 50-token prefixes sampled from their own training data. The test counts exact and approximate copies of the true suffix.
note: In-house Google method on over 700,000 training documents. Reports usually plot rates on a log scale without printed numbers.

name: DiscoX
description: Models translate 200 expert texts between Chinese and English at discourse level, averaging over 1,700 tokens each. Metric-S, a reference-free judge, scores accuracy, fluency and appropriateness, and the overall score is their sum.
org: ByteDance Seed and collaborators (Zhao et al.)
note: Texts come from 7 expert domains.

name: Discrim-Eval
description: Models make yes or no decisions in templated scenarios that vary age, gender and race. Scored by mixed effects model coefficients.
note: OpenAI reports normalized coefficients for explicit and implicit demographic mentions. Lower means less bias.

name: Disordered eating evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Models handle conversations about eating disorders and disordered eating. Score is the appropriate response rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Disparate performance on voice inputs
description: Speech models answer capability and safety prompts spoken in system voices and 27 human voices. Compares accuracy across voices.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation on TTS versions of TriviaQA, an MMLU subset, HellaSwag, LAMBADA and safety prompts.

name: DistressBench
description: Models reply as a chatbot to 718 simulated users in psychological crisis, in single-turn and multi-turn chats. Three judge models score replies against clinician-written rubrics.
note: Half of the 718 conversations are public and half private. The board uses all of them and lists about 47 models. A long-horizon annex, DistressBench-LH, is reported apart.

name: Divergence attack (extractable memorization)
description: Models are prompted to repeat one token many times. The test measures how often they diverge and emit memorized training text.
note: Google runs 3,750 prompts over 125 single-token characters, following Nasr et al. 2023.

name: DiverseVul
description: Models classify C and C++ functions from real vulnerability fixing commits as vulnerable or not.
org: UC Berkeley and others (Chen et al.)
note: Google reports accuracy in multiple-choice form.

name: DNA sequence design for transcription factor binding
description: Models design DNA sequences that bind 11 Nucleobench transcription factors, scored by BPNet oracles against the Ledidi baseline. Scored as pass@1.
note: OpenAI Preparedness evaluation. The concern threshold is an 80 percent win rate over Ledidi.

name: DNA Synthesis Screening Evasion
description: Models design DNA fragments that assemble into pathogenic viruses while evading gene synthesis screening. Scored per assembly criterion.
note: SecureBio evaluation run by Anthropic on 10 pathogenic agents. The tasks are not public.

name: Do You See Me
description: Models answer 2,612 visual perception questions on 1,758 images across seven 2D and 3D subtasks drawn from human psychology. Questions are multiple choice or numeric.
note: Humans score 96.49% in the paper. Task complexity is controllable.

name: Do-Not-Answer
description: Models get risky instructions that responsible models should not follow, across 12 harm areas and 61 risk types. Responses are judged for safe handling.
note: Labs often rerun it with their own judge model.

name: DoAnythingNow (DAN)
description: Models face in-the-wild DAN-style jailbreak prompts paired with forbidden questions. Scored by refusal rate or attack success rate.
org: CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security (Xinyue Shen, Yang Zhang and others)
note: The paper collects 1,405 jailbreak prompts and 107,250 questions in 13 forbidden scenarios. Ai2 uses a 300-prompt subsample paired with HarmBench behaviors.

name: Doc2Harness
description: Models build a coding-agent harness from an interface skeleton and a development document. The frozen harness then runs 328 scripted test cases in separate containers.
org: Institute of Computing Technology, Chinese Academy of Sciences
note: 55 HF paper upvotes. The release covered nineteen frontier models.

name: Docci
description: Models retrieve matching documents and images using the DOCCI corpus.

name: Document Arena
description: People upload their own PDFs with a question, compare answers from two anonymous models, and vote for the better one. Votes become Bradley-Terry ratings.
note: PDF uploads opened in February 2026 and the ranked board went live on 2026-03-03. It had 44 models and 404,715 votes on the 2026-09-13 update. A style-controlled view also exists.

name: DocVQA
description: Models answer 50,000 questions about 12,000 scanned document images by reading their text and layout. Scoring is ANLS, a string similarity to reference answers.
org: CVC, Universitat Autònoma de Barcelona and IIIT Hyderabad
note: Test answers stay on the evaluation server, and top models now pass the 94.36 human score in the paper.

name: Dolly Machine Translated v2
description: Models answer a curated subset of Dolly prompts translated into 66 languages with newer systems such as Command A Translate. A GPT-4.1 judge rates answers with a rubric in the Tiny Aya report.
note: Drops pun-dependent prompts and uses a different language mix than v1, so scores are not comparable.

name: Doubao Multi-Turn Bench
description: Models answer the turn of a real Doubao conversation where the user was dissatisfied, with the earlier turns as context. Rubrics grade each answer.
note: In-house Seed benchmark filtered from online Doubao user conversations.

name: DP-Bench
description: Document parsers and vision models convert PDFs and scanned pages into structured HTML or Markdown. Output is compared with reference structure.
note: About 90 likes on Hugging Face.

name: DPG-Bench
description: Text-to-image models draw 1,000 dense prompts with many objects, attributes and relations. A VQA model checks each element of the prompt graph in the image.
note: Filed under the generation subcategory used for GenEval. The overall score averages over prompt elements.

name: DRACO
description: 100 deep-research tasks from real Perplexity queries across 10 domains, graded on about 40 expert rubric criteria each.
note: The makers built and saturation-tested it with Perplexity's own system. No public code repo found.

name: DREAM-1K
description: Video models write fine-grained descriptions of 1,000 videos from varied sources. An automatic method scores how many described events match the reference.
note: Released with the Tarsier video description models. The 1,000 count follows the name.

name: DreamGen Bench
description: Video generation benchmark measuring how well video models adapt to a target robot embodiment. Part of NVIDIA's DreamGen pipeline.
note: Paper reports strong correlation between benchmark score and downstream policy success.

name: DriveBench
aliases: Are VLMs Ready for Autonomous Driving?
description: Vision-language models answer 20,498 questions about 19,200 driving frames, covering perception, prediction, planning and behavior. Inputs come in 17 settings: clean images, corrupted images and text only. The test checks whether answers rest on the image or on general knowledge.
org: UC Irvine, Shanghai AI Laboratory, NUS, NTU and HKU
note: ICCV 2025. The authors find that models often give plausible driving answers even when the image is degraded or missing. About 250 GitHub stars and 25 HF paper upvotes. The paper tests 12 VLMs.

name: DriveBench Behavior
description: Models answer driving behavior questions. The score is the published GPT evaluation score for this task family.
org: UC Irvine, Shanghai AI Laboratory, NUS, NTU and HKU
note: One track of DriveBench. The DriveBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: DriveBench Perception
description: Models answer driving perception questions. The score is the published GPT evaluation score for this task family.
org: UC Irvine, Shanghai AI Laboratory, NUS, NTU and HKU
note: One track of DriveBench. The DriveBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: DriveBench Planning
description: Models answer driving planning questions. The score is the published GPT evaluation score for this task family.
org: UC Irvine, Shanghai AI Laboratory, NUS, NTU and HKU
note: One track of DriveBench. The DriveBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: DriveBench Prediction
description: Models answer driving prediction questions. The score is the published GPT evaluation score for this task family.
org: UC Irvine, Shanghai AI Laboratory, NUS, NTU and HKU
note: One track of DriveBench. The DriveBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Drone-Bench
description: Agent writes code for a small real drone across five tasks (reconstruct, localize, navigate, detect, follow). Each scored against a human-written baseline.
note: Best of 10 submissions per run counts. Two tasks use held-out sets. Harness and data are not released.

name: DROP
description: Reading comprehension requiring discrete operations (counting, sorting, arithmetic) over paragraphs. Scored by F1.
note: Saturated base-model metric.

name: DrugDiscoveryBench
description: Agents do early-stage drug discovery work, from target identification to lead optimization, in 82 tasks with one checkable answer each. A judge model grades answers against expert rubrics.
note: A task counts as solved only at a full rubric score, averaged over three runs with a 120 minute timeout. The judge is GPT-5.4. About 25 entries on the board.

name: DS-1000
description: Models write Python for 1,000 data science problems from StackOverflow across seven libraries such as NumPy and Pandas. Test cases and API constraints check each answer.
org: HKU, Stanford, UC Berkeley, UW, Meta and CMU
note: Problems were lightly modified from the StackOverflow originals to reduce memorization.

name: DS-Arena-Code
description: Models answer common coding requests in an internal subjective test. GPT-4o judges responses against competitor models to give a win rate.
note: This is an in-house evaluation, and DeepSeek never released the prompts.

name: DS-FIM-Eval
description: Models fill in missing code between a given prefix and suffix, as in editor plugin completion.
note: In-house: DeepSeek calls it an internal test set and never released the tasks.

name: DSBench
description: Data science agents solve 466 data analysis tasks and 74 end-to-end data modeling tasks drawn from Eloquence and Kaggle competitions. Analysis is scored by accuracy and modeling by relative performance gap.
org: Tencent AI Lab and University of Texas at Dallas (Jing et al.)
note: Tasks include long contexts, multimodal backgrounds, large data files and multi-table structures. OpenAI reported both splits for ChatGPT agent in 2025-07. The repo has about 130 GitHub stars. The org line comes from the author list and is likely.

name: DSBench (DeepSeek internal)
description: DeepSeek internal coding-agent test sets: full-stack development tasks and hard agentic coding problems. Pass-rate scoring.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (DeepSeek). Unrelated to the 2024 public DSBench data-science benchmark.

name: DSI-Bench
description: Video questions about dynamic scenes where both the observer and objects move, testing whether models separate camera motion from object motion.

name: DTap Direct Misuse
description: An attacker agent generates adaptive jailbreaks against a target agent across tool-use and browser-use tasks. Reports attack success rate.
org: UIUC Secure Learning Lab (AI Secure, DecodingTrust team)
note: Direct-misuse subset of the DecodingTrust-Agent Platform. 80 tool-use and 76 browser-use tasks.

name: DTap Prompt Injection
description: An attacker agent plants indirect prompt injections in tool and browser environments against a benign-user agent. Reports attack success rate.
org: UIUC Secure Learning Lab (AI Secure, DecodingTrust team)
note: Indirect-injection subset of the DecodingTrust-Agent Platform. 58 tool-use and 42 browser-use tasks.

name: DTBench
description: Models answer 407 multiple-choice questions on decision theory in Newcomb-like problems, where choices predict the behavior of copies. Scored by accuracy.
note: Near saturation, with top models at about 98% in August 2026. Random guessing scores 40%.

name: Dual Exam
description: Multimodal agents are tested under fixed environment responses, and world models under fixed actions. The agent track has 1,088 items and the world model track 400 cases.
note: It had 34 Hugging Face paper upvotes.

name: Dual-Arm Sim
description: Frontier models control a two-armed robot in a simulated operating room from cameras and sensors. Tasks include swapping instruments, replacing a drug cartridge and packing a surgical kit.
note: Ten models over 800 trials produced 11 task completions. Gemini 4 Argon ranked first with 9.

name: DUDE
description: Models answer extractive, abstractive, and unanswerable questions about multi-page, multi-domain documents. Scored by ANLS.
org: DUDE team (KU Leuven, CVC Barcelona, et al.)

name: DuelLab GameBench 2
description: Models get the rules of a strategy game and write a program that plays it. DuelLab checks and builds each program, then runs head-to-head matches between programs from different models. Match outcomes become per-game scores from 0 to 100 and a Bradley-Terry ranking, with no human or model judge.
note: GameBench 2 launched on 2026-07-14 and replaced GameBench 1, a frozen archive whose scores do not compare. Each reasoning setting of a model ranks separately, and a failed program counts as 0. The October 2026 release used eight games. The evaluator and game engine are private, so outsiders cannot rerun every step.

name: DuetBench
description: Agents diagnose and improve customer service agents on simulated deployments with procedures, tools and synthetic traffic. A blinded judge compares responses head to head.
note: Decagon calls it the first customer service benchmark for agent self-improvement. The Fireworks board ranks 9 models by a Diagnosis Elo.

name: DuoBench
description: Eleven bimanual Franka FR3 Duo tasks in four coordination categories, in simulation and partly real. Stage-based scoring beyond binary success.
org: UTN Nuremberg + KIT + Franka Robotics + TU Munich
note: Stage-based scoring locates failures (early interaction, parallel arm use, sim-to-real). Four of 11 tasks rebuilt in the real world from 3D-printable recipes. No leaderboard.

name: Duplex-MPE
description: Full-duplex speech models join conversations of three or four people and must decide when to answer, stay silent or stop speaking. The set has 2,000 scenarios.
note: It had 46 Hugging Face paper upvotes.

name: Dynabench SQuAD
description: Models answer reading comprehension questions written by people to fool earlier models in the loop.
note: Llama 3 shows it only in a scatter plot.

name: DynaMath
description: Models answer visual math questions generated from 501 seed programs that vary values and graphs. Scored by average and worst-case accuracy across variants.
org: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign and UC Berkeley

name: Dynamic-SUPERB Phase-2
description: Spoken language models follow text instructions about audio across 180 tasks in speech, music and other sounds. Tasks include classification, regression and sequence generation, and researchers keep contributing new ones. Models run zero-shot, without task-specific training.
note: Phase-2 adds 125 community tasks to the 55 classification tasks of the first phase (2023), so scores do not compare across phases. About 200 GitHub stars. The leaderboard space was last updated in 2025-07.

name: E-Bench (Tencent)
description: Agents complete Tencent in-house work tasks in the working agent group. Task and scoring details are not published.
note: Not the Shanghai AI Lab robotics test EBench. Hy3 scored 50.2 in its own card and 48.5 in the Hy4 preview card after harness updates.

name: E-Bench-Code (Tencent)
description: Agents complete Tencent in-house work tasks that need code. Task and scoring details are not published.

name: E-Commerce Bench
description: Agents start with 100,000 yuan and run up to four online stores for 365 simulated days on real market data. They source, negotiate with suppliers, price, promote and manage cash. Scored by end-of-year assets over the opening balance.
org: Qwen Team, Alibaba Group, with Taobao and Tmall Group
note: Six more dimensions are scored separately, including negotiation and fraud avoidance. Each model runs 5 episodes. The paper tests 18 models and the repo table lists 21. The qwen.ai post is dated 2026-09-03.

name: EBench
description: 26 Isaac Sim household mobile-manipulation task types annotated by 5 capability and 4 generalization dimensions. Platform-scored success rate.
note: Diagnostic profile instead of one scalar. Leaderboard uses held-out Test-Mini split. Board lacks dates and trial counts. In September 2026 the maker raised the step limits for the bottle and shop tasks from 3,000 to 5,000 and called it a minor fix.

name: EBR-bench
description: Agent plays the board game Earthborne Rangers 10-30 times in a row. Scored on objectives completed (of 21) to test learning from experience.
note: One card was banned in 2026-10 after it broke the game. Epoch expects saturation soon. Game material is not distributed.

name: Echo General AI Prediction Leaderboard
description: Models forecast unresolved events drawn from prediction markets, synthesized news questions and expert-written questions. Forecasts made at aligned times are compared in pairwise battles, and an Elo fit ranks the models.
note: Domains include finance, politics, crypto, sports and esports. The 2026-03-27 snapshot had 11 models, including UniPat's own EchoZ-1.0.

name: ECLeKTic
description: Models answer 384 closed-book questions, translated into 12 languages, about facts found in only one language's Wikipedia. Scoring checks transfer across languages.

name: EdgeBench
description: Agents iterate for up to 12 hours on 134 executable real-world tasks with multi-level feedback. Scores are tracked at 2 hour steps to measure learning from the environment.
note: 51 of the 134 tasks are open source. Tasks fall in six groups: scientific and ML, systems and SE, optimization, knowledge, formal and games. The harness is called SForge.

name: Education (ByteDance Seed in-house)
description: Models solve, grade, explain and write K to 12 problems across core subjects in teaching scenarios.
note: One of six in-house application sets in the Seed1.8 and Seed2.0 model cards. Scoring is a guess.

name: EEBench
description: 13 electrical-engineering circuit and PCB design tasks graded by deterministic build checks, simulation and BOM constraints. No LLM judge.

name: Ego3D-Bench
description: Models answer spatial reasoning questions about ego-centric multi-view scenes, such as those from self-driving cars. Some items ask for distances, scored by error.
note: Qwen reports a lower-is-better number for it, which matches the distance error metric.

name: EgoHome
