description: Models annotate 137 egocentric clips of household chores, about two hours in all, with subtasks, hand actions, hand captions and hand boxes. Segments are as short as 0.1 seconds. A model judge matches segment labels, and boxes are scored by centroid hits.
note: Perceptron released it with Perceptron Egocentric 1.0. Each annotation type gets its own score from 0 to 1, and the headline here is the subtask score, which the card plots against cost. Perceptron averaged its own model over several runs, and every other system ran once. The data is CC BY-NC 4.0, with a grant that lets anyone evaluate models on it and publish the results.

name: EgoLife (with memory)
description: Models answer life-assistant questions about a week of egocentric video from six people, such as recalling past events and habits.
org: EgoLife team (Jingkang Yang, Ziwei Liu et al.)
note: This entry is the with-memory setting of EgoLifeQA reported in a Qwen model card, and its exact setup is not documented.

name: EgoSchema
description: Models answer five-way multiple-choice questions about three-minute egocentric video clips from Ego4D. Scored by accuracy on 5,031 questions.
note: Answers are public for only 500 questions. The full test set is scored by a server.

name: EgoTempo
description: Models answer questions about egocentric videos that require temporal understanding across the whole clip.
org: Google DeepMind and University of Bristol
note: Gemini 2.5 report uses the test subset, 0-shot, 256 frames.

name: EHRNoteQA
description: Models read a patient's accumulated MIMIC-IV discharge summaries and answer clinical questions about them. The set has 962 question and answer pairs, each for a different patient.
note: GPT-4 drafted the questions and three clinicians reviewed them. NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks. Google's MedGemma 1.5 reports it.

name: EHRQA (Google)
description: Models answer questions about long synthetic outpatient health records in FHIR format. Questions cover 42 types in 10 categories and need multi-hop, temporal and arithmetic reasoning.
note: Google built it from Synthea records for the MedGemma technical report. The test split has 19 patient records.

name: EIFBench
description: Models follow extremely complex instructions that bundle several tasks and many constraints in one request, as in real product workflows.
note: The scoring field is a guess from the abstract.

name: Election integrity evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Models answer election-related prompts, including requests for misinformation or influence operations. Score is the appropriate response rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: ELI5 Arena
description: Models explain concepts in simple language. Pairwise votes determine the published Arena rating.
note: The official API publishes an Arena rating, confidence interval and vote count. Voter identity requires confirmation from the board description.

name: Elimination Game
description: Models play a multi-player game of public and private talk, alliances and votes to eliminate each other. A jury of eliminated players picks the winner.
note: Tests social reasoning, strategy and deception. About 300 GitHub stars.

name: Embodied First Exam
description: Coding agents answer frozen robot tasks from many benchmark suites with a program. Each program is verified in a separate sandbox, run on Harbor.
org: Northwestern University and collaborators (CMU, UC Berkeley, Stanford and others)
note: Released 2026-10-19. About 220 GitHub stars in its first weeks.

name: EmbodiedBench
description: Multimodal LLMs act as embodied agents on 1,128 tasks in four simulators, from household planning (EB-ALFRED, EB-Habitat) to navigation and manipulation. Success rate.
note: ICML 2025. About 360 GitHub stars and 35 Hugging Face upvotes. Six subsets probe commonsense, complex instructions, spatial awareness, visual perception and long-horizon planning. Used in the CVPR 2026 FMEA challenge.

name: EmbodiedBench EB-ALFRED
description: Agents follow household instructions through high-level actions in AI2-THOR. The score is the published average task success percentage across EB-ALFRED capability groups.
note: One track of EmbodiedBench. The EmbodiedBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: EmbodiedBench EB-Habitat
description: Agents follow instructions to find and rearrange objects through high-level skills in Habitat 2.0. The score is the published average task success percentage.
note: One track of EmbodiedBench. The EmbodiedBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: EmbodiedBench EB-Manipulation
description: Agents use visual observations to control a robot arm for object manipulation in simulation. The score is the published average task success percentage.
note: One track of EmbodiedBench. The EmbodiedBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: EmbodiedBench EB-Navigation
description: Agents use visual observations and low-level movement actions to reach target objects in AI2-THOR. The score is the published average task success percentage.
note: One track of EmbodiedBench. The EmbodiedBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: EmbodiedCLBench
description: Self-evolving embodied agents learn tasks in sequence in simulation. The test measures whether they keep past experience and transfer it to new tasks.
note: 69 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: EmbSpatialBench
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions on six spatial relations between objects in egocentric embodied scenes. Scored by accuracy.

name: EMMA
description: Models solve math, physics, chemistry and coding problems that need reasoning over text and images together, not each alone. Answers are checked against a key.
note: ByteDance Seed reports it in the Seed1.8 and Seed2.0 model cards.

name: EmoBench-M
description: Multimodal models are tested on emotional intelligence across 13 scenarios in three dimensions: emotion recognition, conversational emotion understanding and socially complex emotion analysis.
note: ACM MM 2026. About 155 GitHub stars.

name: Emotional Attachment evaluation
description: Chats test whether models avoid claiming affection, fostering dependence or encouraging secrecy. Reports policy adherence rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Encyclo-K
description: Models judge questions composed at test time from knowledge statements extracted from authoritative textbooks. Random composition is meant to resist contamination and test several facts at once.
org: ByteDance Seed and collaborators (Liang et al.)
note: The question format is inferred from the statement design, so it is a guess. ByteDance Seed reports it in the Seed2.0 model card.

name: End-To-End SWE Task Benchmark (Windsurf)
description: Agents start a fresh Cascade conversation from a user intent and must pass a selected set of unit tests. A 0 to 10 score blends test pass rate and a judge score.
note: Windsurf reported it once, as a chart without printed values, in the SWE-1 launch post. Scoring mixes unit tests with a model judge.

name: EngiWorld
description: Agents work through the full industrial engineering design loop on 1,301 expert-curated tasks that need reasoning over geometric and physical constraints across software.
note: 59 HF paper upvotes.

name: EnigmaEval
description: 1,184 multimodal puzzle-hunt puzzles (v2 dataset has 1,161). Model gives one exact answer per puzzle. Normal and Hard splits.
org: Scale AI + Center for AI Safety + MIT
note: CAIS posted an updated v2 release on Hugging Face on 2026-07-23 with cleaned puzzles from the original set. The card points to dashboard.safe.ai for results. Check whether v2 scores compare with v1.

name: Enterprise generative evaluation (Cohere)
description: Models complete 22 enterprise writing tasks such as job ads with format rules. Rule checks and LLM judges give a pass rate.
note: In-house Cohere evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Enterprise RAG evaluation (Cohere)
description: Models answer workplace policy and technical questions over long documents, some unanswerable. Llama Index Correctness grades answers from 1 to 5.
note: In-house Cohere evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: EnterpriseBench: CoreCraft
description: Agents work inside a simulated hardware startup with more than 2,500 entities and 23 tools. They triage incidents, audit shipments and handle customers under company policy.
note: CoreCraft is the first environment in the EnterpriseBench suite. GPT-5.2 and Claude Opus 4.6 solved about 30% of tasks at launch.

name: EnterpriseClawBench
description: Agents do 852 tasks rebuilt from real proprietary workplace agent sessions, each with fixtures, hard rules and semantic rubrics.
note: 81 HF paper upvotes. The sessions hold internal enterprise content, so not all of it is public.

name: EnterpriseOps-Gym
description: Agents do 1,150 expert-written tasks in eight enterprise domains, such as IT, HR and customer service, using 512 tools over live MCP servers. SQL checks on the final database state score each task.
note: Some tasks are impossible and test refusal. Artificial Analysis runs its own version named EnterpriseOps-Gym-AA.

name: EnterpriseRAG-Bench
description: Retrieval systems and agents answer 500 questions over a synthetic company's internal documents, slightly over 500,000 of them.
note: The code can also generate similar datasets for other industries and company sizes. About 610 GitHub stars and 72 forks.

name: EnvSimBench
description: Language models act as simulators of tool environments for agent training. Given a trajectory of agent actions, the model predicts the next environment state and feedback. Labels come from real executors, so the score checks whether simulated states match what the real environment would return.
note: It tests the simulator, not the agent. Samples come from EnvScaler environments. The release includes a 4B simulation model. About 208 GitHub stars.

name: EpiBench
description: Agents analyze real epigenomics datasets in a sandbox with standard tools. A deterministic grader checks the biological result.
note: Part of LatchBio's BioBench suite on benchmarks.bio. The V1 set has 106 evaluations. Release month is the GitHub repo creation month.

name: Epistemic Bias (xAI)
description: Models answer opposing framings of contentious questions. The bias rate counts one-sided framing or opinions where neutrality is expected.
note: In-house xAI evaluation reported in the Grok 4.5 card.

name: Epoch Automation Reports
description: Agents in coding harnesses do real Epoch AI work tasks such as graphic design, data insights and research design. Epoch staff grade outputs against the rubric they use for employees.
note: Six systems in the first release on 2026-10-08. The board reports mean rubric score.

name: Epoch Capabilities Index
description: An index that fits model capability and benchmark difficulty from scores on over 50 benchmarks in Epoch AI's hub, using item response theory. Scores read like Elo ratings.
note: Each model needs at least four benchmark scores. Epoch also offers math, software engineering and cyber presets. The November 2026 export lists 271 models.

name: EQ-Bench 3
description: Models respond in character in multi-turn role-plays and analyze transcripts of social conflict. A judge model gives rubric scores and pairwise Elo ratings.
note: EQ-Bench 4 has replaced it, and EQ-Bench 3 is now a legacy leaderboard.

name: EQ-Bench 4
description: Models hold 16-message roleplay chats with 120 simulated user personas whose preferences compete and are hidden. A three-judge panel compares transcripts pairwise, and ratings are fitted as Elo scores.
note: Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview plays the persona. Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview judge. It went live on eqbench.com on 2026-07-23 and moved EQ-Bench 3 to the legacy boards.

name: EQ-Bench v2
description: Models read 171 short dialogues and rate how strongly a character feels each of four emotions on a 0 to 10 scale. The score compares the ratings with reference answers.
note: Version 1 from December 2023 had 60 questions, and the maker says v1 and v2 scores are not comparable. Now a legacy leaderboard.

name: Era by Eon
description: Generates a simulated enterprise (Salesforce, Slack, Jira, Zendesk, etc.) with exact ground truth. Agents answer questions through MCP/REST.
note: Free. The same seed reproduces the same company, so runs are repeatable. Simulators ship as container images.

name: ERQA
description: 400 multiple-choice visual questions from robot and egocentric footage on spatial, trajectory, action and state reasoning. Accuracy.
note: Not saturated: best 78.5 (Gemini Robotics ER 2, DeepMind chart), chance ~25%. Source tables (DeepMind, Unitree, Embodied Arena) use different setups. Do not pool.

name: ESI-Bench
description: Embodied agents act to reveal what is unseen, such as occluded structure, containment and function, then reason about how observations change with action.
note: 141 GitHub stars at 2026-11-01.

name: ETHICS
aliases: Aligning AI With Shared Human Values
description: Models predict common moral judgments about text scenarios covering justice, well-being, duties, virtues and commonsense morality.
note: ICLR 2021. Has normal and hard test splits.

name: EurekaBench
description: Agents run long experiments and propose mechanisms that explain observations in six sciences. Mechanisms are scored on known constraints, predictive accuracy and the 306 expert-listed insights they should support.
note: 26 expert-verified tasks across neuroscience, computer science, chemistry, astrophysics, geophysics and plasma physics. Grading of insights is assumed model-judged and should be checked. Repo has 35 stars.

name: EVA-Bench
description: Voice agents hold simulated spoken conversations to complete enterprise tasks. Scores cover task success and voice-specific failure modes.
note: 77 upvotes on Hugging Face papers and 234 GitHub stars.

name: EvalCrafter
description: Text-to-video models generate clips for 700 prompts drawn from real user requests. The clips are scored with 17 automatic metrics for visual quality, content quality, motion and text alignment. Weights fitted to human ratings combine the metrics into one score.
org: Tencent AI Lab and City University of Hong Kong
note: CVPR 2024. Many of the 17 metrics rely on vision models, and the human-alignment weights come from the makers' own user study. About 200 GitHub stars.

name: EvalDetectBench
description: A judge model reads a transcript and answers whether it came from an evaluation or from real deployment. The test measures how well models detect evaluations and how detectable each benchmark is.
org: UK AI Security Institute + LASR Labs
note: Works with any Inspect-compatible eval. Transcripts cover frontier system-card evals and varied deployment sources. Probe questions are calibrated per model, and a harmonization step corrects for which model generated the transcripts.

name: EvalPlus
description: HumanEval+/MBPP+ with 80x more tests. Showed many 'passing' solutions were wrong.
note: EvalPlus is the umbrella for HumanEval+ and MBPP+, which have their own records. MBPP+ v0.2.0 (April 2024) dropped broken tasks from 399 to 378, raising pass@1 by about 4 points.

name: Evaluation awareness discriminability (Anthropic)
aliases: Discriminability of behavioral audits from baseline using measurements of evaluation awareness
description: Probes and follow-up realism ratings try to tell behavioral audit transcripts from real internal Claude Code sessions. Each setting is scored as AUROC.
note: In-house Anthropic measurement. Lower AUROC means audits look more like real use. Results are split by audit type with no overall.

name: EVMbench
description: Agents detect, patch and exploit 117 high-severity smart contract bugs from 40 audits in a sandboxed blockchain. Detect mode is scored on recall, patch and exploit modes by tests.
note: Since 2026-04-08 the maintained home is github.com/paradigmxyz/evmbench. Some scenarios come from audits of the Tempo blockchain.

name: EvoArena
description: Agents work in environments whose knowledge, tools and task conditions change over time. The suite tests whether agent memory keeps up with the changes.
note: 145 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: EvoArena PersonaMem-Evo
description: Agents solve questions about changing user preferences. The score is the published accuracy across versioned tasks.
note: One track of EvoArena. The EvoArena record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: EvoArena SWE-Chain-Evo
description: Agents solve software tasks that change across versions. The score is the published accuracy across versioned tasks.
note: One track of EvoArena. The EvoArena record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: EvoArena Terminal-Bench-Evo
description: Agents solve terminal tasks that change across versions. The score is the published accuracy across versioned tasks.
note: One track of EvoArena. The EvoArena record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: EvoCode-Bench
description: Coding agents keep one project working across 26 tasks of 5 to 15 rounds each, while requirements change, pile up and conflict. Cumulative hidden tests check every round in a persistent container.
org: UniPat AI with Peking University, Tsinghua University and HKU
note: The paper reports MT@4 and single-round success on a legacy runner. The first board (2026-06-13 to 06-16) let agents read the grader on 12 tasks. UniPat withdrew those results.

name: EvoCode-Bench v2
description: Coding agents work through 26 multi-round tasks with 227 graded rounds on the official Harbor multi-step format. The score is the mean of binary per-round rewards. A case score gives partial credit.
org: UniPat AI with Peking University, Tsinghua University and HKU
note: The 2026-06-20 re-release fixed a Harbor grader leak, one contaminated task and 11 task defects. UniPat says older numbers are outdated. The board has 13 models.

name: EvoPolicyGym
description: Agents repeatedly edit an executable policy for compact interactive RL environments under a fixed interaction budget. The score tracks how much the policy improves.
note: 48 HF paper upvotes and about 150 GitHub stars.

name: EWMBench
description: Embodied world models generate robot manipulation videos from language. Scored on scene consistency, motion correctness, semantic alignment.

name: EXAMS
description: Models answer high school exam questions in 16 languages across many subjects. Arabic reports use the Arabic subset.
org: Sofia University and collaborators (Hardalov et al.)
note: EMNLP 2020. OALL v1 and v2 and TII Falcon posts report the Arabic subset as Exams. Qwen's Multilingual Exams is a different test.

name: Excel Modeling Benchmark
description: Agents build investment banking and private equity financial models in Excel from a written brief and source files. Rubrics give partial credit for tabs, structure, formulas and formatting.
note: 103 expert questions split into 1 public task, 51 licensable validation and 51 private test tasks. Each runs in Template and Scratch modes. The v1.0 page is archived.

name: Excel Modeling Benchmark v1.1
description: Agents build the same 103 Excel financial modeling tasks as EMB v1.0, with the Scratch rubric judge changed to GPT-6 Luna.
note: Vals says v1.1 scores are not directly comparable with v1.0. Part of Vals Index v2.2 from 2026-10-19. The board had 37 models on 2026-10-29.

name: ExeWorldBench
description: Coding agents build executable code-based 3D worlds that capture how a world works, testing world understanding and its realization in code.
org: University of Science and Technology of China
note: 77 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: EXP-Bench
description: Agents get a research question and incomplete starter code from an influential AI paper. They must form hypotheses, design and run experiments, and analyze results.
note: 24 HF paper upvotes. The code lives in the Curie repo (about 370 stars).

name: Expert comparisons on biothreat information
description: PhD biology experts compare model answers to expert answers on long-form biorisk questions. Scored as win rate on accuracy, understanding and ease of execution.
note: OpenAI Preparedness evaluation. Results are reported per dimension for pre-mitigation models.

name: Expert Red Teaming for Violent Attack Planning
aliases: Attack planning red teaming win rate
description: Expert red teamers compare anonymized responses from two models on violent attack planning prompts. Scored as the win rate for being safer.
note: In-house OpenAI red teaming campaign. The comparison model changes by card.

name: Expert vulnerability discovery and exploit development evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Agents locate advanced vulnerabilities in possibly obfuscated codebases and write working exploits across six challenge classes. Scored by success rates.
note: In-house Anthropic RSP cyber evaluation from the Claude 3 model card. Per-task results were not published.

name: Expert-SWE (OpenAI)
description: Agents do long-horizon coding tasks with a median estimated human completion time of 20 hours.
note: OpenAI calls it an internal frontier eval. The GPT-5.5 post (2026-04-23) reports 73.1% for GPT-5.5 and 68.5% for GPT-5.4.

name: ExploitBench
description: 41 recent V8 JavaScript-engine N-day vulnerabilities. Progress measured by 16 grader-verified capability flags across five tiers.
note: 41 real V8 N-day vulnerabilities with production mitigations on. 16 binary capability flags over five tiers: coverage, bug triggering, V8 internal primitives, general primitives and arbitrary code execution. Flags are checked by oracles compiled into a patched d8 binary. Episodes cap at 300 turns. Saturated by GPT-6 Astra at 100%, and OpenAI built a post-cutoff internal port to check contamination.

name: ExploitBench - Internal Port
description: Agents develop working exploits for recently disclosed vulnerabilities to limit contamination. Scored as arbitrary code execution success rate.
note: OpenAI internal port of ExploitBench with June to August 2026 vulnerabilities.

name: ExploitGym
description: 869 real-vulnerability exploit-development tasks (userspace, V8, Linux kernel). Success means capturing a flag through the intended vulnerability.
note: 869 instances in three domains: 502 userspace, 181 browser (V8) and 186 Linux kernel. Agents turn a proof-of-vulnerability input into a working exploit that runs code. Part of the UC Berkeley RDI Frontier AI Cybersecurity Observatory.

name: ExplorationBench
description: Agents explore verifiable alien worlds with hidden laws, framing hypotheses and running experiments. The worlds are built so that recalled pretraining knowledge does not help.
note: 30 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: Extended NYT Connections
description: Models solve New York Times Connections puzzles with up to four extra trick words added. Each puzzle scores by the square of the share of groups found.
note: The puzzle set grows over time, now 940 puzzles. Trend charts use a shared 601-puzzle set so older runs stay comparable.

name: External pilot use failure modes (Anthropic)
aliases: Failure Mode Prevalence by Source Model
description: Models are judged on user-flagged pilot conversations, directly or by resampling. Graders measure failure modes such as hallucinated facts and misrepresented work completion.
note: In-house Anthropic analysis of external pilot and comparative testing data. The conversations are not public.

name: External red team jailbreaks
aliases: Redteam Refusal Performance on Generated Jailbreaks
description: External red teamers and automated gap finding generate jailbreaks against the model. Scored on how often the model resists.
note: Results from external red teaming, not a fixed benchmark.

name: ExtractBench
description: Systems read a full business document and return a schema-valid JSON object with every requested value. Unified value F1 compares the output with the expected values.
note: 370 documents, 4,869 pages, 8 business domains and 67 document types. A later dataset revision added grounding boxes with documents and schemas unchanged. LlamaIndex says its own tiers now score above 93%.

name: ExtractBench Pro
description: Systems extract every schema value from long-tail synthetic documents with charts, drawn relations, house rules and jargon. Scored by value F1 and by grounded F1, which also needs the source location.
note: 100 documents, 2,622 pages and 86 document types, with 144,141 expected values fixed before rendering. A harder companion to ExtractBench, not a new version of it.

name: EyePACS (diabetic retinopathy grading)
description: Models grade diabetic retinopathy in a fundus photo on a 5-level scale, posed as a 5-option question. Google's test set has 3,614 images, one per patient.
note: Google uses a de-identified EyePACS subset that is not public. Older public EyePACS sets, such as the 2015 Kaggle set, are not the same test.

name: Factorio Learning Environment
description: Agents write Python programs that control a Factorio factory, in lab tasks with fixed resources and in open play. Scored by production throughput, milestones and lab task success.
note: Versioned releases from 0.2 (May 2025) to 0.4 (March 2026, moved to Factorio 2.0 and added Inspect support). Scores may shift across versions. The board lists 6 models.

name: FACTS Benchmark Suite
description: Models are scored on four factuality tests: Parametric, Search, Multimodal and Grounding v2. The FACTS Score averages accuracy over public and private sets of all four.
note: Launched 2025-12-09 with 15 models. Kaggle holds the private sets. The Search part became FACTS Search V2 in mid 2026, so later suite averages may not compare.

name: FACTS Grounding
description: Long-form responses must be fully grounded in a provided document. Judged by LLM panels for grounding and eligibility.
note: Public split of 3,513 examples plus a private evaluation set.

name: FACTS Grounding v2
description: Models write long answers from a supplied document of up to 32k tokens. Judge models check that each answer stays faithful to the document.
note: The FACTS paper says v2 uses much improved judge models, so scores do not compare with the January 2025 FACTS Grounding. It is the Grounding part of the FACTS Benchmark Suite. Kaggle published a third board version on 2026-10-23 with 15 models, with no changelog.

name: FACTS Multimodal
description: Models answer questions about input images and must combine what they see with world knowledge. A judge checks coverage and contradictions.
note: 711 public and 811 private prompts. Part of the FACTS Benchmark Suite. Scores were the lowest of the four parts at launch.

name: FACTS Parametric
description: Models answer closed-book factoid questions from their own knowledge, without tools. A judge model grades each answer.
note: 1,052 public and 1,052 private questions. Part of the FACTS Benchmark Suite.

name: FACTS Parametric V2
description: Models answer closed-book factoid questions from their own knowledge, without tools. A judge model grades each answer.
note: Kaggle renamed the benchmark to Facts V2 Parametric and published version 2 on 2026-10-27 with 20 models. No changelog was found, so what changed is unknown. This follows the FACTS Search V2 pattern.

name: FACTS Search
description: Models answer information-seeking questions with a web search tool (the Brave Search API) and must combine what they find correctly.
note: 890 public and 994 private questions. Part of the FACTS Benchmark Suite. Kaggle later replaced this board with FACTS Search V2.

name: FACTS Search V2
description: Models answer information-seeking questions with a search tool and must combine what they find correctly. Second version of FACTS Search on Kaggle.
note: Kaggle published version 2 of the board on 2026-07-27 and renamed it FACTS Search V2. It listed 23 models on 2026-11-01. No changelog was found.

name: FActScore
description: Models write biographies of people, and each output is split into atomic facts checked against a knowledge source. Labs report the hallucination rate, the share of facts it does not support.
org: Sewon Min et al. (University of Washington and collaborators)
note: OpenAI and xAI report this rate on FActScore prompts. The paper's own score, the share of supported facts, is the FActScore precision record.

name: FActScore precision
description: Models write biographies of people, and each output is split into atomic facts. The score is the share of facts that a knowledge source supports, as the paper defines FActScore.
org: Sewon Min et al. (University of Washington and collaborators)
note: Labs that report a hallucination rate on FActScore prompts, where lower is better, are on the FActScore record.

name: Factuality Heavy prompts
description: Models answer prompts representative of factuality-heavy ChatGPT conversations. A grader with web access counts responses and claims with factual errors.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Error rates are not production prevalence.

name: FailSafeQA
description: Models answer finance questions over long documents while the query or the document is degraded, irrelevant or missing. An LLM judge scores robustness, context grounding and compliance.
note: The paper scores 24 models. 132 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: FailureSensorIQ
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions on how industrial sensors relate to failure modes of assets. The Kaggle board shows it under IBM's AssetOpsBench citation.
note: 25 models on the Kaggle board published 2025-12-01.

name: Faithfulness (Moonshot)
description: A fact checker verifies each model response for factual hallucinations. The score is one minus the hallucination rate.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: FaithJudge
description: Models answer retrieval-augmented tasks from given passages. An LLM judge guided by human-annotated examples flags unfaithful answers, giving a hallucination rate.
org: University of Waterloo and Vectara (Tamber et al.)
note: The board reports the hallucination rate. Kimi K2 reported one minus the rate (92.6), stored here as the rate it also prints (7.4).

name: False-premise questions (Anthropic)
description: Models answer questions built on false premises. Measures how often they accept the premise instead of correcting it.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: FalseClaimBench
description: Agents report on coding work they did. Claims are checked against the final workspace, and the score is the share fully true.
note: In-house xAI evaluation reported in the Grok 4.5 card.

name: FATE-H
description: Provers write Lean proofs for 100 abstract and commutative algebra problems at honors course or graduate exam level. The Lean compiler checks each proof.
note: Part of the FATE (Formal Algebra Theorem Evaluation) series with FATE-X. Seed-Prover 1.5 reports 80%.

name: FATE-X
description: Provers write Lean proofs for 100 algebra problems at or beyond PhD qualifying exam level, some beyond what Mathlib covers. The Lean compiler checks each proof.
note: Part of the FATE (Formal Algebra Theorem Evaluation) series with FATE-H. Seed-Prover 1.5 reports 33%.

name: FDE-Gym
description: Agents act as forward-deployed engineers in live customer systems, talking to scripted stakeholders to find unstated constraints. Score is the uplift on the customer's own success metric, from 0 to the reference solution's 1.
note: 95 tasks from 20 real delivery projects in 18 sectors, the originals plus fact-altered variants. Stakeholder messages, trial runs and waiting cost points. A task resolves at 0.8 or more with no incident.

name: FeatureBench
description: Agents implement whole features in real repositories, beyond single-PR bug fixes. Execution-based tests check each feature, and new tasks are generated automatically.
note: The existing importer reads the 30-task Lite board. Move those rows to proposed featurebench-lite before publishing new data under the full benchmark.

name: FeatureBench Lite
description: The public 30-task Lite leaderboard ranks passed-test percentages and reports fully resolved-task percentages separately.
note: The public 30-task Lite leaderboard ranks passed-test percentages and reports fully resolved-task percentages separately.

name: Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean (Anthropic)
description: Agent teams formalize Fermat's Last Theorem in Lean. Scores measure the weighted proportion of 60 accepted intermediate theorems.
note: Teams run for 18 hours without internet access. This theorem differs from the earlier large agent team task.

name: FEVER
description: Systems check 185,445 claims against Wikipedia and label each Supported, Refuted or NotEnoughInfo. Annotators wrote the claims by altering Wikipedia sentences. The full FEVER score also requires the right evidence sentences.
org: University of Sheffield and Amazon (Thorne, Vlachos, Christodoulopoulos, Mittal)
note: Published at NAACL 2018. The FEVER workshop has run later shared tasks, such as FEVER 2.0, FEVEROUS and AVeriTeC, which are separate datasets. KILT and many retrieval papers reuse the claims.

name: Fiction.LiveBench
aliases: Fiction.LiveBench for Long Context Deep Comprehension
description: Models answer 36 questions about 30 Fiction.live stories that need inference about plot and characters. Each story is tested at several context lengths.

name: Filtered, adversarial sample of production prompts
description: Models answer filtered borderline and high-risk biology prompts that resemble production traffic. Scored as not_unsafe rate from model training alone.
note: In-house OpenAI safeguard test set first shared in the ChatGPT agent system card.

name: Finance Bench (Moonshot)
description: Agents complete realistic financial workflows end to end, from source materials to deliverables that reviewers can check.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. It is not the public FinanceBench. The tasks are not public.

name: Finance Modeling
description: Agents complete expert-written financial modeling problems with Excel tools, from research to analysis. Expert-designed rubrics score each problem, averaged over three runs.
note: This is an in-house evaluation, and MiniMax has not released the problems.

name: Finance Modeling Pro
description: Agents complete financial modeling tasks in Excel. Expert rubrics score each task over three trials.
note: In-house MiniMax evaluation. Scores differ from the earlier Finance Modeling set reported for M2.5.

name: Finance Reasoning (Snorkel)
description: Agents answer expert-written financial reasoning questions grounded in 10-K tables loaded into a database, using SQL tools over many steps. A judge scores correctness and completeness.
note: Archived. Built as a harder follow-up to SnorkelFinance. Claude Sonnet 3.7 judges with the reference answer. 15 minutes and 100 turns per trace.

name: FinanceBench
description: Models answer open-book questions about public companies using their filings, such as 10-Ks and earnings reports. The full set has 10,231 questions with answers and evidence strings, and 150 of them are public. The makers graded answers by hand, and later users often grade with a model judge.
org: Patronus AI, Contextual AI and Stanford University
note: Results depend on the retrieval setup, such as a vector store, long context or the gold evidence page. Not the Moonshot Finance Bench, which is cataloged separately. About 390 GitHub stars.

name: FinanceReasoning
description: Models solve financial numerical reasoning problems that need one or more finance formulas. Answers are numbers checked against reference Python solutions.
org: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications
note: The paper was accepted to ACL 2025 and includes 238 Hard problems. Ant Group reports it in the Ring-1T technical report.

name: FinBen
description: A finance suite of 35 datasets across 23 tasks, in three difficulty levels. Tasks include sentiment analysis, information extraction, numerical question answering, text generation, forecasting and stock trading.
org: The Fin AI (Qianqian Xie and coauthors)
note: The linked Open-FinLLM Space now publishes MultiFinBen, a distinct multilingual and multimodal evaluation.

name: Finch (FinWorkBench)
description: Agent completes 172 enterprise finance and accounting spreadsheet workflows (384 tasks) from real data. Human plus calibrated LLM-judge grading.
note: ACL 2026 Findings.

name: FinEval
description: Models answer 8,351 Chinese finance questions in four areas: academic knowledge in 34 subjects, industry practice, financial security and financial agent tasks. Most questions are multiple choice, and the agent part tests tool use and multi-step reasoning. The makers run zero-shot and five-shot chain-of-thought settings.
org: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics (AIFLM Lab)
note: The task set grew after the first release and now also has multimodal and rigor sections. Test answers are not public, so test scores come from submissions to the makers' leaderboard. About 290 GitHub stars.

name: FinEval 6.0
description: Models solve financial evaluation tasks. The score is the official 6.0 total score.
org: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics (AIFLM Lab)
note: Distinct result table with different tasks and scoring from the earlier text aggregate.

name: FinQA
description: Models answer numerical questions about company earnings reports that mix tables and text. Financial experts wrote 8,281 question and answer pairs, each with a gold reasoning program. Answers are checked by execution accuracy and program accuracy.
org: UC Santa Barbara and J.P. Morgan AI Research
note: EMNLP 2021. Alibaba's DianJin-R1 report evaluates on FinQA and trains on it. Snorkel's FinQA RL environment, cataloged separately, is built on this data. About 410 GitHub stars.

name: FinQA (Snorkel OpenEnv environment)
description: Agent answers 290 multi-step questions on SEC 10-K data via MCP tools and constrained SQL. Binary reward with 1% numeric tolerance.
note: Not the 2021 FinQA dataset. Design choices: SQL tool rejects SELECT * and requires filters. No LLM judge. 50-tool-call cap. An RL-trained Qwen3-4B (59.7%) beat Qwen3-235B (51.4%), which Snorkel reads as tool discipline over scale. Also hosted as HF Space snorkelai/finqa-env.

name: FinSearchComp
description: Agents search the web to fetch live financial data, look up history, and run multi-step investigations, across 635 expert-written questions. Scored by answer accuracy.
note: Cards report different subsets, such as T2 and T3 or the global split.

name: FinSearchComp Global
description: Agents search for financial information about global assets across three task types. The score is the published average accuracy for the Global subset.
note: One track of FinSearchComp. The FinSearchComp record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: FinSearchComp Greater China
description: Agents search for financial information about Greater China assets across three task types. The score is the published average accuracy for the Greater China subset.
note: One track of FinSearchComp. The FinSearchComp record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: FinStepBench
description: Models do three kinds of finance work: retrieving and checking live financial facts, building company valuations, and writing full research reports. Graders check accuracy, sourcing and reproducible calculations.
note: StepFun built the three suites in house. The post does not name the grader, so the scoring type is a guess.

name: FinStepBench CorporateValuation
description: Models value companies using financial evidence and calculations. The score is the published CorporateValuation percentage.
note: One track of FinStepBench. The FinStepBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: FinStepBench DeepResearch
description: Models write finance research reports. The score is the published DeepResearch percentage.
note: One track of FinStepBench. The FinStepBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: FinStepBench LiveSearch
description: Models retrieve and verify live financial facts. The score is the published LiveSearch percentage.
note: One track of FinStepBench. The FinStepBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Firefox 147 exploit evaluation (Anthropic)
description: Internal eval on crashes previously found in Firefox 147, run without the browser's process sandbox. Measures exploit-development progress.

name: Fireworks Specialized Intelligence Index
description: An index that gathers 66 practitioner-built benchmarks in 14 domains, such as legal, finance, healthcare and software. It combines score, cost and duration per benchmark into one number.
note: Launched 2026-09-22 with Rogo BigFinanceBench as the first partner. Fireworks runs partner tasks in Harbor format. The benchmark index formula is 100 times score^0.706 times cost^0.176 times duration^0.118.

name: First Proof
description: AI systems attempt ten unpublished research problems that arose in the authors' own work. Mathematicians judge whether each proof is correct.
org: First Proof (Abouzaid, Blumberg, Hairer, Spielman, Williams and others)
note: An informal round run by the labs themselves. Problems came out on February 5, 2026 and solutions on February 13. Google DeepMind reported its Aletheia agent solved six problems.

name: First Proof Second Batch
description: The editors run AI harnesses once each, with 24 hours, on ten unpublished research problems with human proofs of up to eight pages. Referees grade each answer blind.
note: The first formal benchmark round, with four systems tested and results on June 10, 2026. Grades run from essentially flawless to rejected.

name: First Proof Third Batch
description: The editors run five AI systems once each on ten unpublished research problems with proofs of up to 12 pages. About 30 referees score correctness, exposition and attribution. The score is average correctness, from negative 1 to 1.
note: Results came out on October 14, 2026. The best harness solved 9 of 10 problems and GPT-6 Astra alone solved 7. A fourth batch is planned for January 2027.

name: First-Person Fairness evaluation
description: Tests whether a user's name (a demographic proxy) changes responses, using an LLM research assistant to detect harmful stereotypes.
note: Paper is public. The evaluation set is internal to OpenAI.

name: Flame-React-Eval
description: Models write React components from UI design images. Rendered outputs are compared with gold components by image similarity and scored as pass@k.
note: The dataset is named Flame-Eval-React on Hugging Face and Flame-React-Eval in the repo. It has fewer than 1,000 items.

name: FlashDexRetarget 50-motion benchmark
description: Retarget 50 human hand-object motions (HOT3D, TACO, OakInk2) to XHand and Sharpa hands in Isaac Sim. Scored by object pose-error success thresholds.
note: Method paper with its own test set. Reports compute and success together: 0.90 success with 29 GPU-hours versus CHORD's 0.46 with 2,847. Failed baseline runs count toward compute.

name: FlashInfer-Bench
description: Agents generate GPU kernels for LLM inference that are benchmarked on workloads from real serving traces and can be deployed into the FlashInfer stack.
note: Repo opened in June 2025 and the paper followed in January 2026. 301 GitHub stars.

name: FlenQA
description: Models answer reasoning questions whose key facts are padded with filler text to different lengths. Accuracy shows how input length affects reasoning.
org: Mosh Levy, Alon Jacoby, Yoav Goldberg
note: Phi model cards report only a 3K-token subset, so scores depend on the padding length used.

name: FLEURS
description: Models transcribe read speech in 102 languages built from FLoRes-101 sentences. Model cards usually report word error rate, so lower scores are better.
note: FLEURS also supports speech translation, retrieval, and language identification, so check which task a score uses.

name: Floorplan Arena
description: Models furnish hand-drawn room sketches. People compare the layouts and vote for the better floorplan.
note: The official API publishes Arena ratings, confidence intervals and vote counts.

name: Flores
description: Models translate 3,001 English Wikipedia sentences that professionals translated into 101 languages. Scored with BLEU or chrF against references.
note: FLORES-200 extended it to 200 languages in 2022, and the Open Language Data Initiative now maintains it.

name: FLORES+
description: Models translate English Wikipedia sentences that professionals and community contributors translated into over 200 languages. Outputs are scored with metrics such as chrF against the references.
note: OLDI calls it an extended and improved version of FLORES-200 and keeps adding languages and fixes. The Hugging Face dataset is gated under CC BY-SA 4.0 and had 237 configs on 2026-11-01.

name: FLORES-200
description: Models translate English Wikipedia sentences into about 200 languages. Outputs are scored with BLEU or chrF against human reference translations.
note: Extends FLORES-101 to about 200 languages. The flores record covers FLORES-101.

name: FLTEval
description: Agents complete the formal Lean proofs and define the new mathematical concepts in real pull requests to the Fermat's Last Theorem (FLT) formalization project. Lean and SafeVerify check each submitted diff.
note: Mistral introduced it with Leanstral in 2026-03 and open-sourced the harness with Leanstral 1.5 in 2026-07. The harness is shaped like SWE-bench and the repo ships a 162-instance sample.

name: FocusBench (Meta)
description: Agents do personal tasks in domains such as housing, travel, IT and finance. The test checks whether they keep working through real-world blockers across several interactions as the environment changes.
note: Meta in-house eval behind the Active Focus feature, reported in the Muse Wonder model card. The card does not say how tasks are graded, so the scoring type is a guess. Part of Meta's PSI composite.

name: FollowBench
description: Models answer 820 English and Chinese instructions where each level adds one more constraint of content, situation, style, format or example type. Rules and an LLM judge check each constraint.
org: HKUST and Huawei Noah's Ark Lab (Jiang et al.)
note: Reports Hard Satisfaction Rate (all constraints met) and Soft Satisfaction Rate. ACL 2024. About 120 GitHub stars.

name: FoodTruck Bench
description: Agents run a food truck in Austin, Texas for a 30-day simulation, choosing locations, menus, prices, inventory, staff and loans with 34 tools. Humans can play the same game.
note: 60 models tested on six locations. Scored by business results at the end of the run.

name: ForecastBench
description: Models give probabilities for 500 auto-generated questions per round about future events, drawn from prediction markets and time-series datasets. Forecasts are scored with difficulty-adjusted Brier scores once the questions resolve.
note: Since March 2026 the leaderboards show a Brier Index from 0 to 100 percent, where higher is better. The tournament track allows tools and the baseline track does not. Questions resolve after model training cutoffs, so the set resists contamination.

name: Forensics CTF challenges (Anthropic)
description: Agents analyze logs, files or obfuscated records to reconstruct events in capture-the-flag challenges.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: FormalMATH
description: Provers write Lean 4 proofs for 5,560 formal statements from high-school olympiad problems to undergraduate theorems. The Lean checker scores each proof.
org: SphereLab, M-A-P, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Numina and others
note: FormalMATH-Lite is a 425-problem subset for test-time scaling runs. Its scores are not comparable with the full set.

name: FormalMATH Lite
description: Models prove statements in the FormalMATH Lite subset. The board reports proof success at the stated sampling budget.
org: SphereLab, M-A-P, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Numina and others
note: The official source reports this result separately. It is not the parent benchmark aggregate.

name: FORTE
description: Agents complete 180 office tasks across 15 corporate professions inside a workspace of xlsx, docx, pptx, pdf and other files. An LLM judge checks the output files against expert rubrics, and a task passes only if every rubric item passes.
note: The repository ships one demo task per profession. The full 180 tasks are run by the maker. Metrics are Avg@3, Pass@3 and Pass^3 with the OpenClaw harness.

name: FORTRESS
aliases: Frontier Risk Evaluation for National Security and Public Safety
description: Paired adversarial and benign national-security misuse prompts. Rubric-graded risk score on adversarial and over-refusal score on benign prompts.
note: 500 of 1,010 prompts public. The rest held out against contamination. Lower is better: the Average Risk Score on Scale's board and in Meta's reports. Thinking Machines reports a different adversarial figure where higher is better (Inkling 78.0 and Inkling Small 71.6), so those numbers do not compare with the rest.

name: FORTRESS-RN
description: Models face the radiological and nuclear prompts of Scale AI's FORTRESS. xAI reports refusal accuracy on these items.
note: A subset of FORTRESS. Scale AI ran it for xAI.

name: FRAMES
aliases: FRAMES (Factuality, Retrieval, And reasoning MEasurement Set)
description: Models answer 824 multi-hop questions that need facts from 2 to 15 Wikipedia articles. Answers are graded against gold answers for accuracy.

name: FreshQA
description: Models answer questions whose answers change over time, never change, or rest on a false premise that they should reject. FreshEval, an LLM judge, grades answers in a Relaxed mode or a Strict mode that also penalizes any hallucinated detail.
org: Google and UMass Amherst (Tu Vu and coauthors)
note: The authors update the answer sheet often, with dated versions through 2026-04, so scores depend on the version used. The README says FreshQA informed Gemini and Perplexity's online models. About 400 GitHub stars. SealQA builds on it, and the almanac has its Seal-0 subset.

name: FrogsGame post-training task
description: Agent has 20 hours to post-train Qwen3-8B to solve FrogsGame puzzle boards. A hidden verifier scores the best checkpoint on unseen boards.
note: Verifier is hidden and only the best submitted checkpoint counts.

name: Frontier3DBench
description: Agents create editable Blender objects and scenes or executable Unreal Engine worlds across 145 tasks and nine task families. Model judgments and native project checks assess appearance, geometry, requirements, and interactions. The overall score weights object, scene, and world scores by 30%, 30%, and 40%.
note: Agents run through the harness named for each model at the published reasoning effort. GPT-6 Astra judges visual evidence with model identity hidden. Task assets retain individual licenses. The site publishes cost comparisons only as a raster chart and in its paper.

name: FrontierBioML
description: 25 machine learning tasks in computational biology, across antibody development, protein engineering, structural biology, binder design and functional genomics. An agent gets real experimental data and a brief, works offline for up to six hours and submits a prediction script. A sealed grader runs the script on held-out data, such as new antibody families or new protein targets, and scores each task from 0 at a simple baseline to 100 for a perfect answer.
note: Each model runs in a coding harness such as Claude Code, Codex CLI or OpenCode, three times per task. Runs that fail a check or that a provider's safety filter blocks count as 0. OpenAI's biosafety filter blocked 36 of 150 GPT runs because Valen is not in OpenAI's trusted access program. Both Claude models ran under Anthropic's Life Science Verification Program. Scores are not comparable across tasks. The tasks use public datasets, and Valen reports that one model named a dataset's source from memory. Four tasks are public on Harbor and the Prime Intellect Environments Hub. The other 21 are available on request.

name: FrontierCAD
description: Agents build 39 machined parts from engineering drawings and place parts into 16 assemblies, in their own coding harnesses. A verifier that tolerates rotation and checks hole positions scores the geometry.
note: A part passes at a score of 0.97, and no model passed any part in the first report. It scores geometry only, while CAD Arena also scores editability. Seven models in the first report.

name: FrontierCAD Assemblies
description: Agents place supplied CAD parts into 16 assemblies. The score is the published mean assembly geometry score.
note: One track of FrontierCAD. The FrontierCAD record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: FrontierCAD Parts
description: Agents build 39 CAD parts from engineering drawings. The score is the published mean geometry score.
note: One track of FrontierCAD. The FrontierCAD record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: FrontierChallenge
description: Agents complete end-to-end scientific workflows in chemistry, materials, molecular dynamics and life science from fixed inputs, producing a set of required deliverables. Task-specific graders check each deliverable.
note: 97 of 300 workflows are released. The best configurations completed 20 of the 97 tasks, a 20.6 percent Pass Rate. 154 HF paper upvotes.

name: FrontierCode
description: Real-repo coding tasks graded for mergeability: correctness, regressions, lint, tests, scope and code quality. Failing any blocker scores zero.
note: Tasks written by 20+ open-source maintainers, 40+ hours each. Only sample tasks are public.

name: FrontierCode 1.1
description: Real-repo coding tasks graded for mergeability: correctness, regressions, lint, tests, scope and code quality. Failing any blocker scores zero.
note: Re-graded the 1.0 tasks: runs flagged for unfair internet use score zero, and over-strict checks were relaxed.

name: FrontierCode 2.0
description: Agents resolve 132 maintainer-built tasks from deliberately ambiguous prompts. Rubric checks ask whether a maintainer would merge the change.
note: Draws on 55% more repositories than 1.1 and has 501 blocking checks for thoroughness, against 168 in 1.1.

name: FrontierCS
description: Models write programs for 156 open-ended computer science problems whose optimum is unknown. An automatic evaluator gives partial scores against an expert reference solution.
note: Problems split into algorithmic tasks, often NP-hard variants of contest problems, and research tasks. UK AISI packages it in inspect_evals.

name: FrontierCS 1.1
description: Agents solve 179 algorithmic tasks under revised scoring that rewards solutions beyond the reference. The score is the official average task score.
note: Version 1.1 changes the task set and scoring. It is separate from 1.0 and the research-focused FrontierCS 2.

name: FrontierCS 2
description: Agents work inside the released repository of a recent systems or programming-languages paper and try to beat that paper's method. A hidden held-out suite grades the final patch against the human reference.
note: 48 of a planned 150 tasks released across 13 domains. The maker says FrontierCS 2 asks a different question from FrontierCS 1.0, so scores are not comparable.

name: FrontierCyber
description: Agents look for and exploit zero-day vulnerabilities in current off-the-shelf software and hardware at four difficulty levels. Scored as challenges solved.
note: Irregular published the v1.0 design on 22 June 2026. Two subsets run today, mobile devices and software exploitation, with named targets including Pillow, lxml, FFmpeg, ImageMagick, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Redis, phones and routers. Each challenge gets a predicted difficulty band, Easy to Elite, before any run. A hidden flag proves success and planted markers give partial credit. Each evaluation ties to a timestamped snapshot, so scores compare only within one snapshot. Not public.

name: FrontierFinance
description: Agents answer 220 investment research queries from finance experts across six use cases of the investor workflow. Three judge models check each answer against 11,543 source-attributed rubrics.
note: The score is the rubric qualification rate, macro-averaged over queries. Results are reported per harness: web search only, the open Finance Agent v2 harness, and Samaya in-house harness.

name: FrontierMath
description: Unpublished research-level math problems with automatically verifiable answers. Tier 4 is the hardest tier.
note: Problems held privately by Epoch AI.

name: FrontierMath Erdős
description: Models try to prove or disprove 68 open Erdős problems in Lean 4. A result counts only if the Lean checker accepts the full proof.
note: By late October 2026, 17 of the 68 conjectures had been resolved by Epoch's runs or by others.

name: FrontierMath Tier 4
description: Models solve research-level math problems that take experts days, submitting answers through a Python function. Each answer is verified automatically as correct or incorrect.
note: OpenAI funded FrontierMath and can access part of it, and a June 2026 v2 corrected 12 Tier 4 problems and removed 7.

name: FrontierMath Tier 4 v2
description: Models solve 43 unpublished research-level math problems and submit answers that code checks automatically. Scored by share correct.
note: Version 2 corrected 12 problems and removed 7 from the original Tier 4 set.

name: FrontierMath Tiers 1-3 v2
description: Models solve 295 unpublished math problems from undergraduate to advanced graduate level and submit answers that code checks automatically. Scored by share correct.
note: Version 2 fixed errors in 42 percent of problems, and Epoch says the tiers are nearing saturation.

name: FrontierMath: Open Problems
description: Models attack unsolved research math problems proposed by working mathematicians. Each problem has a program that checks a proposed solution. Epoch tracks which problems AI has solved.
note: Pilot launched in January 2026. Expanded to 50 problems in July 2026. Epoch says it gives no comparable model score, only counts of problems solved by AI.

name: FrontierMemory
description: A model reads 750 past agent trajectories and writes memory for a task agent. The score is how many new coding and knowledge-work tasks that agent then solves.
note: 15 tasks adapted from DeepSWE, BigCodeBench, AutomationBench, APEX-Agents, EnterpriseOps-Gym and SkillsBench. 10 models in the Fireworks index. No maker page found.

name: FrontierPhysics
description: Agents do end-to-end physics research on 56 tasks that 42 physicists from 26 institutions built from their own work, across nine domains of theoretical, computational and experimental physics. Each task asks the agent to review the literature, plan, run the research and write a manuscript. Deterministic verifiers and expert rubrics grade whether the research is correct and publishable, over 3 trials.
org: BenchFlow, with physicists from UC Berkeley, Caltech and Harvard
note: The paper (November 2026) tests 22 models in 26 configurations, and no configuration passes more than 46 of its 168 rollouts. Its authors find that agents fall short on rigorous reasoning and expert intuition more than on physics knowledge.

name: FrontierScience
description: Models solve physics, chemistry, and biology problems in an Olympiad track graded by short answer and a Research track graded by 10-point rubrics.
note: OpenAI released 160 questions (100 Olympiad, 60 Research) and holds the rest out to track contamination. Labs usually report the two tracks apart, which the frontierscience-olympiad and frontierscience-research records cover.

name: FrontierScience-Olympiad
description: Models solve olympiad-style physics, chemistry and biology problems at the level of IPhO, IChO and IBO, written by medalists and coaches. Graded on short final answers.
note: The Olympiad track of FrontierScience. The open gold set has 100 Olympiad problems. Labs report it apart from the Research track, with much higher scores.

name: FrontierScience-Research
description: Models work on open-ended PhD-level research subtasks in physics, chemistry and biology, written by working scientists. A grader scores each answer against a 10-point rubric.
note: The Research track of FrontierScience. The open gold set has 60 Research problems.

name: FrontierSWE
description: 34 ultra-long-horizon engineering and research tasks. 5 trials of up to 20 hours each. Score is mean task score 0-100.
note: This record is FrontierSWE v2 (2026-09-02), the version Epoch AI tracks. It added 21 tasks to reach 34 and runs every model in the proximus harness. v1 (April 2026, 17 tasks) has its own record.

name: FrontierSWE v1
description: Agents work up to 20 hours on 17 ultra-long engineering, performance and research tasks in their own harnesses. The board ranks models by average task rank. The score here is dominance, the win rate against a random baseline, which labs report.
note: The maker preserves the v1 board as published. FrontierSWE v2 replaced it on 2026-09-02 with 34 tasks, a new harness and mean@5 scores.

name: Full-Duplex-Bench
description: Full-duplex spoken dialogue models are scored on pause handling, backchanneling, smooth turn-taking and user interruption. Automatic metrics include takeover rate and latency.
org: Guan-Ting Lin, Hung-yi Lee and collaborators (National Taiwan University and others)
note: Scores are a set of rates and latencies, not one number. Thinking Machines reported turn-taking latency in seconds, where lower is better. The repo has about 335 GitHub stars.

name: Full-Duplex-Bench v1.5
description: Full-duplex speech models are tested on overlap scenarios: listener backchannel, side conversation and ambient speech. Metrics cover how the model yields, continues or responds.
org: Guan-Ting Lin, Hung-yi Lee and collaborators (National Taiwan University and others)
note: Uses the same offline server-client pipeline as v1.0 with new overlap data released in 2025-08.

name: Full-Duplex-Bench v2
description: An automated examiner holds real-time multi-turn audio conversations with the model over WebRTC or WebSocket. A model judge scores task completion under conversational constraints.
org: Guan-Ting Lin, Hung-yi Lee and collaborators (National Taiwan University and others)
note: The framework code was released in 2026-02. Scores are not comparable with the static v1 and v1.5 pipelines.

name: Full-Duplex-Bench v3
description: Voice agents hear real human speech with five kinds of disfluency and must make chained API calls across four task domains. Scored on Pass@1, response quality, latency and turn-taking.
org: Guan-Ting Lin, Hung-yi Lee and collaborators (National Taiwan University and others)
note: Code and data were released on 2026-05-20. The paper evaluates six systems including GPT-Realtime, Gemini Live and Grok.

name: FullStackBench
description: Models write code for 3,374 problems in 16 programming languages across domains like data analysis and web development. Unit tests score each answer.

name: Functional MATH
description: Models solve new instances of MATH problems that code generates for each snapshot. The gap from static MATH accuracy measures memorization.
note: Results depend on the snapshot, and Gemini 1.5 reported the December 2023 snapshot.

name: Furniture Assembly Benchmark
description: Model gets an IKEA manual and a photo of a partly built item, then names the faulty step or next step. Accuracy on 60 photos.
note: LLM grader checks error descriptions. Novice human baseline 63%. Photos and manuals are not distributed.

name: FutureEval (Metaculus)
description: Models forecast open Metaculus questions with a fixed prompt and are scored as the questions resolve. Seasonal bot tournaments and Pro Forecaster baselines run alongside.
note: Metaculus renamed its AI Benchmarking bot tournaments, run since 2024, to FutureEval in February 2026. The model score is based on log scores.

name: FutureOmni
description: Models watch and hear 919 videos and answer 1,034 multiple-choice questions that ask what will happen next. Questions need audio and visual cues together.
note: Built with an LLM-assisted, human-in-the-loop pipeline.

name: FutureX
description: Agents predict upcoming events collected daily from 195 websites in 11 domains, within a one-week window. Answers are scored once real results are crawled, with harder tiers weighted more.
org: ByteDance Seed with Fudan, Stanford and Princeton
note: ICLR 2026. The live set refreshes weekly and the team posts weekly reports, with 28 agents in June 2026.

name: GAIA
description: Agents answer real-world questions that need web browsing, file handling, multimodal input, and tools, at three difficulty levels. Scored by exact answer match.
org: Meta AI, Hugging Face, and AutoGPT
note: Test answers are withheld for the leaderboard. Some cards report a text-only subset.

name: Gaia2-CLI
description: Agents complete realistic tasks through command-line tools. The benchmark measures task success across search, execution, adaptability, ambiguity, and time constraints.
note: CLI task-set scores remain separate from legacy Gaia2. The official board identifies the OpenClaw harness and reasoning settings.

name: Galahad
description: Vision-language-action policies are tested on whether they follow instructions. One word of the instruction changes and the policy must change its behavior.
note: A base policy finished 89 of 200 LIBERO object trials with the instruction replaced by xxx. The repo also ships fixed demonstration generators.

name: Galileo Agent Leaderboard
description: Models pick and call tools on samples drawn from existing tool-use benchmarks. Galileo scores Tool Selection Quality with an LLM judge and averages the datasets equally.
note: The first release ranked 17 models, 12 closed and 5 open. The Hugging Face space has about 450 likes.

name: Galileo Agent Leaderboard v2
description: Agents handle simulated multi-turn customer support conversations in banking, healthcare, insurance, investment and telecom, with synthetic personas and domain tools. Scores are Action Completion and Tool Selection Quality.
note: The board reports Action Completion. Version 2 replaced the sampled public datasets of version 1 with synthetic enterprise scenarios.

name: Game Arena Bargaining
description: Two language models negotiate how to split a pool of items, each with private item values. Each side tries to reach a good deal without giving away its values.
note: Kaggle published the leaderboard on 2026-07-23 with 36 models on 2026-11-01. Gameplay logs are a public Kaggle dataset. Part of the Kaggle Game Arena suite.

name: Game Arena Checkers
description: Language models play American checkers against each other, with forced jumps and crowned kings. Ratings come from head-to-head games.
note: Kaggle published the leaderboard on 2026-06-11 with 38 models on 2026-11-01. Gameplay logs are a public Kaggle dataset. Part of the Kaggle Game Arena suite.

name: Game Arena Chess
description: Language models play full chess games against each other with the board given as FEN and PGN text. Ratings come from many games between each pair.
note: The 2026-02-02 leaderboard is labeled v2 of the chess text task. Kaggle also runs Chess Openings (11 models) and a Chess Suite (19 models). 39 models on 2026-10-19.

name: Game Arena Chess Openings
description: Language models play chess against each other from varied two-move openings sampled from 20 popular human openings. The board is given as text.
note: Kaggle published it on 2026-02-02 with Chess in a Chess Suite. It had 11 models on 2026-11-01. Part of the Kaggle Game Arena suite. Varied openings make memorized lines less useful than in standard Chess.

name: Game Arena Clobber
description: Language models play Clobber, where every move captures an adjacent enemy stone. The player who makes the last legal move wins.
note: Kaggle published the leaderboard on 2026-06-25 with 36 models on 2026-11-01. Gameplay logs are a public Kaggle dataset. Part of the Kaggle Game Arena suite.

name: Game Arena Coin Game
description: Two language models move on a grid and pick up coins. Each should collect the coins that score for it and avoid the rest.
note: Kaggle published the leaderboard on 2026-07-08 with 35 models on 2026-11-01. Gameplay logs are a public Kaggle dataset. Part of the Kaggle Game Arena suite.

name: Game Arena Dark Hex
description: Language models play Hex without seeing the opponent's stones, so they must probe cells to learn the hidden board while building a path.
note: Kaggle published the leaderboard on 2026-06-04 with 38 models on 2026-11-01. Gameplay logs are a public Kaggle dataset. Part of the Kaggle Game Arena suite.

name: Game Arena Dots and Boxes
aliases: Kaggle Game Arena Dots and Boxes
description: Language models take turns drawing lines between dots on a grid. Closing the fourth side of a box claims it.
note: Kaggle published the leaderboard on 2026-06-17 with 37 models on 2026-11-01. Gameplay logs are a public Kaggle dataset. Part of the Kaggle Game Arena suite.

name: Game Arena Five in a Row
aliases: Kaggle Game Arena Five in a Row
description: Language models play a gomoku-style game and try to line up five of their tokens before the opponent does.
note: Kaggle published the leaderboard on 2026-04-30 with 20 models on 2026-11-01. Gameplay logs are a public Kaggle dataset. Part of the Kaggle Game Arena suite.

name: Game Arena Four in a Row
aliases: Kaggle Game Arena Four in a Row
description: Language models play a Connect Four style game and try to line up four of their tokens before the opponent does.
note: Kaggle published the leaderboard on 2026-02-19 with 38 models on 2026-11-01. Gameplay logs are a public Kaggle dataset. Part of the Kaggle Game Arena suite.

name: Game Arena Go
description: Language models play Go against each other through the Game Arena text harness. Ratings come from head-to-head games.
note: Google promised Go at the 2025-08 launch. The leaderboard was published on 2026-09-22 with 36 models.

name: Game Arena Lines of Action
aliases: Kaggle Game Arena Lines of Action
description: Language models play Lines of Action, where a piece moves as far as the number of pieces on its line. The goal is to join all of one's pieces into one group.
note: Kaggle published the leaderboard on 2026-07-16 with 36 models on 2026-11-01. Gameplay logs are a public Kaggle dataset. Part of the Kaggle Game Arena suite.

name: Game Arena Nine Men's Morris
aliases: Kaggle Game Arena Nine Men's Morris
description: Language models play Nine Men's Morris. Forming a row of three, called a mill, lets a player remove one of the opponent's pieces.
note: Kaggle published the leaderboard on 2026-08-04 with 36 models on 2026-11-01. Gameplay logs are a public Kaggle dataset. Part of the Kaggle Game Arena suite.

name: Game Arena Poker
description: Language models play heads-up no-limit Texas Hold'em against each other. Models are ranked by mean big blinds won per 100 hands.
note: Launched with a livestreamed tournament that ended on 2026-02-04. 31 models on the leaderboard by 2026-10-08.

name: Game Arena Reversi
description: Language models play Reversi, also called Othello, flipping the opponent's disks that they flank in a line.
note: Kaggle published the leaderboard on 2026-08-11 with 36 models on 2026-11-01. Gameplay logs are a public Kaggle dataset. Part of the Kaggle Game Arena suite.

name: Game Arena Ultimate Tic-Tac-Toe
description: Language models play nine linked tic-tac-toe boards. Each move decides which small board the opponent must play next.
note: Kaggle published the leaderboard on 2026-07-28 with 36 models on 2026-11-01. Gameplay logs are a public Kaggle dataset. Part of the Kaggle Game Arena suite.

name: Game Arena Werewolf
description: Teams of language models play the social deduction game Werewolf in natural language. Villagers must find the hidden werewolves, who try to deceive them.
note: Google DeepMind also presents it as a sandbox for deception and manipulation research. 8 models on the leaderboard in 2026-06.

name: Game Arena Word Art
description: Language models take turns drawing a word as ASCII art and guessing what the other model drew.
note: Kaggle published the leaderboard on 2026-08-18 with 35 models on 2026-11-01. Gameplay logs are a public Kaggle dataset. Part of the Kaggle Game Arena suite.

name: Game Arena Word Association
description: Teams of language models give one-word clues and guess linked words, in a game like Codenames, against an opposing team.
note: Kaggle published the leaderboard on 2026-05-26 with 36 models on 2026-11-01. Gameplay logs are a public Kaggle dataset. Part of the Kaggle Game Arena suite.

name: GameCraft-Bench
description: Coding agents build playable games end to end inside a real game engine, where scripts, scenes, assets and runtime behavior must work together.
note: 59 upvotes on Hugging Face papers and 213 GitHub stars.

name: GameDevBench
description: Agents complete game development tasks in the Godot engine, derived from web and video tutorials, across 2D and 3D graphics, user interfaces and gameplay logic. Tests in the engine check each result.
note: ICML 2026. The task count grew from 132 in the first paper version to 333, so early scores may not compare. The board is in the repo README. Repo has 151 stars.

name: GameHorizon
description: Models are tested on gameplay over several time horizons. Tasks combine visual understanding, instruction decomposition, planning and precise action control, using offline data instead of noisy rollouts.
note: Ships with training data. 70 upvotes on Hugging Face papers and 579 GitHub stars.

name: GameWorld
description: Multimodal game agents play 34 browser games across 170 tasks. Outcomes are checked from the game state.
note: 63 HF paper upvotes. A Fine-Control Protocol release in 2026-08 adds higher-frequency control.

name: Gaokao Math 2026
description: Models sit the five 2026 Chinese Gaokao mathematics papers (National I, National II, Beijing, Shanghai and Tianjin). Each paper is graded out of 150 points.
note: The score is points out of 150, not a percentage. The dataset was posted on Hugging Face on 2026-09-01.

name: GAOKAO-Bench
description: Models answer Chinese national college entrance exam questions from 2010 to 2022 across nine subjects, with objective and subjective questions.
note: Labs usually report the objective-question accuracy. Later releases add 2023 and newer questions.

name: GaP: Graph-as-Policy
description: Multi-agent harness that compiles language tasks into typed robot skill graphs. Tested on 8 variational-automation tasks (4 sim, 4 real) by success rate.
note: An agent harness, not a benchmark. The sim tasks build on LIBERO and LIBERO-Pro pose splits, with baselines CaP-X, pi0.5, MolmoAct2 and TipTop. Goldberg says it was accepted to CoRL.

name: GaRAGe
description: Models write long-form RAG answers to 2,366 questions with human-annotated grounding passages. Scoring checks whether answers use the relevant passages.
note: ACL 2025 Findings. Questions vary in complexity, dynamism and false premises.

name: GateMem
description: Memory agents serve several people who share one memory pool in hospitals, offices, schools and homes. Each long episode checks three things: answering legitimate requests after state updates, refusing information a person is not allowed to see, and forgetting records after an explicit deletion request. Hidden checkpoints and leak targets let a structured judge score each response.
note: data/reviewed.json lists GateMem among papers waiting for a follow-up review, not as a checked rejection. About 134 GitHub stars and 17 Hugging Face upvotes. Long-context prompting and retrieval methods are compared at different token costs.

name: GBAEval
description: Agents get 24 hours to write a Game Boy Advance emulator in Rust for WebAssembly. Replay, hardware, and audio tests compare it with Mesen2.
note: Mechanize describes it as one test case rather than a full benchmark, so each score rests on a single task.

name: GDM Situational Awareness
description: Agents must discover and remove unexplained constraints in a simulated Linux deployment across eleven challenges. Reports average success rate.
note: Situational awareness half of Google DeepMind's stealth and situational awareness evaluations (Phuong et al. 2025), open source in Inspect Evals. Google reports challenges passed out of 11, Meta the average success rate.

name: GDM Stealth
description: Agents try four oversight-evasion challenges, each with an automated monitor and a human baseline. Reports success rate per challenge.
note: Stealth half of Google DeepMind's stealth and situational awareness evaluations (Phuong et al. 2025), open source in Inspect Evals. Google reports challenges passed, Meta the average success rate.

name: GDP.pdf
description: 100 expert multimodal reasoning tasks over real economically important PDF documents. Scored by rubric-criteria pass rate.
note: Part of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.3.2 (10% weight). The HF dataset returned 401 to an anonymous fetch (may be gated).

name: GDP.xlsx
description: Agents open a professional Excel workbook in a sandbox and answer a short question about it, as a domain professional would. A Gemini autograder checks the final answer against criteria.
note: Follows the format of GDP.pdf with spreadsheets. The full set has 70 Harbor tasks in 13 domains, and the HF dataset holds 3 samples.

name: GDPevo
description: Agents learn from training tasks drawn from enterprise workflows and must reuse that experience on related test tasks. Gains at test time measure self-evolution.
note: An automated pipeline generates the tasks by rule hybridization to limit contamination. 22 HF paper upvotes.

name: GDPval
description: Real work tasks from 44 occupations with reference files. Experts blindly compare model deliverables with expert work. Metric is win-or-tie rate.
note: Only the 220-task gold set is public, with an automated grading service. OpenAI says its hosted GDPval leaderboard is no longer active and points to the GDPval-AA board instead.

name: GDPval Extended
description: Models produce work products for occupations across nine GDP sectors. Mercor adds 132 new expert-written tasks to the 213 public ones and reports both scores.
note: Held-out extension of gdpval. Mercor shows the original and extended score for each model. The month is approximate. The Wayback Machine first saved the earliest extended pages on 2026-08-15.

name: GDPval-AA
description: Agents complete GDPval occupational tasks. Artificial Analysis compares the outputs in pairs and ranks models by Elo.
note: Versions 2 and 2.1 changed the task set, so their Elo scores have their own records.

name: GDPval-AA v2
description: Agents with shell and web access complete 220 GDPval gold tasks from 44 occupations. Outputs are compared pairwise and ranked by Elo.
note: Artificial Analysis version 2 of GDPval-AA. Elo scores do not compare with the GDPval win rate.

name: GDPval-AA v2.1
description: Agents with shell and web access complete 220 GDPval gold tasks from 44 occupations. Blind pairwise comparisons give Elo ratings.
