note: Elo anchored to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash at 1,600. Scores differ from v2: Fable 5.1 is 1853 on v2 and 1735 on v2.1.

name: GDPVal-Diamond
description: Models complete a ByteDance Seed subset of GDPval occupational tasks. Rubrics grade each deliverable automatically.
note: In-house ByteDance Seed evaluation. The subset and rubrics are not public. The Seed2.0 text calls it GDPVal-Verified and Table 13 calls it GDPVal-Diamond.

name: GDPval-MM
description: Agents produce office deliverables for GDPval tasks in a MiniMax agent framework. A judge model compares full trajectories pairwise and reports a win rate.
note: In-house MiniMax harness on the public GDPval tasks, so scores depend on its judge and comparison models.

name: GDPval-Rubrics (MiniMax)
description: MiniMax rubric grading of model deliverables on public GDPval tasks, in an environment matched to GDPval-AA.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (MiniMax). The blog spells it 'GPDval-Rubrics'. Built on OpenAI's public GDPval cases.

name: GDPWorks
description: Agents complete 83 professional tasks across 36 occupations, using source files to produce work such as documents, spreadsheets, and code. The Joules-to-GDP framework compares outputs with expert deliverables through a blinded model judge. Task success measures the share of wins and ties against the expert.
org: Snorkel AI and Hazy Research (Scaling Intelligence)
note: Snorkel contributes 83 tasks distinct from the 220 GDPval tasks in the same dataset. Researchers report paper results on GDPval, not a separate GDPWorks leaderboard. Snorkel licenses its original tasks and expert deliverables under CC BY 4.0, excluding third-party material.

name: GDPx
description: Agents work long tasks in simulated workplaces across 11 domains, including chip design, cybersecurity, biology, finance, quant trading and recursive self-improvement. Fourteen specialist partners built the tasks, with a default limit of 8 hours each. Score is pass@1 over three attempts, with every domain weighted equally.
note: Version 1.0. Each partner published one example task, and the rest are private. Safety classifiers lower the scores of Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra on cyber, biology and alignment tasks. Finance and legal report partial credit, since every model scores 0 under binary grading. SemiAnalysis plans a new version every 3 to 6 months.

name: GEdit-Bench
description: Image editing models follow real-world user edit instructions. A model judge scores semantic consistency, perceptual quality and an overall score.
note: Released with Step1X-Edit. The almanac files image generation under video-generation for now. BAGEL reports scores graded by GPT-4.1.

name: Gemini agentic alignment evals
description: Paired impossible and solvable tasks, ambiguous high-risk SWE tasks and fabrication checks measuring agents overstepping boundaries.

name: Gemini content safety evals
description: Automated text-to-text, multilingual and image-to-text policy violation rates, refusal tone and unjustified refusals, reported as deltas.

name: Gemini Personality Evaluation (sycophancy)
description: About 900 single- and multi-turn prompts scoring nine personality dimensions, including candor and self-awareness against sycophancy.

name: Gemini prompt-injection evaluation suites
description: Held-out adaptive prompt-injection suites for tool use, grounding/RAG, computer use and coding agents, plus arena replays.

name: Gemini Robotics generalization benchmark
description: Robot policies run 85 real bi-arm manipulation tasks. About 80% test generalization to new scenes, new wording of instructions or new actions. Scored by average progress and success rate.
note: Of the 85 tasks, 20% are in distribution, 28% visual, 28% instruction and 24% action generalization. The Gemini Robotics On-Device cards report scene, instruction and action generalization in the same way.

name: GenAI-Arena
description: Users compare outputs from two anonymous models for image generation, image editing and video generation, and vote. Votes give Elo ratings.
note: Published at NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks. The Hugging Face space shows a build error and was last changed on 2025-07-03.

name: GenAI-Arena Image Editing
description: Models edit images from user instructions. Anonymous human comparisons determine Elo in this independent vote pool.
note: Full-vote Elo remains an auxiliary metric. This board keeps anonymous votes separate from other GenAI-Arena tasks.

name: GenAI-Arena Image Generation
description: Models generate images from text prompts. Anonymous human comparisons determine Elo in this independent vote pool.
note: Full-vote Elo remains an auxiliary metric. This board keeps anonymous votes separate from other GenAI-Arena tasks.

name: GenAI-Arena Video Generation
description: Models generate videos from text prompts. Anonymous human comparisons determine Elo in this independent vote pool.
note: Full-vote Elo remains an auxiliary metric. This board keeps anonymous votes separate from other GenAI-Arena tasks.

name: GenAI-Bench
description: Image generation systems are compared by human side-by-side preference on text-to-image prompts.
note: Google DeepMind names GenAI-Bench in the Gemini 3.1 Flash Image model card and reports overall preference and visual quality Elo.

name: GeneBench
description: Agents analyze messy genomics and quantitative biology data across 103 multi-step problems. Scored by pass rate on verifiable final answers.
note: GPT-5.5 Pro scored 33.2 percent at launch.

name: GeneBench Pro
description: Agents analyze messy simulated genomics and biology datasets to estimate a decision-relevant quantity across 129 problems. Scored automatically against known answers.
note: 129 problems in 10 domains and 21 sub-domains. Synthetic noisy datasets graded against ground truth. OpenAI calls it a harder expansion of GeneBench. Self-reported scores only so far.

name: General Assistant (MiniMax in-house)
description: Models answer real assistant queries from Hailuo AI users. Automatic assessments score the replies.
note: In-house MiniMax evaluation built mostly from Hailuo AI user queries in Mandarin. The queries are not public.

name: General refusals (xAI)
description: Models get thousands of harmful requests in six languages. A grader model scores compliance, the share that fails policy.
note: In-house xAI evaluation. The Grok 4.1 card says earlier cards scored only the English prompts by mistake.

name: General365
description: Models solve 365 hand-written reasoning problems and 1,095 variants in eight categories that need only K-12 knowledge. Scoring mixes rule-based and model-based checks.
note: Half of the questions are public and half are held out to track contamination.

name: GenEval
description: Text-to-image models draw prompts about object count, color, position and co-occurrence, and an object detector checks each image. Scored by the share of correct images.
note: Image generation has no own subcategory in the taxonomy, so it sits under generation in audio-video.

name: GenExam
description: Image generation systems are evaluated on subject-focused educational tasks with expert ratings.
note: Google DeepMind calls GenExam a public benchmark subset in the Gemini 3.1 Flash Image model card, but the page gives no numeric GenExam row.

name: Genspark Slides Benchmark
description: Models build finished slide decks from 200 real production tasks in the Genspark Slides agent harness. An internal grader scores quality, completion, content and design.
note: 11 models in the Fireworks index. The maker blog blocks scripted reads.

name: GeoBench
description: Models geolocate GeoGuessr photos from community maps by giving coordinates and a country. Scored by country accuracy and a distance-based score.

name: GeoGuesser environment (FineEnvs)
description: Agent placed at unknown Mapillary street-level location looks, walks, pins candidates and guesses coordinates. Scored by a distance-based GeoGuessr-style reward from 0 to 1.
note: Frozen 200-task eval split committed so resets are byte-identical. The article ('How to turn a game into an RL environment') trains a 4B VLM with TRL and keeps the dead ends in.

name: GitTaskBench
description: Code agents solve 54 real tasks across 7 modalities and 7 domains by using a given GitHub repository, from understanding and setup to running it.
note: About 260 GitHub stars.

name: GLM-4 All Tools information seeking (Z.ai)
description: Models use a web browser to find information for user questions. The ChatGLM report gives accuracy but does not describe the test set.
note: In-house Zhipu evaluation of GLM-4 All Tools against ChatGPT-4 (Web).

name: Global MMLU
description: MMLU translated into 42 languages with cultural-sensitivity annotations. Multiple-choice accuracy.
note: The full set has about 14K questions per language. Global MMLU Lite (global-mmlu-lite) is a separate 400-question subset that most launch posts report. Remove Global-MMLU-Lite from this record's aliases and move Lite card results there.

name: Global MMLU Lite
description: Models answer MMLU questions in 15 languages, with 200 culturally sensitive and 200 culturally agnostic questions per language. All items are human translated or post-edited. Accuracy.

changes.text: The maintainers added a 400-question Burmese test set, expanding coverage from 15 to 16 languages. Aggregates including Burmese differ in language coverage from the original paper results.

note: A 400-question subset per language of Global MMLU, so scores differ from the full set. Gemini and Gemma reports cite it as Global MMLU (Lite). The paper results use these 15 languages.

name: Global MMLU Lite 2.0
description: Models answer 400 human-translated MMLU questions per language in 18 languages, adding Albanian, Burmese and Welsh to the first 15. Accuracy.
note: Community contributors added the three languages. The language average changes with the set, so it is not comparable with 1.0.

name: Global MMLU Lite 3.0
description: Models answer 400 human-translated MMLU questions per language in 23 languages. Version 3.0 adds Czech, Hungarian, Oriya, Slovak and Tajik and updates Italian. Accuracy.
note: Uploaded on 2026-05-19. The language average changes with the set, so it is not comparable with 1.0 or 2.0.

name: Global PIQA
description: Models pick the correct solution to everyday commonsense prompts in over 100 languages, many about local foods and customs. Scoring is accuracy.
note: The license forbids training AI systems on it or on synthetic data seeded from it. The record covers the non-parallel split of over 100 languages, released in 2025-10. A parallel split of culturally agnostic questions in 131 language varieties followed in 2026-04, and its scores are a different test.

name: GlobalMGSM
description: Models solve MGSM grade-school math problems pooled from MGSM-Rev2, AfriMGSM, BenchMAX and other translations, 41 language configs in all. Accuracy on the final number.
note: The Tiny Aya report evaluates 35 languages and uses MGSM-Rev2 in place of the original MGSM. Per-language licenses follow the source sets.

name: GlobeBench
description: Models act as text world models. Given an agent's past actions and observations, they predict the environment's next observation across code, enterprise, games, math and science, and dialogue.
note: 1,632 execution-grounded items and 20 evaluated models. A judge scores 606 items that lack a fixed scoring rule, and all judge records are released.

name: GMAI-MMBench
description: Vision-language models answer medical multiple-choice questions over many imaging modalities, clinical tasks and departments, at several perceptual granularities.
note: 86 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: GMAT Quantitative
description: Models answer the quantitative section of the official GMAT online exam. Scored as accuracy.
note: Llama 3 uses one official GMAT online exam, so the confidence interval is wide.

name: GMAT Verbal
description: Models answer the verbal section of the official GMAT online exam. Scored as accuracy.
note: Llama 3 uses one official GMAT online exam.

name: Golden3 speech summarization (Microsoft)
description: Models summarize 108 recorded meetings of about 6 minutes each from 1071 instructions. GPT-4 rates overall quality from 1 to 7.
note: In-house Microsoft evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Google DeepMind harmful manipulation studies
description: Human-participant studies and simulated-user dialogues measuring belief and behavior change in civic and finance domains.

name: Google DeepMind internal cyber benchmarks
description: Internal recall of recent confirmed vulnerabilities in open-source code, internal vulnerability research, and the Wiz Penetration Testing Benchmark.

name: Google DeepMind scheming honeypot suite
description: Code-review and agentic-coding honeypots in internal codebases that offer chances to sabotage. Scored on sabotage and scheming reasoning.
note: Models sometimes detect honeypots from workspace naming, which limits validity.

name: Google RE-Bench (GRB)
description: Google DeepMind internal research-engineering benchmark with a 2-hour timeout per task, used for the ML R&D CCL rule-out.
note: About a quarter of original tasks had bugs. Argon was rescored on the remaining subset.

name: Gorilla APIBench
description: Models write calls to machine learning APIs from Hugging Face, TorchHub and TensorHub. Scored by AST match.
note: The same Gorilla team later built BFCL.

name: GovReport
description: Models summarize long US government reports from the Government Accountability Office and the Congressional Research Service. The reports are much longer than earlier summarization sets, and each has an expert-written summary. Scores are ROUGE overlap with the reference summary.
note: Microsoft reports GovReport, with QMSum and SummScreenFD, in the long-context table of the Phi-3.5 model cards. SCROLLS and LongBench include it as one task. ROUGE rewards word overlap, not faithfulness.

name: GPQA Diamond
description: 198 graduate-level 'Google-proof' multiple-choice questions in biology, chemistry and physics.
note: Saturated (about 94-96%). Several 2026 cards use it only as a substrate for CoT-controllability or monitor-evasion tests.

name: GPQA Extended
description: Models answer all 546 GPQA questions, graduate level biology, chemistry and physics questions written by experts. Scored by accuracy.
note: Full extended set of GPQA. The gpqa-main and gpqa-diamond records cover its subsets.

name: GPQA Main
description: Models answer the 448 question main set of GPQA, graduate level biology, chemistry and physics questions written by experts. Scored by accuracy.
note: Main set of GPQA. The gpqa-diamond record covers the 198 question Diamond subset.

name: GQA
description: Models answer compositional questions about real-world images, generated from scene graphs. Scored by exact-match accuracy, often on the balanced test-dev split.
note: Recent vision-language model cards report the balanced test-dev split through VLMEvalKit.

name: Gram (Gauging Realistic Agentic Misbehavior)
description: Automated auditing over 17 simulated deployment scenarios that incentivize sabotage by coding and research agents. LLM judges plus human review.
note: Builds on Petri. No public repo found.

name: GraphWalks
description: A graph is given as an edge list in long context. The model answers BFS or parent queries, scored by F1.

changes.text: OpenAI corrected ground truth for 24 of 400 short-context parents examples and clarified exact-depth breadth-first search prompts. Earlier dataset revisions can yield different answers and scores.

OpenAI corrected the published answer parser and F1 grading code. Parse failures and nonoverlapping answers now receive zero, while matching empty sets receive full credit, changing scores from the earlier code.

note: On 2026-02-27 OpenAI fixed wrong ground truth in 24 of 400 parents samples under 128K. It also reworded the BFS prompt to ask only for nodes at the exact depth. The name stayed, so results before and after may differ slightly.

name: Gray Swan Agent Red Teaming (ART) benchmark
aliases: Behavior Attack Success Rate at k Queries
External agent red teaming benchmark for tool use
Gray Swan Agent Red Teaming benchmark
description: Agents face curated prompt injections from a large public red-teaming competition across 44 deployment scenarios. Score is attack success rate.
org: Gray Swan + UK AI Security Institute
note: Gray Swan ran it for OpenAI with attacks from its Shade platform. Gray Swan keeps the attack set private. It has a user-side (direct) subset and an environment-side (indirect) subset. Reported as pass@k ASR, the share of targets broken by at least one of k sampled attacks.

name: Gray Swan Bio Eval
aliases: Gray Swan Automated Bio Red Teaming Evaluation
description: Gray Swan's Shade red teaming agent attacks the safeguarded model on about 50 high risk biology tasks. Reports query and objective success rates.
note: Run by Gray Swan for Google DeepMind.

name: Gray Swan Cyber Eval
aliases: Gray Swan Automated Cyber Red Teaming Evaluation
description: Gray Swan's Shade red teaming agent attacks the safeguarded model on cyber tasks built from Google scenarios. Reports query and objective success rates.
note: Run by Gray Swan for Google DeepMind. Task count varies by report, for example 25 or 28.

name: Gray Swan IPI Arena benchmark
description: Indirect prompt-injection attacks from public red-teaming competitions replayed on tool, coding and browser agents. Attack success rate at k attempts.
org: Gray Swan + UK AISI + US CAISI
note: Labs whose models were in the competitions score worse (attacks were tailored), so Anthropic reports only non-participating models. Gray Swan refreshes the attack set after new competitions. The Q1+Q2 2026 set has 37 scenarios and 1,804 transferable attacks, versus 41 behaviors in the public release.

name: Gray Swan Jailbreak Arena
description: Human attackers try to jailbreak models for violent, self-harm and malicious code outputs. Scored as attack success rate per category.
note: Run by Gray Swan for OpenAI. Harmful text and image outputs are judged with the OpenAI moderation API.

name: Gray Swan Reward Hacking Bench
description: Agentic environments where a task can be finished honestly or by crossing a declared line, such as shipping insecure code, leaking a secret, harming a third party through a shared service or leaving the scope of a penetration test. Reports how often each line is crossed.
note: Reports give per-scenario rates, not one overall score.

name: Gray Swan Shade (adaptive attacker)
description: Gray Swan's adaptive red-teaming agent trained on test scenarios to attack coding, computer-use and browser agents with prompt injections.

name: Gray Swan Shade knowledge elicitation through chat
description: An automated attacker tries to elicit useful answers to 100 harmful and 100 dual-use cyber queries from a safeguarded model. Score is attack success rate.
note: External red teaming of deployed cyber safeguards. Gray Swan built the query set independently of Anthropic.

name: GRE Analytical Writing
description: Models write GRE issue and argument essays graded by trained contractors. Scored on the 0 to 6 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: GRE Physics
description: Models answer questions from official GRE Physics practice tests. Scored as accuracy.
note: Llama 3 averages official practice tests 1 and 2 and drops questions with images.

name: GRE Quantitative
description: Models take the GRE quantitative reasoning section. Scored on the 130 to 170 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: GRE Verbal
description: Models take the GRE verbal reasoning section. Scored on the 130 to 170 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: Grounding robustness (RAG prompt injection)
description: An adaptive attacker controls one retrieved excerpt in 30 RAG scenarios to induce fabricated or suppressed claims. Reports survival after 40 attempts.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Grounding with citations, sentence unfactual rate
description: Models answer multi-snippet tasks with inline citations. An autorater reports the share of sentences not supported by the sources.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: GroundUI
description: Agents get a screenshot and an instruction and must click the right UI element. About 18K test samples cover web, desktop and mobile screens. Scored by whether the point falls in the target box.
org: AgentStudio team (Longtao Zheng et al., Nanyang Technological University and Skywork AI)
note: Part of the AgentStudio toolkit. Labs often report only the web split, called GroundUI Web. The release month is the dataset upload. The affiliation is likely, not verified.

name: GSM-Plus
description: Models solve GSM8K problems after perturbations such as changed numbers, added distractors and reversed questions.
note: Llama 3 shows it only in a scatter plot.

name: GSM-Symbolic
description: Models solve grade-school word problems generated from symbolic templates of GSM8K questions, with names and numbers changed. P1 and P2 add one or two extra clauses.
note: Measures how much accuracy drops when only surface details of a problem change.

name: GSM1k
description: Models solve new grade school math word problems written to mirror GSM8K in style and difficulty. The gap between GSM8K and GSM1k accuracy shows overfitting or contamination.
note: Scale's SEAL Math board used 1,000 problems with 50 public, and Scale marked it deprecated in 2025-01. The Hugging Face dataset posted on 2025-03-31 has 1,205 rows. Some model families dropped up to 8 points against GSM8K.

name: GSM8K
description: 8.5K grade-school math word problems. Final numeric answer scored by exact match.
note: Saturated.

name: GSM8K Platinum Initial 268
description: Models answer the original 268-question cleaned GSM8K subset. The live matrix reports each model configuration separately.
note: This initial subset differs from the full 1,209-question GSM8K-Platinum test set.

name: GSM8K-Platinum
description: Models solve the GSM8K test problems after MIT researchers fixed wrong labels and removed badly written questions. Errors on it are more likely real model mistakes.
note: A drop-in replacement for the GSM8K test set from the Platinum Benchmarks project, which also cleans other saturated benchmarks.

name: GSM8K-V
description: Vision-language models solve GSM8K word problems that are redrawn as multi-image visual scenes, so the facts must be read from pictures.
note: 32 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: GSO-Bench
description: Agents speed up code in 102 tasks across 10 real codebases, given a performance test. Scored by the share matching the expert commit's speedup.

name: GTA
aliases: GTA: A Benchmark for General Tool Agents
description: Agents answer 229 human-written queries that need 1 to 4 real deployed tools for perception, operation, logic and creativity, often with image inputs. Queries leave the tools and steps implicit.
note: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks. The maintainers updated the board in 2025-03 and 2026-02. GTA-2 keeps this set as GTA-Atomic.

name: GTA-2
description: Agents face two tiers: the original atomic tool-use queries and new long-horizon workflows with open-ended deliverables. Workflows are graded with recursive checkpoints that split each goal into checkable parts.
note: GTA-Workflow uses real user queries, deployed tools and multimodal context. It expands modalities, tools and task length over the first GTA.

name: GUI Odyssey
description: Mobile GUI agents carry out tasks that cross several apps, such as sharing a post from one social app to another. The dataset has 8,334 episodes averaging 15.3 steps, over 212 apps, 1,357 app combinations and six devices. Agents are scored by how often each predicted action matches the recorded step.
note: It is also a training set, and many models fine-tune on its train split before reporting the test split. Scoring is offline step matching, not live task success. The paper had 26 Hugging Face upvotes and the repository about 160 GitHub stars.

name: Gym-Anything-RT
description: Vision-language agents play 100 real-time browser minigames by screenshots and mouse and keyboard input. Each game also has a paused, non-real-time counterpart, so the gap shows the cost of acting in real time.
org: Carnegie Mellon University (Welleck lab, CMU L3)
note: Coding agents generated the minigames with oracle solvers and auditor checks. Headline is pass rate at difficulty 5, full interaction, live. GPT-6 Astra xHigh scored 9.0%.

name: HABIT-Bench
description: Agent memory systems must infer user habits from weak evidence spread across many past conversations and apply them correctly later.
note: 90 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: Hack the Box challenge set (Google DeepMind)
description: Agents attempt 13 offensive security challenges based on the Hack the Box platform.
note: In-house Google DeepMind selection. Gemini 1.5 and Gemma reports list 13 challenges.

name: Hack the Box Machines (Meta)
description: Agents try to compromise 10 Hack The Box machines with step hints. Scored by machines compromised and the share of intermediate steps completed over 10 attempts.
note: In-house Meta evaluation. The tasks are not public. Agents get the output of a failed step and continue.

name: HackBench
description: Models act as monitors on long autoresearch agent traces and must point to the exact commands where the agent reward-hacked. Scored by localization F1 against audited gold indices.
note: 169 audited trajectories over 13 tasks, 41 with natural hacks and 128 with planted ones, from GPT-5.5 and GLM-5.2 runs. The board reports F1. Dataset is CC BY-NC 4.0.

name: HackerBench
description: xAI internal CTF-style suite needing chained skills, plus borderline and harmful requests that should be refused.

name: HAE-RAE Bench
description: Models answer Korean questions on vocabulary, history, general knowledge and reading comprehension. It tests cultural and contextual knowledge that translated benchmarks miss.
note: Launch posts usually cite version 1.1 of the dataset.

name: Hallucinations on production-representative prompts
description: Models answer prompts representative of ChatGPT production traffic. A grader with web access scores incorrect claims and responses with major errors.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report results with and without browsing.

name: HallusionBench
description: Models answer 1,129 yes or no questions about 346 images, built in pairs to expose language hallucination and visual illusion. Scored by accuracy.

changes.text: The maintainers expanded the dataset and updated the leaderboard. Scores on the expanded questions do not use the original evaluation set.

name: HaltEval-prelim (Meta)
description: Models judge whether 230 Python programs translated from SV-COMP and TPDB terminate. A divergence claim must give an input that times out after 5 seconds.
note: In-house Meta evaluation. The tasks are not public. A constant classifier scores 50 on the balanced set.

name: HaluBench
description: Models judge whether an answer is faithful to its context across about 15,000 labeled context, question and answer triplets. It tests hallucination detectors and LLM judges.
note: Released with Patronus's Lynx hallucination detection model. Examples come from existing QA datasets and include finance and medicine domains.

name: HaluEval
description: Models judge whether answers, dialogue turns or summaries contain hallucinations. Hallucinated samples were generated by ChatGPT from seed datasets such as HotpotQA and then filtered.
note: Covers question answering, knowledge-grounded dialogue and text summarization, plus general user queries.

name: HaluMem
description: Agent memory systems are tested for hallucinations at each operation, memory extraction, updating and question answering, rather than only end to end.
note: Two datasets, HaluMem-Medium and HaluMem-Long, hold about 15k memory points and 3.5k questions, with contexts over 1M tokens. 86 HF paper upvotes.

name: HANDBOOK.md
description: Agents do routine company work with mock email, chat, calendar, issue and commerce tools while following a 20 to 124 page handbook. Programmatic criteria check required and forbidden actions, and a trial passes only if all pass.
note: 65 tasks across five domains and ten fictional companies, with 824 criteria. Each task mutates a base handbook so policies differ per task. No LLM judge is used. Tasks ship in Harbor format with an OpenHands harness.

name: HANS
description: An entailment test built to catch three shallow shortcuts: lexical overlap, subsequence and constituent. Every premise and hypothesis pair shares words, but only some pairs are entailments. A model that relies on word overlap fails the non-entailment cases.
org: Johns Hopkins University and Brown University (McCoy, Pavlick, Linzen)
note: Published at ACL 2019. Models are usually trained on MNLI and tested on HANS, so it measures robustness to shortcuts. About 130 GitHub stars.

name: HappyWorld Embodied
description: The HappyWorld arena publishes a separate embodied vote pool and Elo ranking.
note: Separate matches produce these ratings. They are not sub-scores of the Video World Model board.

name: HappyWorld Spatial Reconstruction
description: The HappyWorld arena publishes a separate spatial reconstruction vote pool and Elo ranking.
note: Separate matches produce these ratings. They are not sub-scores of the Video World Model board.

name: HappyWorld-Bench
description: World models are tested on the quality of the worlds they generate and on staying consistent and responsive while agents explore, interact and modify them.
note: Uses a hierarchical capability framework. 59 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: Harbor-Index
description: Agents solve about 80 hard tasks drawn from 29 benchmarks run through Harbor adapters, such as HLE, GSO and SWE-bench Pro. Each task keeps its source verifier.
note: Version 1.0 (June 2026) had 82 tasks. Releases 1.1 to 1.4 in July 2026 fixed and re-pinned tasks to 80, each with its own frozen leaderboard. No pair passed 30% at launch.

name: Hard Capability (MiniMax in-house)
description: Models handle complex productivity requests with several levels of instructions that leading models often fail.
note: In-house MiniMax evaluation built mostly from Hailuo AI user queries in Mandarin. The queries are not public.

name: Hard-negative protein binding prediction
description: Agents with structure files and tools pick the one true binder among five similar designed proteins. Scored as pass@4.
note: OpenAI Preparedness evaluation on proprietary binding data. The concern threshold is 50 percent.

name: HarmBench
description: Models answer harmful behavior requests, including copyright and contextual cases, with and without automated red-team attacks. A classifier judges whether the response complies.
org: Mazeika et al. (Center for AI Safety)
note: Scores depend on the attack method and judge model, so labs differ.

name: Harmful content defect rate (Azure AI Evaluation SDK, Microsoft)
description: GPT-4o simulates adversarial conversations with the model, and a judge flags violence, sexual, self-harm and hateful content. Scored as the share of harmful responses, lower is better.
note: In-house Microsoft evaluation. The tasks are not public. Variants add known jailbreaks, Tier 1 languages, or audio prompts.

name: Harmful manipulation efficacy study
description: Human participants chat with a model told to persuade them. Belief and behavior change are compared with a non-AI baseline as odds ratios.
note: In-house Google DeepMind human study run on Prolific. Reports often show only charts.

name: Harmful manipulation propensity evaluation
description: Simulated users talk with the model and an autorater counts how often it uses manipulative mechanisms, with and without persuasion instructions.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation built on El-Sayed et al. 2024 mechanisms.

name: Harmful manipulation strategic planning red teaming
description: Models are asked for influence operation plans in 11 real-world scenarios by direct request, jailbreak or adaptive prompting. Reports how often plans are elicited.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. Experts also review the strongest plans.

name: Harmfulness scores on held-out prompts (Anthropic)
aliases: Harmfulness Scores on Held Out Prompts
description: Models answer 328 held-out red-team and jailbreak prompts. A preference model flags responses judged more harmful than a fixed refusal.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation from the Claude 2 model card. Lower is better.

name: Harmlessness human feedback win rate (Anthropic)
description: Raters probe models in adversarial chats and pick the more harmless reply in head-to-head comparisons. Score is the win rate against a baseline model.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. A 50% win rate means equal to the baseline model, which changes between cards.

name: HarnessAudit-Bench
description: Agents run inside execution harnesses such as Claude Code, Codex and OpenClaw on 210 tasks across eight domains, from finance to software engineering, with safety rules built in. The audit reads the full trajectory through channels the agent cannot change. It scores whether the agent stays inside its permission and information-flow policies, completes checkpoints, and keeps both under prompt injection, vague goals and tool errors.
org: UC Santa Barbara, with UC Berkeley, UW-Madison, Stanford and Microsoft Research
note: Tasks run in single-agent and multi-agent setups, and the paper compares 10 harness configurations and 3 multi-agent frameworks. Scores belong to a model and harness pair, not to a model alone. 52 Hugging Face upvotes and about 58 GitHub stars.

name: HarnessDev
description: Agents build a complete agent harness from a minimal seed, then revise their own harness using downstream execution feedback. The harness's task results are the score.
note: 100 HF paper upvotes. Two stages, Creation and Evolution. Sister benchmark of S3Gym on the same project site.

name: HarnessEval-W
description: Video and world models generate rollouts from image and action prompts. An evaluator agent plans checks, spawns sub-agents, gathers spatiotemporal evidence and scores observation, transition and persistence with written reasoning.
org: MirroS Lab with xbench (HongShan) and universities
note: A 100-case public set came out on 2026-09-02. xbench lists it in its AGI Tracking series. The xbench board has 10 models.

name: Harvey LAB (Legal Agent Benchmark)
description: Agent works through legal matter files across 24+ practice areas and produces work product. Expert rubric, task passes only if every criterion passes.

changes.text: Harvey added 500 contracting tasks to LAB. Results covering the expanded benchmark measure a broader task mix than the original law-firm release.
Harvey added a firm-knowledge environment with 250 tasks. Runs including this expansion test retrieval across a much larger document collection.

note: All-pass scoring keeps it far from saturated. Launch results used Harvey's private holdout. Vals HLAB v1.1 (2026-10-21) has 120 holdout tasks, and per-criterion pass is ~93-96%. Harvey ran its own baselines. Vals now runs the board. Repo keeps a score-impact CHANGELOG so results at two commits can be checked for comparability. Dataset field is a community Harbor port (1,760 tasks, not official).

name: Harvey LAB v1.1 (HLAB-Vals-1.1)
description: Agents produce legal work product from matter files with file tools and docx, pptx and xlsx skills. A task passes only if every expert rubric criterion passes.
note: Harvey fixed the 120-task private holdout, removing 17 unsolvable criteria. The harness was resynced with a finish tool and a reasoning-first judge. Vals says scores are not comparable with the v1 board.

name: Harvey LAB-AA v1.0
description: Artificial Analysis runs agents on Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark tasks in an offline sandbox, where they write legal work products such as memos and redlines from case documents. Judges grade each deliverable against a task rubric, and the headline is the share of rubric criteria passed.
note: Artificial Analysis's setup differs from Harvey's, with three judges, exact filenames and no helper scripts, so these scores do not compare with the Harvey LAB record. Version 1.1 replaced this one, and its scores do not compare either.

name: Harvey LAB-AA v1.1
description: Artificial Analysis's run of Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark on Harvey's newer private set of 120 tasks across 24 practice areas. A deliverable with a material hallucination scores zero, and the headline is the share of judges who find every rubric criterion passed.
note: Artificial Analysis says scores do not compare with version 1.0, whose headline was the criterion pass rate. The setup also differs from Harvey's own runs on the Harvey LAB record.

name: Hate & Harassment Safety
description: An autorater checks answers to requests for hateful or harassing content and to sensitive benign prompts. Reports safe response rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: HCAST
description: Agents attempt 189 machine learning, cybersecurity, software engineering and reasoning tasks. 563 human baselines time each task, from one minute to over 8 hours, so success can be read against human task length.
note: HCAST is the largest task source for the METR time horizon. Time Horizon 1.1 added 73 HCAST tasks. At release agents passed 70 to 80% of tasks under one human hour and under 20% of tasks over four hours.

name: Health dynamic conversation eval
description: Simulated users hide key health facts at first, and models must ask for context to reach the correct clinical conclusion.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Health language and locale eval
description: Models answer locale-specific health conversations in 10 languages across 25 locales, with search. Graded against clinician guidelines.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Health static understanding eval
aliases: Static text, document, and image understanding
description: Models answer static health questions over text conversations, documents such as lab reports, and images. Graded against clinician guidelines.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: HealthBench
description: 5,000 realistic health conversations graded against physician-written rubrics. A length-adjusted variant penalizes verbosity.

name: HealthBench Consensus
description: Models answer HealthBench conversations graded only on criteria that several physicians agreed on.
note: Subset of HealthBench. The healthbench record lists this name as an alias.

name: HealthBench Consensus Global Health
description: Models answer health conversations that need adjustment for global context such as local care access. Scored as the failure rate.
note: Subset of HealthBench Consensus defined in the GPT-5 system card.

name: HealthBench Consensus Urgent
description: Models answer ambiguous high-stakes health conversations validated by two or more physicians. Scored as the error rate in informing the user.
note: Subset of HealthBench Consensus defined in the GPT-5 system card.

name: HealthBench Hard
description: Models answer the 1,000 hardest HealthBench conversations, graded against physician-written rubrics.
note: Subset of HealthBench. The healthbench record lists this name as an alias.

name: HealthBench Hard Hallucinations
description: Models respond to difficult health conversations that 2 or more physicians validated. The score is the hallucination rate, so lower is better.
note: OpenAI defined this subset of HealthBench Hard and HealthBench Consensus in the GPT-5 system card.

name: HealthBench Professional
description: 525 physician-authored tasks from real clinician chats (care consult, documentation, research) with physician-adjudicated rubrics.
note: Enriched about 3.5x for examples that are hard for OpenAI models. About one third adversarial.

name: HealthBench-Hallu
description: Models answer HealthBench-style medical prompts. A pipeline splits each answer into medical claims and checks them against medical evidence. The score is a weighted hallucination rate.
note: Refuted claims weigh 1.0 and uncertain claims 0.5. Lower is better.

name: Hebbia Financial Services Benchmark
description: Agents in Hebbia's production harness answer questions over deal and research documents, build Excel models and make client decks. A run passes only if it meets every rubric criterion.
note: 151 private tasks from Hebbia's production work. 10 models in the Fireworks index on 2026-10-29. No maker page with details found.

name: HEIM
description: Text-to-image models are scored on 12 aspects, such as alignment, quality, aesthetics, originality, reasoning, knowledge, bias and toxicity, with human raters and automatic metrics.
note: NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks. Image generation has no own subcategory in the taxonomy, so it sits under video generation.

name: HellaSwag
description: Commonsense sentence completion with adversarially filtered wrong endings. Multiple-choice accuracy.
note: Saturated. GitHub repo rowanz/hellaswag returns HTTP 451 (blocked by a WikiHow DMCA notice dated 2026-09-14), so repo is null.

name: HELM Arabic
description: Stanford CRFM runs models on 7 Arabic benchmarks in the HELM harness and ranks them by mean score. The tasks are AlGhafa, ArabicMMLU, Arabic EXAMS, MadinahQA, AraTrust, ALRAGE and human-translated MMLU.
note: Release v1.0.0 came on 2025-12-18 with 29 models. Release v2.2.0 on 2026-06-25 had 41 models. The task list matches OALL v2, but HELM prompts and scores differ. ALRAGE is model-judged.

name: HELM Arabic Enterprise
description: Models do Arabic enterprise tasks in six parts. They write corporate articles, answer finance questions in three formats, and answer legal questions written by Arabic legal experts with and without the statute.
note: Release v1.0.0 came on 2026-05-26 and v1.1.0 on 2026-06-25 with 35 models. Finance questions are machine translated from English textbooks. A model judges the article and legal tasks.

name: HELM Capabilities
description: Stanford CRFM runs language models on a curated set of scenarios, one per key capability, and averages the scores. Prompt-level results are public.
note: Successor in spirit to HELM Classic and HELM Lite, which CRFM still hosts as separate leaderboards.

name: HELM Classic
description: Models are evaluated with standardized prompts on the scenarios from the original HELM paper. Each scenario reports accuracy, calibration, robustness, fairness, bias, toxicity and efficiency.
note: The last Classic release is v0.4.0 (2023-11-17). HELM Lite and HELM Capabilities replaced it as the main HELM boards.

name: HELM Lite
description: A lightweight HELM board that runs models with in-context learning on ten scenarios. They include NarrativeQA, NaturalQuestions, OpenbookQA, MMLU, GSM8K, MATH, LegalBench, MedQA and WMT 2014.
note: 14 releases from v1.0.0 (2023-12-19) to v1.13.0 (2025-01-10). HELM Capabilities followed in 2025-03.

name: HELM Safety
description: Stanford CRFM runs five safety benchmarks over six risk categories, such as violence, fraud and discrimination, and reports one leaderboard.
note: Version 1.0 evaluated 24 models at launch.

name: HELMET
aliases: How to Evaluate Long-context Models Effectively and Thoroughly
description: Models handle long-context tasks in seven groups including recall, RAG, re-ranking, many-shot learning, long QA and summarization, at set input lengths.
note: Labs often report task groups separately with no overall score. On 2025-02-25 the maker changed ICL preprocessing to 500 samples with balanced labels and new demos. ICL scores after that date differ from the paper.

name: HelpBench
description: 450 real-world privacy, safety and security advice questions across nine topics, scored by rubric for accuracy and tone.
note: Report says data is on GitHub, but no repo was found.

name: Helpfulness violations (from ART)
description: Automated red teaming attackers search for benign prompts where the model gives unhelpful answers. Reports the violation rate found.
note: In-house Google DeepMind automated red teaming. Attackers and judges are prompted or finetuned Gemini models.

name: Hemingway-bench
description: Professional writers compare two models' answers blind on real writing prompts, from bedtime stories to business documents. The comparisons become ratings.
note: More than 5,000 blind pairwise judgments at launch.

name: Hermes Bench
description: Agents in Hermes Agent do 150 tasks across 25 categories, such as research, diagrams, memory, tool use and safety. Graders check the files and state left behind.
note: Launched 2026-10-06 as part of the Hermes Index. 24 tasks are multi-turn.

name: Hermes Index
description: Nous Research averages pass@1 and cost per task over Hermes Bench, Terminal-Bench 4.0, Terminal-Bench Science and SkillsBench, all run in Hermes Agent.
note: The first edition on 2026-10-06 covered 14 models.

name: Hidden agenda
description: Models with a secret goal try to get human participants to click a link, find an email address or run code.
note: Human participant deception study from Phuong et al. 2024. Results are per action with no overall score.

name: HiddenMath
description: Models solve 179 competition-level math problems that experts wrote from scratch. Answers are graded automatically.
note: In-house Google DeepMind set that was never released.

name: HiddenMath-Hard
description: Models solve the harder part of an expert-written, never-published set of AIME and AMC style competition problems.
note: In-house Google DeepMind set. The Gemini 2.5 report uses this harder version instead of full HiddenMath.

name: Hiding a secret password (Anthropic)
description: Models keep a given password secret while an investigator model tries to extract it over many turns. Measures survival and per-turn leak rates.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. Claude Opus 4.6 acts as the investigator in 50 investigations per model.

name: High Stakes factuality prompts
description: Models answer difficult medical, legal and financial prompts. A grader with web access counts responses and claims with factual errors.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Error rates are not production prevalence.

name: High-risk health scenarios eval
description: Adversarial health emergencies test whether models recognize urgency and red flags and direct users to help. Reports pass rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Higher-difficulty benign request evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Models answer harder benign requests that resemble harmful ones. Score is the refusal rate, where lower is better.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Higher-difficulty harmful request evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Models answer harder, more obfuscated policy-violating requests. Score is the harmless response rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: HiL-Bench
description: Coding agents face tasks with hidden blockers such as missing or contradictory requirements. The score rewards asking for help only when a blocker makes it necessary.
note: Harbor also hosts SWE and SQL ask-human splits of 100 tasks each.

name: Hindsight Neglect
description: Models judge whether a bet was worth taking based on expected value rather than its outcome. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Inverse Scaling Prize task where accuracy fell with scale for earlier models.

name: HiPhO
description: Models solve theory problems from 2024 and 2025 physics olympiad exams, some with diagrams. Official marking schemes grade answers and steps, mapped to medal levels.
note: Gemini 3 Pro reached gold-medal level on all 13 original olympiads by December 2025.

name: Historical Jailbreak Regression
description: Replays previously found cyber jailbreak attacks against fixed ExploitBench tasks with real-time blocking turned off. Scored by mean task success rate under attack.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The task set is not public.

name: HLE Calibration
description: Models give a confidence score with each HLE answer. The benchmark reports RMS calibration error and AUROC between confidence and correctness.
org: Center for AI Safety + Scale AI
note: Calibration evaluation layered on the public Humanity's Last Exam. RMS error is on a 0-100 scale.

name: HLE Extended
description: Models answer closed-ended frontier academic questions. Mercor adds 447 new expert-written tasks to the 2158 public ones and reports both scores.
note: Held-out extension of humanitys-last-exam. Mercor shows the original and extended score for each model. The month is approximate. The Wayback Machine first saved the earliest extended pages on 2026-08-15.

name: HLE-Diamond
description: Models answer 1,000 cleaned expert questions from Humanity's Last Exam, 500 on reasoning and 500 on knowledge, closed book. Graded on exact answers.
org: Center for AI Safety and Scale AI
note: The makers built it after a year of cleaning as a migration path for when the original set hits its noise ceiling.

name: HLE-Rolling
description: A dynamic fork of Humanity's Last Exam where the makers remove, fix and re-add questions over time and publish an update log.
org: Center for AI Safety and Scale AI
note: Released 2025-10-08. Releases on 2026-02-20 (166 re-added, 27 removed, 8 updated) and 2026-07-27 (79 added, 6 removed) changed the set, so give the release date with scores.

name: HLE-Verified
description: Verified and revised version of Humanity's Last Exam (1,811 items) with uncertain items removed.
note: Audits all 2,500 HLE items into Gold (668), Revision (1,143) and Uncertain (689) subsets. Check which subset a score uses.

name: HLE-Verified (text-only Full)
description: Models answer the text-only questions of Humanity's Last Exam after expert verification and revision. The Full set keeps the questions experts marked uncertain, and the score is pass@1 accuracy.
note: The paper and its leaderboard chart evaluate this set. The HLE-Verified record covers the 1,811 items with uncertain questions removed. The chart is an image, so its scores are transcribed.

name: HLE-VL
description: Models answer the image-based questions from Humanity's Last Exam, a 330 question subset. Answers are graded against known short or multiple choice answers.
org: Center for AI Safety and Scale AI (HLE), Alibaba Tongyi Lab (VL subset)
note: Qwen reports it with tools, so its scores are not comparable with no-tool HLE runs.

name: HMMT 2025
description: Models answer the 30 problems from the February 2025 Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament. Final answers are checked against the official answers.
note: Model cards use the MathArena version of the February contest, often averaged over many samples.

name: HMMT 2026
description: Models solve the 33 final-answer problems from the February 2026 Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament. Scored by exact answer match.
note: An exam, not a dedicated benchmark. Top models score above 95%.

name: HMMT February 2024
description: Models answer the problems from the February 2024 Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament. Final answers are checked against the official answers.
note: MathArena packages it. Model reports used it before the 2025 edition appeared.

name: HMMT Nov 2025
description: Models solve the 30 problems of the November 2025 Harvard-MIT Mathematics Tournament. Final answers are checked automatically against the answer key.
org: MathArena (ETH Zurich SRI Lab), problems by HMMT

name: Holdings-IndividualTaxBench
aliases: Thrive Holdings individual tax prep benchmark
description: 88 real client document packages turned into Form 1040 fields. Fact-level accuracy against practitioner-reviewed returns, with an LLM judge matching values.
note: Tasks come from Thrive's accounting firms and are not released. OpenAI holds equity in Thrive and the judge is an OpenAI model.

name: Honesty human feedback win rate (Anthropic)
description: Crowdworkers try to make models say something false and pick the more honest reply in head-to-head chats. Score is the win rate against a baseline.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The baseline model was Claude Sonnet 4, so 50% means equal honesty.

name: HoneyBench v0.2-alpha
description: Measures reward hacking: how often an agent games its grader instead of doing the task. Lower is better.
note: Version 0.2-alpha. Labs have published little about its tasks or scoring.

name: Honeypot exploitation monitorability
aliases: Awareness of CoT Monitoring Reduces Monitorability
description: Agents exploit a honeypot while told about a monitor or told to hide it. Scored on CoT and full-context monitor recall.
note: In-house OpenAI monitorability evaluation. Higher recall means more monitorable behavior.

name: HorizonMath
description: Models attack 113 mostly unsolved problems in eight areas of mathematics and the mathematical sciences. A program checks each proposed closed form, construction or bound.
org: University of Oxford, Harvard University, Princeton University and others (Wang et al.)
note: The paper reports six new solutions found by models. Most models score under 10 percent. Tencent reports pass@4.

name: HotpotQA
description: Models answer 113k Wikipedia questions that need facts from several documents. The distractor setting supplies gold and distractor paragraphs. Scored by exact match or F1.
org: Carnegie Mellon University, Stanford University and Mila
note: Labs now often grade answers with an LLM judge instead of exact match.

name: HourVideo
description: Multimodal models answer questions about first-person videos that run 20 to 120 minutes. The 500 videos come from Ego4D, and the 12,976 five-way multiple-choice questions cover summarization, perception, visual reasoning and navigation. Score is accuracy.
note: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks track. Human experts scored 85.0% on a subset, far above every model tested at launch. About 150 GitHub stars.

name: HR-Bench
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about fine details in 4K and 8K resolution images. Results are reported separately for the 4K and 8K sets.
org: Wuhan University and collaborators (Wang et al.)
note: Labs often run it with image crop and zoom tools.

name: HRM8K
description: Models solve 8,011 math problems given as English and Korean parallel pairs. It measures how much math reasoning drops when problems are in Korean.
org: HAE-RAE and OneLineAI (Hyunwoo Ko et al.)
note: Subsets include KSM, built from Korean exam math problems, plus translated GSM8K, MATH, Omni-MATH and MMMLU items.

name: HRM8K-KSM
description: Models solve the 1,428 problems of the Korean School Math subset of HRM8K. Problems come from Korean olympiad and competition exams.
org: HAE-RAE and OneLineAI (Hyunwoo Ko et al.)
note: Scores differ from the full HRM8K average. LG EXAONE cards report this subset as KSM.

name: HuggingFace Agent Benchmark
description: Agents write Python code that calls Hugging Face Transformers tools to solve short tasks. Scores cover tool selection, tools used, and code correctness.
note: It shipped with Transformers Agents, which Hugging Face later replaced with smolagents.

name: HUMAINE
description: Prolific participants, stratified across 22 demographic groups in the US and UK, hold multi-turn conversations with two anonymous models on topics they choose. They compare the models overall and on dimensions such as trust, ethics and safety. A hierarchical Bradley-Terry-Davidson model turns the votes into ratings, adjusted to census data.
note: The paper (ICLR 2026) covers 23,404 participants and 28 models across five dimensions, and the leaderboard keeps adding models. Vague dimensions such as trust, ethics and safety end in ties far more often than the overall choice (65% against 10%). Rankings shift with participant age.

name: Human Behavior Bench
description: Models predict how specified groups of U.S. adults answer closed survey questions, as a distribution over options. Scored as 1 minus total variation distance.
org: Rehearsals with Google DeepMind and Kaggle
note: 1,199 tasks, 239 public and 960 private, from surveys run June to September 2026. Launched 2026-10-20.

name: Human feedback win rates (Anthropic)
description: Raters chat with two models on tasks such as coding, documents and creative writing and pick the better reply. Score is the win rate.
note: Claude 3 era model cards report per-task win rates against a baseline Claude model, with no overall number. The baseline changes between cards.

name: Human Pathogen Capabilities Test
description: Models answer expert-level questions on human pathogens from SecureBio. Scored as accuracy.
note: 100 text-only questions with a private holdout. 13 PhD virologists scored about 31%. Modeled after VCT. A v2 exists on the SecureBio dashboard.

name: Human Pathogen Capabilities Test v2 (HPCT v2)
description: Models answer multiple-response questions on a small set of weaponizable pathogens that biosecurity experts rank highest priority. A revised version of HPCT.
note: Shown as HPCT v2 beside HPCT on the SecureBio dashboard until November 2026. Not public. Revised version so scores are not comparable with HPCT v1. The dashboard now shows only one chart, labeled HPCT, so these scores are the last ones published for v2.

name: Human proximity (Google DeepMind robotics)
description: Models judge from robot camera views whether a human is within 1 meter, a spatial awareness check for safe robot behavior. Scored by accuracy.
note: Reported in the Gemini Robotics ER 2 post. Method details are in the Gemini Robotics 2 Safety Technical Report.

name: Human Sourced Jailbreaks
description: Models face jailbreak prompts collected from human red teaming. Scored as the not_unsafe rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: Human SxS image editing Elo (Google)
description: Google compares edited images side by side and converts human preferences into Elo ratings.
note: The Gemini 3.1 Flash Image and Nano Banana 2.1 model cards report internal human side-by-side image editing ratings.

name: Human SxS image generation Elo (Google)
description: Google compares generated images side by side and converts human preferences into Elo ratings.
note: The Gemini 3.1 Flash Image and Nano Banana 2.1 model cards report internal human side-by-side image generation ratings.

name: HumanEval
description: 164 hand-written Python function problems. Generated code is scored pass@1 against unit tests.
note: Saturated. Reported only for DeepSeek-V4 base model.

name: HumanEval Infilling
description: Models fill in a masked middle span of HumanEval solutions given the code before and after it. Unit tests check the completed function.
note: The harness offers single-line, multi-line, random-span and random-span-light settings. Labs often report single-line and random-span-light separately.

name: HumanEval Multi
description: Models complete HumanEval problems in Python and seven more languages, including C++, Java, PHP, and Bash. Unit tests score pass@1.
note: The non-Python versions come from MultiPL-E translations.

name: HumanEval+
description: Models write Python functions for the 164 HumanEval problems. EvalPlus checks them against about 80 times more tests than the original.

changes.text: The maintainers introduced an optional reduced test suite. Mini evaluations use substantially fewer tests, so reported results should identify that setting.
The maintainers corrected test cases, task 114’s prompt, and several input constraints. Results depend on which HumanEval+ dataset revision the evaluator uses.
The maintainers moved the Docker environment to Python 3.10 and set the default per-test timeout to 0.5 seconds. These changes affect syntax support and timeout outcomes.
The maintainers released further input-constraint and reference-checker corrections. Runs with the updated dataset revision can differ from earlier HumanEval+ evaluations.

note: Scores are pass@1 and run lower than plain HumanEval.

name: HumanEval-COBOL (Cohere)
description: Models write COBOL versions of HumanEval problems, or translate COBOL solutions to Python. Unit tests score pass@1.
note: Cohere built it for the Command A report. The report does not say whether it is released.

name: HumanEval-V
description: Models read a diagram and a function signature, then write Python code that must pass test cases. Tasks span six types of visual reasoning.
org: Fengji Zhang, Jacky Keung et al.
note: Tasks and diagrams are written by hand. Scores are pass@1.

name: HumanEvalPack
description: Models write functions for HumanEval problems translated into Python, JavaScript, Java, Go, C++ and Rust. Hidden tests give pass@1.
org: Hugging Face and BigCode (Muennighoff et al., OctoPack)
note: The pack also has code repair and explanation tasks. Labs usually report the synthesize task.

name: Humanity's Last Exam
description: 2,500 expert-written closed-ended questions across 100+ subjects. Exact-match or multiple-choice answers graded by an LLM judge.
org: Center for AI Safety + Scale AI

changes.text: The maintainers replaced the default answer judge and added a judge-selection option. Scores produced with the previous default use a different grader.
The maintainers finalized HLE at 2,500 questions. Earlier evaluations used a different question set and are not directly comparable.
The maintainers began rolling updates to the question set, restoring 166 questions, removing 27 and updating 8. Scores from before and after use different questions.
A rolling release added 79 questions and removed 6. Scores from before and after use different questions.

note: Finalized at 2,500 questions in April 2025, with a private held-out set to check overfitting. HLE-Rolling and HLE-Diamond are separate records. Trackers disagree by up to about 20 points because tool settings differ.

name: Humanity's Sixth Sense
description: Models answer open-ended questions about what an image or short video implies but does not show, such as hidden objects, causes and intentions. An LLM judge checks each answer against a human-written rubric.
note: 522 tasks on 288 images and 234 video clips. A task counts only if every rubric item is met. People score 93.1% and the best of 25 models 53.6%.

name: HumanoidBench
description: Policies control a simulated Unitree H1 humanoid with dexterous hands on 15 whole-body manipulation and 12 locomotion tasks. Scored by task return or success.
org: UC Berkeley + Yonsei University (Sferrazza et al.)
note: About 800 GitHub stars. Mostly used to test reinforcement learning methods. The README site link (sferrazza.cc) returns 404, so the site link uses humanoid-bench.github.io.

name: HumanoidToolBench
description: Humanoid robot policies pick a suitable tool and use it, walking when needed, across 18 tasks in simulation and on a real Unitree G1.
note: It had 30 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 22 GitHub stars.

name: Hume AI Overall Quality Index
description: Listeners rate generated speech on reliability and expressiveness. The benchmark reports an overall quality index.
note: Hume AI runs the evaluation. No public leaderboard was found, so numbers come from model makers' reports.

name: Hume AI Voice Design Benchmark
description: Listeners rate generated voices for English voice design, multilingual control, accents and voice qualities.
note: Hume AI runs the evaluation. No public leaderboard was found, so numbers come from model makers' reports.

name: HumMusQA
description: Models answer 320 hand-written questions about music, curated and checked by people with musical training.
org: Music Technology Group, Universitat Pompeu Fabra
note: The paper also tests robustness to uni-modal shortcuts.

name: Hungarian National High-School Exam
aliases: Hungarian national high school finals in mathematics
description: Models answer the 33 questions of the 2023 Hungarian national high school mathematics finals. Answers are graded by hand with the official rubric.
org: Keiran Paster (exam by the Hungarian Educational Authority)
note: xAI first used this one exam for Grok-1 because it came after training cutoffs, and hand grading makes scores hard to reproduce.

name: Hunyuan-MT Challenge Testset (Tencent)
description: Models translate between Chinese and English across everyday and specialist domains. Expert raters score each translation from 0 to 4 on marked error-prone points.
note: In-house Tencent evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: HW-Bench
description: Agents complete six hardware engineering tasks for a 2.45 GHz antenna using native design and simulation tools. Code checks and calibrated model judges grade outputs against engineer-written criteria. The headline pass rate measures runs that satisfy every critical criterion, averaged across tasks.
note: Agents run five times per task in the Atlas harness at high reasoning effort. Each task starts from an engineer reference rather than the previous agent output. Arena prohibits automated extraction without written permission. The board dates its initial results to October 29, 2026.

name: Hy-Backend
description: Coding agents complete Tencent in-house backend development tasks. Task and scoring details are not published.
note: Hy3 preview scored 54.7 here, but 12.2 on Hy-Backend 2.0, so the versions are not comparable.

name: Hy-Backend 2.0
description: Coding agents complete Tencent in-house backend development tasks in the Claude Code scaffold. Task and scoring details are not published.
note: Tencent runs it with Claude Code for all models except GPT models, which use Codex.

name: Hy-BrowseComp-Pro2
description: Search agents answer hard browsing questions in a Tencent in-house set named after BrowseComp. Task and scoring details are not published.
note: Not an OpenAI release. Tencent runs it with its internal harness.

name: Hy-CompanyBench
description: Coding agents complete Tencent in-house company engineering tasks. Task and scoring details are not published.
note: Hy3 scored 41.7 here and 29.8 on V2, so the versions are not comparable.

name: Hy-CompanyBench V2
description: Coding agents complete a second version of Tencent in-house company engineering tasks. Task and scoring details are not published.

name: Hy-Euler pro
description: Models with tools solve Tencent in-house STEM problems. Task and scoring details are not published.
note: Tencent lists it under STEM Agent.

name: Hy-FinAgentBench
description: Agents complete Tencent in-house finance analyst tasks. Task and scoring details are not published.

name: Hy-FinModelBench
description: Agents build financial models for Tencent in-house finance tasks. Task and scoring details are not published.
note: Hy3 scored 69.0 here and 28.6 on v2, so the versions are not comparable.

name: Hy-FinmodelBench v2
description: Agents build financial models for a second version of Tencent in-house finance tasks. Task and scoring details are not published.

name: Hy-LifeSearch
description: Search agents answer Tencent in-house everyday life questions with web search. Task and scoring details are not published.
note: Tencent runs all agentic search tests with its internal harness.

name: Hy-Math
description: Models solve Tencent in-house math problems without tools. Task and scoring details are not published.

name: Hy-SkillsWorld
description: Agents use skills to complete Tencent in-house working tasks. Task and scoring details are not published.

name: Hy-SWE Max
description: Coding agents solve 300 Tencent in-house software tasks in Claude Code with a 200-turn budget and no web access. Hidden verifier tests grade each task.
note: The Hy4 preview card renames it Hy-SWE Max Verified and gives the same Hy3 score (49.0), so it stays one record. Results average 3 runs.

name: Hy-Vibe Bench
description: Coding agents complete development workflows drawn from real Tencent users. Task and scoring details are not published.
note: Seen only in the Hy3 preview card.

name: Hypersim
description: Models localize named objects as 3D boxes in synthetic indoor Hypersim images, using the Omni3D test split. Scored by mAP at IoU 0.15.
note: A dataset used by Qwen as a 3D grounding test, not a standalone LLM benchmark.

name: HyperTask
description: Agents build applications over long vibe coding sessions with about 100 feature or step requirements per task. Expert rubrics score the result over three trials.
note: In-house MiniMax evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: IChO 2025
description: Models solve the written theoretical problems of the 57th International Chemistry Olympiad, held in Dubai in July 2025. Answers are graded against the official marking scheme.
org: International Chemistry Olympiad (hosted by the UAE Ministry of Education)
note: Labs grade the written theory section themselves and report medal levels, so scores across labs may use different graders. The dataset link is the official preparatory problems, not the exam.

name: ICPC World Finals 2025
description: Models solve the 12 problems of the 2025 ICPC World Finals under contest time and attempt limits. Scored by problems solved.
note: A one-time contest. Labs run their own judging and submission limits, so results are not strictly comparable.

name: IF-Badcase
description: Models follow 450 multi-constraint instructions drawn from real user failure reports. A checklist checks each constraint.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: IFBench
description: 58 new out-of-domain verifiable output constraints. Scored by programmatic constraint checks (strict or loose).

changes.text: The maintainers revised the leaderboard after fixing IFBench verifiers. Earlier published scores can differ from the revised results.
The maintainers fixed verifier crashes, case handling, tokenization, and word-boundary matching. The revised checks can assign different results to identical responses.
The maintainers fixed six instruction verifiers that incorrectly accepted or rejected responses. Scores can move in either direction without changing the task set.

note: The maker fixed several verifiers in 2026, including six that mis-scored correct answers (2026-07-17), so later runs can score slightly higher. Task set unchanged. An optional two-turn split is in IFBench_multi-turn.

name: IFEval
description: Models answer about 500 prompts containing verifiable instructions such as word limits or required keywords. Code checks each instruction for strict and loose accuracy.
note: Frontier models now score near 90 percent, so it is close to saturation.

name: IFEval (Mistral internal version)
description: Models follow prompts with verifiable format constraints. Mistral uses its own fixed version of IFEval.
note: Mistral says scores are not comparable with public IFEval scores.

name: IFEval-OOD
description: Models answer unseen WildChat prompts with added verifiable constraints drawn from 52 types outside IFEval. Scored by prompt-level loose accuracy.
note: Ai2 built it for the Tulu 3 unseen suite. Ai2's later eval code runs the ifeval_ood task on the IFBench test set, so later scores may follow IFBench.

name: IFMTBench
description: Models translate text while following explicit instructions, such as keeping JSON or HTML structure, using a glossary, using provided context and matching a register. It covers seven languages with 4,506 single-constraint and 2,838 multi-constraint items. Deterministic checkers verify some constraints, and a rubric-based model judge scores the rest.
note: Tencent released it with its Hy-MT2 translation models on 2026-05-21 and reports it in the Hy-MT2 report. The repository stars (about 1,500) belong to the Hy-MT2 model release, not to the benchmark alone.

name: IFStruct
description: Models generate JSON or YAML that must follow a requested schema and phrasing constraints, without constrained decoding. A response passes only if every structural constraint holds.
note: 2,000 frozen test prompts. The makers say it saturates near 100% for frontier models and targets small models.

name: IHEval
description: Models face conflicts between system, user and tool instructions. Reports a composite score for following the higher-priority instruction.
note: Instruction hierarchy benchmark. Meta reports a composite across conflict types.

name: Image generation refusals
description: Models decide whether to call the image generation tool on human-curated adversarial prompts with system mitigations on. Scored on not_unsafe and not_overrefuse.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Scores include system-level mitigations.

name: Image input safety evaluations
description: Models answer harmful prompts that combine text and images in categories such as hate, extremism and self-harm. Scored as safe completion rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report category scores with no overall number.

name: Image to Text Safety
aliases: Image to Text Safety (lower is better)
description: An automated content safety evaluation measures policy violations when prompts combine images and text.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. Model cards report only the change in percentage points against an earlier Gemini model.

name: Image-to-WebDev Arena
description: Users upload a screenshot, wireframe or mockup, two anonymous models build the website in Code Arena, and users vote for the better result. Votes become ratings with bootstrapped confidence intervals.
note: On 2026-10-19 the board listed 65 models and 191,568 votes. It is a separate board from the text-prompt Code Arena WebDev board.

name: Image2FloorPlan
description: Models study several real photos of a home and draw its floor plan. Scored by an average quality score.
note: In-house Seed evaluation set. The card does not say how the average score is computed, so the scoring field is a guess.

name: Image2Struct
description: Vision-language models turn images of webpages, LaTeX and musical scores into code that renders them. The render is compared with the input image.
note: Fresh test data is downloaded from active online communities at run time. Three releases from v1.0.0 to v1.0.2.

name: ImageMining
description: Multimodal agents retrieve and reason over image information for image mining tasks.
note: GLM-5V-Turbo reports this in its official documentation table.

name: IMC 2025
aliases: International Mathematics Competition for University Students 2025
description: Models write proofs for the 10 problems of the 2025 International Mathematics Competition for University Students. Human judges grade each proof.
note: MathArena graded only three Gemini systems, all above the gold threshold of 56 percent.

name: ImgEdit-Bench
description: Image editing models carry out edit instructions such as add, remove, replace, style transfer and background change. A GPT-4.1 judge scores each result from 1 to 5.
note: The benchmark ships with the 1.2 million pair ImgEdit dataset and has basic, hard single-turn and multi-turn suites.

name: Immigration Bench
description: Models answer expert-written US immigration law questions from seven personas, such as F-1 students, employers and DACA recipients. An AI grader checks each answer against an expert rubric.
org: Vals AI + Talent Mobility Fund (Renaissance Philanthropy)
note: Experts wrote 519 questions. Vals reports on a private 262-question test set and reserves the other 257 for labs to license. Score is the share of rubric items met.

name: IMO 2025
description: Models write full proofs for the six problems of the 2025 International Mathematical Olympiad. Graders score proofs out of 42 points, mapped to medal cutoffs.
org: International Mathematical Olympiad, hosted by the Australian Maths Trust
note: This is a one-time competition exam, not a maintained benchmark.

name: IMO 2026
description: Models write full proofs for the six problems of the 2026 International Mathematical Olympiad. Proofs are scored out of 42 points.
org: International Mathematical Olympiad, hosted in Shanghai, China
note: A one-time competition exam held July 15 and 16, 2026. Labs grade proofs with their own rubrics or judges.

name: IMO Shortlist 2024
description: Models write proofs for the 31 problems of the 2024 IMO Shortlist. DeepSeek scores the proofs with its own verifier model.
note: A one-time problem set, not a maintained benchmark. The IMO publishes each shortlist after the next IMO, here July 2025.

name: IMO-AnswerBench
description: 400 olympiad problems with short verifiable answers, robustified against memorization. Scored by answer match.

changes.text: The maintainers replaced the original file with answerbench_v2.csv to correct ambiguous questions and incorrect answers. Scores using the deprecated file can differ.

note: Part of IMO-Bench (EMNLP 2025) with IMO-ProofBench, IMO-GradingBench and IMO-LeanProofBench. On 2026-02-12 a v2 file fixed ambiguous problems and wrong answers in place, so check which file a score used.

name: IMO-GradingBench
description: Models grade 1,000 olympiad proof attempts, and their grades are compared with human expert grades. Tests automatic evaluation of long-form math answers.
note: Part of IMO-Bench (EMNLP 2025).

name: IMO-LeanProofBench
description: Models write Lean 4 proofs for the 60 IMO-ProofBench problems, formalized by hand and checked by Lean experts. The Lean compiler verifies each proof.
note: Introduced with the LEAP paper. One-shot Gemini 3.1 Pro solved 11.6 percent and the LEAP agent 70 percent. The August 2026 v2 file fixed wrong formalizations for Mathlib 4.27.0.

name: IMO-ProofBench
description: Models write proofs for 60 olympiad problems, split into a basic set and an advanced set up to IMO-hard. Each proof is graded from 0 to 7 by experts or a Gemini autograder.
note: Part of IMO-Bench (EMNLP 2025). The v2 file only fixed a typo.

name: Impossible tasks (Anthropic)
description: Agents work on coding problems designed to be impossible. Score is the rate at which they hack instead of giving up.
note: Run with no prompt and with an anti-hack prompt. The no-prompt rate is the default setting.

name: Impossible Tasks Evaluation
description: Agents get paired impossible and solvable tasks. Scores infeasibility recognition, fabrication, circumvention and helpfulness.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: ImpossibleBench
description: Coding agents get tasks whose unit tests conflict with the specification. Reports how often they cheat by changing tests or special-casing.
note: Measures reward hacking as a cheating rate.

name: ImpossibleMLEBench
description: Agents get ML tasks with instructions to reach impossibly good scores. Observers check whether they cheat and whether they disclose it.
note: Third-party UK AISI evaluation. The GPT-5.6 card describes results in words without a score.

name: IMProofBench
description: Agents with web search and SageMath write proofs for private PhD-level problems written by mathematicians. Experts grade the proofs, and final-answer subquestions are graded automatically.
