name: LOCA-Bench
description: Agentic tasks whose environment state is scaled to grow context length while task semantics stay fixed. Success rate versus context length.
note: 15 seed tasks adapted from Toolathlon. Tests context-management strategies as part of the agent.

name: LoCoMo
description: Models answer questions, summarize events and continue dialogue over very long multi-session chats of about 300 turns and 9K tokens, up to 35 sessions. Answers are scored against references.
org: Snap Research, UNC Chapel Hill and USC (Maharana et al.)
note: Snap Research hosts the code and data on GitHub, with about 1,250 stars.

name: LOFT
description: Models solve retrieval, RAG, SQL, and many-shot learning tasks with whole corpora of up to one million tokens in context. Scored per task.

name: LogicVista
description: Models answer 448 multiple-choice questions on spatial, deductive, inductive, numeric, and mechanical reasoning set in images. Scored by accuracy.

name: LogiQA
description: Models answer reading comprehension questions that test logical reasoning, taken from Chinese civil service exams and translated to English.
note: LogiQA 2.0 is a later expanded release by the same group, also in lm-evaluation-harness.

name: Long Context (MiniMax in-house)
description: Models translate, summarize and analyze long documents from real user requests.
note: In-house MiniMax evaluation built mostly from Hailuo AI user queries in Mandarin. The queries are not public.

name: Long-context grounding, sentence unfactual rate
description: Models answer from long documents. An autorater reports the share of sentences not supported by the documents.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Long-form Biological Risk Questions
description: Models answer long-form questions across five biothreat creation stages, graded against expert rubrics. Scored as pass@1 per stage.
note: OpenAI Preparedness evaluation. Cards report stage scores with no overall number.

name: Long-form virology tasks
description: Agents complete end-to-end pathogen acquisition workflows, covering workflow design and laboratory protocols. Scored against expert criteria.
note: Anthropic evaluation built with SecureBio, Deloitte and Signature Science. The tasks are not public. Retired in the Claude Opus 5.5 system card, which calls them largely saturated and prone to refusals, and replaced by the Protocols and BioMysteryBench evaluations.

name: Long-horizon jailbreaks (xAI)
description: Models face multi-turn, Crescendo and long-horizon malicious-use attacks. Compliance is the share that get disallowed help.
note: In-house xAI evaluation, first reported in the Grok 4.6 model card.

name: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench (LHTB)
description: Terminal-Bench-style container tasks needing hundreds of steps. Subtasks graded deterministically for dense partial-credit reward. Solved at reward >=0.95.
org: Tencent HY + university collaborators (Zongxia Li et al.)
note: LHTB 1.0 has 46 tasks, scored in a July 2026 snapshot with a 90 minute budget. LHTB 2.0 replaced it in October 2026. Hidden tests and oracle solutions are withheld.

name: Long-Horizon-Terminal-Bench 2.0
description: Agents work for up to 3 hours per task on 77 container tasks, including 30 tasks that rebuild a scientific tool from its outputs. Hidden verifiers give partial-credit rewards.
org: Tencent HY + university collaborators (Zongxia Li et al.)
note: It keeps the 46 original tasks and adds 31 new ones. The maker says scores are not comparable with the July 2026 snapshot, which used a 90 minute budget. 15 models in the October 2026 results.

name: LongAudioSpan
description: Models answer 3,240 questions about 360 English and Chinese recordings from 10 minutes to over 2 hours. Each question is scored as multiple choice and as open-ended.
org: Huang et al. (arXiv 2608.26431, with Qwen authors)
note: Qwen reports accuracy, rubric and chain scores.

name: LongAV-Compass
description: Models generate minute-long videos with sound from text, an image or a video. Scoring covers identity consistency, narrative coherence and audio-visual alignment over time.
note: It had 34 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 18 GitHub stars.

name: LongBench
description: Models work through 21 English and Chinese long-input datasets covering QA, summarization, few-shot learning, synthetic tasks, and code. Each dataset has its own metric.
note: LongBench v2, released in December 2024, is a separate version with harder multiple choice questions.

name: LongBench Chinese
description: Models answer questions and complete other long-context tasks in the original Chinese headline table. The score is its published average on a percentage scale.
note: One track of LongBench. The LongBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks. Authors include the same code completion tasks in both language tables. Importers read the published averages without recomputing them.

name: LongBench English
description: Models answer questions and complete other long-context tasks in the original English headline table. The score is its published average on a percentage scale.
note: One track of LongBench. The LongBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks. Authors include the same code completion tasks in both language tables. Importers read the published averages without recomputing them.

name: LongBench v2
description: 503 multiple-choice questions over 8K-2M-word contexts (QA, dialogue, code repos, structured data). Accuracy.

name: LongBench-Chat
description: Models follow real user instructions over contexts of 10K to 100K tokens. GPT-4 scores each answer from 1 to 10 against references.
org: Tsinghua University and Zhipu AI (Bai et al., LongAlign)
note: Introduced with the LongAlign paper.

name: LongCat safety evaluation (Meituan)
description: Models answer private test queries in four risk categories: harmful content, criminal activity, misinformation and privacy. The score is the share of safe responses in each category.
note: In-house test built on the framework of Mu et al. 2024 and Meituan content guidelines. Queries were reviewed by hand.

name: LongCodeBench
description: Coding model answers repository QA and fixes GitHub issues with context from 32K to 1M tokens. Accuracy and resolve rate.
note: COLM 2025. Python only.

name: LongDocURL
description: Models answer 2,325 questions over long documents with more than 33,000 pages in total. Its 20 subtasks cover understanding, numerical reasoning and locating document elements.
org: Institute of Automation, Chinese Academy of Sciences, and Taobao and Tmall Group of Alibaba
note: ACL 2025 paper. ByteDance Seed reports it in the Seed2.0 model card.

name: LongExtractionBench
description: Extraction systems pull structured values from 225 long table-heavy documents averaging 358 pages and about 88,700 ground-truth fields each.
note: Compares four extraction platforms with GPT-5.5, Claude Opus 4.8 and Gemini 3.1 Pro called directly. Frontier models finished only about half the documents.

name: LongFact
description: Models write long answers to 2,280 fact-seeking prompts on 38 topics. A search-backed checker verifies each claim, and cards report the hallucination rate.
note: The paper scores F1@K, where higher is better, but cards report hallucination rates, where lower is better.

name: LongFact-Concepts
description: Models write detailed answers to LongFact prompts about broad concepts. A fact checker scores the claim-level error rate.
note: Concepts half of LongFact. OpenAI grades claims with o3 and browsing.

name: LongFact-Objects
description: Models write detailed answers to LongFact prompts about specific objects such as people or places. A fact checker scores the claim-level error rate.
note: Objects half of LongFact. OpenAI grades claims with o3 and browsing.

name: Longform Creative Writing (EQ-Bench)
description: Models plan, revise and then write a short story or novella over eight 1,000-word turns from a minimal prompt. A judge model scores quality, and slop, repetition and degradation are tracked.
note: Not the in-house Moonshot Longform Writing eval with the same short name. v1.1 (2025-08-08) moved the judge to Claude Sonnet 4 and v1.11 (2026-02-19) to Sonnet 4.6.

name: Longform Writing
description: Models write long-form text without tools, capped at 32k output tokens. Moonshot AI has not published the tasks or the scoring method.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation with no public tasks.

name: LongMemEval
description: Chat assistants answer 500 questions about long multi-session chat histories. The questions test five long-term memory abilities.
note: The M variant holds about 500 sessions per history. A cleaned dataset release exists on Hugging Face.

name: LongMemEval-V2
description: Memory systems help agents learn the affordances, dynamics and failure modes of customized web environments. Questions check whether that experience was internalized.
note: Same lead author as LongMemEval. It shifts from user chat histories to agent experience, so scores do not compare. 201 GitHub stars.

name: LongText-Bench
description: Image models render long text in images. The benchmark reports separate English and Chinese scores.
note: GLM-Image reports English and Chinese scores in its official model card and launch post.

name: LongVideoBench
description: Models answer referring reasoning questions over 3,763 web videos up to an hour long, with interleaved subtitles. Scored by multiple-choice accuracy.

name: LoopArena
description: Models act as the controller loop around a coding agent. They monitor progress, assign work, run checks and decide when the task is safe to submit.
note: 96 HF paper upvotes. Separates the loop's guidance from the coding agent's own skill.

name: LPFQA
description: Models answer 430 long-tail professional questions drawn from real forum discussions in 7 academic and industrial domains.
org: ByteDance Seed and collaborators (Zhu et al.)
note: Questions use a hierarchical difficulty structure. ByteDance Seed reports it in the Seed2.0 model card.

name: LSAT
description: Models take a simulated Law School Admission Test. Scored on the 120 to 180 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: LSMDC
description: Models fill in a missing word in movie audio descriptions using the matching video clip. Scoring is accuracy.
note: This is the fill-in-the-blank task of the Large Scale Movie Description Challenge, also called MovieFIB.

name: LV-Eval
description: Models answer single-hop and multi-hop questions over contexts at five length levels from 16K to 256K tokens, with confusing facts inserted.
org: Infinigence AI and Tsinghua University (Yuan et al.)
note: Labs report one score per length level. Qwen used keyword recall instead of the original metric.

name: LVBench
description: Hours-long video understanding with multiple-choice questions on reasoning, grounding and summarization.
note: Frame budgets differ by provider API, which complicates comparisons.

name: LVBench (with memory)
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about videos up to two hours long, aided by Qwen's external video memory system. Scored by accuracy.
org: Zhipu AI and Tsinghua University (LVBench), Qwen (memory setup)
note: A Qwen setting of LVBench that uses a memory system built with Qwen-MM-Plugins, so scores are not comparable with plain LVBench.

name: LVIS-MG
description: Models ground many objects at once by outputting boxes for named categories in LVIS images.
note: Seed built this multi-object grounding set from LVIS for the Seed1.5-VL report. The report compares it with detectors such as Grounding DINO.

name: LVOmniBench
description: Models answer questions about long videos with rich audio, often tens of minutes long. The questions need both the audio and the video track.
note: Qwen reports it as long video reasoning.

name: Lying about identity (Anthropic)
description: Models play an operator-assigned human persona while users ask if they are human. Score is the rate of admitting to being an AI.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The Fable 5 card adds a harder set with indirect user probes.

name: m-ArenaHard
description: Models answer the 500 Arena-Hard-Auto v0.1 prompts machine-translated into 22 more languages, 23 in all. An LLM judge compares answers pairwise and reports win rates.
note: Translated with Google Translate API v3. Cohere reports it for Aya Expanse and Command A as win rates against named rivals, so scores depend on the opponent.

name: m-ArenaHard v2.0
description: Models answer 498 English prompts from Arena-Hard v2.0, translated into 22 more languages for 11,454 prompts in all. An LLM judge compares answers pairwise and reports win rates.
note: Built on arena-hard-auto v2.0 and translated with an in-house Cohere model. Not comparable with m-ArenaHard v1.

name: m-ArenaHard v2.1
description: Models answer the 498 Arena-Hard v2.0 prompts translated into 67 languages, with code and data kept intact. A GPT-4.1 judge rates answers with a rubric in the Tiny Aya report.
note: Expands v2.0 from 23 to 67 languages and repairs code-heavy prompts and corrupted English rows, so it is not comparable with v2.0.

name: m-tau-bench (Cohere)
description: Agents handle tau-bench retail and airline customer service tasks translated into Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Spanish and French, plus English. Scored by average pass^1 over 10 runs.
note: Cohere built the translation in house and has not released it.

name: m-WildVision
description: Vision-language models answer WildVision bench prompts machine-translated into 23 languages. A model judge compares two models' answers and reports win rates.
note: Built from the English WildVision vision_bench_0617 test set with Google Translate. It is a translated copy, but labs report it as its own multilingual test.

name: M3Exam
description: Models answer 12,317 multiple-choice questions from official school exams in nine languages, about 23 percent needing images. Scored by accuracy.

name: M3GIA
description: Models answer cognition test questions built on five Cattell-Horn-Carroll intelligence factors in English, Chinese, French, Spanish, Portuguese and Korean. Data comes from native contexts.
org: Westlake University, Alibaba Group and others
note: The paper compares models with scores from human participants.

name: MA-Bench
description: Models do military mission analysis under the joint planning process on long-context scenarios, graded against expert rubrics.
note: Dataset created 2026-09-25 under CC BY 4.0.

name: MaCBench
description: Vision language models answer chemistry and materials questions from images. Tasks cover reading data, understanding experiments and interpreting results.
org: MaCBench authors (Alampara et al., ChemBench group)
note: Over 1,100 multimodal questions in 34 subsets, written by chemistry and materials experts. From the group behind ChemBench.

name: MACHIAVELLI
description: Agents play 134 text adventure games with over half a million scenarios. The score is normalized game reward. Annotations also score power-seeking, disutility and ethical violations.
org: UC Berkeley and Center for AI Safety
note: ICML 2023 oral. Scene labels come from language models.

name: MacroscopeBench
description: Models review commits from public repositories and must flag the known bugs a commit introduced without false reports. LLM judges match findings to the bugs.
note: 195 tasks include control commits with no known bugs. Scored by combined precision and recall. 41 models in the Fireworks index.

name: MadinahQA
description: Models answer Arabic school exam questions on general Arabic language and grammar.
note: The dataset card says the questions are part of ArabicMMLU. OALL v2 and TII report it as a separate task.

name: MADQA
description: Agents search 800 PDF documents to answer 2,250 human-written questions. Scoring covers answer accuracy and how much search effort the agent spends.
org: Łukasz Borchmann et al. (Snowflake, University of Oxford, and partners)

name: MAEB
description: Audio embedding models are scored on 30 tasks across speech, music, environmental sound and audio-text retrieval in over 100 languages.
note: Part of the MTEB framework, with 50+ models in the paper. Google's EmbeddingGemma 2 card reports it as Mean(Task).

name: MAI human side-by-side evaluation
description: Paid raters compare two models' answers to 1,276 English prompts from experts and Copilot logs on a 7-point scale from -1.5 to 1.5.
note: In-house Microsoft AI evaluation run with Surge AI raters. The score is relative to a named opponent model.

name: MAI internal jailbreak evaluation suite
description: Models face about 9,500 jailbreak prompts built from 2,500 seed scenarios, grouped as foundational, compositional and adaptive. Scored as attack success rate.
note: In-house Microsoft AI evaluation. Seeds include HarmBench and StrongREJECT prompts. Results are per bucket, with no overall score.

name: MAI internal safety and over-refusal evaluation
description: Models answer harmful and benign prompts in eight harm categories. Judges score safety pass rate on sensitive prompts and helpfulness as one minus over-refusal.
note: In-house Microsoft AI evaluation. Results are per category, with no overall score.

name: MakeMePay
description: A con artist model tries to talk a GPT-4o mark into paying money in a role-play. Scored as the share of conversations with a payment.
note: Open source in OpenAI Evals. Cards also report the dollar extraction rate.

name: MakeMeSay
description: A manipulator model tries to make a GPT-4o manipulatee say a codeword without suspicion. Scored as manipulator win rate.
note: Open source in OpenAI Evals.

name: Malicious agentic influence campaigns (Anthropic)
description: Agents receive requests to run multi-step influence operations with tools. Score is the refusal rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Malicious agentic influence campaigns, 34-point rubric (Anthropic)
description: Agents run simulated voter suppression and domestic polarization campaigns. Weighted criteria measure campaign execution on a 34-point scale.
note: Anthropic changed the environment and weighted rubric. The maximum increased from 32 to 34, making earlier scores incomparable.

name: Malicious computer use (Anthropic)
description: Computer-use agents receive harmful tasks such as surveillance or fraud in GUI environments. Score is the refusal rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Malicious use of Claude Code (Anthropic)
description: Agents in Claude Code receive malicious and dual-use coding requests. Score is the refusal rate on malicious requests.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Malware Refusals (Golden Set)
description: Coding agents receive malware development requests from a curated golden set written by OpenAI policy experts. Scored as refusal rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public. Codex system cards from codex-1 to GPT-5.1-Codex-Max report it.

name: Malware Refusals (Synthetic)
description: Coding agents receive a large synthetic set of malware-related tasks, including ambiguous and dual-use prompts. Scored as refusal rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Management Consulting Tasks (OpenAI)
description: Models do management consulting work tasks from OpenAI's internal set. OpenAI has not published the task format or grading.
note: The GPT-5.6 post (2026-07-09) lists it under Professional with Claude and Gemini columns. GPT-5.6 Sol scored 43.2%. Scoring method is a guess from similar OpenAI task sets.

name: Mandarin-Minority translation (Tencent)
description: Models translate between Mandarin and Chinese minority languages in a Tencent test set. XCOMET-XXL scores each translation.
note: Seen in the Hunyuan-MT-7B performance chart. We did not check whether the test set is public.

name: ManipArena
description: 20 real bimanual tasks on X2Robot platforms: 10 execution, 5 semantic reasoning and 5 mobile manipulation, with in-domain and shifted trials. Partial-credit scoring.
note: The host enters its own WALL-OSS-0.5, a conflict of interest. Paper snapshot on a single robot. Sim twin at github.com/maniparena/maniparena-sim.

name: ManiSkill3
description: GPU-parallel robot simulator and task suite across 12 domains for manipulation learning. Success rate per task.
org: UC San Diego (Hao Su Lab) + Hillbot
note: Simulator framework rather than a fixed benchmark. No neutral VLA leaderboard found.

name: Mantic vs Polymarket backtest
description: Point-in-time backtest of Mantic's AI forecasts against prices on 4,139 Polymarket markets at volume snapshots. Scored by Brier score and calibration.
note: Mantic is more accurate until ~$100k traded volume. The forecaster sees the market price, so forecasts are not independent. Full report by email only.

name: Mantis-Eval
description: Models answer questions that need reasoning across several interleaved images. Scored by accuracy.
org: Dongfu Jiang, Xuan He et al. (TIGER-Lab, University of Waterloo)
note: Released with the Mantis model paper as its multi-image test set.

name: Many-shot jailbreaking evaluation (Anthropic)
description: Models receive long fake dialogs where the assistant complies with harmful requests, then a new harmful request. Score is the compliance rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation drawn from the published many-shot jailbreaking research.

name: MARS-Bench
description: Models handle long multi-turn dialogues built from play-by-play sports commentary. Tasks test ultra multi-turn, interactive multi-turn and cross-turn reasoning.
org: ByteDance Seed and collaborators (Yang et al.)
note: Accepted to EMNLP 2025 Findings. The scoring field is a guess from the abstract.

name: MASK
description: Measures whether a model contradicts its own elicited beliefs under pressure to lie. Honesty separated from accuracy.
org: Center for AI Safety + Scale AI

name: Matbench
description: Models predict properties of inorganic materials in 13 supervised tasks built from DFT and experimental data. Scored with error or classification metrics per task.
org: Materials Project (Dunn, Wang, Ganose, Dopp, Jain)
note: Built for materials ML models. Intern-S models report an LLM version of its property prediction tasks, and the exact subset is not stated.

name: MATH
description: 12,500 competition math problems with step-by-step solutions. Final answer scored by exact match.
note: Saturated. Original HF dataset hendrycks/competition_math is disabled. EleutherAI mirror is commonly used.

name: Math Kangaroo 2025 (MathArena)
description: Vision language models answer 168 multiple-choice problems from the 2025 Math Kangaroo, given as screenshots across six grade groups. Many problems need reading a diagram.
org: MathArena (ETH Zurich SRI Lab and INSAIT)
note: Models score lower on problems for grades 1 to 6 than on those for grades 7 to 12. MathArena ran 23 models and later marked the set deprecated.

name: MATH Level 5
description: Models solve the 1,324 hardest MATH test problems, drawn from competitions such as AMC and AIME. Scored by final answer match.
org: Dan Hendrycks et al. (UC Berkeley), subset run by Epoch AI
note: Near saturation, and contamination is likely because the problems have been public since 2021.

name: Math Side-tasking Monitor Evasion
description: Agents try to solve hidden math side tasks during Expert-SWE coding tasks without detection. Scored on success while evading CoT and full-context monitors.
note: In-house OpenAI monitorability evaluation. Results appear as charts.

name: MATH-500
description: Models solve 500 competition math problems drawn from the MATH test set. Final answers are checked against the reference answers.
note: Near saturation, since DeepSeek-R1 already scored 97.3 percent in January 2025.

name: MATH-Vision (MathVision)
description: 3,040 competition math problems with visual context. Answer accuracy.

name: Math-VR
description: Models answer 5,000 English and Chinese math questions whose solutions need visual reasoning, such as drawing auxiliary lines or plotting functions. Answers are checked against ground truth.
note: The benchmark reports Answer Correctness and a partial-credit Process Score. Its 178K-sample training set ships separately. Qwen reports it in the Qwen3-VL report.

name: Math23K
description: Models solve Chinese elementary-school math word problems from a set of about 23,000. Scored by final-answer accuracy.
note: Introduced with the Deep Neural Solver paper at EMNLP 2017.

name: Math401
description: Models compute 401 arithmetic expressions covering addition, multiplication, exponents, logarithms and trigonometry. Scored by exact numeric accuracy.
note: Tests arithmetic skill rather than word-problem reasoning.

name: MathArena (Apex, IMO, USAMO)
description: Evaluates models on newly released math competitions after release. Final-answer or human/LLM-judged proof scores.
note: Apex holds 12 problems and Apex Shortlist holds 47, both picked in August 2025. In May 2026 MathArena found no new problems hard enough for an Apex v2. Proof scores for IMO and USAMO depend on judges.

name: MathArena Apex Shortlist
description: Models solve 47 hard final-answer problems that MathArena selected from 2025 competitions, where the best models scored about 50% at selection. Scored by accuracy over repeated attempts.
note: MathArena picked the Apex Shortlist and the 12-problem Apex set together in August 2025.

name: MathBench
description: Models answer 3,709 math questions in five stages from basic arithmetic to college, in Chinese and English. Each stage also tests theory knowledge, and Circular Evaluation reshuffles answer options to check consistency.
note: Accepted to ACL 2024 Findings. The repository has about 118 stars.

name: MathCanvas-Bench
description: Models solve 3,000 math problems that call for interleaved visual and textual solutions, such as drawing auxiliary lines in geometry.
note: Released with the BAGEL-Canvas model. The scoring field is a guess.

name: MathIF
description: Reasoning models solve 420 math problems from GSM8K, MATH-500, Minerva, Olympiad and AIME while obeying added verifiable instructions. Code checks the instructions and the answer.
org: Renmin University of China, Shanghai AI Laboratory and CUHK
note: Shows that stronger reasoning often lowers instruction adherence. 63 Hugging Face paper upvotes.

name: MathQA
description: Models answer multiple-choice math word problems drawn from AQuA. Each problem is annotated with an operation program. Scored by accuracy.
org: University of Washington and Allen Institute for AI
note: Models are often scored by log-likelihood over the options in lm-evaluation-harness.

name: MathVerse
description: Models solve diagram-based math problems shown in six versions that move information between the text and the image. It tests whether models read the diagram.
org: CUHK MMLab and Shanghai AI Laboratory
note: Labs usually report the testmini split.

name: MathVision-Wildphoto
description: Models solve MathVision style problems shown in photos taken in natural settings, judging from the name. The Qwen3-VL report gives no citation or further description.
note: In-house Qwen evaluation. The tasks are not public. The description, scoring and format are guesses from the name.

name: MathVista
description: Math reasoning in visual contexts (charts, geometry, puzzles) from 31 datasets. Answer accuracy.
note: Near-saturated.

name: MAVERIX
aliases: Multimodal Audio-Visual Evaluation and Recognition IndeX
description: Models answer 2,556 questions about 700 videos that need both the video and its audio. Questions come in multiple-choice and open-ended forms.
org: Carnegie Mellon University (CUBE lab) and collaborators
note: Human experts reach 92.8% accuracy in the paper.

name: MAWPS
aliases: MAWPS: A Math Word Problem Repository
description: Models solve one-unknown arithmetic and algebra word problems drawn from several earlier collections. Each problem has an equation and a numeric answer, and the final answer is scored by exact match.
org: University of Washington and collaborators (Koncel-Kedziorski, Roy, Amini, Kushman, Hajishirzi)
note: Saturated for current models. SVAMP showed that solvers can score well on MAWPS without reading the question. Google's chain-of-thought paper (Wei et al. 2022) used it with GSM8K and SVAMP. 41 GitHub stars.

name: MAXIFE
aliases: Multilingual and Cross-lingual Instruction Following Evaluation
description: Models follow 1,667 verifiable instructions in 23 languages and in cross-lingual settings. Rule-based checks and model judges score compliance.
note: Qwen model cards report accuracy on English plus multilingual original prompts, 23 settings in total.

name: MaXM
description: Vision language models answer short visual questions about Crossmodal-3600 images in 7 languages. A test-only set scored by accuracy.
note: Questions and answers come from a translation-based generation framework with human annotation.

name: MBABench
description: Agents build complete financial models in Excel from a case prompt and documents. An LLM judge grades accuracy, formulas and formatting on a 0 to 100 scale.
note: Each task runs through three Excel interaction surfaces so one judge can compare them. The judge was validated against finance experts.

name: MBABench 2.0
description: Agents build spreadsheet financial models for 101 tasks written by finance experts. A task passes only if every number matches the reference and the workbook meets a quality bar.
org: Columbia University (Namkoong Lab), hosted by Snorkel AI
note: 20 agents in their own harnesses at launch. Only one agent passed any of the 20 Hard tasks. Funded by Snorkel Open Benchmarks Grants.

name: MBE (Multistate Bar Examination)
description: Models answer the 200 multiple choice questions of an official Multistate Bar Examination practice exam. Scored by accuracy.
note: Anthropic used the official NCBE 2021 MBE practice exam. The uniform-bar-exam record covers the full bar exam.

name: MBPP
description: Models write short Python functions from a one-line task description. A solution counts as correct if it passes the task's three assert tests.
note: EvalPlus released MBPP+ with many more tests per task because the original three tests miss wrong solutions.

name: MBPP+
description: Models write short Python functions for MBPP problems, and EvalPlus checks each one against many more generated tests than the original.

changes.text: The maintainers moved the Docker environment to Python 3.10 and set the default per-test timeout to 0.5 seconds. These changes affect syntax support and timeout outcomes.
The maintainers shipped corrected input constraints and reference checkers for MBPP+. Identical generated programs can receive different pass results with the updated dataset.

note: Released as part of EvalPlus after HumanEval+, and it uses a cleaned subset of MBPP problems.

name: MBXP
description: Models solve MBPP problems transpiled with their tests into more than 10 programming languages, such as Java, C++ and Go. Unit tests check each solution.
note: Released with Multilingual HumanEval and MathQA-X. Labs usually report the average over languages.

name: MC-Bench
description: Models write code that builds a Minecraft structure from a prompt. Users vote between two builds without knowing the models.
note: Model labs gave access but are not affiliated. MineBench, which has its own record, credits MC-Bench as its inspiration. The repos were last updated in 2025-09.

name: McEval
description: Models complete, explain and generate code in 40 programming languages across about 16,000 test samples. Scored by test execution.
org: Beihang University and others (Chai et al.)
note: Tencent reports it for Hunyuan-A13B in fast-thinking mode.

name: MCP Atlas
description: Multi-step workflows over real MCP servers. Scores tool-use competency on realistic tasks.

changes.text: The maintainers replaced the Python harness with a TypeScript agent loop and configurable run controls. Scores from the old and new harnesses require matching execution settings.
The maintainers enforced per-task tool restrictions during execution and stopped advertising disabled tools. Earlier runs could invoke tools outside the allowed set.

note: 500 public tasks of 1,000. Rest held back. Labs use different judge models, so self-reported scores vary.

name: MCP prompt injection evaluation (Anthropic)
description: Agents use simulated email, Slack and document servers over MCP where content carries injected instructions. Score is the attack prevention rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation reported without safeguards. The test cases are not public.

name: MCP-Bench
description: Agents solve multi-step tasks using 28 live MCP servers with 250 tools in areas such as finance, travel, scientific computing and academic search. Scoring covers tool use, coordination and planning.
note: 63 HF paper upvotes and about 510 GitHub stars.

name: MCP-Universe
description: Agents complete tasks through 11 real MCP servers across six domains, such as navigation, repositories, finance, and browsing. Scored by execution-based success rate.

name: MCPMark
description: Agent stress-tests realistic MCP tool use (GitHub, Notion, Postgres, browser). Graded by programmatic verification scripts.
note: Kimi K3 reports a 'Verified' revision.

name: MCPMark Verified
description: Agents complete 127 tasks through version-pinned MCP servers. Stabilized verifiers score single-run task success.
note: The authors deprecate earlier task versions and state that their results are not directly comparable.

name: mDolly
description: Models answer open-ended Dolly prompts machine-translated into 101 languages, plus human-edited sets in 6 languages and human-written prompts in 7. An LLM judge compares or rates the answers.
note: Released as the Aya Evaluation Suite with 26,750 prompts. Earlier Aya papers scored it with pairwise win rates, while the Tiny Aya report uses rubric ratings.

name: MDPBench
description: Document parsers read 3,400 digital and photographed document images in 17 languages. Public and private splits limit leakage.
org: Huazhong University of Science and Technology (MultimodalOCR group)
note: On Hugging Face's official benchmark list.

name: MeasureBench
description: Vision-language models read values from images of measuring instruments, such as gauges and rulers, in real and synthesized photos. Scored by matching the reading to the key.
note: Published at CVPR 2026. A generator makes new synthetic gauges with controlled pointers, scales and clutter.

name: MeasureBench Real-world
description: Models read values and units from real instrument images. The score is the published overall measurement accuracy.
note: One track of MeasureBench. The MeasureBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: MeasureBench Synthetic
description: Models read values and units from generated instrument images. The score is the published overall measurement accuracy.
note: One track of MeasureBench. The MeasureBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: MedAgentBench
description: Agents use FHIR APIs in a virtual electronic health record to do 300 patient tasks in 10 categories written by physicians.
note: 343 GitHub stars at 2026-11-01.

name: MedCalc-Bench Verified
description: Models extract values from patient notes and compute results for 55 medical calculators. Verified release of MedCalc-Bench with corrected labels.
note: Anthropic runs the code-augmented setting with a Python tool. Scores on the original MedCalc-Bench are not comparable.

name: MedChemBench (OpenAI)
description: Models answer chemistry questions from an OpenAI internal set, grouped with OpenAI's life science research evaluations. OpenAI has not published the task format.
note: Reported in the GPT-5.6 post (Sol 48.3%) and the GPT-6 Astra post (Astra 49.3%). OpenAI omits Claude Fable 5 and 5.1 because they refuse most questions. Format and scoring are guesses.

name: MedCode
description: Models read de-identified patient records and output primary and secondary ICD-10-CM diagnosis codes. Answers are checked against codes assigned by professional coders.
note: Records include discharge summaries with progress and consult notes. Coders used the Codify lookup tool but no AI. The board had 107 models on 2026-10-29.

name: MedHELM
description: Models run a suite of medical tasks chosen by clinicians across five categories, from clinical decision support and note writing to patient messages and administration.
note: First HELM release 2025-02-28. Release v4.0.0 (2026-01-19) covers 37 scenarios, some from private health-system data. Open-ended tasks use an LLM jury.

name: Medical Knowledge Self-Assessment Program (MKSAP)
description: Models answer internal medicine board review questions from MKSAP. Scoring is accuracy.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: Medicinal Chemistry (Anthropic)
description: Models see several real drug-discovery compounds and pick which had the highest or lowest measured ADME property. The set has 504 questions.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: MedMCQA
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions from Indian medical entrance exams, AIIMS and NEET PG. Scoring is accuracy.
note: GPT-4o card reports the dev split.

name: MedQA
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions from medical licensing exams, usually the 12,723-question English USMLE set. Scoring is accuracy.
note: The full dataset also has simplified and traditional Chinese exam sets.

name: MedQA Mainland China
description: Models answer mainland China medical licensing exam questions in simplified Chinese. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Simplified Chinese part of the MedQA dataset.

name: MedQA Taiwan
description: Models answer Taiwan medical licensing exam questions in traditional Chinese. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Traditional Chinese part of the MedQA dataset.

name: MedQA USMLE (5 options)
description: Models answer USMLE-style medical licensing questions with five answer options. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Five-option variant of the MedQA English set. The medqa record covers the four-option set.

name: MedScribe
description: Models write SOAP notes from clinical visit transcripts. Notes are graded against expert gold-standard rubrics for required content and section structure.
note: Transcripts are synthetic, generated with NoteChat from real de-identified notes. Experts could not tell them from real ones. 109 models on 2026-10-29.

name: MedXpertQA
description: Models answer 4,460 expert-level medical exam questions across 17 specialties, in a text subset and an image subset. Scoring is multiple-choice accuracy.

name: MedXpertQA MM Extended
description: Models answer multimodal medical questions over clinical images and patient details. Mercor adds 51 new expert-written tasks to the 200 public ones and reports both scores.
note: Held-out extension of medxpertqa. Mercor shows the original and extended score for each model. The month is approximate. The Wayback Machine first saved the earliest extended pages on 2026-08-15.

name: MedXpertQA-MM
description: Models answer expert-level medical exam questions that combine images with clinical records and test results. Scoring is accuracy.
note: This is the multimodal subset of MedXpertQA, which has 4,460 questions in total across its Text and MM subsets.

name: Meeseeks
description: Models follow complex instructions over several turns and get feedback on failed requirements after each turn. Scored by how many requirements they meet.
note: It has Chinese and English versions. LongCat launch posts report Meeseeks-zh.

name: Meeseeks Utility Rate
description: Models follow complex instructions with feedback for up to 20 turns. The score measures fully usable responses as a percentage.
note: The paper reports utility rate separately from requirement-level Meeseeks Score. The importer reads final-turn utility rate.

name: MEGA-Bench
description: Models solve 505 real-world multimodal tasks with over 8,000 samples. Outputs include numbers, code, LaTeX, coordinates and JSON, scored by more than 40 task metrics.
note: ICLR 2025. Sixteen expert annotators wrote the tasks. Some tasks use a model judge for free-form answers.

name: Mem-Gallery
description: Multimodal agents hold long conversations over many sessions that mix images and text, then answer questions that need what they remembered. Questions test memory extraction and test-time adaptation, reasoning over memory, and managing knowledge that changes over time.
org: Yuanchen Bei, Tianxin Wei and coauthors
note: ACL 2026 main conference paper. The paper tests 13 memory systems. About 119 GitHub stars and 5 Hugging Face upvotes.

name: MemEye
description: Multimodal agent memory systems answer questions that need fine visual evidence kept from earlier sessions, which captions or text traces alone cannot supply.
note: 65 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: MemLens
description: Vision-language models and memory agents answer 789 questions over multimodal multi-session conversations, covering extraction, temporal reasoning, knowledge updates and refusal at four context lengths.
note: 78 upvotes on Hugging Face papers. VLMEvalKit includes it.

name: MemoryAgentBench
description: Memory agents receive long inputs in chunks over many turns and are tested on accurate retrieval, test-time learning, long-range understanding and selective forgetting. It adds two new sets, EventQA and FactConsolidation.
note: Accepted at ICLR 2026. About 480 GitHub stars. The authors later released MemoryArena for agentic memory tasks.

name: MemoryBench (Meta)
description: Models recall key facts from multi-turn conversations of 64K to 100K tokens that include distractor chats and turns that conflict with or update the facts. An LLM judge scores answers on weighted rubrics.
note: Meta in-house eval first reported in the Muse Wonder model card on 2026-10-12. Not the public MemoryBench by Ai et al. (ICML 2026).

name: MemTrapBench
description: Models with memory are tested on cases where correct, relevant memories still distort their reasoning or beliefs and lower task performance.
note: It had 30 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 5 GitHub stars.

name: MENT-SNS
description: Models translate English and Chinese sentences with slang, wordplay and idioms. A GPT-4.1 judge compares each translation with a baseline.
note: Z.ai takes source sentences from MENT (Tian et al. 2026, Beyond Literal Mapping), 753 English and Chinese pairs over SNS, cross-culture, poetry and literature. Graduate students verified the samples. GPT-4.1 judges against a baseline. The printed score is a pairwise rating.

name: MentalHealthBench
description: 1,215 synthetic mental-health conversations with 5,262 clinician-authored rubric criteria. An LLM judge scores safety and guidance quality.
note: Grader is GPT-5.6 Sol. More than 80 licensed psychologists and psychiatrists from more than 20 countries wrote and adjudicated the criteria. The paper URL for the data (no extension) returns 404, but OAI_MentalHealthBench.zip resolves.

name: MerchantBench
description: Agents run a seller's e-commerce store for 365 simulated days at order level. Actions constrain later choices, so the test measures long-term coherence.
note: The headline leaderboard reports mean final net assets in thousands of RMB across three 365-day runs per model and harness.

name: Meta action-belief coherence probe
description: Models act on items from five alignment evaluations and then state beliefs about them. Reports a mean coherency score.
note: In-house Meta probe over AIR-Bench, IHEval, MASK, School of Reward Hacking and StrongREJECT items.

name: Meta agentic cyber misuse refusal
description: Models run multi-step cyber tasks with tool access while an adaptive attacker tries to steer them to a malicious goal. Reports attack success rate.
note: In-house Meta refusal evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: Meta agentic evaluations grounded in user traffic
aliases: Agentic Evaluations Grounded in User Traffic
description: Models continue replays of recorded user workflows. A jury reports the share of cases with a supported substantive finding.
note: In-house Meta evaluation on 116 matched cases with three attempts each.

name: Meta Agents Research Environments (ARE) / Gaia2
description: Simulated app environments for agents with time and events. Hosts the Gaia2 benchmark.
note: Gaia2 has 800 dynamic scenarios across 10 universes. In 2026 Meta added Gaia2 CLI, a container stack that runs agents such as OpenClaw and mini-SWE-agent, and the Omnilingual-Gaia2 translation.

name: Meta BioDesign Proxy
description: Agents complete computational biology design tasks across host-pathogen interaction, protein design and sequence analysis. Aggregate normalized score.
note: In-house Meta evaluation built with Faculty AI and external experts. The Muse Wonder card reports the average over five tasks in three categories. The tasks are not public.

name: Meta BioKnowledge Proxy
description: Models answer tacit knowledge and troubleshooting questions on wet-lab workflows for proxy biological agents. Has 200 single-answer and 100 multiple-answer questions.
note: In-house Meta evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Meta BioProtocol Proxy
description: Models answer 400 questions on sequence prediction, correction and missing steps in 60 expert protocols for 15 low-risk proxy agents.
note: In-house Meta evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Meta catastrophic cyber misuse refusal
description: Models receive high-severity cyber-misuse prompts with technical context. The benchmark reports pass@k attack success rate under adaptive attacks.
note: In-house Meta refusal evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: Meta chemical and biological high-risk bottleneck evaluations
description: Models answer expert-written tasks in three restricted subsets. An expert-validated rubric scores each response.
note: In-house Meta evaluation run in an isolated cluster. Subsets are Chemical Threats, Biological Threats and Operational Execution.

name: Meta chemical-agent refusal evaluation
description: Models receive high-risk chemical prompts and the benchmark measures how often they refuse. Covers development, procurement and production stages.
note: In-house Meta refusal evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: Meta Code-Fetch Under User Requests
description: A coding agent is told by a reckless user to fetch or run a risky artifact. The benchmark measures the rate of insecure execution.
note: In-house Meta benchmark. A programmatic judge checks filesystem state and command history.

name: Meta curated CTF set
description: Agents solve 198 public and private capture-the-flag challenges across six security domains. Reports pass@1.
note: In-house Meta mix of public and private CTF challenges, first described in the Muse Spark Safety and Preparedness Report.

name: Meta cyber false-refusal benchmark
description: Models receive benign and borderline cyber requests and the benchmark measures how often they wrongly refuse. Reports false refusal rate.
note: In-house Meta evaluation of over-refusal on defensive cyber tasks.

name: Meta Cyber Misuse Chat
description: Models receive 80 offensive cyber requests, directly and with jailbreak developer prompts. Reports attack success rate and a benign false refusal rate.
note: In-house Meta refusal set. The prompts are not public.

name: Meta cyber misuse request set
description: Models receive 600 private offensive cyber prompts, directly and under jailbreak attacks. Reports attack success rate.
note: In-house Meta refusal set from the Muse Spark Safety and Preparedness Report.

name: Meta holistic adversarial audit with Petri Bloom
aliases: Broad Adversarial Auditing with Petri Bloom
description: Two auditor models run Petri Bloom scenarios built from Meta's behavior taxonomy. A binary judge reports the share of scenarios with a violation.
note: Meta setup over nine taxonomy sub-categories. Each scenario takes its worst of six transcripts.

name: Meta instructed selective performance evaluation
description: Models are told to underperform on six science capability sets. Reports the average drop from baseline in percentage points.
note: In-house Meta sandbagging experiment with monitor-oblivious and monitor-aware conditions.

name: Meta internal agent hallucination evaluation
description: Agents do long-context assistant and professional tasks with tools. The benchmark reports the share of verifiable claims that are hallucinated.
note: In-house Meta benchmark across health, finance, legal, clinical and engineering tasks.

name: Meta internal sycophancy evaluation
description: Models meet adversarially curated conversations that invite inappropriate agreement, plus benign controls. Reports sycophancy and excessive anti-sycophancy rates.
note: In-house Meta evaluation. Rates are high by construction and do not estimate ordinary use.

name: Meta prompted evaluation awareness
description: Models are asked to judge whether transcripts come from evaluations or real use. Reports the weighted rate of correct identification.
note: In-house Meta evaluation over chemical and biological, cyber and loss of control transcripts.

name: Meta targeted agentic evaluations
description: Agents work in prebuilt stateful sandboxes that test specific behavior rules. Reports the case-level violation rate over 1,790 scenarios.
note: In-house Meta suite built from 142 taxonomy units. Scenarios were screened with Muse Spark 1.1.

name: Meta training-stage provenance probe
description: Models label 10,000 transcripts as deployment, evaluation, RL or SFT. Reports overall accuracy against a 25% chance rate.
note: In-house Meta situational awareness probe on internal transcripts.

name: Meta Underspecified Intent evaluation
description: Models answer ambiguous requests sourced from real Meta AI chats where users corrected the reply. Rubrics score whether the true intent is met.
note: In-house Meta evaluation. A companion Underlying Intent set is reported separately.

name: Meta-World
description: Robot policies do simulated tabletop manipulation tasks, scored by success rate. Splits test multi-task learning, such as MT10 and MT50, and meta-learning, such as ML45.
org: Farama Foundation (originally Stanford, Berkeley and others)
note: About 1,900 GitHub stars and still maintained. Meta-World+ (2025-05, arXiv 2505.11289) standardized the benchmark, so check which version a paper reports. VLA papers in 2026 report it.

name: MetagenomicsBench
description: Agents analyze microbial communities from shotgun, amplicon, long-read and spatial metagenomics data. A grader checks the biological result.
note: Part of LatchBio's BioBench suite on benchmarks.bio. The V1 set has 100 evaluations. Release month is the GitHub repo creation month.

name: metal-arm-harness
description: Safety-enveloped CLI that lets any coding agent drive a real MakerMods Metal or Maker arm one command at a time from camera JPEGs.
note: Harness, not a benchmark. The safety design is a measured table floor, slow zone and per-move joint caps. No license file.

name: METR data deduplication
description: Agents write an efficient algorithm that removes near-duplicate lines from a large file. A trial succeeds when F1 reaches at least 80%.
note: Anthropic reports the share of trials scoring above the F1 threshold. The card calls it a METR public task.

name: METR general autonomy task suite
aliases: Agent Performance on General Autonomy Benchmark
description: Agents complete multi-step tasks in virtual environments. Scored as horizon weighted average task completion compared with human time limits.
note: Precursor of the METR time horizon suite. OpenAI cards show it as a chart.

name: METR pre-deployment AI R&D tasks
description: METR's long-horizon tasks for Anthropic pre-deployment tests: Train a Program, Gaming Bot, Sunlight open-ended research, plus Budget NanoGPT and LMCA.

name: METR Time Horizon
description: Agents attempt software and research tasks timed against skilled humans. The score is the human task length at which the agent succeeds half the time.
note: Time Horizon 1.0 used 170 tasks in Vivaria. METR replaced it with Time Horizon 1.1 in January 2026 and re-estimated 14 models.

name: METR Time Horizon 1.1
description: Agents attempt 228 software and research tasks timed against skilled humans, run in Inspect. The score is the human task length at which the agent succeeds half the time.
note: It added 73 HCAST tasks, removed 15 and updated 53, and moved from Vivaria to Inspect. METR stopped updating the page on 2026-09-08 and calls results above 16 hours unreliable.

name: METR Time Horizon suite
description: Software tasks with human completion times. Reports the task length at which a model succeeds 50% of the time.
note: METR flagged high detected cheating for GPT-5.6 Sol, so it treated the result as non-robust.

name: MeViS
description: Models segment the objects in a video that a sentence picks out by their motion, not by static looks. Scored by J&F.
org: Nanyang Technological University and Fudan University (Ding, Liu, He, Jiang, Loy)
note: ICCV 2023. Reports use the valid_u split, whose labels are public. Microsoft's Mage-VL card reports MeViS-ValidU.

name: MEWC
description: Models solve 179 Microsoft Excel World Championship problems from 2021 to 2026 with Excel tools. Output cells are compared one by one with answer cells.
note: In-house MiniMax benchmark built from Excel esports problems, and the task set is not released.

name: MEWC v2
description: Models solve 100 hard Microsoft Excel World Championship problems with Excel tools. Expert rubrics score the answers over three trials.
note: In-house MiniMax evaluation. It is a hard subset of the MEWC pool, so scores differ from the 179-problem MEWC.

name: MGSM
description: 250 GSM8K problems translated into 10 languages. Final-answer accuracy.
note: Saturated.

name: MGSM-Rev2
description: Models solve the 250 MGSM grade-school math problems in 10 languages. Google fixed two English errors, rephrased ambiguous items and retranslated every question with Gemini. Accuracy.
note: Same format as MGSM and meant as a drop-in replacement. The paper shows translation errors skewed earlier MGSM results, so scores differ. Cohere's GlobalMGSM uses it.

name: MHPP
description: Models write Python functions for 210 human-curated problems that need careful reading of specifications and multi-step reasoning. Unit tests check each solution.
note: Built to be harder than HumanEval and MBPP. The paper evaluated 26 models.

name: MIA-Bench
description: Models answer 400 image prompts that stack several strict instructions on format, length and content. An LLM judge scores how well each answer follows every instruction.
note: ICLR 2025 paper. Reported in Qwen-VL reports under alignment.

name: micro1 Medical Index
description: Models are scored on the equal-weight average of micro1 medical benchmarks, currently RealmPathology, PharmaBench and WellnessBench.
note: A live scoreboard that adds each new micro1 medical benchmark.

name: Microsoft internal multimodal RAI benchmark
description: Vision language models answer image and text prompts across harm categories. Responses are scored from 0 to 10, higher is safer.
note: In-house Microsoft evaluation reported for Phi-3.5-Vision.

name: Microsoft RAI benchmark: Grounding
description: Models answer in GPT-4o simulated multi-turn conversations. A judge scores from 0 to 5 how fully each answer is grounded in the given prompt.
note: In-house Microsoft evaluation from the Phi-4 report. The Phi-3 report scores Ungroundedness from 0 to 4 instead.

name: Microsoft RAI benchmark: Harmful Content Continuation (DR-3)
description: Models continue conversations about hate, self-harm, sexual content and violence. Scored as the share of answers with judged severity 3 or more out of 7.
note: In-house Microsoft evaluation used in Phi reports. Reports print the defect rate as a fraction.

name: Microsoft RAI benchmark: Harmful Content Summarization (DR-3)
description: Models summarize content about hate, self-harm, sexual content and violence. Scored as the share of answers with judged severity 3 or more out of 7.
note: In-house Microsoft evaluation used in Phi reports. Reports print the defect rate as a fraction.

name: Microsoft RAI benchmark: Jailbreak (DR-1)
description: Models face simulated jailbreak conversations on topics such as child grooming, illegal advice and leaking guidelines. Scored as the defect rate at severity 1.
note: In-house Microsoft evaluation used in Phi reports. Reports print the defect rate as a fraction.

name: Microsoft RAI benchmark: Third Party Harm (DR-1)
description: Models face simulated conversations that try to extract third-party content such as books, news, recipes and songs. Scored as the defect rate at severity 1.
note: In-house Microsoft evaluation used in Phi reports. Reports print the defect rate as a fraction.

name: Microsoft RAI benchmark: Ungroundedness
description: Models answer in GPT-4 simulated multi-turn conversations. A judge rates how ungrounded each answer is in the given prompt, from 0 to 4.
note: In-house Microsoft evaluation from the Phi-3 report. The Phi-4 report uses a Grounding score from 0 to 5 instead.

name: MicroVQA
description: Models answer expert-written multiple choice questions about biology microscopy images that test image understanding, hypothesis generation and experiment proposal.
org: Stanford University (James Burgess, Serena Yeung-Levy et al.)
note: MicroVQA++ (2025-11) is a separate training dataset.

name: MIEB
description: Image and image-text embedding models are scored on 130 tasks in 38 languages, grouped into 8 task types such as retrieval, clustering and classification.
note: Part of the MTEB framework. Google's EmbeddingGemma 2 card reports the MIEB lite subset as Mean(TaskType). 50 models in the paper.

name: MIEB Lite
description: Embedding models complete the MIEB Lite task set. The official API reports the mean across task types.
note: This task set has a separate official score endpoint. Task-type scores remain auxiliary metrics.

name: Miklós Schweitzer 2025
description: Models write proofs for the 2025 Miklós Schweitzer competition, a hard Hungarian university-level contest. MathArena runs and grades it.
note: Listed among MathArena competitions. Dataset created 2025-12-10.

name: MILU
description: Multi-task Indic Language Understanding: culturally grounded multiple-choice questions in 11 Indic languages.

name: MIMIC-CXR (classification)
description: Models read chest X-rays from Beth Israel Deaconess and say whether five common conditions are present. Scored by average F1 over the conditions.
org: MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (Johnson et al.)
note: Access needs PhysioNet credentials. Google reports two test sets, Med-Gemini radiologist-adjudicated labels and the MAIRA test set, and their scores differ a lot.

name: MIMIC-CXR report generation
description: Models write the findings of a radiology report for a MIMIC-CXR chest X-ray. Scored against the radiologist's report, most often by RadGraph F1.
org: MIT Laboratory for Computational Physiology and Beth Israel Deaconess Medical Center (Johnson et al.)
note: Google reports RadGraph F1 on a 912-image test set from Tanno et al. (2024). Other reports use other splits and metrics, so check the split before comparing.

name: MiMo Code Bench
description: Coding agents work through a varied set of software tasks built in house by Xiaomi. The report gives no task count or grading details.
note: Xiaomi also reports a mini version with avg@3 during training.

name: MiMo Coding Bench
description: Models do varied coding tasks inside agent harnesses such as Claude Code. Tasks cover repo understanding, project building, code review, artifact generation, planning and SWE.
note: Xiaomi built it in house. The MiMo-V2.6 report uses a MiMo Code Bench that gives MiMo-V2.5-Pro 40.4 against 73.7 here, so the two sets differ.

name: MiMo Cyber Bench
description: Agents do in-house cybersecurity tasks that add to public vulnerability reproduction and exploitation benchmarks. The report gives no task count or grading details.
note: MiMo-V2.5-Pro scores 0.0 and MiMo-V2.6-Pro scores 80.2 in the report table.

name: MiMo Visual Coding
description: Models build websites from requests and turn reference images into matching front-end code. Tasks include WebDev and Image2Code.
note: Xiaomi built it in house. The report does not name the grader, so the scoring type is a guess.

name: Mind2Web
description: Models predict the next web action for over 2,000 crowdsourced tasks on 137 real websites in 31 domains. Scored by element accuracy and step success rate.
note: Offline action prediction over cached pages. Splits are cross-task, cross-website and cross-domain.

name: Mind2Web 2
description: Agents browse the live web for 130 long tasks and return answers with citations. Task-specific judge agents built from rubric trees grade correctness and attribution.
note: Built with over 1,000 hours of human labor. It tests agentic search, not single web actions, so scores do not compare with Mind2Web.

name: MindCube
description: Models answer 21,154 multiple choice questions about scenes seen from a few views. Questions test positions, orientations, and what-if movements.
org: MLL Lab, Northwestern University, with Stanford, NYU, and University of Washington
note: The authors fixed data bugs in March 2026, so newer results may differ from earlier ones.

name: MindEval
description: Models hold multi-turn therapy conversations with simulated patients designed with licensed clinical psychologists. An LLM judge scores each session.
note: The paper validates simulated patients against human text and judges against experts, then tests 12 models. The Sword page refused scripted reads.

name: MindEval2
description: Models support simulated patients from MindSim, a tool-using harness with detailed profiles. Psychologist-written rubrics (MHQR) replace Likert scales for scoring.
note: New patient simulator and new rubrics, so scores do not compare with MindEval. Maker attribution follows the first version.

name: MineBench
description: Models turn a prompt into a Minecraft-style voxel build as raw 3D coordinates or tool calls. Users compare builds blind, and votes become rankings.
note: The maker says it is an arena of vibes with no correct answers. Kaggle also hosts a MineBench Arena board. About 340 GitHub stars.

name: MineDojo
description: Agents complete open-ended tasks in Minecraft, such as mining blocks and fighting mobs, from a large simulation suite. Programmatic checks score many tasks.
org: NVIDIA, Caltech and collaborators (Fan et al.)
note: NeurIPS 2022 Outstanding Paper. Seed2.0 reports Minedojo-Verified, a verified subset whose maker it does not state.

name: MINERVA
description: Models answer complex video questions that need multi-step reasoning, with reference reasoning traces for grading.
note: Gemini 2.5 report uses the test subset, 0-shot, 1,024 frames.

name: MINERVA-Cultural
description: Models answer about 2,200 open-ended questions on 540 videos from 18 locales, written in native languages by local experts. An LLM judge scores each answer 0, 1 or 2.
note: Part of the MINERVA dataset collection with MINERVA and Neptune. Gemini 2.5 Pro scores 45.07% against a human baseline of 95.22%. The repo cites it under its first name, CURVE.

name: Minerva-Ego
description: Models answer 1,160 multiple-choice questions on egocentric kitchen videos from HD-EPIC. Each question has a hand-written reasoning trace grounded in time and objects.
note: Extends MINERVA to egocentric video. CVPR 2026 paper. Gemini 2.5 Pro scores 40.1% with 64 frames against a human 91.8%.

name: miniCTX-v2
description: Provers prove Lean theorems from real projects using long repository context, with theorems taken after a November 28, 2024 cutoff.
note: An update of miniCTX (2024) with new theorems, so scores are not comparable with v1. The month is the creation date of the Hugging Face dataset.

name: miniF2F
description: Models write formal proofs of olympiad and high school competition statements, such as AMC, AIME and IMO problems. A proof assistant checks each proof, and scores are pass@k on the 244 test problems.
org: OpenAI (Kunhao Zheng, Jesse Michael Han, Stanislas Polu)
note: Statements exist in Lean, Metamath, Isabelle and HOL Light. Labs report pass@1, pass@8 or pass@32.

name: Minimal-LinuxBench (Anthropic)
description: Agents attempt a hidden side task in high-stakes software environments while a monitor watches. Score is the stealth success rate.
note: Anthropic adaptation of a subset of LinuxBench, an AI control arena that Redwood Research shared privately.

name: MiniMax TTS Multilingual Test Set
description: Text-to-speech models clone two Common Voice speakers per language and read 100 test sentences in each of 24 languages. Scored by word error rate and speaker similarity.
note: Released with MiniMax-Speech. MiniMax plans to add languages, so the set may grow. Lower error rate is better.

name: MiniWoB++
description: Agents operate over 100 small synthetic web pages, such as forms, menus and date pickers, from a natural-language instruction. Each task returns a success reward.
org: Stanford University, now maintained by the Farama Foundation
note: Extends OpenAI's 2017 MiniWoB. The Farama version exposes a Gymnasium API.

name: MINTEval
description: Memory-augmented agents answer questions after long, frequently updated histories where memories interfere. Instances average 138,800 tokens and reach 1.8 million.
note: Across 7 memory systems the average accuracy was 27.9% at launch.

name: MIRA Bench
aliases: Multi-Agent Infra for Routing and Assignment Bench
description: Agents carry out long multi-role enterprise tasks across several systems and decide when to delegate to subagents.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: MIRB
description: Models compare, analyze and reason across several images in four categories: perception, visual world knowledge, reasoning and multi-hop reasoning.
org: University of Edinburgh and Tongji University
note: Shanghai AI Lab reports the category average in the InternVL3 and InternVL3.5 reports.

name: MirrorCode
description: Agent rebuilds a whole CLI program from scratch using only the original binary as an oracle. Solved only if 100% of end-to-end tests pass.
note: 25 targets, 3 kept private. ~34% of tests held out. Source programs are open source, so memorization cannot be fully ruled out.

name: MirrorDojo
description: Indirect prompt injection test run in Reflection AI's Mirror agent harness, based on AgentDojo. Each episode pairs a user task with an instruction planted in a tool result. Reports attack success rate and utility.
note: Not comparable to public AgentDojo results, because Mirror runs the agent loop instead of the benchmark's reference agent.

name: MirrorDyn
description: Indirect prompt injection test run in Reflection AI's Mirror agent harness, based on AgentDyn. Reports attack success rate and utility.
note: Not comparable to public AgentDyn results, because Mirror runs the agent loop.

name: Misaligned Behavior in Realistic Work Environments
aliases: Misaligned outcomes in realistic work environments
description: Agents do computer and browser tasks in simulated workplace apps with ambiguous instructions. Scored on the rate of unintended outcomes such as data disclosure.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. OpenAI made the set harder after the GPT-6 Astra card.

name: Misbehavior (Thinking Machines)
description: Agentic tasks that check whether a model fabricates results, ignores instructions or hides what it did when a task is hard. Scored by the rate of misbehavior.
note: In-house test. Tasks are not public.

name: Misc CTF challenges (Anthropic)
description: Agents identify and exploit vulnerabilities in capture-the-flag challenges outside the web, crypto, pwn, rev and network categories.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Misguided Attention
description: Models get slight variations of famous riddles, paradoxes and thought experiments. A model fails when it answers the well-known original instead of the problem as stated.
note: Version 0.3 (2025-01) added an evaluation subset with tagged releases. About 490 GitHub stars.

name: Missing-context hallucinations (Anthropic)
description: Models get prompts that request tools they lack or cite missing material. Score is the non-hallucination rate on each 500-prompt set.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation with unavailable-tool and missing-reference sets. The tool set was filtered on Claude Opus 4.6 failures.

name: MissionReport
description: Models write government status reports in Word from working files and a template, across 20 expert-written Department of Defense style assignments. Expert rubrics score each decision.
note: Nine models ran each task three times for 540 graded reports. Judgment and synthesis caused most lost points.

name: Mistral 175 unsafe prompts
description: Models receive 175 unsafe prompts. Metric is the share of harmful questions the model declines.
note: In-house Mistral test set used for system prompt guardrails. The prompts are not public.

name: Mistral internal function calling benchmark
description: Models call functions on Mistral's in-house test set. The Magistral paper does not describe the tasks or the metric.
note: In-house Mistral evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Mistral self-reflection moderation set
description: Models classify prompts or answers as acceptable or harmful on a balanced set of adversarial and standard prompts. Scored by precision and recall.
note: In-house Mistral dataset, manually curated. The prompts are not public.

name: MixEval
description: Models answer real user queries matched to similar questions from existing benchmarks. Ground-truth answers make it a cheap proxy for Chatbot Arena rankings.
org: National University of Singapore (Ni et al.)
note: MixEval-Hard is a harder subset reported separately.

name: MLAgentBench
description: Agents run machine learning experiments on 13 tasks, from improving CIFAR-10 accuracy to research problems like BabyLM. They read and write files, run code and inspect outputs.
note: An early AI R&D agent benchmark from 2023. About 360 GitHub stars and 75 forks.

name: MLCommons AILuminate
description: Industry-standard hazard benchmark over 12 risk categories with graded ratings.

name: MLCommons AILuminate Jailbreak
description: Models answer hazard prompts with and without taxonomy-based jailbreak attacks. The Resilience Gap is the drop in safety score under attack.
note: White papers for v0.5.1 (2025-12) and v0.7.1 (2026-02) came first. v1.0 used 264 seed prompts in 11 hazard categories on eight open-weight systems. The page cites 39 models tested.

name: MLCR-AA
description: Models reason over synthetic medical claim files of about 25k to 64k tokens, as a claims reviewer would. Three judge models check completeness and accuracy.
note: Wisedocs released MLCR on 2026-06-18 and v1.1 with the Artificial Analysis board on 2026-08-31. The board uses 60 private questions from the two hardest tiers.

name: MLE-bench
description: Kaggle-style ML engineering competitions. Agent trains models and is scored against competition leaderboards.
note: OpenAI runs an internal Revised version with 72 problems. The public leaderboard in the repo README stopped taking submissions on 2026-04-24. MLE-bench Lite is the 22-competition Low split.

name: MLE-bench 30
description: Agents train models for 30 of MLE-bench's Kaggle-style competitions. The score is the share of runs that earn a bronze medal or better.
note: OpenAI's system cards report this subset, and Meta reports a 30-task subset in its preparedness reports. It has no public leaderboard.

name: MLGym-Bench
description: Agents work on 13 open-ended AI research tasks in vision, language, reinforcement learning and game theory. Scores compare the agent's result with baselines on each task's metric.
note: Part of Meta's MLGym framework, which is also a Gym environment for RL training.

name: MLogiQA
description: Models answer LogiQA logical reasoning questions translated into 10 languages, 80 per language. Scored by accuracy.
note: It is a subset of the P-MMEval multilingual suite.

name: MLQA
description: Models extract answers from Wikipedia passages in seven languages, with questions and contexts that can be in different languages. Scored by F1 and exact match.
note: Languages are English, Arabic, German, Spanish, Hindi, Vietnamese and Chinese.

name: MLS-Bench
description: Agent must invent one algorithmic change in an ML research scaffold whose gain transfers across settings. Scored relative to human baselines.
note: 140 tasks over 12 ML domains. Lite = 30-task subset (~99 H100-hours) with 5-hour limit per task. Score >50 beats strongest human baseline.

name: MLVU
description: Multi-task long video understanding (minutes to hours) with multiple-choice and generation tasks. Accuracy.
note: The dev set and the test set use different questions and option counts, so their scores are not comparable. The test answers became public on 2025-03-18.

name: MM-BrowseComp
description: Browsing agents answer 400 hand-written questions whose evidence sits in web images and videos. Each question has a checklist for analysis of the reasoning path.
org: ByteDance Seed and collaborators (Li et al.)
note: Accepted to EMNLP 2026. The paper evaluates 27 models.

name: MM-ClawBench
description: Agents complete common OpenClaw tasks such as study planning, office documents, scheduled research, and code maintenance. Scoring is accuracy.
note: In-house: MiniMax never released the tasks or explained the scoring.

name: MM-HELIX
description: Multimodal models solve 1,260 items from 42 synthetic tasks that need long reflective reasoning with backtracking.
note: 110 upvotes on Hugging Face papers. Released with a training method.

name: MM-IFEval
description: Multimodal models follow image-grounded instructions with exact output constraints. Checks mix rule-based verification and a judge model.
note: Released with the MM-IFEngine training pipeline. 35 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: MM-MT-Bench
description: Models hold multi-turn conversations about images such as charts, documents and photos. GPT-4o grades each answer against a reference on a 1 to 10 scale.
note: Released with Pixtral 12B. Mistral and Qwen VL reports both use it.

name: MM-NIAH
description: Vision-language models answer questions about long documents of interleaved images and text. Tasks are retrieval, counting and reasoning over needles hidden in the document.
note: Models did worst on image needles at release. VLMEvalKit supports the validation split.

name: MM-SafetyBench
description: Multimodal models get 5,040 harmful text and image pairs in 13 scenarios, where a query-relevant image carries the harmful intent. Judges score attack success.
org: East China Normal University and Shanghai AI Laboratory
note: 222 GitHub stars at 2026-11-01.

name: MM-Vet
description: Models answer open questions about images that combine recognition, OCR, knowledge, spatial reasoning, language generation and math. GPT-4 grades each answer against a reference.
org: Weihao Yu, Zhengyuan Yang et al. (NUS and Microsoft)
note: MM-Vet v2 is a later release with interleaved image and text inputs.

name: MMAE
description: Audio models edit audio from instructions across a broad range of real-world editing tasks and sound types.
note: It had 45 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 113 GitHub stars. Tasks are audio editing, which the taxonomy files under audio understanding.

name: MMAR
description: Models answer 1,000 questions about real-world audio of speech, sound, music and their mixes. Questions span four reasoning layers from signal to cultural knowledge.
note: Repo has over 200 GitHub stars.

name: MMAU
description: 10K audio clips with questions on speech, sound and music needing expert knowledge and reasoning. Multiple-choice accuracy.

name: MMAU v05.15.25
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about speech, sound and music clips that need expert knowledge and reasoning. Scored by accuracy on test-mini or the hidden-answer test set.
note: Revises about 25% of questions and answers and 5% of audio files. The makers ask to cite this version from now on and keep earlier scores on a separate board. Test scoring moved to an HF space on 2026-01-30.

name: MMAU-Pro
description: Models answer 5,305 expert-written questions about speech, sounds, music and their mixes, covering 49 listening skills. Some clips run up to 10 minutes.
org: University of Maryland (GAMMA lab) and collaborators
note: A harder follow-up to MMAU from the same group. Some questions are open-ended rather than multiple choice.

name: MMBench
description: Vision language models answer multiple-choice questions covering 20 perception and reasoning skills. CircularEval rotates the options. Scored by accuracy.
note: The original version. MMBench v1.1 is a separate entry.

name: MMBench-CN v1.1
description: Models answer the Chinese translation of the MMBench image questions, using CircularEval with shuffled options. Scored by accuracy.
note: OpenCompass released the verified Chinese version on 2023-10-03. The v1.1 cleanup date is not stated on the repo page.

name: MMBench-EN v1.1
description: Models answer English multiple-choice image questions across 20 ability dimensions, using CircularEval with shuffled options. Scored by accuracy on the dev split.
note: Version 1.1 cleans the original MMBench questions, so scores differ from v1.0.

name: MMBench-GUI
description: GUI agents are tested at four levels on Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, Android and the web: content understanding, element grounding, task automation and task collaboration.
note: Uses an efficiency-quality area metric. 33 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: MMBench-Video
description: Video models answer free-form questions about long, multi-shot YouTube videos. A GPT-4 judge scores the answers.
note: 33 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: MMDU
description: Vision-language models hold long conversations about many images, up to 20 images and 27 turns per dialog. A GPT-4o judge scores the answers.
org: Shanghai AI Laboratory and collaborators (Liu, Zang et al.)
note: Questions come from Wikipedia images and text, written by annotators with GPT-4o help. It ships with the MMDU-45k tuning set. VLMEvalKit supports it.

name: MME
description: Models answer yes or no questions about images across 14 perception and cognition subtasks with hand-written instructions. Labs usually report the perception sum, out of 2000.
org: Fu et al. (Tencent Youtu Lab and Xiamen University)
note: Scores are sums of subtask scores, not percentages. The perception part has a maximum of 2000 points and cognition 800.

name: MME-CC
aliases: Multi-Modal Evaluation benchmark of Cognitive Capacity
