description: Models answer 1,173 expert-annotated vision-grounded questions in 11 task types grouped as spatial, geometric and visual knowledge reasoning.
org: ByteDance Seed and collaborators (Zhang et al.)
note: The release covered 16 models. The scoring field is a guess from the abstract.

name: MME-CoT
description: Models reason step by step on image questions in math, science, OCR, logic, space-time and general scenes. A judge scores reasoning quality, robustness and efficiency.
note: Part of the MME family with MME, MME-RealWorld and Video-MME. Reports often give the CoT quality F1.

name: MME-RealWorld
description: Models answer human-annotated multiple choice questions about high-resolution real-world images in scenarios such as remote sensing, autonomous driving, monitoring and OCR.
org: MME team (Yi-Fan Zhang, Chaoyou Fu et al.)
note: It has English and Chinese versions.

name: MME-Reasoning
description: Multimodal models answer logic questions grouped into inductive, deductive and abductive reasoning.
note: 83 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: MME-VideoOCR
description: Models answer 2,000 questions about text that appears in 1,464 videos, across 25 tasks from recognition to reasoning.
note: Motion blur and visual effects make video OCR harder than image OCR.

name: MMEB
description: Multimodal embedding models are scored on classification, visual question answering, multimodal retrieval and visual grounding, with 16 evaluation datasets in and out of distribution.
note: Introduced with the VLM2Vec model, ICLR 2025. 36 datasets in total, 20 for training and 16 for evaluation. Repo has 701 stars.

name: MMEB-V2
description: Multimodal embedding models are scored on 78 tasks over images, videos and visual documents. V2 adds visual document retrieval, video retrieval, temporal grounding, video classification and video QA.
note: Released with VLM2Vec-V2, accepted to TMLR 2026. Google's EmbeddingGemma 2 card reports its Image, VisDoc and Video splits.

name: MMEB-V3
description: Omni-modality embedding models are scored on 190 tasks across text, image, video, audio, visual documents and agent-centric retrieval.
note: Adds 111 tasks to MMEB-V2. Also adds OmniSET, tuples of the same content in different modalities, for finer diagnosis.

name: MMEnterprise-Bench
description: Enterprise agents answer 1,613 questions over workplace documents, chats and figures that change over time. They must resolve conflicting versions and say when evidence is not enough.
note: It had 32 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 16 GitHub stars.

name: MMIU
description: Vision-language models answer 11,000 multiple-choice questions over sets of images. 52 tasks cover 7 kinds of multi-image relationship.
note: Spatial tasks are the weakest area in the paper's results.

name: MMLongBench
description: Vision-language models solve 13,331 long-context examples in five task types, such as visual RAG, needle search and many-shot in-context learning. Each example comes at five lengths from 8K to 128K tokens.
org: University of Edinburgh and collaborators (Wang et al.)
note: Labs report the 128K length as MMLongBench-128K. It is a different test from MMLongBench-Doc. The paper benchmarks 46 models.

name: MMLongBench-Doc
description: Models answer 1,062 questions about 130 long PDF documents averaging 49 pages, and some questions are unanswerable. Scoring is accuracy and F1.

name: MMLU
description: 57-subject multiple-choice exam questions from elementary to professional level. Scored by accuracy.
note: Saturated and contaminated. Reported only as a base-model metric.

name: MMLU Anatomy
description: Models answer MMLU multiple-choice questions from the Anatomy subject. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Single-subject subset of MMLU.

name: MMLU calibration (expected calibration error)
description: Models answer an MMLU subset and their answer probabilities are compared with accuracy. Scored as expected calibration error.
note: Reported in the GPT-4 Technical Report for the pre-trained and post-trained models.

name: MMLU Clinical Knowledge
description: Models answer MMLU multiple-choice questions from the Clinical Knowledge subject. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Single-subject subset of MMLU.

name: MMLU College Biology
description: Models answer MMLU multiple-choice questions from the College Biology subject. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Single-subject subset of MMLU.

name: MMLU College Medicine
description: Models answer MMLU multiple-choice questions from the College Medicine subject. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Single-subject subset of MMLU.

name: MMLU Medical
description: Models answer the multiple-choice questions from the medical subjects of MMLU, such as anatomy, clinical knowledge and professional medicine.
org: UC Berkeley (Hendrycks et al.), subset chosen by medical model reports
note: It is a subset of MMLU, so its score differs from full MMLU. Reports differ on which subjects they include. Google's MedGemma cards report it as MMLU Med.

name: MMLU Medical Genetics
description: Models answer MMLU multiple-choice questions from the Medical Genetics subject. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Single-subject subset of MMLU.

name: MMLU Professional Medicine
description: Models answer MMLU multiple-choice questions from the Professional Medicine subject. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Single-subject subset of MMLU.

name: MMLU translated with Azure Translate
description: Models answer MMLU questions machine translated into 26 languages with Azure Translate. Scoring is 3-shot accuracy per language.
note: Different from the professionally translated MMMLU that OpenAI released later.

name: MMLU-CF
description: Models answer new MMLU-style multiple-choice questions written to avoid training data contamination. A 10,000 question test set stays private.
note: Only the 10,000 question validation set is public. The makers score the test set on request through GitHub issues. OpenCompass supports it. ACL 2025.

name: MMLU-Pro
description: Harder 10-option version of MMLU with reasoning-focused questions across 14 subjects.

changes.text: The maintainers removed inconsistent leading spaces from answer options in STEM subjects. This correction removed a formatting shortcut that could inflate earlier scores.

note: Launch posts report it widely. The makers fixed answers and formatting many times from 2024-07 to 2026-01, including a leading-space shortcut in STEM options on 2026-01-18, and kept one dataset.

name: MMLU-ProX
description: MMLU-Pro translated into up to 29 languages with expert review. Multiple-choice accuracy per language.
org: University of Tokyo (Li Lab) and collaborators
note: The full set has 11,829 questions per language. It launched in March 2025 with fewer languages and reached 29 in May 2025, so early averages differ. MMLU-ProX Lite is a separate 658-question subset.

name: MMLU-ProX Lite
description: Models answer 658 MMLU-Pro questions per language, the same items in each of 29 languages. Multiple choice accuracy.
org: University of Tokyo (Li Lab) and collaborators
note: A fast subset of MMLU-ProX, whose full set has 11,829 questions per language. IBM Granite cards report it as MMLU-ProX lite.

name: MMLU-Redux
description: Manually re-annotated subset of MMLU that fixes wrong labels. Multiple-choice accuracy.
note: Saturated. This first release has 3,000 questions in 30 subjects. The authors now recommend MMLU-Redux 2.0, and cards that write only MMLU-Redux do not say which version.

name: MMLU-Redux 2.0
description: Models answer 5,700 MMLU questions from all 57 subjects that experts re-annotated for errors. Flawed questions are marked so scoring can skip or fix them.
note: Extends the first release from 3,000 questions in 30 subjects to all 57 subjects. Single label fixes in 2025-02 kept scores comparable.

name: MMLU-stem
description: Models answer the STEM subjects of MMLU, such as physics, chemistry, mathematics, and computer science, as multiple choice. Scoring is accuracy.
note: A subject subset of MMLU rather than a separate benchmark, so subject lists can differ between reports.

name: MMMB
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about images in six languages across 15 categories. The set has about 12,000 questions.
note: VLMEvalKit runs it as MMMB. The same repo adds a multilingual MMBench that VLMEvalKit names MTL_MMBench_DEV.

name: MMMLU
description: MMLU professionally translated into 14 languages. Multiple-choice accuracy.

changes.text: The maintainers merged improved multilingual answer parsing into the official evaluator. Evaluations using the earlier parser can classify the same responses differently.

name: MMMU
description: 11.5K college-level multimodal questions across 30 subjects. Multiple-choice and open accuracy.

changes.text: The MMMU team released the test answers, allowing local test scoring. Later test results no longer come exclusively from evaluation against hidden answers.

note: Near-saturated. The test set answers became public on 2026-02-12, so test scores can now be computed locally.

name: MMMU-Pro
description: Harder MMMU: college-level multimodal questions with more options and vision-only inputs to remove text shortcuts.
note: Variant (standard vs vision, 4 vs 10 options) often unstated in cards.

name: MMMU-Pro Extended
description: Models answer multimodal questions that need both the image and the text. Mercor adds 140 new expert-written tasks to the 1730 public ones and reports both scores.
note: Held-out extension of mmmu-pro. Mercor shows the original and extended score for each model. The month is approximate. The Wayback Machine first saved the earliest extended pages on 2026-08-15.

name: MMOU
description: Models answer 20,000 questions about 11,877 long web videos, using sound, images and text together. Questions cover 13 skill categories.
org: NVIDIA and University of Maryland (Goel, Ghosh et al.)
note: At release the best closed model scored 64.2% and the best open model 46.8%. Microsoft's Mage-VL card reports the test-mini split.

name: MMSearch
description: Multimodal agents search and answer questions that require visual and textual evidence.
note: GLM-5V-Turbo reports MMSearch separately from MMSearch-Plus.

name: MMSearch-Plus
description: Multimodal browsing agents solve 311 search tasks that need fine-grained visual reasoning, provenance checks and long tool use. Answers are short and checked against a key.
note: Qwen evaluates it with search tools enabled.

name: MMSI-Bench
description: Models answer 1,000 human-written questions that need spatial reasoning across several images. Images come from indoor scans, driving, egocentric video and robot data.
note: Tasks cover camera, object and region relations, plus a multi-step reasoning category. arXiv v3 was posted on 2026-05-23.

name: MMSI-Video-Bench
description: Human-annotated questions on video-based spatial intelligence, organized in four levels from perception to planning and prediction.

name: MMStar
description: Models answer 1,500 human-curated image questions that cannot be solved without the image, across 6 core capabilities. Scored by accuracy.

name: MMSU
description: Models answer questions about spoken language that need its content, its paralinguistic cues such as emotion and pitch, and its phonology.
note: Qwen reports it as audio understanding.

name: MMT-Bench
description: Vision-language models answer 31,325 multiple-choice questions across many multimodal tasks such as recognition, localization, reasoning and planning.
note: ICML 2024.

name: MMTU
description: Models answer about 30,000 questions over real tables across 25 tasks, such as data cleaning, table joins, column and table transformation, table question answering and turning language into code. The tasks come from decades of computer science research on tabular data. Answers are checked automatically against references.
note: The Hugging Face leaderboard had 26 entries on 2026-11-05 and last changed in 2025-10, so newer models are missing. A long-context case study hides target cells in large tables. About 20 GitHub stars and no HF paper upvotes.

name: MMVP
description: Models answer 300 questions about 150 image pairs that CLIP embeds as near duplicates. A pair counts only when both answers are right.
org: New York University and UC Berkeley (Tong et al.)
note: Introduced in the paper Eyes Wide Shut on visual shortcomings of multimodal LLMs.

name: MMVU
description: 3,000 expert-annotated questions on videos across 27 disciplines. Multiple-choice and open-ended accuracy.

name: Mobile Actions
description: Model converts natural-language phone requests into on-device function calls (calendar, email, maps, flashlight, Wi-Fi). Call accuracy.
note: Identification inferred: the Reka Edge card lists 'Mobile Actions (Tool Use)' without a link. The dataset is mainly a FunctionGemma fine-tuning set.

name: MobileGym
description: Mobile GUI agents use 28 simulated apps in a browser-hosted phone, across 416 parameterized task templates. Deterministic judges check the app state.
note: EMNLP 2026. Also an online RL training platform. A 9-agent leaderboard was published in April 2026.

name: MobileMiniWoB++
description: Agents complete MiniWoB++ web tasks inside the Android emulator of AndroidWorld. Scored by task success rate.
note: Runs as the miniwob suite of AndroidWorld. MiniWoB++ itself comes from Liu et al. 2018.

name: MobileWorld
description: Agents complete 201 tasks across 20 mobile apps, including tasks that need user clarification or MCP tools. Backend checks verify success.
note: It was built because agents had passed 90 percent on AndroidWorld.

name: Mol-Instructions
description: Models answer molecule-oriented, protein-oriented and biomolecular text instructions, such as reaction prediction, molecule description and protein function questions. Scored per task with task metrics.
note: It is mainly an instruction-tuning dataset. Labs report its test split as a benchmark.

name: Mol-Instructions Chemical Entity Recognition
description: Models identify chemical entities in biomedical text. The score is test-set F1.
note: One track of Mol-Instructions. The Mol-Instructions record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Mol-Instructions Chemical-disease Interaction Extraction
description: Models extract chemical and disease interactions from text. The score is test-set F1.
note: One track of Mol-Instructions. The Mol-Instructions record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Mol-Instructions Chemical-protein Interaction Extraction
description: Models extract chemical and protein interactions from text. The score is test-set F1.
note: One track of Mol-Instructions. The Mol-Instructions record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Mol-Instructions Description-guided Molecule Design
description: Models generate molecules from descriptions. The score is exact-match accuracy on the molecule design test set.
note: One track of Mol-Instructions. The Mol-Instructions record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Mol-Instructions Forward Reaction Prediction
description: Models predict reaction products from reactants. The score is exact-match accuracy on the forward reaction test set.
note: One track of Mol-Instructions. The Mol-Instructions record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Mol-Instructions Multi-choice
description: Models answer biomedical multiple-choice questions. The score is test-set accuracy.
note: One track of Mol-Instructions. The Mol-Instructions record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Mol-Instructions Reagent Prediction
description: Models predict reaction reagents. The score is exact-match accuracy on the reagent prediction test set.
note: One track of Mol-Instructions. The Mol-Instructions record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Mol-Instructions Retrosynthesis
description: Models predict reactants for target products. The score is exact-match accuracy on the retrosynthesis test set.
note: One track of Mol-Instructions. The Mol-Instructions record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Mol-Instructions True or False
description: Models answer biomedical true or false questions. The score is test-set accuracy.
note: One track of Mol-Instructions. The Mol-Instructions record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Molecular Biology Capabilities Test
description: Models answer expert-level molecular biology questions from SecureBio. Scored as accuracy.
note: 200 text-only questions with a private holdout on everyday molecular biology methods. 14 PhD biologists scored about 34%. Modeled after VCT.

name: MolecularIQ
description: Models answer questions about molecular graphs, such as counting, indexing and constrained generation, and a symbolic checker verifies each answer.
org: Johannes Kepler University Linz (Bartmann, Klambauer, Luukkonen et al.)

name: MolmoAct2 sim_eval
description: Zero-shot ManiSkill evaluation of MolmoAct2 policies: put-everything-in-box tasks for Franka DROID and bimanual YAM, 10 episodes per task.
note: Two tasks, used as a sim harness. Assets come from a third-party HF account. No leaderboard.

name: MolmoSpaces
description: Zero-shot Franka (DROID) policies in held-out procedurally generated MuJoCo houses: pick, place, open, close. ~1,000 episodes per task.
note: ~1,000 episodes per task with 95% CIs. Not saturated for zero-shot policies: best MolmoBot pick-and-place ~67%, pi0.5 DROID ~10-12%. Ai2's sim-trained MolmoBot nears ceiling on Pick (~92%).

name: Moment finding (Google DeepMind)
description: Models find the moment in a robot video when an event happens. Scored by accuracy and mean absolute time distance in seconds.
note: Reported in the Gemini Robotics ER 2 post as 91.3% accuracy and 0.96s mean absolute distance.

name: Moneda AdviceBench
description: Models answer personal finance requests and paired education questions. Moneda’s default board scores paired pass rate on 50 EU personal requests with education twins.
note: One benchmark of Moneda Bench. The suite publishes no combined score. Moneda has not published combined results for US requests or discretion requests. Moneda reports personal directive rate separately. Moneda’s scores do not certify legal compliance.

name: Moneda Bench
description: Models answer finance questions across seven separate benchmarks. AdviceBench, CiteBench, FilingsBench, GroundBench and PortfolioBench have their own records. KnowledgeBench and MarketBench have no published results yet. Moneda publishes no combined score.
note: Moneda publishes samples while retaining private test sets. Public samples include 44 filing questions, 16 portfolio tasks, 11 companies for citation checks, and 23 advice items. Moneda also scores its own Numa 1 system. Moneda first listed the suite on November 1, 2026.

name: Moneda CiteBench
description: Models write company research notes with linked sources. Moneda scores the weighted share of linked claims that the cited pages support across 100 notes.
note: One benchmark of Moneda Bench. The suite publishes no combined score. Moneda labels current results experimental because human validation is incomplete. Moneda’s API marks these rows as ranked despite that caveat. Moneda’s model audit estimates are not benchmark scores.

name: Moneda FilingsBench
description: Models answer questions about SEC filings without receiving documents. Moneda scores accuracy on the private questions using filing data and judges for segment questions.
note: One benchmark of Moneda Bench. The suite publishes no combined score. Moneda’s first run covers 361 private questions, including 13 segment questions assessed by two judges. Moneda has not completed the segment judges’ human audit.

name: Moneda GroundBench
description: Models answer live questions about market figures. Moneda’s default board reports the share of correct answers against reference data, with incorrect answers reported separately.
note: One benchmark of Moneda Bench. The suite publishes no combined score. Moneda labels the current run experimental and unranked. Moneda reports that 116 of 132 answer keys rely on one reference source. Moneda runs each question three times.

name: Moneda PortfolioBench
description: Models solve hypothetical portfolio tasks involving rebalancing, risk, position sizing, and constraints. Moneda’s default board scores accuracy on 150 tasks with fixed answers.
note: One benchmark of Moneda Bench. The suite publishes no combined score. Moneda has not scored the planned forecasts or mandate funds. Moneda’s current score covers portfolio tasks only and does not measure investment performance.

name: Money talks
description: Models try to persuade human participants to donate part of a 20 pound study bonus to charity.
note: Human participant persuasion study from Phuong et al. 2024. Reported as mean pounds donated.

name: Monitor Evasion Capability Under Prompted Sandbagging
description: Models are told to sandbag on WMDP and Monorepo-Bench, sometimes while evading a monitor. Scored as CoT and production monitor recall of sandbagged items.
note: In-house OpenAI monitorability evaluation adapted from Li et al. 2025. Higher recall means sandbagging is easier to catch.

name: Monitorability Sandbagging
description: Models on Impossible Coding Tasks are prompted to be more or less monitorable. Scored as CoT monitor recall on rollouts that hack.
note: In-house OpenAI monitorability evaluation. Tests whether models can manipulate measured monitorability.

name: Monorepo-Bench
description: Agents replicate pull-request style contributions in a large internal OpenAI repository. Graded by hidden unit tests as pass@1.
note: In-house OpenAI AI self-improvement evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Monthly-SWEBench
description: Coding agents resolve 100 fresh GitHub tasks each month, half bug fixes and half features, from newly merged pull requests. Harbor verifiers score pass@1.
note: Each monthly snapshot is a new task set, so scores from different months do not compare. The 2026-06 snapshot rated 19 models.

name: Morphology-to-molecule matching (Anthropic)
description: Models match four sets of multi-channel liver cell images to the four shuffled molecule and dose treatments that produced them.
note: Built with Axiom Bio from its in-vitro liver assay data.

name: MORSE-500
description: Models answer questions embedded in 500 scripted video clips across six reasoning categories, including abstract, physical, planning, spatial and temporal reasoning.
note: Clips are generated by scripts, so harder versions can be made as models improve. The Seed2.0 page spells it Morese-500.

name: MortgageTax
description: Vision models read mortgage tax certificates given as images. They extract the year, parcel number and county, and compute the annualized amount due.
note: 1,258 documents with a 20-sample public validation set. Vals archived it as saturated by 2026-09-01.

name: MotionBench
description: Models answer questions about fine-grained motion in video clips across six motion question types. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Test answers are hidden and scored through the leaderboard, while the dev set has public answers.

name: Movie Gen Video Bench
description: Video generation models make clips from a fixed prompt set, and people compare them. Meta released non-cherry-picked Movie Gen videos for comparison.
note: Described in section 3.5.2 of the Movie Gen technical report.

name: MP-DocVQA
description: Models answer questions about scanned documents of up to 20 pages, where the answer sits on one page. Scored by ANLS against the reference answer.
org: Computer Vision Center, Universitat Autonoma de Barcelona (Tito, Karatzas, Valveny)
note: It extends the single-page DocVQA questions to multi-page documents. Microsoft's Mage-VL card reports it as MultiDocVQA-val.

name: MPIE-Bench
description: Image editing models place several named people into shared contact actions such as an embrace or a carry. Scoring targets fused limbs, extra extremities and bodies passing through each other.
note: It had 40 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 10 GitHub stars.

name: MR-NIAH (Multi-Round Needles-In-A-Haystack)
description: Models must repeat one earlier answer from a long multi-turn dialogue history of 2K to 1M tokens. Scored by adjusted recall of key parts.
note: MiniMax built it as an open alternative to MRCR, in English and Chinese.

name: MRCR (Michelangelo, original)
description: Models retrieve the n-th of several similar requests hidden in a long synthetic conversation. Original Michelangelo version before MRCR v2.
note: Google reports from 2024 and early 2025 use this version. Later Google cards use the 8-needle MRCR v2.

name: MRCR v2
description: Multi-round coreference: retrieve the n-th of several similar requests hidden in a long synthetic conversation, up to 1M tokens.
note: Google's internal 8-needle MRCR, reported as up to 128K average and 1M pointwise since the Gemini 2.5 GA cards. Google open-sourced it in eval_hub on 2026-02-18. OpenAI's dataset is a separate test (openai-mrcr).

name: MS-CXR-T
description: Models compare a current and a prior chest X-ray of one patient and say whether a finding improved, stayed stable or got worse.
note: Released with BioViL-T (CVPR 2023) on PhysioNet. Google's MedGemma 1.5 reports macro accuracy on 1,326 examples.

name: MSEarth
description: Models answer questions about figures from Earth science papers across the atmosphere, cryosphere, hydrosphere, lithosphere and biosphere. Labs report the multiple choice split.
org: Shanghai AI Lab (Xiangyu Zhao, Lei Bai et al.)
note: The dataset has more than 289K figures with refined captions. It also has open-ended and captioning splits.

name: MSEB
description: Audio representations from any multimodal system are scored on eight core tasks, including transcription, classification, retrieval, reasoning, segmentation, clustering, reranking and reconstruction.
note: Google's EmbeddingGemma 2 card reports the Retrieval subset as MRR@10. A follow-up paper in 2026-05 benchmarks LLMs on MSEB. Not the same as MTEB's MAEB.

name: MSQA
description: Models answer culture-specific knowledge questions in 11 major languages.
note: In-house Seed benchmark. The blog gives no format or grader, so those fields are guesses.

name: MSR-VTT retrieval
description: Models retrieve videos from text queries in the MSR-VTT collection.

name: MSRVTT-QA
description: Models answer short open-ended questions about web video clips from the MSR-VTT captioning dataset. The question and answer pairs were generated automatically from the clip descriptions. Scored by answer accuracy.
org: Zhejiang University and collaborators (Xu et al.)
note: The repository also holds the sibling MSVD-QA set and the authors' model, and its 177 stars cover all three. Video language model papers report it often, but many now grade answers with a GPT judge, so scores vary by protocol.

name: MT-AIME (Cohere internal)
description: Cohere's internal machine translation of AIME 2025 problems into many languages (via Command A Translate). Answer accuracy.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Cohere).

name: MT-AIME2024
description: Models solve the 30 AIME 2024 problems translated into 55 languages. A rule-based verifier checks each final answer.
org: Yonsei University, OneLineAI, and KAIST AI
note: It is a subset of the MCLM multilingual math benchmark.

name: MT-Bench
description: 80 two-turn questions graded by GPT-4 as judge. Introduced LLM-as-judge methodology.

changes.text: The LMSYS maintainers doubled the default single-answer judge output limit from 1,024 to 2,048 tokens. Later runs can complete longer grading explanations before truncation, so comparisons should identify the harness revision.

note: Saturated. Historically important for judge-bias analysis.

name: MT-Bench-101
description: Models hold 1,388 multi-turn dialogues with 4,208 turns across 13 tasks from a three-tier ability taxonomy. GPT-4 scores each turn from 1 to 10.
org: Alibaba Group, CUHK MMLab and Shanghai AI Lab (Ge Bai, Jie Liu et al.)
note: Not the original MT-Bench from LMSYS. Accepted at ACL 2024.

name: MTEB
description: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark: retrieval, clustering, classification across languages and modalities.

name: MTEB Arena
description: Users compare retrieval, clustering and similarity results from two anonymous embedding models and vote for the better one.
note: The space says the arena is unavailable because of resource limits. It has about 116 likes.

name: MTOB
description: Models learn to translate between English and Kalamang, a language with under 200 speakers, from one grammar book. Scored by chrF.
note: Cards report half-book or full-book context and either translation direction, so scores vary by setup.

name: MTVQA-Test
description: Models answer 6,778 expert-written questions about text in 2,116 images across 9 languages, such as Arabic, Japanese, and Thai. Scoring is accuracy.
note: Humans score 79.7 in the paper, far above the models tested at release.

name: MU-Bench
description: Speech-to-text providers transcribe 4,270 caller utterances from real 8 kHz customer service phone calls in five locales, scored against human word-level transcripts.
note: Locales are en-US, es-MX, tr-TR, vi-VN and zh-CN. Data is CC BY-NC 4.0.

name: MuChoMusic
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about music recordings. It tests music knowledge and reasoning in audio-language models.
org: Weck et al. (Universitat Pompeu Fabra, Queen Mary University of London and others)
note: Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash reports a variant named MuchoMusic-RUL that the post does not define.

name: MuirBench
description: Models answer multiple choice questions over sets of several images, including unanswerable variants. Scored by accuracy.
org: Fei Wang, Xingyu Fu et al.

name: Multi-agent search (Anthropic internal benchmark)
description: Agents solve difficult information retrieval problems with web search, alone or as orchestrators that delegate to subagents.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Multi-dialect SQL evaluation (Cohere)
description: Models write SQL for SQLite, PostgreSQL, MySQL, PL/SQL and T-SQL databases. Scored by execution accuracy against gold databases.
note: In-house Cohere evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Multi-factual (Anthropic)
description: Models answer questions that each combine several closed-ended sub-questions on one topic. Answers are graded correct, incorrect or unsure against references.
note: In-house Anthropic factuality evaluation. Questions were built from article quotes and checked by hand. Score is the share answered correctly.

name: Multi-hop search factuality
description: Models with search answer multi-hop and tail-fact questions that need several sources. Reports accuracy and unfactual rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Multi-IF
description: Models follow verifiable instructions over three-turn conversations in eight languages, extending IFEval. Scored by instruction accuracy at each turn.

name: Multi-LCB
description: Models solve LiveCodeBench-style contest problems in twelve programming languages, with dated problems for contamination-aware evaluation.
note: Extends LiveCodeBench beyond Python. 60 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: Multi-SWE-bench
description: Agents resolve 1,632 GitHub issues in Java, TypeScript, JavaScript, Go, Rust, C, and C++ repos. Patches must pass the repos' tests.
note: A 300-instance subset, Multi-SWE-bench flash, followed in July 2025.

name: Multi-SWE-bench flash
description: Agents fix real GitHub issues in several languages, a 300-instance subset of Multi-SWE-bench chosen for fast evaluation and agent rollouts. Scored by tests passing.
note: Released 2025-07-15. Scores differ from the full Multi-SWE-bench and from the mini subset.

name: Multi-SWE-bench mini
description: Agents fix real GitHub issues in 8 programming languages, a 400-instance subset of Multi-SWE-bench made for cheaper runs. Scored by tests passing.
note: Released 2025-04-15. Scores differ from the full Multi-SWE-bench.

name: Multi-turn testing (Anthropic)
description: Models face multi-turn conversations that escalate toward harmful requests across risk areas. Score is the appropriate response rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: MultiChallenge
description: Multi-turn conversations testing instruction retention, inference memory, versioned editing and self-coherence. Graded by LLM judge with rubrics.
note: On 2026-02-03 Scale switched the judge to Gemini 2.5 Pro and rewrote the rubric questions of 54 tasks. Scores published before that date may not match the current board.

name: MultiChallenge Audio (OpenAI)
description: Speech-to-speech models answer an audio-friendly subset of MultiChallenge multi-turn questions that OpenAI converted from text to speech. Scored on instruction following accuracy.
note: OpenAI built it for the gpt-realtime launch on 2025-08-28. It differs from Scale's later Audio MultiChallenge (audio-mc), which uses native audio conversations.

name: MultiChallenge Audio (Xiaomi)
description: Models answer the final turn of MultiChallenge conversations converted to speech, with speech-to-text and speech-to-speech versions. Xiaomi built the conversion in house.
note: In-house Xiaomi evaluation. The tasks are not public. It differs from the OpenAI MultiChallenge Audio set.

name: MultiFinBen
description: Models complete 36 financial datasets across five languages and text, vision, and audio. The board reports a modality-balanced score.
org: The Fin AI (Qianqian Xie and coauthors)
note: The headline is the mean of text, vision, and audio averages. Unsupported modalities receive zero, as the official board specifies.

name: MultiHop-RAG
description: Retrieval-augmented systems answer 2,556 queries whose evidence is spread across two to four news articles. The queries also use document metadata, such as source and date. The benchmark scores both retrieval quality and answer accuracy.
org: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Yixuan Tang, Yi Yang)
note: COLM 2024. About 477 GitHub stars. It tests a whole retrieval pipeline, so scores depend on the retriever and reranker as well as the model.

name: Multilingual AIME 2024 (Mistral)
description: Models solve AIME 2024 problems translated into French, Spanish, German, Italian, Russian and Chinese, reasoning in the question language.
note: Mistral made the translations itself. The Magistral paper reports one score per language and no average.

name: Multilingual Exams
description: Models answer multilingual exam and MMLU-style questions. Qwen reports the average of M3Exam, IndoMMLU, ruMMLU, and translated MMLU.
note: A Qwen aggregate of public exam sets rather than a separate benchmark, and its parts changed between model releases.

name: Multilingual human evaluation
description: Human raters score model answers in 10 languages, including Arabic, Korean, and Thai, on a 1 to 5 scale. Results are averaged across languages.
note: This is an in-house evaluation, and Qwen never released the prompts.

name: Multilingual IFEval
description: Models follow IFEval instructions translated into eight languages, 100 examples each, which paid volunteers reviewed. Instruction compliance is checked as in IFEval.
note: A Qwen translation of IFEval described only in the Qwen2.5 blog.

name: Multilingual LibriSpeech
description: Models transcribe read audiobook speech in eight languages from LibriVox. Scored by word error rate.
note: Published at Interspeech 2020. Launch posts often report a subset of languages.

name: Multilingual MMBench
description: Models answer MMBench dev image questions in English, Chinese, Portuguese, Arabic, Turkish and Russian. Scored as accuracy per language.
note: The Parrot authors added it to VLMEvalKit in August 2024 as MTL_MMBench_DEV, next to MMMB.

name: Multilingual MMLU (Meta)
description: Models answer MMLU questions machine-translated into German, French, Italian, Portuguese, Hindi, Spanish and Thai, 5-shot.
note: In-house Meta translation made with Google Translate. It differs from OpenAI's MMMLU.

name: Multilingual performance on translated expert-domain tasks
description: Models answer an internal evaluation of tasks in expert domains such as science, law and engineering, machine translated into 17 languages. Scored as pass rate per language.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public. OpenAI made the grader stricter after running it on deep research.

name: Multilingual Safety
description: An automated safety policy evaluation measures policy violations across multiple languages.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. Model cards report only the change in percentage points against an earlier Gemini model.

name: Multilingual Understanding
description: Models answer five multilingual comprehension sets, BELEBELE, XCOPA, XWinograd, XStoryCloze, and PAWS-X. Qwen reports the average accuracy.
note: This is a Qwen composite score, not a standalone benchmark.

name: MultiLoKo
description: Locally relevant knowledge questions in 31 languages, plus translations. Scored by exact match.

name: Multimodal policy red-teaming (Anthropic)
aliases: Trust & Safety multimodal policy red teaming
description: Models answer multi-turn image and text conversations on harmful topics such as child safety, weapons and fraud. Score is the share of harmless responses.
note: In-house Anthropic Trust and Safety evaluation. The Claude 3 model card used 378 prompts.

name: Multimodal Troubleshooting Virology
description: Models troubleshoot virology lab scenarios, sometimes with images, and must select every correct answer. Scored as refusal-adjusted pass@1.
note: Questions come from SecureBio. OpenAI Preparedness evaluation.

name: MultiNRC
description: Models answer over 1,000 reasoning questions written by native speakers in French, Spanish and Chinese. Questions cover linguistic reasoning, wordplay, cultural knowledge and culturally grounded math. A GPT-4.1 judge compares each answer with a short reference answer.
note: Each question made at least 3 of 5 frontier models fail. Cultural and math questions also have English translations. No model scored above 50% at release.

name: MultiPL-E
description: Models write code for HumanEval and MBPP problems translated into 18 other programming languages. Scored by pass@1 on unit tests.
org: Northeastern University Programming Research Lab (NuPRL) et al.

changes.text: The maintainers added translated MBPP tasks alongside HumanEval tasks. Scores must identify which source task set they use.
The maintainers added four programming languages and corrected four Scala problems in version 3.0. The release also changed prompt whitespace across several existing languages.
The maintainers removed a spurious Lua stop token. New Lua evaluations avoid premature truncation and can score higher than earlier runs.

name: MultiRC
description: Models pick all correct answers to questions that need reasoning over several sentences of a paragraph. Scored by F1 over answer options.
note: Saturated. Also part of SuperGLUE.

name: Multiturn Jailbreak Evaluations
description: Models face adaptive multi-turn jailbreak attackers with growing attack budgets. Scored as worst-case defender success rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Results appear as charts by attacker budget.

name: Muse-targeted cyber misuse and violation red-teaming
description: An automated red-teaming agent tries to misuse the Muse runtime across six attack categories. Reports attack success rate per category.
note: In-house Meta pre-launch stress test of early Muse builds. No overall score.

name: Music Arena
description: Users write a music prompt, listen to tracks from two text-to-music systems, and vote. Preferences, listening data and feedback feed a leaderboard.
org: Carnegie Mellon University (G-CLef) with Arena and Sony researchers
note: An LLM router adapts each prompt to the input types of different music systems. Preference data is released on Hugging Face.

name: Music Arena Vocal
description: Models generate music with vocals. Listeners compare anonymous tracks, and separate vocal preference votes determine the Arena score.
org: Carnegie Mellon University (G-CLef) with Arena and Sony researchers
note: Vocal votes form a separate pool from the instrumental leaderboard.

name: MuSR
description: Models answer questions about long generated narratives such as murder mysteries, object placement and team allocation. Each item needs several soft reasoning steps over the story.
note: One of the six tasks of the Hugging Face Open LLM Leaderboard v2.

name: MusTBench
description: Models answer five kinds of music questions that need the correct time region of the audio, such as instrument entries. Music experts validated the items.
note: Qwen reports it as music understanding.

name: MVBench
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions across 20 temporal video tasks that a single frame cannot solve. Scored by accuracy.
note: TVBench authors found many MVBench questions solvable without temporal reasoning.

name: MVPBench
description: Models answer video questions on spatial, temporal and intuitive physics. Each question comes in a pair of near-identical videos with opposite answers, so text or single-frame shortcuts fail.
note: Released with V-JEPA 2. The leaderboard uses the mini split of about 5,700 items. Videos come from nine public datasets.

name: MyClaw Bench
description: Models run inside the OpenClaw agent on 45 tasks in four difficulty tiers built from real usage data. Some tasks use an LLM judge.
note: Vendor benchmark for picking a model for OpenClaw. About 220 GitHub stars.

name: MyPCBench
description: Computer-use agents work in a personalized Linux desktop with 17 simulated logged-in web apps and a user's history, across 184 tasks.
note: Best reported model at launch was Claude Opus 4.6 at 55.4%.

name: Mystery Game Puzzles
description: 100 mid-game positions from an undisclosed puzzle variant of a well-known game. Model picks the single best move, checked against an answer key.
note: Game identity, prompts and positions are kept secret to prevent targeted preparation. Likely the 'game-puzzles' benchmark in the Epoch post.

name: MysteryMechanism
description: Agents recover a hidden mathematical law from two noisy observations and a few experiments they choose. The submitted expression is run on private probes and passes if its error is under a noise-aware threshold.
note: Inputs are anonymous, with no domain context. A blinded audit records whether each solved trace named the source domain.

name: NanoGPT Speedrun
description: Improve a small GPT training script to reach a target validation loss as fast as possible on fixed hardware.
org: Keller Jordan (community); OpenAI and METR variants
note: OpenAI and METR run their own constrained variants on one H100 or a budget. METR used it in July 2026 to define an expenditure horizon, the budget where humans become cheaper than agents.

name: NanoGPT-Bench
description: Coding agents with a fixed H100-hour budget and no internet try to improve on a strong NanoGPT speedrun starting point. The score is the share of later human progress recovered.
note: At launch the best agent recovered 9.3% of five months of human record progress. Different from the community NanoGPT Speedrun record.

name: NarrativeQA
description: Models answer questions about books and movie scripts, either from a Wikipedia summary or from the full story. The questions need an understanding of the whole narrative rather than one matching passage. Answers are free text, scored against two reference answers with F1, ROUGE-L or BLEU.
org: DeepMind and University of Oxford (Kočiský et al.)
note: HELM Lite runs it as one of its ten scenarios. Long-context suites reuse the full-story version. About 521 GitHub stars.

name: Native Code Exploitation (Meta)
description: Agents exploit private native binary challenges end to end, usually to gain remote code execution. Uses 12 templates with randomized memory layouts, scored by challenges solved at pass@10.
note: In-house Meta evaluation. The tasks are not public. The set has 5 easy, 5 medium and 2 hard templates.

name: Natural Questions
description: Models answer real Google search questions. Model cards usually use the open-domain version, scored by exact match against short answers from Wikipedia.
note: The original task reads a full Wikipedia page, while model cards mostly report the closed-book variant.

name: Natural2Code
description: Models write Python functions in HumanEval format from new prompts kept off the web. Unit tests decide correctness.
note: In-house Google DeepMind set that was never released, built to avoid web leakage.

name: NaturalBench
description: Models answer 10,000 human-checked questions on natural images. Each question pairs with two images that need different answers, so a model cannot pass without looking.
org: Carnegie Mellon University and others (Baiqi Li, Zhiqiu Lin et al.)
note: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks paper. Group scores credit a model only when it gets all paired questions and images right.

name: NaturalCodeBench
description: Models solve 402 Python and Java problems taken from real user queries to online coding services in 6 domains. Semi-automatically built tests check each solution.
note: Prompts come in Chinese and English versions. Labs report a total over both.

name: NatureBench
description: Coding agents work on 90 tasks distilled from Nature-family papers, each in its own container, and try to match or beat the published results.
note: 67 upvotes on Hugging Face papers and 137 GitHub stars.

name: Needle In A Haystack
description: Models retrieve a planted fact from long filler text at varied context lengths and insertion depths. Scored by retrieval accuracy.
note: Most long-context models score near 100%, and labs run their own variants, so scores are not comparable.

name: NeedleBench
description: Models retrieve and reason over one or several facts inserted at different depths in bilingual long texts of set lengths.
note: Labs report one score per context length.

name: NeedleBench V2
description: Models retrieve one or several needles and reason over fictional multi-needle facts in English and Chinese haystacks from 4K to 1M tokens. The overall score is the plain average of three tasks.
note: V2 replaces the R4C-based reasoning needles with fictional facts, spaces Ancestral Trace needles in powers of 2 and drops the weighted average. Scores are not comparable with V1. The release month follows arXiv v2 (2025-05-09).

name: Neptune
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about long videos that need reasoning over many segments.
note: Gemini 2.5 report uses the test subset, 0-shot, 1,024 frames.

name: Network CTF challenges (Anthropic)
description: Agents perform reconnaissance and exploit vulnerabilities across multiple networked machines in capture-the-flag challenges.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Neutrality evaluation
description: Single and multi-turn prompts on politics, civics, identity and religion test whether models avoid taking sides. Reports neutral response rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: NExT-QA
description: Models answer causal, temporal and descriptive questions about short videos of daily life. Labs usually report the multiple choice split.
org: National University of Singapore (Junbin Xiao et al.)

name: Next.js Agent Evals
description: Coding agents with their models do real Next.js tasks. The board reports success rate with and without an AGENTS.md file, plus duration and cost.
note: Rerun whenever the evals change, last on 2026-10-30. Top agents reach 97%, so it is near saturation. About 330 GitHub stars.

name: Nexus
description: Models write function calls for queries over real-world APIs, including nested and parallel calls. Scoring is the function calling success rate.
note: Nexusflow released 8 of its 9 tasks and kept one internal to limit overfitting.

name: NL2Repo-Bench
description: From one natural-language requirements document and an empty workspace, agent builds an installable Python library. Scored by original project's test pass rate.

changes.text: The maintainers revised test-count denominators for 34 tasks. The harness divides passed tests by these counts, so unchanged test outcomes can produce different success rates.

note: 104 tasks. Labs add anti-cheat blocks on pip download/git clone of the target repo to stop reward hacking.

name: No-CoT math time horizon
description: Models solve math problems without a visible chain of thought. Scored as the human task length in minutes the model solves reliably.
note: Third-party UK AISI measurement. Higher means more reasoning without visible CoT, which UK AISI treats as less monitorable.

name: nocot-bench (NCRI)
description: Reasoning problems answered without chain of thought (e.g., Brew multi-hop tasks). Measures forward-pass reasoning relevant to monitorability.

name: NoisyBench
description: Models answer tasks from 11 existing datasets in RAG, reasoning, alignment and tool use while their context holds distractors, such as random documents, unrelated chat history and hard negatives. The score shows how much accuracy drops from the clean version of each task.
note: Built from existing datasets with added noise. The paper also proposes a training reward (RARE). 33 Hugging Face upvotes. No code link was listed on the paper page on 2026-11-05.

name: NoLiMa
description: Models find a needle in a long haystack when the question and the needle share almost no words, so they must infer a latent link. Accuracy is compared across context lengths.
org: Adobe Research and LMU Munich (Modarressi et al.)
note: At 32K tokens, 10 of 12 tested models fell below half their short-context score. Data uses an Adobe Research License for non-commercial use. About 210 GitHub stars.

name: NoLiMa-Hard
description: Models retrieve latent associations for the ten hardest NoLiMa question-needle pairs. Results are reported separately at four context lengths.
org: Adobe Research and LMU Munich (Modarressi et al.)
note: The parent has no cross-context aggregate. Context boards contain the scores. The first release month is not established by the source.

name: NOVA-63
aliases: Native Omni-lingual Versatile Assessments of 63 Disciplines
description: Models answer questions written by native speakers in 14 languages across 63 academic disciplines. Scoring is accuracy.
note: The Hugging Face dataset is empty and marked under review, and nearly all reported scores come from Qwen.

name: Novel compiler task (Anthropic)
description: Agents build a compiler for an unusual programming language from a specification and test cases.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Novel logical reasoning problems expert evaluation (Z.ai)
description: Human experts score model answers to new multi-step logic problems with a fixed scoring standard for each question.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation built to avoid contamination. The problems are not public.

name: NTREX-128
description: Models translate 1,997 English news sentences into 128 languages, with human reference translations. Scored with metrics such as COMET or chrF.
note: Cohere's Command A report scores it with COMET-20. The English source is the WMT19 newstest2019 set, with document boundaries kept.

name: Nuscene
description: Models localize named objects as 3D boxes in nuScenes driving camera images. Scored by mAP.
note: The catalog description infers a camera grounding setup from a model report. The official nuScenes detection board ranks NDS and has a separate nuscenes-detection proposal.

name: nuScenes Detection
description: Models detect 3D objects in nuScenes sensor data. The official test leaderboard ranks submissions by nuScenes Detection Score.
note: NDS stays on its raw 0–1 scale. Sensor configurations and submission identities remain separate. This is not an inferred vision-language grounding setup.

name: NV Chat Benchmark
description: Models answer chat prompts from an internal NVIDIA set. The Nemotron 3.5 Super VL card labels the score an LMArena v3 proxy.
note: The technical report calls it an internal chat benchmark developed at NVIDIA and gives no method details. The scoring type is a guess.

name: NYU CTF Bench
description: Agents solve 200 capture the flag challenges from seven years of CSAW competitions. Six categories cover crypto, forensics, pwn, reverse, web and misc. Each runs in Docker.
note: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks track. Selected from 528 CSAW challenges over a decade. Earlier arXiv versions used the name NYU CTF Dataset. Used beside Cybench and InterCode-CTF in later work.

name: o11y-bench
description: Agents query metrics, logs and traces in a live Grafana stack, investigate incidents and fix dashboards. Grading checks claims against facts read from the same environment.
note: 64 tasks built on Harbor, scored pass^3. Version 1.1 (2026-10-28) made grading more grounded and reproducible, so check comparability with 1.0 scores.

name: OAI-repo Sabotage v2
description: Agents try to complete a hidden sabotage side task in OpenAI code without detection. Scored on side task success while evading CoT and action monitors.
note: In-house OpenAI monitorability evaluation. Results appear as charts by reasoning length.

name: Objectron
description: Models predict 3D bounding boxes of objects in short object-centric videos across nine categories. Scored by 3D intersection over union.
note: Released as a dataset with 14,819 annotated videos. Qwen3-VL reports it as 3D grounding.

name: OBLIQ-Bench
description: Retrievers search large real corpora for documents that match a latent pattern, such as an implicit stance. The suite has five such oblique search problems.
note: Targets first-stage retrieval. AINews called it a major IR benchmark release.

name: OCBench
description: 28 simulated manipulation tasks with human-like scripted demonstrators for controlled BC and RL studies. Policies scored by task success rate.
note: Design: scripted policies mimic human demos (narrow, temporally correlated, smoothly random via Hermite splines, with mistakes and recoveries), giving unlimited controllable data. Reproduces known BC effects. No leaderboard.

name: OccuBench
description: Agents do 100 professional task scenarios across 10 industries and 65 domains. Language world models simulate each domain's tools so tasks stay solvable.
note: 69 HF paper upvotes.

name: OCR Arena
description: Users upload a document, compare two anonymous OCR or vision-language models side by side, and vote. Votes become Elo ratings.
note: Launched with more than 10 models on Hacker News on 2025-11-21 (216 points).

name: OCR-Reasoning
description: Models answer 1,069 human-annotated questions that need reasoning over text-rich images. The questions cover 6 reasoning abilities and 18 practical tasks.
note: Accepted at ICLR 2026. The data also holds step-by-step reasoning annotations. NVIDIA grades answers with a GPT-4o-mini judge.

name: OCRBench
description: Models answer 1,000 checked questions on text recognition, scene text, documents, key information extraction, and handwritten math. The score counts correct answers.
org: Yuliang Liu, Xiang Bai et al.
note: OCRBench v2, released in December 2024 with 10,000 pairs, is a separate version.

name: OCRBench v2
description: Visual-text localization and reasoning tasks across 31 scenarios (documents, scenes, charts). Averaged task accuracy.

changes.text: The maintainers introduced a private evaluation dataset and quarterly leaderboard updates. Private-set results measure a different question set from the public release.
The maintainers corrected English answer-length routing. Longer answers now receive edit-distance scoring, while short answers use substring matching.

name: OctoCodingbench
description: Agents complete 72 coding tasks while following rules from system prompts, AGENTS.md files, skills, and memory. An LLM judge checks 2,422 pass or fail items.
note: MiniMax first reported it as internal, then released the tasks in January 2026.

name: ODinW-13
description: Models detect objects in 13 varied real-world datasets, such as aquarium and aerial images, from text category names. Scored by mean average precision.
note: A 13-dataset subset of the 35-task ODinW benchmark in ELEVATER.

name: ODV-Bench
description: Streaming video models answer real-time questions about autonomous driving footage.
note: Introduced with the StreamForest model, a NeurIPS 2025 spotlight. The format field is a guess.

name: OdysseyArena
description: Agents explore interactive environments built from four transition primitives and must work out the hidden dynamics over long horizons. OdysseyArena-Lite has 120 standard tasks.
note: 61 HF paper upvotes.

name: OdysseyArena AI Trading
description: Agents trade under hidden market dynamics. The score is average return relative to initial capital over four trials.
note: One track of OdysseyArena. The OdysseyArena record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: OdysseyArena Energy Dispatch
description: Agents manage energy dispatch under hidden rules. The score is average task success over four trials.
note: One track of OdysseyArena. The OdysseyArena record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: OdysseyArena Repo System
description: Agents operate repositories with changing hidden rules. The score is average task success over four trials.
note: One track of OdysseyArena. The OdysseyArena record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: OdysseyArena Turn on Lights
description: Agents learn hidden switches and turn on lights. The score is average task success over four trials.
note: One track of OdysseyArena. The OdysseyArena record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: OfficeQA
description: Grounded reasoning over a large corpus of U.S. Treasury Bulletin documents: locate tables and compute precise numeric answers.
note: Pro = 133 hard questions. Pro V2 (90 questions, new corpus) followed. Answers gated on HF to limit crawling.

name: OfficeQA Pro
description: Models answer the 133 hardest OfficeQA questions by finding tables in U.S. Treasury Bulletin documents and computing exact numeric answers.
note: Harder subset of OfficeQA recommended for frontier models. Kept apart from the full OfficeQA set.

name: OfficeQA Pro V2
description: Agents answer 90 analytical questions using about 120,000 pages of U.S. Treasury Accounts of Receipts and Expenditures from 1793 to 2024. Answers are scored by exact match.
note: Databricks built it for the Grounded Reasoning Cup and released it on 2026-08-06. It uses a new corpus, so scores are not comparable with OfficeQA Pro. The paper link is the original OfficeQA suite.

name: OIBench
description: Models write programs for 250 original olympiad in informatics problems. Hidden tests check correctness, and time and space completion curves compare efficiency with reference solutions.
note: The paper compares models with human contest participants. LongCat launch posts report the English split as OIBench EN.

name: OJBench
description: Models write C++ or Python solutions to 232 competition problems from NOI and ICPC. Judge test cases score each solution by pass@1.
org: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications, Tsinghua University, and others

name: OK-VQA
description: Models answer over 14,000 visual questions that need outside knowledge beyond the image. Scoring is VQA accuracy against human answers.
org: Allen Institute for AI and Carnegie Mellon University

name: Okapi MMLU
description: Models answer MMLU multiple choice questions that ChatGPT translated into 26 languages. Scoring is accuracy.
note: The questions are machine translated, so translation errors and English cultural bias remain.

name: olmOCR-Bench
description: OCR systems convert 1,403 PDFs to markdown. 7,010 unit tests check text presence and absence, reading order, tables and math.
note: On Hugging Face's official benchmark list. Many OCR model cards report it.

name: OlympiadBench
description: Models solve bilingual olympiad-level math and physics problems in Chinese and English, many with images. Answers are checked against a key.
org: OpenBMB and Tsinghua University (He et al.)
note: Accepted at ACL 2024. The dataset was updated on 2024-03-24 and 2024-07-17. Labs report the full multimodal set or a text-only subset.

name: OlympicArena
description: Models solve 11,163 bilingual problems from 62 international olympiad competitions in seven fields, some with images. Answers are checked against keys.
org: Shanghai Jiao Tong University GAIR Lab
note: Fields are math, physics, chemistry, biology, geography, astronomy and computer science. Baidu reports it under math.

name: OMEGA
description: Models solve generated competition-style math problems that test exploratory, compositional and transformative generalization beyond training patterns. Answers are checked automatically.
org: UC Berkeley, Ai2 and University of Washington (Sun et al.)
note: Ai2 hosts the explorative, compositional and transformative splits and a 500-problem set on Hugging Face. Olmo 3 cards report it.

name: Omni-Cloze
description: Models write detailed captions of audio, visual and audio-visual clips. A cloze test on the caption content scores the detail.
note: Released with the Omni-Captioner paper. Qwen3.5-Omni and Qwen3.8-Omni-Flash report it.

name: Omni-InteractScope
description: Omnimodal models watch continuous video and audio streams and must respond at the right moment with answers, alerts, warnings, tool calls or step guidance. Scoring joins content and timing.
org: Alibaba Group (Qwen, Alibaba Token Hub) + Hong Kong Polytechnic University
note: 1,479 interactions and 1,790 response targets in eight task groups. GPT-4o judges content, and tool calls are scored by rule. 12 model setups in the first release. Dataset is CC BY-NC 4.0.

name: Omni-InteractScope Explicit Request
description: Models answer explicit requests during audio and video streams. The score is the published average across tasks T1 through T7.
org: Alibaba Group (Qwen, Alibaba Token Hub) + Hong Kong Polytechnic University
note: One track of Omni-InteractScope. The Omni-InteractScope record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Omni-InteractScope Proactive
description: Models provide timely proactive assistance during audio and video streams. The score is the published T8 assistance recall.
org: Alibaba Group (Qwen, Alibaba Token Hub) + Hong Kong Polytechnic University
note: One track of Omni-InteractScope. The Omni-InteractScope record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Omni-MATH
description: Models solve 4,428 Olympiad-level competition math problems across 33 subdomains and 10 difficulty levels. A GPT-4 or Omni-Judge grader checks answers.
org: Peking University and Alibaba et al.

name: Omni3D
description: A large benchmark for 3D object detection from a single image, built by unifying indoor and outdoor datasets such as SUN RGB-D, ARKitScenes, Hypersim, Objectron, KITTI and nuScenes. Vision-language models answer its 3D grounding questions.
note: Language-model reports use question sets drawn from Omni3D rather than the original detection metric, so numbers differ by harness.

name: OmniAI OCR Benchmark
description: Multimodal models and OCR providers extract text and JSON fields from documents. Accuracy is measured on both plain text and structured extraction.
note: About 75 likes on Hugging Face.

name: OmniBench
description: Models answer multiple choice questions that need an image, an audio clip and text together. Scored by accuracy.
note: Omni models such as Qwen Omni and LongCat-Flash-Omni report it.

name: OmniCap-IF
description: Models write captions for videos with audio while following detailed user constraints. Captions are scored on format and content compliance.
note: Labs report two rates, CSR and ISR.

name: OmniDocBench
description: Diverse PDF pages with layout, text, table and formula annotations. Parsing scored by edit distance and TEDS.
note: The first release has 981 pages and reports edit distance, where lower is better. The repo main branch moved to v1.5 in 2025-09 and v1.6 in 2026-04, and v1.0 lives on branch v1_0.

name: OmniDocBench v1.5
description: Models parse 1,355 PDF pages into text, tables and formulas. The Overall score averages text accuracy from edit distance, table TEDS and formula CDM.
note: Adds 374 pages to v1.0, raises newspaper and note scans to 200 DPI, and drops the Chinese and English split. Higher Overall is better, unlike the v1.0 edit distance.

name: OmniDocBench v1.6
description: Models parse 1,651 PDF pages, including nested tables, dense formulas and unusual layouts, into text, tables and formulas. Scored by the v1.5 Overall formula.
note: Adds 296 harder pages and a new matching method, MGAM, on the prediction side. v1.7 on 2026-04-30 added skills-based evaluation without new pages, so it stays in this record.

name: OmniGAIA
description: Agents answer multi-hop questions that need reasoning and multi-turn tool use across video, audio and image inputs. Questions come from an omni-modal event graph built on real data.
org: Renmin University of China (RUC-NLPIR) and others
note: Qwen reports it as omni-modal web search with no harness.

name: Omnilingual-Gaia2
description: Agents run Gaia2 execution, search, ambiguity and adaptability scenarios translated into 10 languages, graded against the scenario oracle with multilingual judge prompts.
note: Meta says a correct non-English answer is often scored as a miss without the multilingual judge prompt. Dataset created 2026-08-11.

name: OmniMMI
description: Omni models answer 2,290 questions on 1,121 streaming videos, including proactive tasks where they must decide when to respond.
note: Published at CVPR 2025. Seed1.8 evaluates it in a proactive manner.

name: OmniParseBench
description: Document parsers convert single pages to text, and 16,288 binary unit tests on 2,937 pages check the output. The headline joins text, table and layout subscores.
note: The results table also lists cost per 1,000 pages and refusals. Code is Apache 2.0 and page data keeps each source's license. Datalab includes its own parsers.

name: OmniSpatial
description: Vision language models answer over 8,400 spatial reasoning questions in four groups: dynamic reasoning, complex spatial logic, spatial interaction and perspective taking.
note: Questions are manually annotated and span 50 subcategories grounded in cognitive psychology.

name: OmniVBench
description: Video generators make videos that follow many kinds of reference inputs at once. Scoring checks that each reference factor is kept, separated and placed correctly.
note: It had 33 Hugging Face paper upvotes.

name: OmniVideoBench
description: Models answer 1,000 questions about videos that need audio and visual evidence together. Each question has annotated reasoning steps.
note: Qwen reports a static setting and an agent setting with Qwen Code.

name: OncologyBench
description: Separate agents run analyses of cancer research data, and a final agent makes a decision on detection, diagnosis or treatment. Strict scoring needs full marks on both parts.
note: Part of LatchBio's BioBench suite on benchmarks.bio. The V1 set has 25 evaluations. Release month is the GitHub repo creation month.

name: OneIG-Bench
description: Image models generate images from prompts with English and Chinese evaluation splits.
note: GLM-Image reports English and Chinese overall scores in its official model card.

name: Online Experience (Moonshot)
description: Agents produce the deliverable file types that real online users request most often, following the distribution of real usage.
note: In-house Moonshot AI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Online-Mind2Web
description: Web agents do 300 tasks on 136 live websites. An LLM judge reads the agent's trajectory and decides whether the task succeeded.
note: From the paper An Illusion of Progress? Assessing the Current State of Web Agents.

name: Open Arabic LLM Leaderboard v1
description: Models are scored on AlGhafa with native and translated sets, the ACVA and AceGPT sets, and translated MMLU and EXAMS. The board ranks by the average.
org: Open Arabic LLM Leaderboard team (2A2I and TII) with Hugging Face
note: Version 2 (2025-02) removed saturated and machine-translated tasks and fixed an AlGhafa scoring bug. Scores are not comparable across versions.

name: Open Arabic LLM Leaderboard v2
description: Models are scored on native Arabic tasks (AlGhafa native subsets, ArabicMMLU, Exams, MadinahQA, AraTrust, ALRAGE, ArbMMLU-HT) and ranked by the average.
org: Open Arabic LLM Leaderboard team (2A2I and community) with Hugging Face
note: Version 2 dropped saturated and machine-translated tasks from version 1 (2024) and fixed a scoring bug in AlGhafa, so scores are not comparable with version 1. ALRAGE is judged by a model.

name: Open ASR Leaderboard
description: Speech recognition models transcribe the test sets of several English and multilingual corpora. Scored by average word error rate, with speed reported next to it.
note: Built on the ESB test sets. ASR model cards often report its average WER.

name: Open Ended Questions (hallucination)
description: Models write open-ended factual text such as biographies, checked against Wikipedia. Scored as average number of incorrect statements.
note: In-house OpenAI hallucination evaluation.

name: Open LLM Leaderboard v2
description: Hugging Face ran open models on IFEval, BBH, MATH Level 5, GPQA, MuSR and MMLU-Pro and averaged normalized scores.
note: Ran thousands of open models. Every Eval Ever files it as hfopenllm_v2.

name: OpenAI agentic alignment evals
description: Respecting auto-review and warnings, an ExploitGym honeypot, coding and blocker deception, broken search tool, realistic work environments, agent-to-agent messages.

name: OpenAI cyber safety evaluations (incl. Daybreak Blue)
description: Refusal and helpfulness evaluations for cyber requests, including the Daybreak Blue set for enabling defensive security work.

name: OpenAI Deployment Simulation
description: Replays representative production or internal Codex traffic on a candidate model to forecast misaligned or disallowed behavior before launch.

name: OpenAI Dynamic Mental Health Benchmarks
description: Multi-turn conversations with adversarial simulated users on mental-health risks. Scored on safe and supportive responses.

name: OpenAI GPT-Red jailbreak and prompt-injection evals
description: Static jailbreaks from attacker models (half from a held-out attacker), adaptive multi-turn attackers, and direct and indirect prompt-injection sets.

name: OpenAI internal AI self-improvement evals
description: Internal Research Debugging (41 real research bugs plus alignment-auditing tasks) and KernelGen 1P (kernels for OpenAI first-party hardware).
note: Replaced saturated Monorepo-Bench and OPQA.

name: OpenAI internal cyber evaluations
description: Internal suites: curated public CTF challenges, VulnLMP long-horizon vulnerability research on real software, and Sandbox Bench (22 mostly zero-day targets).

name: OpenAI monitorability evals
description: Open suite from 'Monitoring Monitorability' testing whether CoT and action monitors catch hidden properties of agent behavior.

name: OpenAI MRCR
description: Models read a long synthetic chat that hides 2, 4 or 8 identical writing requests and must reproduce the response to the i-th one. Scored by mean string match ratio, in context bins from 4K to 1M tokens.
note: Inspired by Google's MRCR but built from new GPT-4o text, so it is a different dataset from GDM MRCR v2. Labs report it by needle count and context bin.

name: OpenAI MRCR v2
description: Models read a long synthetic chat that hides 2, 4 or 8 identical writing requests and must reproduce the response to the i-th one. Scored by mean string match ratio per context bin.
note: The 2025-12-05 fix replaced about 10% of samples that held too many needles and about 5% with wrong ground truth. OpenAI calls the result version 2 from GPT-5.2 on, and Anthropic system cards use the same name.

name: OpenAI performance in cases flagged by users
description: Model answers de-identified ChatGPT prompts that users flagged for factual errors. Scored on any error and on repeating the flagged error.
note: Adversarially selected set. OpenAI warns error rates are far above production and are not hallucination rates. Results only in a chart. An appendix version for GPT-6 Sol and Luna was added 2026-09-22.

name: OpenAI Production Benchmarks and safe-completion evals
description: Hard production-derived prompts per policy category, under-18 evals, agentic safe completions and image-input evals. Scored on safe completion rate.

name: OpenAI PRs
description: Agents replicate internal OpenAI pull requests from a pre-PR branch and a prompt. Graded by hidden unit tests as pass@1.
note: In-house OpenAI AI self-improvement evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: OpenAI Research Engineer Interview: Coding
description: Models solve 18 self-contained coding problems like those in OpenAI interviews. Scored as pass@1.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation from the internal interview question bank.

name: OpenAI Research Engineer Interview: Multiple Choice
description: Models answer 97 multiple-choice questions drawn from OpenAI machine learning interview topics. Scored as cons@32.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation from the internal interview question bank.

name: OpenAI user-flagged hallucination eval
aliases: Performance in Cases Flagged by Users
description: Production conversations users flagged for factual errors. Measures the rate of incorrect claims.

name: OpenAI-Proof Q&A
description: Agents diagnose 20 real OpenAI research and engineering bottlenecks using code, logs and run artifacts. Scored as pass@1.
note: In-house OpenAI AI self-improvement evaluation. Each problem took an OpenAI team over a day.

name: OpenAudioBench
description: Models answer spoken questions in five sets: Reasoning QA, Llama Questions, Web Questions, TriviaQA and AlpacaEval. Knowledge sets use accuracy and the open sets use a model score.
note: Released with Baichuan-Omni-1.5. Labs report the five subsets separately.

name: OpenAudioBench AlpacaEval
description: Models respond to spoken AlpacaEval instructions. The score is the published judge quality score.
note: One track of OpenAudioBench. The OpenAudioBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: OpenAudioBench Llama Questions
description: Models answer spoken Llama Questions. The score is the published accuracy.
note: One track of OpenAudioBench. The OpenAudioBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: OpenAudioBench Reasoning QA
description: Models answer spoken reasoning questions. The score is the published accuracy.
note: One track of OpenAudioBench. The OpenAudioBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: OpenAudioBench TriviaQA
description: Models answer spoken TriviaQA questions. The score is the published judge quality score.
note: One track of OpenAudioBench. The OpenAudioBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: OpenAudioBench Web Questions
description: Models answer spoken Web Questions. The score is the published judge quality score.
note: One track of OpenAudioBench. The OpenAudioBench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: OpenBookQA
description: Models answer elementary science multiple-choice questions that need a given core science fact plus common knowledge. Scored by accuracy.
note: Saturated by frontier models.

name: OpenComputer
description: Computer-use agents complete 1,000 desktop tasks across 33 real applications, including browsers, office tools, creative software, development environments and messaging apps. App-specific verifiers inspect the final application state, and the harness gives partial credit from the recorded trajectory.
note: The tasks are generated by a pipeline and then finalized, and the verifiers improve themselves from execution feedback. The authors report that open models score much lower here than on OSWorld-Verified. 42 Hugging Face upvotes and about 32 GitHub stars.

name: OpenDesign Arena
description: Models create design artifacts in the OpenDesign tool, and the board reports an evaluation score out of 100 with cost and speed per artifact.
note: Vendor board inside a design product. How scores are judged needs a check.

name: OpenEQA
description: Agents answer over 1,600 open-vocabulary questions about real indoor scenes from recorded episodes or active exploration. A judge model scores answers against human answers.

name: OpenFrontiers-Bench
description: Agents try to rediscover proofs of research math problems, most resolved during 2026, stated in Lean 4. Two independent checkers grade the formal proofs, with closed-book, frozen-retrieval and live-web settings.
note: 200 problems, 110 resolved in 2026 and 90 still open. Seven agents were run on the HQ-50 subset. Closed-book agents rediscovered at most 7 of 40 resolved problems. A corpus of 12,151 open problems comes with it.

name: OpenHands Index
description: Models run in the same OpenHands agent setup on five areas: issue resolution, greenfield builds, frontend work, test writing and information gathering. Accuracy and cost are both reported.
note: Built from SWE-bench Verified, commit0, SWE-bench Multimodal, SWT-Bench and GAIA. A public API serves the leaderboard.

name: Opening Lines Arena
description: Models write opening lines for stories. Pairwise votes determine the published Arena rating.
note: The official API publishes an Arena rating, confidence interval and vote count. Voter identity requires confirmation from the board description.

name: OpenRCA
description: Agents find the root cause of 335 software failures from enterprise telemetry logs, metrics and traces. Scored on component, start time and reason.
org: Microsoft, CUHK-Shenzhen and Tsinghua University (Xu et al.)
note: Published at ICLR 2025. The data covers telecom, banking and online marketplace systems.

name: OpenRSI Index
description: Agents run autoresearch on real open-source model development projects with their original code, data and checkpoints, for 60 or more hours. Fixed verifiers score the result against the human recipe they started from.
org: OpenRSI Foundation (UW-led, academic and industry partners)
note: Signature tasks, such as Qwen-122B RL and a Marin scaling-ladder optimizer, use 256 H100s and up to about 20,000 H100-hours per run. Public tasks need 1 to 8 H100s. Repo has 289 stars.

name: OpenRSI Index ACE Playbook Inspection and Repair
description: Agents repair a reasoning playbook under a fixed budget. The score is held-out Formula exact-answer accuracy as a fraction.
org: OpenRSI Foundation (UW-led, academic and industry partners)
note: One track of OpenRSI Index. The OpenRSI Index record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: OpenRSI Index Isaac Lab PegInsert Reward Search
description: Agents design robot training rewards under a fixed budget. The score is held-out peg-insertion success as a fraction.
org: OpenRSI Foundation (UW-led, academic and industry partners)
note: One track of OpenRSI Index. The OpenRSI Index record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.
