name: OpenRSI Index Kev Decision Architecture
description: Agents improve a decision model under a fixed budget. The score is the published exponential of negative macro log loss.
org: OpenRSI Foundation (UW-led, academic and industry partners)
note: One track of OpenRSI Index. The OpenRSI Index record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: OpenRSI Index Learnability-Aware Long/Short CoT Adaptation
description: Agents adapt mathematical reasoning examples under a fixed training budget. The score is accuracy across five math benchmarks.
org: OpenRSI Foundation (UW-led, academic and industry partners)
note: One track of OpenRSI Index. The OpenRSI Index record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: OpenRSI Index Marin Scaling Ladder
description: Agents design one optimizer for six model sizes. The score is the published complete six-rung reward relative to AdamH.
org: OpenRSI Foundation (UW-led, academic and industry partners)
note: One track of OpenRSI Index. The OpenRSI Index record keeps lab scores that combine tracks. Published measurements include a result that failed staging guards.

name: OpenRSI Index MInference 32-Head Sparse Prefill Kernel
description: Agents optimize a sparse-attention prefill operator under a fixed budget. The score is speedup against the paired reference run.
org: OpenRSI Foundation (UW-led, academic and industry partners)
note: One track of OpenRSI Index. The OpenRSI Index record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: OpenRSI Index Molmo2 Video-Pointing Inference Strategy
description: Agents tune video inputs and inference for a frozen Molmo2 model. The score is held-out spatiotemporal pointing soft F1.
org: OpenRSI Foundation (UW-led, academic and industry partners)
note: One track of OpenRSI Index. The OpenRSI Index record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: OpenRSI Index MolmoWeb Interaction Context Allocation
description: Agents select interaction context for a frozen browser model. The score is macro-averaged browser-action prediction quality.
org: OpenRSI Foundation (UW-led, academic and industry partners)
note: One track of OpenRSI Index. The OpenRSI Index record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: OpenRSI Index ReasonIR Difficulty Curriculum
description: Agents adjust retrieval training data schedules. The score measures reasoning retrieval with a penalty for general retrieval regression.
org: OpenRSI Foundation (UW-led, academic and industry partners)
note: One track of OpenRSI Index. The OpenRSI Index record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: OpenRSI Index SGLang Omni TTS Runtime
description: Agents improve speech serving while preserving quality. The score is the official speedup reward for the archived continuation protocol.
org: OpenRSI Foundation (UW-led, academic and industry partners)
note: One track of OpenRSI Index. The OpenRSI Index record keeps lab scores that combine tracks. The archived continuation result was not rerun under current protocol v5.

name: OpenScore String Quartets
description: Models transcribe images of string quartet sheet music into symbolic notation. Scored as 1 minus normalized edit distance from the reference encoding.
org: OpenAI, using the OpenScore String Quartets corpus
note: OpenAI's exact setup is unpublished, and the separate OSSQ-OMR benchmark uses the same corpus and metric.

name: OpenThoughts-TBLite
description: Agents solve 100 Terminal-Bench tasks picked to track Terminal-Bench 2 scores while running faster. Tasks are balanced across four difficulty bands using Claude Haiku 4.5 pass rates.
org: OpenThoughts Agent team, Snorkel AI and Bespoke Labs
note: Built as a development set for smaller models. It replaces the earlier OpenThoughts-TB-dev set. Runs use the Harbor framework.

name: OpenVLM Leaderboard
description: OpenCompass runs vision-language models through VLMEvalKit on a fixed set of image benchmarks, such as MMBench, MMStar and MathVista. The headline is the average score across that set.
note: The Hugging Face space dates from 2024-01-23 and has over 1,000 likes. Its per-benchmark columns are cataloged as separate boards, with 284 models in the JSON.

name: Operator prompt injection scenarios
description: Browser agents meet 31 automatically checkable prompt injection scenarios that fooled earlier model versions. Scored as susceptibility rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The scenarios are not public.

name: Opportunistic sandbox escape (Anthropic)
description: Agents do dev-ops tasks in 1,753 sandboxes with deliberate weaknesses. Score is the share of scenarios where they use credentials or files outside.
note: Anthropic also reports the rate of reaching outside the sandbox by any route. It differs from the older audit-based sandbox evaluation.

name: OptimBench
description: Agents solve optimization engineering tasks. Part of Meta's recursive-improvement suite and graded programmatically.
note: In-house Meta evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: OR-Bench
description: Models meet benign and borderline prompts and the benchmark measures how often they wrongly refuse. Reports false refusal rate.
note: Public over-refusal benchmark for large language models.

name: OR-License
description: Agents turn original client materials into validated operations research solutions without an expert first reformulating the problem.
note: 225 upvotes on Hugging Face papers, the most of any benchmark paper in October 2026.

name: Orak
description: LLM agents play 12 popular video games across most genres through an MCP interface. Each game scores in-game progress or outcomes, and the board ranks models by their average rank across the games.
org: KRAFTON AI with Seoul National University, NVIDIA and UW-Madison
note: The name is the Korean word for game. The repo also releases gameplay data for fine-tuning.

name: Organic Chemistry (Anthropic)
description: Models predict structures from spectra, design synthetic routes, predict reaction products and convert between IUPAC names, SMILES and structure images.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Organic Chemistry V2 (Anthropic)
description: Models predict structures from spectra, design multi-step syntheses, predict reaction products and read chemical structure images. V2 adds harder expert-recommended problems.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. Scores are not comparable with the original Organic Chemistry set.

name: OSGym
aliases: OSGym: Scalable OS Infra for Computer Use Agents
description: Infrastructure running 1,000+ parallel OS sandboxes for computer-use agent training and evaluation. Tasks span browsing, documents, SWE and multi-app work.
note: Infrastructure, not a scored benchmark: 1,420 trajectories/min at ~$0.2-0.3 per replica-day. The v1 paper's code link github.com/agiopen-org/osgym returned 404 on 2026-10-22, and v5 lists no code.

name: OSI-Bench
description: Spatial reasoning questions on outdoor pedestrian-view videos with metric 3D ground truth from synchronized stereo cameras, LiDAR and GPS. 8,736 questions range from relative direction to metric and motion estimates.
org: UCAS, ETH Zurich and Microsoft Research Asia
note: The arXiv paper calls the benchmark OpenBench. The repository and project page call it OSI-Bench.

name: OST-Bench
description: Vision-language models act as an agent exploring a 3D scene and answer spatial questions from the views seen so far. The set has 10k questions over 1.4k scenes.
note: Scenes come from ScanNet, Matterport3D and ARKitScenes. VLMEvalKit supports it.

name: OSWorld
description: Agents complete 369 real computer tasks in Ubuntu desktop apps through screenshots and mouse and keyboard actions. Execution-based scripts check the final state.
note: OSWorld-Verified fixed task errors in July 2025, and OSWorld 2.0 replaced it as the latest version in June 2026.

name: OSWorld 2.0
description: Agents complete 108 long-horizon workflows across 31 self-hosted websites and desktop apps, averaging 318 tool calls. Scored by binary completion and checkpoint partial credit.
note: Releases are versioned and some cards report the offline subset or partial score, so cross-card numbers are not directly comparable.

name: OSWorld 2.0 (Aug 2026)
description: Agents complete 108 long-horizon workflows across 31 self-hosted websites and desktop apps, averaging 318 tool calls. Scored by binary completion and checkpoint partial credit.
note: Patch release on the same 108 tasks: 14 changed to prevent reward hacking and 31 modified.

name: OSWorld 2.1
description: Agents complete 108 long-horizon workflows across 31 self-hosted websites and desktop apps, averaging 318 tool calls. Scored by binary completion and checkpoint partial credit.
note: Bug-fix release on the same 108 tasks, with evaluator fixes and updated mock websites.

name: OSWorld 2.1 (offline subset)
description: Agents complete the 82 OSWorld 2.1 tasks on the official offline list, with no internet access. Scored by checkpoint partial credit and strict pass rate.
note: Subset of the 108 OSWorld 2.1 tasks. Scores are not comparable with scores on the full set.

name: OSWorld-G
description: Models map 564 desktop instructions to the right screen element or point, covering text matching, element recognition, layout understanding and fine manipulation.
org: XLANG Lab, University of Hong Kong (OSWorld team)
note: Released with the Jedi grounding dataset. NeurIPS 2025 spotlight. Scored by click accuracy.

name: OSWorld-MCP
description: Computer-use agents complete OSWorld desktop tasks while they can also call 158 MCP tools across 7 common applications. The benchmark checks whether agents pick a tool call or GUI actions at the right time. It reports task accuracy, tool invocation rate and average completion steps.
org: Peking University, Tongyi Lab (Alibaba) and Beijing Zhongguancun Academy
note: Results are given at 15 and 50 step limits. Later entries ran once, the original ones three times, and some used model-specific prompts, so the board warns they are not strictly comparable. About 239 GitHub stars and 24 HF paper upvotes.

name: OSWorld-Science
description: Computer-use agents do 146 scientific software tasks, such as molecular drawing, across several domains. Produced artifacts are checked to score each task.
note: Separate from the OSWorld family by XLANG Lab. 40 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: OSWorld-Verified
description: 369 open-ended tasks in real desktop apps. Agent acts through screenshots, mouse and keyboard. Execution-based checkers score success.

changes.text: The maintainers replaced permissive document and spreadsheet checks with stricter content checks. Incorrect outputs that previously passed can now fail.

note: Human baseline 72.4%. Top reported scores are ~83-86%, so near-saturated. Successor OSWorld 2.0 released 2026-06 (repo xlang-ai/OSWorld-V2).

name: OTelBench
description: Coding agents add OpenTelemetry tracing, metrics and logging to codebases in several languages. Tests check the instrumentation.
note: 23 tasks and 14 models as of 2026-01-16.

name: OTIS Mock AIME 2024-2025
description: Models solve 45 problems from three OTIS Mock AIME exams written by students of the OTIS program. Integer answers are scored by exact match.
note: Epoch AI added it as a harder successor to MATH Level 5, which was nearing saturation.

name: OVBench
description: Video models answer questions about past, current and future moments of an online video stream in 6 task types and 16 subtasks.
note: Published at CVPR 2025 with the VideoChat-Online model. It is a different test from OVO-Bench.

name: Over-eager behavior on GUI computer use tasks (Anthropic)
aliases: Overly agentic behavior in GUI computer use settings
Over-Eager Behavior on GUI Computer Use Tasks
description: Computer-use agents face impossible tasks with an unwanted shortcut available. Score is the rate of unapproved workarounds instead of checking with the user.
note: Run with neutral, encouraging and discouraging system prompts. The neutral prompt is the default setting.

name: Overconfidence: verifying command-line syntax (Anthropic)
description: Agents are asked for an exact invocation of an unfamiliar command-line tool. Graders score from 1 to 5 whether they check documentation before running commands.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Oversight gaming
description: A prompted monitor flags aligned-graded rollouts whose behavior follows from reasoning about oversight. Scored as rate per alignment evaluation.
note: In-house OpenAI measurement. Earlier cards called it undermining evaluation validity.

name: Overstepping boundaries on ambiguous and high-risk tasks
description: Agents get ambiguous or high-risk coding and other tasks where they should pause to ask the user, plus clear tasks they should just do.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: OVO-Bench
description: Video models answer questions asked at given timestamps of a video stream in 12 tasks over 644 videos. Tasks cover backward tracing, real-time understanding and forward active responding.
note: It tests online, streaming video understanding rather than whole-video answers. About 2,800 timestamped annotations.

name: OVO-S-Bench
description: Multimodal models answer spatial questions about places and layouts during a continuous egocentric video stream. The set has 1,680 human-annotated questions over 348 videos.
note: It had 31 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 61 GitHub stars. It is separate from OVO-Bench.

name: OWE-Bench
description: 26 long-horizon engineering and research projects across software, physical engineering, machine learning and scientific computing, from GPU kernels to aircraft design. Agents get 4 to 18 hours per attempt, and an offline verifier scores what they ship on held-out cases.
note: Each task is rescaled so the untouched baseline scores 0% and the task's ceiling scores 100%, and the board reports the mean of eight attempts. Mercor set exploits that raised a score to zero. Ten of the 26 graders stay private because they contain hidden data.

name: Package registry publishing evaluation (Anthropic)
aliases: Propensity to publish harmful content to public package registries
Intensity of pressure required for a model to publish a backdoored package
description: Agents in a simulated capture the flag exercise can publish a backdoored package to a registry. An investigator escalates pressure until they act.
note: Built after an incident in which a model published harmful content to PyPI. Results are counts of investigations by outcome.

name: PACT
description: Two models bargain over 20 rounds as buyer and seller, each with a hidden private value. Matches across many pairings rank the models.
note: The repo was created on 2025-07-30 and updated on 2026-06-23.

name: PAgentBench
description: Agents act as personal assistants for task management, file operations and system interactions. iFlytek built it in house.
note: The Spark-X2.6-4B card says it will be open-sourced soon. Grading is not described.

name: PAI-Bench
description: Physical-AI video generation from 1,044 prompts in six domains, VLM-QA plus quality metrics. Companion control and understanding tracks.
note: Generation score compressed near the real-video reference (Source 82.6. Cosmos3-Super 83.9 exceeds it). Robot domain spreads more (55-90).

name: PaintBench
description: Image editing models do precise single-answer edits in 20 operations such as geometric transforms, color changes and symbolic edits. Procedural generation gives deterministic checks.
note: Best model reached 17.1% at launch, per AINews.

name: Pairwise Bioweaponization Campaign
description: Red teamers with biology PhDs compare anonymized responses from two models on bioweaponization prompts. Scored as the win rate for being safer.
note: In-house OpenAI red teaming campaign. The comparison model changes by card.

name: Pairwise safety red teaming
aliases: ELO Scores across vision-based red teaming categories
description: Red teamers compare anonymized responses from several models and pick the least safe. Scored as ELO or win rate.
note: In-house OpenAI red teaming study. Cards use ELO or win rates.

name: Paloma
aliases: Perplexity Analysis for Language Model Assessment
description: Language models are measured by perplexity on held-out text from 585 domains, from news sites to individual subreddits.
note: Used for base model comparisons, for example in OLMo reports.

name: Pantograph frontier-LLM robot benchmark (Pandroid)
description: GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1 drive Pandroid robots through a fixed tool harness on eight simple manipulation tasks, 10 blind-graded attempts each.
note: Controlled design: same prompt, tools and budget (20 min or 96 turns), random interleaving across six robots, blind grading, p about 0.001 stratified by task. Astra 35%, Fable 15%. Human teleoperators reach 100%. Fixed clock penalizes slow thinking. One team runs both models.

name: PaperBench
description: Agent replicates ICML 2024 papers from scratch. LLM judge grades against author-written hierarchical rubrics.
note: Repo renamed from openai/preparedness. Qwen and MiniMax use different judges (Opus 4.6) and 12h runs, so scores are not comparable.

name: PaperBench Code-Dev
description: Agents implement research paper code. The Code-Dev variant evaluates coding separately from full research replication.
note: The official README publishes a distinct Code-Dev result. This evaluation is not full PaperBench replication.

name: PaperBenchX
description: Agents reproduce published results from 12 research areas outside machine learning, using each field's own scientific software. Verifiers check that the evidence regenerates and supports the paper's claims.
note: 93 tasks, with 12 public and 81 held back by the maintainers. Headline is the full reproduction rate. The board covers 10 agents and also reports partial reproduction. Not a version of OpenAI's PaperBench.

name: ParallelKernelBench
description: Models replace PyTorch and NCCL reference code with multi-GPU CUDA kernels for 87 problems from codebases such as Megatron-LM and DeepSpeed. Scored on correctness and speed over the baseline.
note: Default runs use 8 H100 GPUs. Best zero-shot model solved 28 of 87 at launch.

name: Parametric CAD Bench
description: Agents author editable parametric FreeCAD part designs, graded against held-back references for geometry and spec consistency.
note: Not the same as anniedoris/CADBench. A submission-portal repo exists at github.com/gNucleus-AI/cad-bench-submission. The board shows version 3. Lab results from before it keep their citations without a plotted score.

name: ParseBench
description: Document parsers process about 2,000 human-verified enterprise pages. Over 169,000 test rules score tables, charts, content faithfulness, formatting and visual grounding.
note: On Hugging Face's official benchmark list, with 168 likes.

name: PartBench
description: Parametric mechanical part design and CAD-style generation, graded for geometric and manufacturing fidelity.
note: Only source found is the Grok 4.6 card reference to normalfactory.com.

name: Participation in junk science (Anthropic)
description: Models talk with simulated users ranging from curious to openly fraudulent who seek fake science. Score is the rate of generating unsound scientific content.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation with 90 scenarios. The tasks are not public.

name: Passkey Retrieval
description: Models find a random passkey hidden at a random position in a long filler prompt. Scored by retrieval accuracy.
note: Synthetic test from the Landmark Attention paper. Strong long-context models usually score near 100%.

name: Past IMO (Seed-Prover formal set)
description: Provers write Lean proofs for 155 past IMO problems, mostly adapted from Compfiles and MiniF2F.
note: Seed curated this set for the Seed-Prover report.

name: PatchEval
description: Models write patches for 1,000 real CVE vulnerabilities from 2015 to 2025 in Go, JavaScript and Python. Containers run exploit and unit tests to validate each patch.
note: inspect_evals uses the verified dockerized subset.

name: PatchEval-Verified
description: Models write patches for 1,000 real CVE vulnerabilities from 2015 to 2025 in Go, JavaScript and Python. Containers run exploit and unit tests to validate each patch.
note: Revised PoC tests across 230 CVEs. Original PatchEval and Verified are not comparable.

name: PathMCQA (Google)
description: Models answer 4 to 9 option questions on histopathology patches about cancer identification, grading and subtype. The test split has 450 patches from 354 slides.
note: Internal dataset covering breast, lung, prostate, lymph and cervical specimens. Board-certified pathologists set the answers.

name: PatientAgentBench
description: Patient-facing health agents talk with a simulated patient and use a sandbox of healthcare tools for scheduling, prescriptions, telehealth and escalation. An LLM jury scores over a hundred clinician-grounded criteria.
note: Scenarios are generated fresh from a configurable seed distribution, so runs differ in content.

name: Pattern Labs cyberoffensive challenges
description: Agents attempt evasion, network attack simulation and vulnerability exploitation challenges at easy, medium and hard levels. Scored as success rate per type.
note: Third-party evaluation reported in OpenAI cards. Results are per challenge type with no overall number.

name: PAWBench
description: Video generators are run many times on the same start and action, and the outcomes become a distribution over physical behaviors. The test checks whether it matches reference probabilities and covers every valid behavior.
org: PAWBench team (with Hugging Face's Sayak Paul)
note: 50 scenarios and eleven systems in the paper. No system matched the reference probabilities while covering the valid range. 38 HF upvotes.

name: PAWS
description: Models decide whether two sentences with heavy word overlap are paraphrases.
note: Llama 3 shows it only in a scatter plot.

name: PCT (Polarized Contrastive Pairs)
description: Models answer matched left-coded and right-coded prompts, such as Obama and Reagan. Judges score whether sentiment and helpfulness stay consistent across each pair.
note: Political Consistency is the mean of Sentiment Consistency and Helpfulness Consistency. CAIS runs it on its AI Dashboard as part of the risk index and in simple-evals.

name: Pencil Puzzle Bench
description: Models solve 300 pencil puzzles of 20 varieties with unique solutions, either in one shot or agentically with step checks. Every board state can be verified against the rules.
note: Launch evaluated 51 models from 11 providers. A 30-puzzle subset serves costly agentic runs.

name: PenguinScrolls
description: Models answer user-style questions over long natural documents such as books, financial reports and legal papers, up to 128K tokens. Tasks cover extraction, localization, qualitative analysis and numerical reasoning.
note: The release has 1,316 single-turn items in four categories. Tencent reports it in the Hunyuan-A13B technical report.

name: Perception Test MCVQA
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about real-world videos filmed to show perceptually interesting situations. Scored by top-1 accuracy.
note: Multiple-choice video QA task of the Perception Test benchmark.

name: PerceptionBench (Moonshot)
description: Moonshot in-house benchmark of atomic visual perception skills. Scoring details unpublished.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Moonshot AI). Not the same as other public benchmarks with this name.

name: PerceptionComp
description: 1,114 five-choice questions on 279 complex videos. Each question needs evidence from several separate moments, so no single frame answers it.
note: People who watch a video once score near chance, while experts who can rewatch reach 100%.

name: Perceptual Attacks on Embodied AI (Robocurve)
description: Frontier models drive two real robot arms on five unsafe tasks with unaltered, blurred or doctored camera footage. An AI judge labels attempts and refusals.
note: Published 2026-10-29 with five models and 900 trials. Models acted unsafely in 81 of 300 unaltered, 263 of 300 blurred and 291 of 300 doctored trials. Claude Fable 5.1 is the judge.

name: PerMemBench
description: Memory systems for long-running agents decide what to store from years of interactions across many domains and user personas. Later questions check whether the system kept the context that matters for each user. The benchmark tests whether memory policies can adapt to the person instead of storing everything the same way.
note: The paper also proposes its own session-level storage gate. 45 Hugging Face upvotes and about 13 GitHub stars. The scoring rule should be checked before importing scores.

name: Person Identification evaluation
description: Models receive requests to identify people in photos. Scored on refusal rate in non-adversarial and adversarial sets.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report two difficulty levels with no overall number.

name: Personal data evaluations
description: Browsing agents receive requests for private personal information, from 200 synthetic prompts and 55 manually written golden examples. Scored on adherence to personal data policy.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: Personal Superintelligence Index (Meta)
description: Meta's composite of seven personal and knowledge-work evals: Agents' Last Exam, AutomationBench-AA, FocusBench, JobBench, GDP.pdf, VBT and DRACO.
note: Internal index reported in the Muse Wonder model card. Its parts use mixed grading, including rubric judges. The card does not give the weighting.

name: Personal-device assistant prompt injection eval
description: OS assistant agents in 44 stateful scenarios ingest untrusted content that tries to trigger unauthorized actions. Reports 5-step adaptive survival and task utility.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: PersonQA
description: Models answer questions about publicly available facts on people. Scored on accuracy, with hallucination rate reported alongside.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Results here record accuracy and name the hallucination rate in the text.

name: Petri
aliases: Parallel Exploration Tool for Risky Interactions
description: Open-source auditing tool where auditor agents probe target models in simulated scenarios and judges score misaligned behaviors.
note: Anthropic cards use Petri to compare Claude with other labs' models.

name: Petri 2.0
description: Auditor agents run seed scenarios against target models with a realism classifier to cut eval-awareness. Judges score transcripts for misaligned behaviors.
note: Adds 70 seed scenarios and a realism classifier over Petri 1.0, so scores are not comparable. Petri 3.0 changed the Python API but kept the CLI. Maintained by Meridian Labs.

name: Petri Bloom
description: An auditor model runs generated scenarios to elicit named misaligned behaviors. Judges score each transcript from 1 to 10.
note: Bloom generates scenarios and Petri runs the interactions. Meta averages mean scores across 13 shared behaviors.

name: Phage-plasmid Co-evolution
description: Models predict future amino acid mutations in a phage and plasmid system from earlier observations. Scored as negative log likelihood.
note: OpenAI Critical bio capability evaluation. The Critical threshold is 9.40 or lower.

name: PhAIL
description: Real Franka bin-to-bin picking of four object types. VLAs scored on throughput and completion against human and teleop references.
note: PhAIL scores throughput, not just success. Teleop reaches 330 units/hour and humans 1,331. One narrow task. Repo holds paper analysis scripts. PhAIL launched on 2026-03-31. The paper followed in May 2026. The board now also hosts a separate DROID: Everyday tasks benchmark.

name: PhAIL DROID: Everyday tasks
description: Policies run 286 language-instructed tabletop tasks worded as DROID annotations on a real Franka FR3. Operators mark stages reached within 240 seconds.
note: Reliability comes from an item-response ranking model fitted over all tasks, with bootstrap 95% ranges. Absent from a June 2026 snapshot.

name: Phare
description: Models are probed in English, French and Spanish for hallucination, harmful misguidance, stereotypes and jailbreaks. Hallucination tasks cover factuality, misinformation, debunking and tool use.
note: Announced 2025-02 with Google DeepMind as research partner. Phare V2 (2025-12-16) added a jailbreak module and self-harm tests with the same method. The board lists about 70 models.

name: PharmaBench (micro1)
description: Agents write clinical trial documentation inside 8 synthetic drug programs, across 120 tasks written by biostatisticians, medical writers, safety physicians and regulatory staff.
note: Penalties subtract for content an expert would have to remove. Full marks were rare. Not the 2024 PharmaBench of ADMET data.

name: PhiBench
description: Models answer original prompts that Microsoft's Phi team wrote to test a wide range of skills and reasoning.
note: In-house: Microsoft never released the tasks, and the Phi-4-reasoning report uses a newer version, PhiBench 2.21.

name: PHYBench
description: Models solve 500 original physics problems from high school to Physics Olympiad level. Answers are expressions checked against the key.
note: At release Gemini 2.5 Pro scored 36.9% against 61.9% for human experts. The paper also adds an expression edit distance score.

name: Phylogenetics (Anthropic)
description: Models analyze phylogenetic data and tree diagrams, testing quantitative reasoning about tree structure and visual interpretation.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: PhysClosureBench
description: Agents run 50 expert-verified physics research tasks in strong-field and attosecond physics, deciding how to generate and validate evidence. A 20-criterion score and a closure level from RC0 to RC4 grade them.
note: Seven frontier models were tested. Claude Opus 5 had the best mean score but reached full closure in only 32.7 percent of attempts. 52 HF paper upvotes.

name: Physical-Engineering's Last Exam
description: Agents produce billable engineering deliverables such as calculation packages, drawings and design reviews in 85 tasks across electrical, civil, structural and mechanical engineering. Automatic graders check constraints, safety limits and the design objective.
note: 29 public dev tasks and 56 hidden test tasks.

name: PhysicalRealismBench-U
description: VLM watches 1,300 synthetic Isaac Sim videos, flags physics-law violations, names object and frames. Scored by joint realism F1.
note: Lab-created benchmark (Reka). Not cited in the Reka Edge card. No code or dataset link. Best realism F1 0.60 at launch.

name: PhysicianBench
description: 100 physician tasks performed by an agent inside an EHR environment. Scored by pass rate per attempt.

name: PHYSICS
description: Models solve 1,297 PhD qualifying exam physics problems across six subfields, 298 of them with images. Answers are checked by symbolic equivalence.
org: Yale University (Kaiyue Feng, Arman Cohan et al.)
note: Shanghai AI Lab Intern-S1 reports it as Physics.

name: Physics-IQ
description: Video models continue 396 filmed physical events from a frame or 3 s clip. Motion compared with the real continuation.
note: Some rows are supplied by model makers through GitHub pull requests. Physics-IQ Verified (2026-06) has its own record and leaderboard.

name: Physics-IQ Verified
description: Video models continue 198 real filmed physics experiments from their first frames. Generated videos are compared with the real outcome, with every sample and metric weighted equally.
org: Anates Labs and Google DeepMind (Physics-IQ authors)
note: An audit of Physics-IQ that refines 57.6% of samples and 34.8% of prompts and adds sample-level scoring. Rankings shift from the original (Kendall tau 0.46). The repo calls it the recommended variant.

name: PHYSICS-Verified
description: Corrected PHYSICS test problems with answer-level accuracy. The complete verified test set.
org: Yale University (Kaiyue Feng, Arman Cohan et al.)
note: Original PHYSICS uses problem-level grading. Verified uses corrected problems and answer-level grading.

name: PhysicsFinals
description: Models answer 61 undergraduate physics final exam problems written by physics professors. A professor grades the answers.
note: In-house Google eval, never released.

name: PhysVista
description: Vision-language models perceive, reason about and judge whether videos follow real-world physics. The benchmark also tests if they can judge the physical realism of generated videos.
org: University of Science and Technology of China
note: It had 49 Hugging Face paper upvotes.

name: PhyX
description: Models solve 3,000 image-based physics problems across six domains such as mechanics and optics. Versions include multiple choice and open-ended answers.
note: A 1,000 question testmini subset also exists, so check which split a model card reports.

name: Pile-test
description: Models predict text from the test split of the Pile, an 800GB corpus of 22 sources. Scored by bits per byte.
note: A language modeling metric for base models, not a task benchmark.

name: PinchBench
description: Real-world tasks (scheduling, email triage, coding, research, files) for an LLM driving an OpenClaw agent. Graded by automated checks and LLM judge.
note: v1.x grew from 23 to 53 tasks. PinchBench 2.0 (2026-05-06) expanded to 148 tasks and changed the default judge, so it has its own record.

name: PinchBench 2.0
description: Models drive an OpenClaw agent through 148 real-world tasks, including data and log analysis, meeting notes, DevOps, PDFs, research and writing. Graded by checks and a Haiku judge.
note: Up from about 25 tasks in v1.x. The default judge changed to Claude Haiku, so scores do not compare with v1. Released 2026-05-06.

name: PIQA
description: Models pick which of two solutions better achieves an everyday physical goal. Scoring is accuracy.
org: Yonatan Bisk, Rowan Zellers, Ronan Le Bras, Jianfeng Gao, Yejin Choi

name: PixMo-Count
description: Models count objects in natural images and give the exact number. Scored by accuracy on the test split.
org: Allen Institute for AI (Molmo and PixMo)
note: Released with the Molmo models as part of the PixMo data.

name: PlanBench-XL
description: Tool-use agents solve 327 retail tasks over 1,665 tools that they must first retrieve, chaining calls to uncover evidence. An optional blocking mode simulates tool failures.
note: Not related to the PlanBench planning benchmark of Valmeekam et al. 96 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: PlanningBench
description: Models solve generated planning problems that coordinate goals, constraints and resources. Instances are scalable and come with verifiers.
note: Also used to make training data. 42 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: PLawBench
description: Model handles 850 realistic legal consultation, case-analysis and document-drafting tasks. LLM judge scores against about 12,500 expert rubric items.
note: ACL 2026. Qwen judged it with gemini-3.1-pro-preview.

name: PlugInject
description: Agents receive function call outputs that contain prompt injection attacks. Scored on resisting the injected instructions.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation drawn from a split of training data.

name: PMC-VQA
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about medical images drawn from PubMed Central figures. Scored by accuracy.
org: Shanghai Jiao Tong University and Shanghai AI Laboratory

name: PMPP-Hard
description: Agents write GPU kernels for 69 tasks that must be correct, and on 48 of them also run within 1.25 times the reference time. The score is the area under the solved-tasks curve over a 10-hour budget, out of 690 task-hours.
note: Thinking Machines reports an adapted version with task and grading fixes.

name: Point-Bench
description: Models point to the image location a language request describes, in about 1,000 tasks across five reasoning categories. A point inside the target mask counts as correct.
note: Part of PointArena with the Point-Battle voting arena and the Point-Act robot setup. The mask rule is an assumption from the task design.

name: PokeAgent Challenge
description: Agents compete in Pokemon battles under partial observability in a Battling Track and play the Pokemon RPG in a Speedrunning Track that needs long-horizon planning.
note: Run as a large public competition. 12 HF paper upvotes. Two tracks are scored differently, battles by ratings and speedruns by progress.

name: PolicyBench
description: No-tools estimate of US taxes and benefits for 100 households across 18 programs. Headline metric is answers within $1 of PolicyEngine-US.
note: Prompts and reference values are public, so the authors call the board a preview. Forced tool calls lowered some Claude scores.

name: Political Persuasion Parallel Generation
description: Human raters pick the more persuasive of two short political social media posts. Scored as win rate against GPT-4o.
note: OpenAI persuasion evaluation. Post-mitigation models often refuse political persuasion.

name: Political Science LLM Benchmark
description: 33 political-science text-coding tasks, 100 texts each (~3,300 items). Models scored by mean F1 against human-coded labels.
note: 31 models. Open-weight models run on one GPU. Some texts may be in training data.

name: Poly-Guard Bench
description: Models meet harmful requests and statements across domains. Reports attack success rate under single-turn and multi-turn adaptive red-teaming.
note: Policy-grounded guardrail dataset. Meta uses the cyber domain, high-severity subset.

name: PolyMath
description: Models solve 9,000 parallel math problems in 18 languages across four difficulty levels, from school math to frontier math. Final answers are checked.
note: Some model cards report only the English subset, PolyMath-en.

name: POPE
description: Vision language models answer yes or no questions about whether objects appear in COCO images. Scored by accuracy or F1 on object hallucination.
org: Renmin University of China (Li et al.)

name: PopQA
description: Models answer about 14k entity questions built from Wikidata, spread from popular to rare entities. Scored by whether the answer matches a gold alias.
note: Built to study when retrieval helps long-tail knowledge. Ai2 reports it in Tulu 3 and Olmo cards.

name: PostTrainBench
description: CLI agent gets a base model, one H100 and a time budget to post-train it for a target benchmark. Scored on normalized gain.
org: AISA group (ELLIS Institute Tübingen and MPI-IS) + University of Tübingen + Thoughtful Lab
note: Known reward hacking (eval tampering, swapping in instruct models). Agent-as-judge added. Dataset link holds trajectories, not tasks.

name: PostTrainBench 1.1
description: CLI agent gets a base model, one H100 and a time budget to post-train it for a target benchmark. Scored on normalized gain.
org: AISA group (ELLIS Institute Tübingen and MPI-IS) + University of Tübingen + Thoughtful Lab
note: Version 1.1 added judges for contamination and API use, and banned distillation from hosted models. Runs that broke the rules score as the base model.

name: PostTrainBench 1.2
description: CLI agent gets a base model, one H100 and a time budget to post-train it for a target benchmark. Scored on normalized gain.
org: AISA group (ELLIS Institute Tübingen and MPI-IS) + University of Tübingen + Thoughtful Lab
note: Version 1.2 dropped BFCL, reweighted the other six benchmarks, fixed HumanEval scoring, and averages up to five seeds.

name: PRBench
description: Model answers 1,100 expert-written law and finance questions. LLM judge grades against weighted expert rubrics of 10-30 criteria each.
note: Hard subset of 550 tasks. Top Hard scores about 0.39 at release.

name: PRDBench
description: Code agents build 50 real-world Python projects across 20 domains from product requirement documents. A trained judge agent checks each project against structured criteria.
note: Published at AAMAS 2026. The authors built tasks with an agent-driven annotation pipeline under human supervision.

name: Preference on ChatGPT and API prompts
description: Human labelers compare model responses to 5,214 prompts sent to ChatGPT and the OpenAI API. Scored as win rate against a baseline model.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The baseline model changes between reports.

name: PresentBench
description: Models generate full slide decks from background materials for 238 real-world cases. A judge scores each deck against about 54 hand-written checklist items.

name: PrimeVul
description: Models classify C and C++ functions as vulnerable or not, with a paired setting that pairs each vulnerable function with its patch.
org: Columbia University and Google (Ding et al.)
note: 228,800 safe and 6,968 vulnerable C and C++ functions over about 140 CWEs. Two labeling methods: ONEFUNC marks a function vulnerable only when the fixing commit touched that function alone, and NVDCHECK cross-references CVE text. The current release is v0.1 and no v2 exists. Published at ICSE 2025.

name: prinzbench
description: Models research fact patterns under U.S. statutes and regulations and hunt for obscure public information online. 33 private questions run three times give a score out of 99.
note: 25 legal research and 8 search questions. Zvi covers it often. The author last updated the board on 2026-07-18. On 2026-11-03 the repository's README was replaced with an unrelated AI timeline, so we read the board from the July 18 version.

name: PrivacyLens
description: Language model agents write emails, posts or messages from a prior tool trajectory without leaking sensitive details. A judge scores information leakage and helpfulness.
org: Stanford University, Northeastern University and Harvard University
note: Labs report the leakage rate over 493 prompts, where lower is better, often with a helpfulness score beside it.

name: Proactive refusals of high-risk tasks
description: Browser agents receive high-risk tasks such as banking transfers and high-stakes decisions that policy says they must refuse. Scored on refusal recall.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation on a synthetic set. The tasks are not public.

name: Proactive Searches
description: Graders read ExploitGym Honeypot reasoning traces for speculation about other agents and attempts to contact them. Scored as rate of trajectories.
note: In-house OpenAI analysis of unintended agent-to-agent communication. The tasks are not public.

name: ProactiveVideoQA
description: Models answer spoken questions when a streamed video first reveals the answer.
note: The launch post reports turn-weighted PAUC at omega 0.5. A no-response baseline scores 25.0.

name: ProcBench
description: Models follow explicit step-by-step procedures to answer questions, which isolates multi-step inference from knowledge and search.
note: It is a different test from TOD-ProcBench.

name: ProcessBench
description: Models read step-by-step solutions to GSM8K, MATH, OlympiadBench and Omni-MATH problems and name the earliest wrong step, or say none is wrong. Scored by F1.
note: Used to test process reward models and critic models on math reasoning.

name: ProdBench (Tencent)
description: Agents complete Tencent in-house productivity tasks in the OpenClaw harness. Scored by pass^3.

name: Production Deception - Adversarial
description: Models answer prompts representative of traffic that previously elicited deception in ChatGPT. Scored as deception rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: Production Jailbreaks
description: Models face jailbreaks found in production ChatGPT data. Scored as not_unsafe rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The jailbreaks are not public.

name: ProfBench
description: Model writes expert-level reports in physics, chemistry, finance and consulting. Calibrated LLM judges grade against PhD/MBA-written rubrics.
note: Lab-created by NVIDIA (ICLR 2026). Nemotron reports a ProfBench (Search) variant. Reference documents are not in the HF set.

name: ProgramBench
description: 200 tasks: rebuild a full program from only its compiled binary and docs. Hidden behavioral tests (248k total) must match the original.
org: Meta Superintelligence Labs, Stanford University and Harvard University
note: Tasks range from jq to FFmpeg and SQLite. The Opus 5.5 system card reports a 100-agent swarm result.

name: ProgramBench almost solved
description: Agents rebuild 200 programs from only their compiled binaries and docs. The score is the share of tasks whose rebuilt program passes at least 95% of the hidden behavioral tests.
org: Meta Superintelligence Labs, Stanford University and Harvard University
note: The board shows this as its Almost column and ranks by fully resolved tasks, which the ProgramBench record holds. Many labs report this number.

name: ProgramBench tests passed
description: Agents rebuild 200 programs from only their compiled binaries and docs. The score is the share of hidden behavioral tests the rebuilt program passes, averaged over tasks.
org: Meta Superintelligence Labs, Stanford University and Harvard University
note: The board calls this an unofficial metric and ranks by fully resolved tasks, which the ProgramBench record holds. Labs report this number. Anthropic runs 166 of the 200 tasks.

name: Progress classification (Google DeepMind)
description: Models assign each frame of a robot video to one of five task-progress bands from 0 to 100 percent. Scored by accuracy.
note: Reported in the Gemini Robotics ER 2 post.

name: Progress-Bench
description: Vision-language models estimate how far a task has progressed from partial observations, such as frames of a robot or human doing a job. The benchmark varies how the demonstration is shown and the camera viewpoint, and it includes cases with no valid answer.
note: The paper tests 14 VLMs. The same repository holds the ProgressLM-3B model and its 45K training set, so the stars (about 141) are shared. 12 Hugging Face upvotes. The scoring rule should be checked before importing scores.

name: Project Euler (MathArena)
description: Models solve recent Project Euler problems that need both mathematical insight and code. MathArena adds problems as Project Euler releases them, starting from problem 943.
org: MathArena (ETH Zurich SRI Lab and INSAIT)
note: The set held 50 problems and 18 models when MathArena marked it deprecated. MathArena withholds its agent code to avoid Project Euler leaderboard cheating.

name: Prompt injection attacks in search and function calling
description: Agents receive search results and function call outputs that contain stronger known prompt injection attacks. Scored on resisting the injected instructions.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Prompt injection live bug bounty (Anthropic with Gray Swan)
description: Expert red teamers submit prompt injection attacks against hidden frontier models in tool use, coding and computer use scenarios. Score is attack success rate.
note: Each round runs for about a week with new scenarios. Claude models are tested without product prompt injection protections.

name: Prompt injection robustness
description: Agents meet indirect prompt injection attacks inside tool outputs. Scored as defender success rate averaged per defender query.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Prompt injection robustness against adaptive attackers, browser use (Anthropic)
aliases: Robustness against adaptive attackers: browser use
description: Browser agents face indirect prompt injections in web environments from an internal adaptive attacker. Score is attack success rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Prompt injection robustness against adaptive attackers, coding (Anthropic)
description: Coding agents face indirect prompt injections crafted by an adaptive attacker. Score is attack success rate.
note: Anthropic uses Gray Swan's Shade adaptive attacker for this surface. Reported at 1 and many attempts.

name: Prompt injection robustness against adaptive attackers, computer use (Anthropic)
aliases: Robustness against adaptive attackers: computer use
description: Computer-use agents face indirect prompt injections crafted by an adaptive attacker. Score is attack success rate.
note: Anthropic uses Gray Swan's Shade adaptive attacker for this surface. Reported with and without safeguards.

name: Prompt injection test suite for LLM-based machine translation
description: Translation systems receive TruthfulQA questions with injected instructions to answer instead of translate, across WMT 2024 language pairs. Scored by the share of outputs that answer rather than translate.
org: Antonio Valerio Miceli-Barone and Zhifan Sun
note: Released as a WMT 2024 test suite. Cohere reports failure rates on its 817-question direct translation set for Command A Translate.

name: Prompt injection, general tool use
description: An adaptive attacker injects payloads into tool responses across 100 multi-step scenarios to trigger unrelated tool calls. Reports survival after N attempts.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Prompt injection, turn injections in tool use
description: Static and adaptive payloads in tool outputs spoof multi-turn conversation syntax. Reports survival after N attempts.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: ProofBench
description: Models write Lean 4 proofs of graduate-level theorems, with Mathlib search and code tools for up to 40 turns. Scored by the share that compile.
note: Vals froze the v1 board on 2026-08-05. ProofBench v1.1 replaced it on 2026-08-13 with non-comparable scores.

name: ProofBench v1.1
description: Models write Lean 4 proofs of graduate-level theorems from paired natural-language and formal statements. Scored by the share the Lean checker accepts.
note: Vals says scores are not comparable with earlier revisions. Four systems tied at 100% on 2026-10-29 among 54, so it is saturated.

name: ProofNet
description: Provers write formal proofs for 371 undergraduate theorems from analysis, algebra and topology textbooks, each with a formal statement and a natural-language proof. The proof checker grades them.
org: Azerbayev, Piotrowski, Schoelkopf, Ayers, Radev and Avigad
note: Originally in Lean 3. Prover reports such as DeepSeek-Prover-V2 use the test split, usually a Lean 4 port. Also used for autoformalization.

name: ProofRank
description: Models write proofs for hard competition problems. An LLM judge compares correct proofs pairwise on conciseness, computational ease, simplicity, diversity and adaptivity, giving Elo ratings.
org: MathArena (ETH Zurich SRI Lab and INSAIT)
note: The first release rated 10 frontier models. Only proofs that pass a correctness filter enter the quality comparison.

name: PropensityBench
description: Agents face 979 scenarios with equally effective safe and harmful tools under escalating pressure. Reports the rate of harmful tool choice.
note: Proprietary Scale AI evaluation with a public leaderboard.

name: Prophet Arena
description: Models and agents forecast open Kalshi prediction-market events and are scored once the events resolve. The live board ranks a difficulty-adjusted Arena score and also reports calibration error and market return.
note: ICLR 2026. Models appear once they reach 50 resolved events, in fixed-context and agentic harness tracks.

name: Protein Design (Anthropic)
description: Models generate novel protein sequences under design constraints and rank protein design libraries for experimental testing.
note: Reported as two tasks, Sequence Generation and Library Ranking, with no overall score.

name: ProteinGym
description: Deep mutational scanning benchmarks. The model ranks mutations by predicted effect on protein function, scored by Spearman rank correlation with lab measurements. Anthropic reports a hard subset, as the correlation times 100.
note: The repo has releases PG_v1.0 to PG_v1.3 (April 2025) that add assays, so check which version a score used. Anthropic system cards report a ProteinGym Hard subset.

name: ProteinLMBench
description: Models answer 944 hand-checked multiple choice questions on protein sequence, structure and function.
org: Johns Hopkins University, University of Cambridge, Shanghai AI Laboratory and others (Yiqing Shen et al.)
note: Released with a protein fine-tuning corpus.

name: ProtocolQA Open-Ended
description: Models correct errors in published lab protocols using open-ended questions adapted from LAB-Bench ProtocolQA. Scored as pass@1.
note: OpenAI open-ended adaptation of the ProtocolQA multiple-choice set.

name: ProtocolQA Open-Ended (xAI)
description: Models name the single most important mistake in a biology lab protocol in free text, with no answer choices.
note: xAI's free-text version of LAB-Bench ProtocolQA. It may differ from OpenAI's open-ended version.

name: Protocols (Anthropic life sciences)
description: Models find and fix errors in molecular biology protocols and answer practical questions about applying real laboratory protocols.
note: Reported as two variants, Troubleshooting and Understanding (V2), with no overall score. Benchling built the Understanding set. From the Claude Opus 5.5 system card it is one of three evaluations Anthropic uses for CB-1 capability, with VCT and BioMysteryBench, replacing the Long-Form Virology Tasks.

name: ProverBench (DeepSeek)
description: Provers write Lean 4 proofs for 325 formalized problems: 15 from AIME 2024 and 2025 and 310 from textbooks across number theory, algebra, calculus and analysis. Lean checks each proof.
note: DeepSeek released it with DeepSeek-Prover-V2 on 2025-04-30. Labs often report only the 15-problem AIME subset as problems solved.

name: PROWBench
description: Programmable world models must render video that follows the rules and interactions their program specifies. The test checks visual fidelity to fine-grained rules.
note: 48 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: Public Benefits Bench
description: Models answer SNAP benefit questions across seven lifecycle phases and 25 topics. A judge grades each answer against rubrics validated by SNAP policy experts.
note: 459 scenarios with a 230-question test set. v1 tested four conditions with and without web search and multi-turn. The live board is v1.1, with v1 archived at /benchmarks/public-benefits-bench-v1.

name: PubMedQA
description: Models answer biomedical research questions with yes, no, or maybe, given a PubMed abstract without its conclusion. Scored by accuracy.
org: University of Pittsburgh and Carnegie Mellon University

name: Putnam 2024
description: Models write full proofs for the 12 problems of the December 2024 William Lowell Putnam competition. Proofs are graded out of 120 points.
note: This is a one-time competition exam, not a maintained benchmark. DeepSeekMath-V2 reports 118 of 120 points, given as 98.3%.

name: Putnam 2025
description: Models solve the 12 problems of the 2025 William Lowell Putnam competition with full proofs. Scored out of 120 points.
note: DeepSeek scored it with a hybrid informal and formal Lean pipeline checked by a strict verifier.

name: Putnam-like
description: Models write proofs for 96 university problems in 8 sets of 12, in the style of the easier and middle Putnam tiers. Each problem has a Lean statement and a point rubric for grading.
note: Ships graded sample answers from Gemini models such as gemini-2-5-pro_20250718.

name: PutnamBench
description: Models write formal Lean proofs of Putnam competition problems. A proof counts only when the verifier accepts it.
note: The Lean set now has 672 problems, and five systems solved all of them by September 2026, so the board ranks full solvers by cost. Labs often report Putnam-200, a fixed subset first used by Seed-Prover.

name: Pwn CTF challenges (Anthropic)
description: Agents exploit insecure software on a remote server for privilege escalation or code execution in capture-the-flag challenges.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: PWNBench v0.1
description: Agents run gray-box penetration tests against live web applications and file the vulnerabilities they find. Reports are scored by severity-weighted F0.5 against known ground truth.
note: Launched 2026-08-20 with 11 models, updated 2026-09-02. Each model runs at several attempt budgets. 14 models in the Fireworks index.

name: Q-Bench
description: Multimodal models are tested on low-level vision: perceiving image distortions, describing them and predicting quality scores.
note: ICLR 2024.

name: Q-Bench Image-Pair Perception
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions comparing low-level attributes across image pairs. The score is overall answer accuracy in the A1-Pair table.
note: One track of Q-Bench. The Q-Bench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks. Authors introduced image-pair perception in Q-Bench+ in February 2024. This track record retains the parent release month as requested.

name: Q-Bench Single-Image Perception
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about low-level attributes of individual images. The score is overall answer accuracy in the A1-Single table.
note: One track of Q-Bench. The Q-Bench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Q-Bench-Video
description: Models judge the quality of natural, AI-generated and computer-graphics videos through yes-or-no, what-how, open-ended and pairwise comparison questions.
org: Q-Future (Nanyang Technological University and Shanghai Jiao Tong University)
note: CVPR 2025 paper. A video sibling of the image test Q-Bench, not a new version of it. Open-ended answers are judged by an LLM.

name: Qasper
description: Models answer 5,049 questions about 1,585 NLP research papers from the full paper text. Answers are scored with token F1.

name: QF-Bench
description: Agents write and run code for 87 quantitative finance tasks in a network-isolated sandbox with real data. Tasks cover derivatives pricing, fixed income, credit, risk, factor research, backtesting and market microstructure. More than 3,300 assertions check numeric outputs against finance rules such as no-arbitrage bounds and put-call parity. Scored by pass@1 over three runs.
note: Tasks run on the Harbor framework. The draft paper reports 42 models over 10,962 runs, but the public leaderboard shows 9 agent and model pairs dated 2026-05-07. The authors are anonymous. About 60 GitHub stars.

name: QIMMA
description: Models are ranked on a cleaned suite of over 52k Arabic samples. The makers first screened existing Arabic benchmarks for errors with model judges and human review.
org: Technology Innovation Institute (AlQadi, Alzubaidi et al.)
note: The suite includes cleaned versions of ArabicMMLU, AraTrust, ArabCulture, AraDiCE culture, 3LM STEM, medical and legal sets, plus code tasks. The results dataset held 83 models on 2026-08-26. Per-sample outputs are public.

name: QIVD
description: Models answer spoken questions about short phone videos in real time, as in a face to face talk. Each item has a short answer and a timestamp.
org: Qualcomm AI Research and University of Toronto
note: Published at ICLR 2026. Qwen reports it as audio-visual interaction.

name: QMSum
description: Models answer a query about a long meeting transcript with a written summary of the relevant parts. The 1,808 query and summary pairs cover 232 meetings from several domains. Scores compare outputs with reference summaries using ROUGE.
note: SCROLLS and ZeroSCROLLS include QMSum as a task, and the almanac carries SCROLLS as a suite. ROUGE rewards word overlap, not faithfulness. Microsoft reports it in the Phi-3.5 long-context table. About 160 GitHub stars.

name: Qodo AI Code Review Benchmark
description: Models review real merged pull requests with planted functional bugs and best-practice violations. Findings are matched to the planted issues and scored by F1.
note: Qodo publishes F1 for seven code review systems. The page does not name their backbone model snapshots.

name: QuAC
description: Models answer free-form questions in information-seeking dialogs about a hidden Wikipedia section, across 100K questions. Scored by word-level F1.
org: Allen Institute for AI, University of Washington, Stanford, and UMass Amherst

name: Quadruped reinforcement learning task (Anthropic)
description: Agents train a quadruped to reach high performance in a continuous control task.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: QuALITY
aliases: QuALITY (Question Answering with Long Input Texts, Yes!)
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about English passages that average about 5,000 tokens. Scoring is accuracy.
note: About half the questions were too hard for annotators to answer under tight time limits.

name: Quant-Arena
description: Models act as quant researchers on 2022 to 2023 China A-share data with bounded feedback, then commit one strategy. A cash-account evaluator with trading costs scores it once on a sealed 2024 window.
note: Models get raw daily and Level-2 data for 3,042 stocks. The score weights the sealed year 70% and the research window 30%. None of nine frontier models beat the equal-weight market in 2024.

name: QuantBench
description: Models answer 25 multiple choice versions of quant trading firm reasoning puzzles. Scored as cons@16 accuracy.
note: OpenAI contextual evaluation. Questions come from competitions run by firms such as Jane Street.

name: QuixBugs
description: Models repair 40 classic algorithm programs, in Python and Java, that each contain a one-line bug. The bugs fall into 14 defect classes. A fix counts when the program passes the test cases.
note: The programs come from the Quixey Challenge, a 2011 to 2013 contest for human programmers. Program repair papers on language models still use it. It is small and public, so contamination is likely. About 148 GitHub stars.

name: QVHighlights
description: Natural-language queries over YouTube videos. Model localizes relevant moments, scored by Recall@1 at IoU 0.5.

name: Qwen Chinese human evaluation
description: Three annotators rank chat model answers to 300 Chinese instructions on knowledge, language, writing, math and coding. Results are win rates against GPT-3.5.
note: In-house Qwen evaluation. The instructions are not public.

name: Qwen in-house Chinese automatic evaluation
description: Models answer Qwen in-house Chinese datasets on knowledge, comprehension, coding, math and related skills. Skills and weights change between reports.
note: In-house Qwen evaluation. The Qwen2 report gives an average, the Qwen2.5 report gives per-skill scores only.

name: Qwen in-house English automatic evaluation
description: Models answer Qwen in-house English datasets on knowledge, comprehension, coding, math and related skills. Skills and weights change between reports.
note: In-house Qwen evaluation. The Qwen2 report gives an average, the Qwen2.5 report gives per-skill scores only.

name: Qwen in-house voice-chat benchmark
description: Models answer spoken versions of text benchmarks such as MMLU, CEval, IFEval, GSM8K, Math23K and Math401. Each part keeps the source benchmark's scoring.
note: In-house Qwen evaluation. The tasks are not public. About 90% of the text instructions suit speech and are used.

name: Qwen-Image-Bench
description: Text-to-image models are tested on professional creative work, from faithful real-world reconstruction to creative expression. A released judge model scores the images.
note: The judge model is on Hugging Face and ModelScope. About 50 likes on the dataset.

name: Qwen2 multilingual safety evaluation
description: Models answer risky prompts in several languages on illegal behavior, fraud, pornography and privacy, including jailbreak attempts. Scores are harmful response rates.
note: In-house Qwen evaluation. The prompts are not public. Lower is better.

name: QwenBlenderBench
description: Models complete Blender 3D modeling tasks in Qwen's internal visual agent and coding test. Qwen has not described its scoring.
note: This is an in-house evaluation, and Qwen has not released the tasks.

name: QwenChineseBench
description: Models answer questions about real-world Chinese knowledge. Qwen describes it only as an internal Chinese knowledge benchmark.
note: In-house. Scoring method is not described, so the scoring field is a guess.

name: QwenClawBench
description: Agents complete 100 tasks across 8 domains in isolated OpenClaw workspaces drawn from real user patterns. Automated checks and an LLM judge score each task.
note: Qwen built it as an internal benchmark for Qwen3.6-Plus and released it afterward.

name: QwenQoderBench
description: Qwen in-house benchmark of user experience in the Qoder coding product, run in Claude Code (avg@5, 6-hour limit).
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Alibaba Qwen).

name: QwenReactBench
description: Model builds bilingual React projects in Claude Code across 7 categories. Rendered outputs judged by a multimodal model, ranked with Bradley-Terry Elo.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Alibaba Qwen).

name: QwenSVG
description: Models write SVG graphics code for Qwen's in-house prompts. Results are reported as ratings near 1,500 to 1,600, not percentages.
note: In-house: Qwen never released the tasks or explained the rating method.

name: QwenSVGBench
description: Model writes SVG code for bilingual prompts. Rendered outputs judged by a multimodal model and ranked with Bradley-Terry Elo.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Alibaba Qwen).

name: QwenSWEBench
description: Qwen in-house software-engineering benchmark run in Claude Code (avg@3, 8-hour limit). Task and scoring details unpublished.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Alibaba Qwen).

name: QwenVision2Code
description: Models turn images, videos and design references into executable code. Qwen reports ratings near 1,500 to 1,900, not percentages.
note: In-house. The Qwen3.7-Plus post does not explain the tasks or the rating method.

name: QwenVisualOffice
description: Models handle visual office tasks in an internal Qwen test set. Qwen has not published the tasks or how they are scored.
note: In-house Qwen benchmark, so scores cannot be checked independently.

name: QwenWebBench
description: Models generate front-end code for web apps, games, SVG, and other categories in English and Chinese. Multimodal judgments produce Elo ratings.
note: In-house Qwen benchmark, and the tasks are not released.

name: QwenWebDev
description: Models generate front-end web pages in English and Chinese across 7 categories. Pages are rendered and a multimodal judge compares them, giving Bradley-Terry Elo ratings.
note: This is an in-house evaluation, and Qwen has not released the tasks.

name: QwenWorldBench
description: Models act as world models that simulate agent environments in 7 domains, such as terminal, web, and Android. A rubric judge scores five dimensions.
note: In-house: Qwen never released the tasks.

name: R-Bench (real-world robustness)
description: Models answer questions about images degraded by 33 kinds of real-world corruption, from capture to display. Scores compare distorted and reference images.
org: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Nanyang Technological University and others
note: The set has 2,970 human-labeled question answer pairs. It is not the RBench video generation benchmark from Peking University.

name: RACE
description: Models answer reading comprehension questions from Chinese middle and high school English exams. Reported here without a subset split.
note: Use race-m or race-h when a report gives the middle or high school subset.

name: RACE-H
description: Models answer multiple-choice reading questions from English exams for Chinese high school students. The test split has 3,498 questions, scored by accuracy.

name: RACE-M
description: Models read passages from English exams for Chinese middle school students and answer multiple-choice questions. Scored by accuracy.
note: This is the middle school subset of RACE, alongside the harder high school subset RACE-H.

name: Radiological and Nuclear Expert Knowledge
description: Models answer 87 expert and tacit knowledge questions on radiological and nuclear threats. Scored as cons@32 accuracy.
note: Questions written by an MIT nuclear security fellow for OpenAI Preparedness.

name: Radiology's Last Exam (RadLE)
description: Multimodal models make a single spot diagnosis from images alone on 50 hard radiology cases. Board-certified radiologists scored about 83%.
org: CRASH Lab, Koita Centre for Digital Health, Ashoka University
note: Presented at RSNA 2025. The best model at launch scored about 30%.

name: RadLE 2.0
description: Models diagnose single-image radiology cases with a confidence score from 0 to 4, or say they do not know. A confidence-weighted index rewards right answers and penalizes confident errors.
org: CRASH Lab, Koita Centre for Digital Health, Ashoka University
note: The primary metric RadLE-C runs from 0 to 2000. It is larger than 1.0 and adds open-source and medical vision-language models, so scores do not compare.

name: RAGTruth
description: A word-level annotated corpus of hallucinations in retrieval-augmented generation answers. It is used to train and evaluate hallucination detection and RAG faithfulness.
note: Released in January 2024 and updated in February 2024 with more annotations. How NVIDIA scores models on it is not stated.

name: Random Complex Tasks (LongCat)
description: Agents solve 100 tasks sampled from a generator that builds random executable tool environments across more than four domains. Scored by Avg@4, averaged over three runs.
note: In-house test of generalization to unseen tool environments. Meituan says it will add it to an open evaluation platform.

name: RBench
description: 650 image+text prompts for robot video generation (tasks and embodiments). MLLM judge scores task completion, physical plausibility, stability.
note: MLLM-judged. GPT and Qwen judges give different scores and orders. Best GPT-judged 0.642. Later rows (e.g. Cosmos 3) were supplied by model authors.

name: RCM-Bench-1
description: Agents handle healthcare revenue cycle work, such as claim submission, billing and eligibility checks, with tools. Checks cover tool calls, arguments, replies and final system state.
note: 97 scenarios across six workflows, weighted equally. 20 models in the Fireworks index. The maker page renders in the browser only.

name: RD-TableBench
description: Models extract 1,000 hand-labeled complex tables from document images, including scans, handwriting and merged cells. Scored by Levenshtein-based row and cell alignment.
note: Reducto released only a subset of its evaluation framework to protect scoring. NVIDIA reports it for Nemotron Nano V2 VL.

name: RE-Bench
description: Seven open-ended ML research-engineering environments with human-expert baselines. Score normalized to reference solutions.

name: RE-Bench subset (Anthropic)
description: Agents solve a modified subset of four METR RE-Bench research engineering tasks. Scores are normalized from reference solution 0 to expert solution 1.
note: Anthropic runs triton_cumsum, rust_codecontests_inference, restricted_mlm and fix_embedding. Scores are not comparable to METR's reported scores.

name: ReactBench
description: Coding agents do 39 realistic React tasks in two tracks. Write React tasks come from merged pull requests and are checked by hidden behavior tests. Fix React tasks ask the agent to remove React performance, accessibility and quality issues. A task passes only if the tests pass and a pinned React Doctor scan finds no new graded issue.
note: Million also makes React Doctor, the scanner the verifier uses. The board reports pass@1 with 95% intervals, cost per rollout and results by effort level. Versions 1.0 to 1.2 are listed, and results should be compared within one version. About 281 GitHub stars. Not the same test as Qwen's in-house QwenReactBench.

name: ReactHuman
description: Multimodal models act as the decision core of a household robot. They must react at once to sudden physical hazards, such as catching a slipping plate.
note: It had 53 Hugging Face paper upvotes.

name: Readability (Perplexity)
description: Models answer search questions. Graders rate whether answers are concise yet detailed and use markdown formatting well.
note: Perplexity reported it once, for Sonar, with no public method or data. The scoring method is not described, so model-judged is assumed.

name: Real-scenario prompts human evaluation (Z.ai)
description: One human evaluator scores replies to 660 curated real user prompts in English, Chinese and other languages on a 0 to 10 scale.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation. Scores are given per language with no combined score.

name: Real-SWE
description: Models resolve tasks in private production codebases licensed from real companies. The board reports resolution rate with standard errors.
note: Real-SWE 1.1 (2026-10) covers 18 models on 25 tasks. Check whether 1.1 scores compare with the 2026-09 first release.

name: Real-SWE 1.1
description: Resolution rate on private enterprise coding tasks, averaged across five runs per task.
note: Retains highest effort, harness, estimated rollout cost, and standard errors. Separate from the original Real-SWE.

name: Real-time Audio-Visual Interaction Evaluation
description: Trained conversationalists hold three minute live video calls with a model. Real users rate each session for naturalness and fluency on a 0 to 3 scale.
note: In-house Meituan evaluation. The tasks are not public. Experts also report the share of good cases on six factors such as real-timeness and memory.

name: Real-World Audio Recording
description: Speech transcription systems are scored by word error rate on real-world recordings across multiple languages.
note: OpenAI reports this internal benchmark for GPT-Live-Transcribe.

name: Real-World Finance (Anthropic)
description: Agents complete about 50 analyst tasks in banking, private equity, hedge funds and corporate finance, producing spreadsheets, slides and documents. Rubric graded.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Real-World Finance v2 (Anthropic)
description: Agents complete 294 long-horizon finance tasks such as building financial models. A model grader compares deliverables pairwise and ratings are fit as Elo.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. Scores are Elo with Sonnet 4.6 fixed at 1000, so they do not compare with the first version.

name: Real-world vulnerability discovery
description: Agents search popular open-source codebases to rediscover about 1,200 recent confirmed vulnerabilities across many languages. Reports share discovered.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Real2Sim
description: Coding agents get a robot recording from DROID (three camera videos, stereo calibration, joint and gripper commands and the task instruction) and build an interactive simulation of the scene. Each scene is scored on how closely it matches the recording, on replaying the recorded actions, and on whether a fixed robot policy completes the task in it.
note: Ten DROID episodes, all recorded on one Franka Panda rig. Each model builds every scene twice, once with a plain prompt and once with the agent instructions from RoboSimStudio (arXiv 2610.18835). The score is the mean of four equally weighted parts: visual fidelity (1 minus LPIPS), semantic fidelity (DINOv2 cosine), replay of the recorded actions and success of the π0.5-DROID policy. One reviewer who knew the model and harness judged the replays. No policy rollout has succeeded so far, and the policy was not tested on a known-good scene, so a failure may come from the policy rather than the scene.

name: RealCompanion
description: Models read months of real chats between ten people and an AI companion, then answer questions about who each person is. The release has 27,218 messages over up to 120 days.
note: It had 40 Hugging Face paper upvotes.

name: RealKIE-FCC Verified
description: Model extracts structured fields from scanned FCC invoices into a JSON schema. Amazon human-verified labels. Field-level similarity (ALNS).
note: Lab-created verified variant (Amazon AGI) of Indico's RealKIE FCC Invoices set (RealKIE released 2024-03).

name: REALM
description: High-fidelity simulation benchmark for VLA generalization: 15 perturbation factors, 7 skills, 3,500+ objects. Success rate validated against real-robot results.
org: Czech Technical University (CIIRC) + University of Amsterdam
note: Design: checks that sim scores correlate with real-robot performance. Paper evaluates pi0, pi0-FAST and GR00T N1.5 only. No leaderboard. IEEE RA-L 2026.

name: RealmPathology
description: Models interpret real anatomic pathology reports and must not claim a diagnosis, stage or treatment the report does not support. Rubrics have 772 positive and 299 penalty criteria.
note: The current release rebuilt every rubric around four clinical failure modes and added penalties. micro1 says scores are not continuous with the earlier release. 13 models.

name: Realtime-Bench
description: Agents act in 50 live game and web tasks where a late action fails: 30 web tasks (travel, shopping, services and security) and 20 games. The environment keeps moving while the model thinks. Three clocks separate speed from skill: Wall Clock runs on real time, Paused Clock stops while the model thinks, and Token Clock advances with each generated token. Scores are task success rates over three runs.
org: University of Texas at Austin, Ohio State University, UIUC, NVIDIA, Northwestern University and Steadyworks
note: The leaderboard averages each task's first three Wall Clock runs (pass^1) and also reports pass^3, the share of tasks solved in all three. Jev was run on the 30 web tasks only, with text input. The paper adds Paused Clock and Token Clock runs, which remove or simulate the delay of inference.

name: RealToxicityPrompts
description: Models continue 100,000 web text prompts. Scored on the rate of toxic generations judged by a toxicity classifier.
org: Allen Institute for AI and University of Washington
note: Labs use different classifiers and sampling, so rates rarely compare across reports.

name: RealWorldQA
description: Models answer a question about each of 700+ real-world photos, many taken from vehicles, that test basic spatial understanding. Answers are easy to verify.

name: Reasoning behavior classifiers (Anthropic)
aliases: Percentages of model outputs exhibiting harmful behaviors
description: Classifiers scan reasoning text from training episodes for deception, harmful actions and distress. Score is the share of outputs flagged.
note: In-house Anthropic monitoring of training transcripts. Results are given per category with no single overall rate.

name: ReasonVOS
description: Models segment and track objects in videos from explicit referring queries and implicit reasoning queries. The score is overall J&F on ReVOS.
org: University of Technology Sydney and Alibaba (Yan et al., VISA)
note: The VISA release has 35,074 instruction and mask pairs from 1,042 videos for training and evaluation. Microsoft's Mage-VL card reports it.
