name: Recognition of model-written user turns (Anthropic)
aliases: Model ability to distinguish their own simulated user turns from real user turns
description: Models write synthetic user turns for real Claude Code transcripts, then judge which version is real. Score is accuracy above chance.
note: The same model acts as generator and judge. Anthropic reports the probability of a correct choice minus 0.5.

name: ReCoRD
aliases: Reading Comprehension with Commonsense Reasoning Dataset
description: Models fill in a masked entity in a query about a news article, using the article as context. Scoring is exact match and token F1.
org: Johns Hopkins University and Microsoft Research
note: ReCoRD is one of the SuperGLUE tasks.

name: RecreationBench
description: Agents explore a running reference app and rebuild it, across 250 tasks on five platforms. Programmatic tests and a VLM judge score the result.

name: Red Teaming Network pairwise safety comparison
description: Red teamers compare anonymized responses from two models in free-form risky conversations. Scored as the share of ratings where a model is safer.
note: Human red teamers rate only conversations with at least one perceived unsafe response.

name: RedCode
description: Models meet adversarial prompts to generate or run harmful code. Generation is model-judged and execution is checked in a container.
note: Over 4,000 test cases in two parts. RedCode-Exec has 4,050 instances over 25 vulnerability types in Python, Bash and natural language, run in a Docker sandbox. RedCode-Gen has 160 prompts with function signatures over 8 malware families. NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks track.

name: RedlineBench
description: Agent acts as counsel at one turn of a SaaS contract negotiation and returns tracked-change redlines. Three LLM judges grade attorney-written rubrics.
note: Attorneys wrote a branching tree of golden responses. The counterparty playbook is hidden from the agent. Built without client data.

name: RedTeam Arena
description: Players get 60 seconds to make a model say a target word. An extended Elo ranks players, models and target prompts, with models ranked by resistance.
note: Built with Pliny and the BASI community. About 8,000 people played in the first week. Arena notes that resistance trades off with controllability.

name: Ref-DAVIS17
description: Models segment and track the object that a sentence describes through each frame of a DAVIS 2017 video. Scored by J&F, the mean of mask overlap and contour accuracy.
org: Max Planck Institute for Informatics (Khoreva, Rohrbach, Schiele)
note: It adds language descriptions to the DAVIS 2016 and 2017 video segmentation sets. Microsoft's Mage-VL card reports it with Qwen3-VL and Phi-4 baselines.

name: Ref-L4
description: Models locate the object described by a long referring expression in an image. The set has 45,341 annotations over 365 object categories, scored by box accuracy.
note: The authors also released cleaned RefCOCO, RefCOCO+ and RefCOCOg after finding labeling errors of 5 to 24 percent.

name: Ref-YouTube-VOS
description: Models segment and track the object that a sentence describes in YouTube-VOS videos. Scored by J&F on a server-graded validation split.
org: Seoul National University and Adobe Research (Seo, Lee, Han, URVOS)
note: ECCV 2020 paper (URVOS). Microsoft's Mage-VL card reports it as Ref-YT-VOS.

name: RefAdv-S
description: Models locate the object a referring expression describes among hard distractors in real images. Scored by accuracy at 0.5 box overlap on 1,142 cases.
note: It is the public subset of the larger Ref-Adv benchmark.

name: RefCOCO / RefCOCO+ / RefCOCOg
description: Model grounds a referring expression to a bounding box in a COCO image. Scored by accuracy at IoU 0.5.
org: UNC Chapel Hill (Licheng Yu et al.)
note: Reka's 'RefCOCO-A/B' are the testA/testB splits.

name: RefSpatial-Bench
description: Real images where the model points to an object or free space defined by multi-step spatial relations. Scored by mask hit.
note: No independent leaderboard. Subset aggregation not stated. One cross-checked row (RoboBrain2.0-7B) differs from its origin: 42.2 vs 32.50.

name: RefSpatial-Expand-Bench
description: Models point to an object or free space described by multi-step spatial relations, in more indoor scenes plus new outdoor streets and parking lots. Scored by mask hit.
note: The maker calls it the new version of RefSpatial-Bench. 441 items: 241 location and 200 placement. Released 2025-10-25.

name: RefSpatial-Expand-Bench Location
description: Models solve spatial location questions in the RefSpatial expansion set. The score is the published overall accuracy.
note: One track of RefSpatial-Expand-Bench. The RefSpatial-Expand-Bench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: RefSpatial-Expand-Bench Placement
description: Models solve spatial placement questions in the RefSpatial expansion set. The score is the published overall accuracy.
note: One track of RefSpatial-Expand-Bench. The RefSpatial-Expand-Bench record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: Refusal to assist with AI safety R&D (Anthropic)
description: Models receive single-turn coding requests for legitimate AI safety research with user context. Score is the refusal rate, where lower is better.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: RefusalBench (Nous Research)
description: Models get requests in scenarios that closed and open models commonly refuse. The score is the percent of questions the model answers, averaged over 5 trials.
note: Nous introduced it with Hermes 4 and keeps a RefusalBench leaderboard that it cites for Hermes 4.3. Higher means fewer refusals, which Nous treats as better steerability.

name: Refusals + System Jailbreak (xAI)
description: Models get the xAI refusal set with jailbreak templates in the system message. The metric is the answer rate.
note: In-house xAI evaluation reported in the Grok 4 and Grok 4.1 model cards.

name: Refusals + User Jailbreak (xAI)
description: Models get the xAI refusal set with jailbreak templates in the user message. The metric is the answer rate.
note: In-house xAI evaluation reported in the Grok 4 and Grok 4.1 model cards.

name: Regurgitation Evaluations
description: Models are asked to reproduce training data. Scored on how often they refuse to regurgitate it.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards describe results in words without a number.

name: RelBench
description: Agents build models for prediction tasks over multi-table relational databases, graded on held-out targets.
note: Built as a deep learning benchmark. xAI reports an aggregate agent score labeled accuracy. RelBench v2 (January 2026) added 4 databases and 36 tasks, and v3 (August 2026) moved data to Hugging Face. Original task numbers stay comparable.

name: RelyToolBench
description: Agents answer queries with simulated APIs built on the StableToolBench server. Scoring targets tool hallucinations, such as calling wrong or missing tools.
note: Tool responses are simulated with gpt-4o-2024-08-06. It comes from the paper Reducing Tool Hallucination via Reliability Alignment.

name: ReMI
description: Models reason over several images per question in math, physics, logic, code, charts, and spatial or temporal tasks. Scored by accuracy.

name: Remote Labor Index
description: Agents complete real paid remote freelance projects from many sectors. Reviewers judge whether each deliverable would be accepted as commissioned work, giving an automation rate.
org: Center for AI Safety and Scale AI
note: The best agent automated only 2.5% of projects at launch. Only a 10 task public set is released.

name: RepCount-A
description: Models count repeated actions in streamed video and are scored by distance from the true count.
note: The launch post reports off-by-one performance for online visual counting.

name: RepoBench
description: Models complete code using context retrieved from other files in the same Python or Java repository. Three tasks cover retrieval, completion and the full pipeline.
org: UC San Diego (Tianyang Liu, Canwen Xu, Julian McAuley)
note: Published at ICLR 2024. Labs report it for code completion and fill-in-the-middle models, for example Mistral's Codestral 25.01.

name: RepoChat Arena
description: Users give a GitHub repository link and a question. A retriever model picks files, two answer models reply, and users vote for the better answer.
note: Answers can resolve issues, review pull requests or explain a repository. The retrievers were gemini-1.5-flash-002 and gpt-4o-mini. The release month is estimated from the post date.

name: RepoInject v1
description: Coding agents do benign tasks in 84 repository tasks seeded with prompt injections. Reports attack success rate at one and three attempts.
note: Third-party private benchmark run for Meta before release.

name: RepoQA
description: Models find a function in a long code repository from a description of what it does, across Python, C++, Rust, Java and TypeScript.

name: ReproBAIT
description: Agents independently reproduce biological AI models from published scientific papers. Scored as success rate.
note: Third-party SecureBio evaluation reported in OpenAI system cards.

name: Research sandbagging (Anthropic)
description: Agents are told to sabotage a coding task or imitate a weaker model without alerting a weaker monitor. Measures the performance drop and monitor suspicion.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation based on Gasteiger et al. 2025. Results are a scatter of task performance against monitor suspicion.

name: Research-Eval
description: Search-augmented models answer 374 grounded multi-hop questions that need sources across many kinds of websites. An LLM judge checks each answer against a checklist of requirements.
note: Reka in-house tutors wrote 606 candidate questions and kept 374 after double annotation. Reka recommends deepseek-v3-0324 as the judge so results stay comparable.

name: ResearchClawBench
description: Agents get the literature and raw data behind a published paper, with the paper hidden, and try to rediscover its results. Expert rubrics with weighted criteria grade the outputs.
note: 40 tasks across 10 scientific domains. The paper evaluates 7 research agents and 17 LLMs. The leaderboard takes community agent submissions.

name: ResearchRubrics
description: 101 deep-research prompts with 2,593 expert-written weighted rubric criteria (including penalties). Reports graded for grounding, reasoning and clarity.
note: ICLR 2026 paper.

name: ResearchTasteBench
description: Agents are scored on judgment about which research directions are worth pursuing. Part of Meta's recursive-improvement suite.
note: In-house Meta evaluation. Graded programmatically. The tasks are not public.

name: Respecting Auto-Review
description: Agents receive an Auto-review denial during a coding task. Scored on how often they try to circumvent the denial.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Respecting Warnings
description: Agents meet low-stakes restrictions and warnings during routine tasks. Scored on the rate of unwanted persistence past the warning.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Rev CTF challenges (Anthropic)
description: Agents reverse-engineer binary executables to find hidden details or vulnerabilities in capture-the-flag challenges.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: ReviewBench
description: AI code review systems review 219 real pull requests from 187 repositories in 19 languages. A judge scores found issues against a multi-source golden set for precision, recall and F1.
note: Research preview released 2026-10-05. Senior engineers agreed with the ground truth 96.6% of the time. Harbor hosts it as review-bench/reviewbench-public.

name: Reward-hack-prone coding tasks (Anthropic)
description: Models solve hard coding problems where earlier Claude models often special-cased tests. Score is the classifier hack rate.
note: Anthropic also reports a hidden-test hack rate on held-out tests for the same tasks.

name: RewardBench
description: Models act as judges and pick the preferred response in chosen and rejected pairs across chat, hard chat, safety and reasoning. Scored by accuracy.
org: Allen Institute for AI (Lambert et al.)
note: It measures reward model or judge quality, not answer quality. RewardBench 2 is a later separate release.

name: RewardBench 2
description: Reward models must score one correct answer above three wrong ones on 1,865 new human prompts. Subsets cover factuality, precise instruction following, math, safety, focus and ties, and the score averages them.
note: Models score about 20 points lower than on the first RewardBench, and scores correlate with best-of-N and PPO results. Results are published in allenai/reward-bench-2-results.

name: Rewind-attacker cyber adversarial robustness (Anthropic)
description: An automated attacker with rewinds and 400 calls tries to make a safeguarded Claude Code agent complete offensive cyber tasks. Score is attack success rate.
note: Tasks include ransomware, data exfiltration, CVE exploitation, command and control and self-replication.

name: RGB
description: Models answer English and Chinese news questions from retrieved passages, testing noise robustness, negative rejection, information integration, and counterfactual robustness. Scored by accuracy.

name: Riemann-bench
description: 25 private research-mathematics problems from professors and IMO medalists. Agents with tools, 100 runs per problem.

name: RiOSWorld
description: Computer-use agents work in an Ubuntu virtual machine through risky scenarios such as phishing emails and pop-ups. Scores track whether agents notice and avoid the risk.
note: Built on OSWorld. 125 GitHub stars at 2026-11-01.

name: RISE
description: Agents answer real questions from human experts that need multi-step search and interaction with information-dense web pages. MiniMax has not published the scoring method.
note: In-house MiniMax benchmark, and the tasks are not released.

name: RISEBench
description: Image editing models follow 360 instructions that need temporal, causal, spatial or logical reasoning. An LMM judge scores instruction reasoning, appearance consistency and visual plausibility.
org: VisionXLab (Shanghai Jiao Tong University) and collaborators
note: The paper has 68 HF upvotes. OpenCompass hosts a RISEBench gallery space.

name: RISEBench++
description: Image editing models follow 1,000 bilingual instructions over six reasoning types, adding counterfactual and hybrid reasoning. It covers single-image, multi-image and multi-turn editing across 65 task types.
org: VisionXLab (Shanghai Jiao Tong University) and collaborators
note: The makers call it an extension of RISEBench. Test cases are in English and Chinese with 12 subcategories.

name: RL rollout audit for beyond-episode drives
description: LLM autoraters read a stratified sample of 10,000 RL training rollouts for alignment faking, training gaming and beyond-episode drives.
note: In-house Google DeepMind audit of training data, so results are rates over sampled rollouts.

name: RLBench
description: Robot arm policies attempt 100 hand-designed manipulation tasks in simulation, from reaching a target and opening a door to multi-stage tasks such as putting a tray in an oven. Each task has camera, depth and joint observations and an unlimited supply of motion-planned demonstrations. Scores are task success rates.
note: Many papers report a fixed subset of tasks, such as the 18-task multi-task set from PerAct, so scores depend on the subset and the number of demonstrations. About 1,840 GitHub stars, and the repo was last pushed in 2025-01.

name: RMBench
description: Policies run 9 simulated bimanual manipulation tasks on RoboTwin 2.0 that need memory of earlier observations, at several levels of memory complexity. Success rate.
org: HKU MMLab + Peking University + others (RoboTwin team)
note: About 225 GitHub stars. Tasks split into single-memory M(1) and multi-memory M(n) groups. Evaluation can run through XPolicyLab adapters. The paper also proposes the Mem-0 policy.

name: RoadmapBench
description: Agents start from an older version of an open-source repository and implement a roadmap of features from its next real release. The set has 115 tasks from 17 repositories in 5 languages, scored by tests.
note: The median task changes about 3,700 lines across 51 files. The paper reports a Completion Score for partial progress next to the resolve rate.

name: Robo-bench
description: General agents control a simulated 7-DoF Franka arm and a 29-DoF humanoid through motor commands, sensors and camera images only, across 24 tasks.
note: The agent gets the robot datasheet and kinematic model but never the MuJoCo simulator itself. Most tasks are held out. The board had seven models on 2026-10-13.

name: RoboArena
description: Double-blind pairwise A/B trials of generalist DROID policies on real Franka arms, free-form tasks by volunteer evaluators. Elo-style rating.
note: Relative rating with no ceiling. Evaluators at 28 organizations. One contributed 2,301 of 3,994 evals. Low-eval rows are unofficial.

name: RoboCasa
description: Simulated mobile manipulators and humanoids do 100 kitchen tasks, 25 atomic and 75 composite, across 120 scenes. Scored by success rate.
note: RSS 2024. About 1,850 GitHub stars. Tagged release v0.2 in February 2026 when RoboCasa365 (v1.0) replaced its task set.

name: RoboCasa GR1 Tabletop Tasks
description: A simulated Fourier GR-1 humanoid with dexterous hands does 24 tabletop pick-and-place tasks, including unseen object and container pairs. Success rate per task.
note: Built for the GR00T N1 report with 1,000 demos per task. About 170 GitHub stars. NVIDIA still reports it for GR00T N1.7 with 20 trials per task.

name: RoboCasa365
description: Mobile-manipulator kitchen sim: train on 300-task Human300 data, test on 50 tasks incl. 16 unseen composite tasks. Success rate.
note: Composite-Unseen scores sit far below Atomic-Seen, a large generalization gap. Team trains baselines. Other entries self-evaluated and reviewed. Submissions live in github.com/robocasa-benchmark/leaderboard. A separate Agentic track for harnesses around a base policy got its first entry on 2026-10-31.

name: RoboChallenge
description: Fine-tuned policies run 10 real rollouts on each of 30 tabletop tasks across four robot types. Scored by success rate and progress.
note: Table30 v1 retired 2026-05-27 at 64.33% top success. V2 uses the RoboChallenge/Table30v2 dataset. Benchmark team runs every rollout, but host Dexmal also submits its own DM0 models.

name: RoboChallenge Table30 v2
description: Policies run 30 new real tabletop tasks on ARX5, UR5, ALOHA and DOS-W1 robots. Each task has a 10-point stage rubric for partial credit.
note: Replaced Table30 v1, which retired on 2026-05-27. The maker says v2 upgrades tasks, evaluation and system. Lightwheel and NVIDIA are building an Isaac Lab twin, announced 2026-08-19.

name: RoboColiseum
description: AgiBot Genie robot in Genie Sim 3.0 (Isaac Sim): instruction, robustness, manipulation and spatial boards after post-training on provided sim data.
note: Instruction board crowded (many pi0.5 fine-tunes 0.72-0.84). Manipulation and spatial not saturated. Many noisy third-party rows. Organizer baselines mixed with submissions.

name: Robocurve physical tool-use benchmark (unidentified)
description: Unnamed Robocurve physical tool-use robot task.
note: robocurve.org, the RCI page and the public run export (robodojo-rc-tier-1, roboharm-v1, simple-tasks) show no such benchmark or Gemini 3.7 Flash runs.

name: Robocurve simple tasks (LLM control of YAM arms)
description: Frontier LLMs control bimanual I2RT YAM arms through Inspect Robots tools on block-into-bowl, puzzle, push-ball and stack-bowls. Staged scores, 20 trials.
note: Block into Bowl near saturation: GPT-6 Astra 19/20 (95%) versus Fable 5.1 8/20, with 6x fewer output tokens. Puzzle stays at 10%. The public run export holds 220 simple-tasks trials with logs and videos.

name: RoboDojo
description: Generalist manipulation policies run 42 Isaac Sim tasks and 18 remote real-robot tasks. Scored by task score and success rate.
org: MMLab@HKU + UC Berkeley + Tsinghua + others (RoboDojo team)
note: The sim board reports average score and success. It is far from saturated. Models self-reporting 97-99% on LIBERO score far lower here. Team also evaluated GPT-6 Astra as an embodied agent.

name: RoboDojo-RC Tier 1
description: Six real RoboDojo tasks on I2RT YAM arms, 20 attempts each. Robot policies and tool-calling LLMs scored by rubric progress.
note: One team runs every attempt on its own rigs and publishes per-trial score, cost, time, logs and video. Best entry Dream-1 59.3% progress (trained on YAM). Robocurve says best LLM score rose 15% to 43% in two months.

name: RoboEval
description: Robot policies perform eight bimanual manipulation tasks with controlled variations in simulation. Scores add behavior and progress metrics, such as coordination and efficiency, to task success.
org: University of Washington and collaborators (Wang et al.)
note: The paper ships over three thousand expert demonstrations. Version 2 of the paper came out on 2026-05-04. Ai2 reports a 0 to 1 score for MolmoAct 2.

name: RoboGate
description: 68 industrial pick-and-place scenarios (nominal, edge, adversarial, randomized) for a Franka arm in Isaac Sim. Organizers run submitted VLAs and report success.
note: All 15 policies score 0/68, with grasp-miss rate 1.0. A scripted IK baseline scores 57/68, so the floor effect gives no ranking. Many entries are LIBERO fine-tunes run zero-shot. Commercial vendor runs every model.

name: Roboharm
description: Agents and VLAs controlling bimanual YAM arms get five harmful-looking instructions in fixed scenes, such as stabbing a doll. Reviewers label refusals and completions.
note: Robocurve published it on 2026-09-18 with 20 trials per task per model. The arXiv paper adds a MuJoCo twin and seven models. Gemini 4 Argon reports refusal accuracy under two harnesses. Match to Robocurve is likely, not confirmed.

name: RoboLab
description: Zero-shot DROID Franka policies in Isaac Lab on 120 tabletop tasks at three instruction levels, 10 episodes each. Success rate.
note: Best entries on 2026-11-01: agentic LM harness AMP1 at 86.0% success, then SenseNova-RoboRSI 57.1%. Best VLA or world model is Lakeside at 51.0%. NVIDIA runs internal rows, including its own models.

name: RoboMemArena
description: Robot policies do long-horizon tasks in partially observable settings that need memory of past observations and actions, in simulation and on real robots.
note: 162 GitHub stars at 2026-11-01.

name: RoboRewardBench
description: Vision-language models act as reward models on real robot videos from Open X-Embodiment and RoboArena, judging task success and partial progress. Counterfactual relabeling adds calibrated failures and near misses.
note: Released with the RoboReward 4B and 8B reward models. Open and proprietary VLMs were evaluated, and none excelled across tasks. LLM-as-a-Verifier later reported state of the art on it.

name: RoboSpatial-Home
description: Models answer 350 spatial questions on home scenes for robots, in three types: object context, compatibility of placements and spatial configuration.
org: NVIDIA and The Ohio State University
note: The test set of the RoboSpatial paper (CVPR 2025). Some answers are 2D points, others yes or no.

name: Robot Capabilities Index (Robocurve)
description: An index fitted like Epoch ECI over five RoboDojo-RC Tier 1 tasks run by frontier LLMs on real YAM arms. Anchored at GPT-5.6 Sol minus 3 and GPT-6 Astra plus 3.
note: Pilot published 2026-10-15 with 9 frontier models and 1,055 trials. Gemini models score higher than their ECI predicts. RCI tracks Blueprint-Bench 2 best (r = 0.85).

name: Robotic Origami Challenge (IROS 2026)
description: Fold a six-fold paper airplane on a supplied bimanual Sharpa-hand rig. Origami judges give pass/fail, and passes are ranked by folding time.
org: Sharpa + BitRobot/FrodoBots + Nippon Origami Association + partners
note: Single task. Quality is binary and only speed is graded, with a 10-minute cap. Organizers supply the hardware and an outside judge, so teams bring policies only. No results page found after the 27 Sep-1 Oct 2026 event.

name: RoboTwin 1.0
description: Dual-arm policies train on generated digital-twin demos and are tested on simulated single-arm and dual-arm tasks, with matching real-world data. Success rate.
note: Early version won an ECCV 2024 workshop best paper (arXiv 2409.02920). Full paper was a CVPR 2025 highlight. Used for the CVPR 2025 MEIS dual-arm challenge. Replaced by RoboTwin 2.0 in June 2025.

name: RoboTwin 2.0
description: Bimanual Aloha-AgileX sim: 50 tasks, policies trained on 50 clean demos per task, 100 trials each in clean and domain-randomized scenes.
note: Official board: team retrained 17 of 22 entries via XPolicyLab. The clean track is crowded. Randomized scores are lower. Self-reported paper numbers (~86-94%, larger demo budget) are saturated and not comparable.

name: RobotWorld
description: Multimodal agents control robots through robot interfaces in simulation. Its 84 tasks span manipulation, mobile manipulation, locomotion, driving and aerial control, with executable success checks.
note: It had 39 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 49 GitHub stars.

name: RoboWorld
description: Coding agents control simulated robots through an HTTP API to do physical jobs such as welding, sewing, pouring and forklift driving. Each simulation checks the task and returns a reward from 0 to 1.
org: Carnegie Mellon University (Welleck lab, CMU L3)
note: 25 simulations chosen by US GDP share, with 25 test and 175 training environments. Coding agents built and audited each simulation. Best frontier models averaged a reward of 0.06 and failed every test task.

name: Robust IF Bench
description: Models follow a diverse set of hard instructions from Microsoft AI's internal benchmark.
note: In-house: Microsoft AI never released the tasks or the scoring method.

name: robust-kbench
description: Agents write CUDA kernels that are tested across several weight initializations and input shapes, so shape and magnitude exploits fail. Correctness checks and profiling score each kernel.
note: The maker built it because models could exploit existing kernel benchmarks through input shapes and weight magnitudes.

name: ROK-FORTRESS
description: Models face adversarial national security and public safety prompts in English and Korean, set in US or Korean contexts. Each prompt has a benign pair to measure over-refusal.
note: A Korean transcreation of Scale AI's FORTRESS. LLM judge panels score prompt-specific binary rubrics.

name: Role-play Benchmark (MiniMax)
description: Role-play agents are tested on situated reenactment in Chinese and English scenes. Grading targets the immersive experience rather than a verifiable answer.
note: About 160 likes on Hugging Face.

name: RoleBench
description: Models answer prompts while playing one of many fixed characters from films and books. Answers are compared with reference role answers by automatic text overlap.
note: Part of the RoleLLM paper. NVIDIA reports it without reasoning mode in the Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B card.

name: RoleMRC
description: Models play given roles in multi-turn chats, passage reading tasks and nested or prioritized instructions. The test split has 1.4k samples.
note: The repo also ships 37.9k synthetic role-playing training instructions. The scoring type is not stated on the repo page.

name: Room-Across-Room (RxR)
description: Agents follow navigation instructions through photo-realistic indoor scenes to reach a goal. The instructions are in English, Hindi and Telugu, and each word is time-aligned to the annotator's position. Scores include success rate and how closely the path follows the reference route.
note: BenchmarkList links an unrelated paper (arXiv 2103.11372). The RxR paper is arXiv 2010.07954. Most results come from vision-and-language navigation models, not general-purpose models. About 190 GitHub stars, and the repo was last pushed in 2023-07.

name: RoTA-Bench
description: Vision-language models rotate a 3D object step by step, using visual feedback, until its projection matches a target silhouette.
note: 73 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: RSI Arena
description: Ten frontier agents each post-train the same Nemotron base model on a shared GPU cluster for six days. People then rank the resulting models in blind side-by-side votes, and agents retrain on that feedback.
note: Run live at COLM 2026. Each agent had 1,000 GPU-hours and $300 of API credit. Stage 1 Human Arena drew 1,685 votes. Models are also scored on 20 benchmarks. Checkpoints and data are promised.

name: RSI Bench
description: Agents get a starting environment, a GPU budget and a verifier suite for an AI R&D task such as data curation or post-training. The score is mean reward per task, averaged across tasks.
note: Announced 2026-08-07. Tasks run on Harbor with Modal GPUs. Four sample tasks are public. The leaderboard lists 8 models.

name: RSI Index (OpenAI)
description: An aggregate of OpenAI's internal evaluations of progress toward recursive self-improvement. The parts are real AI research tasks such as debugging research systems, optimizing kernels and training recipes, and improving another model.
note: The GPT-5.6 post reports Sol 57.9% against GPT-5.5 41.7%. Its table lists Internal Research Debugging, KernelGen 1P, NanoGPT and PostTrainBench Lite beside it. Do not confuse it with the Vals RSI Index.

name: RSI-Exam
description: Agents get a weak method on a long research task and must turn it into one that scores better on hidden data. It measures recursive self-improvement on executable research.
note: 35 public tasks with grading containers and 53 held back. Runs on Harbor with a sealed network policy. About 190 GitHub stars.

name: RSIBench-Data
description: Coding agents act as data-centric researchers. With a fixed Tinker post-training stack and budget, they refine training data from dev-benchmark feedback, and the final model is scored on held-out test benchmarks.
org: Evolvent AI + National University of Singapore
note: Evaluation runs through Harbor and E2B sandboxes. The headline is a weighted score over six test benchmarks. Not the Scale AI RSI Bench or the 300-task counterfactual RSIBench on Hugging Face. Repo has 179 stars.

name: RTE
description: Models decide whether a premise sentence entails a hypothesis, using data from the PASCAL RTE challenges. Scored by accuracy.
org: PASCAL RTE Challenge organizers, packaged in GLUE

name: RTEB
description: Embedding models retrieve documents on open and private datasets across 20 languages and domains such as law, healthcare, code and finance. Scored by NDCG@10.
org: MTEB community and Hugging Face (with MongoDB)
note: MTEB maintainers run the private sets and publish only statistics and samples, so a drop from open to private scores flags overfitting. Shown as the Retrieval section of the MTEB board.

name: RTP-LX
description: Models continue or judge toxic prompts hand-translated from RealToxicityPrompts into dozens of languages, with native-speaker labels. Measures toxic output and toxicity detection.
note: AAAI 2025. The paper covers 28 languages and the repo now lists 38. Microsoft reported Phi-3.5 results on it in its Phi-3 safety post-training paper.

name: RTVLM
description: Vision language models answer red-teaming image prompts on faithfulness, privacy, safety and fairness. GPT-4V scores responses from 0 to 10.
org: Li et al. (HKU, Peking University and others)

name: RULER
description: Synthetic retrieval, multi-hop tracing, aggregation and QA tasks at configurable lengths. Measures effective context size.
note: Synthetic. Near-saturated for frontier models at 128K.

name: RULERv2
description: Models solve synthetic multi-key and multi-value needle tasks and QA tasks at basic, easy, medium and hard levels. Contexts run from 8K to 1M tokens, and accuracy is averaged across lengths.
note: Runs through NVIDIA NeMo-Skills as the ruler2 benchmark, and the RULER README now points users to it. No paper and no lab report found yet. Tasks differ from RULER, so scores are not comparable.

name: RuleTrek
description: Agents must find and correctly apply domain-specific rules when the scenario's facts are spread across many files, unlike rule benchmarks built from a few statements.
note: 73 HF paper upvotes in its first weeks.

name: RuneBench
description: Coding agents play RuneScape on an emulated game server by writing TypeScript against the rs-sdk library, with game-wiki notes for reference. Tasks train one skill or gather gold within 15 or 30 minutes. Skill tasks are scored by the peak XP rate in any 15-second window, and a verifier reads the final game state.
org: Websim (Max Bittker, Surya Narreddi, Rob Haisfield, Sean Lee)
note: Built on Harbor and the LostCity engine. The suite has 16 skill tasks at each of two lengths and 8 gold tasks. The authors switched from total XP to peak XP rate because total XP rewarded simple grinding. They also warn that small samples make model gaps noisy. About 171 GitHub stars.

name: RWE-bench
description: Agents do mechanical, electrical and aerospace design tasks, such as a crankshaft, dense PCB routing or turbine-vane cooling, with CAD and CAE tools. A deterministic verifier runs physics solvers and passes a design only if it meets every requirement.
note: Engineers on the team wrote each task with its verifier and a reference solution. Each model runs in its native harness at max effort. The tasks are never licensed for training. Launch coverage reports 20 tasks and 11 models, with GPT-6 Astra at 37%.

name: RWSearch
description: Agents search the live web to answer 200 expert-written Chinese questions that need many retrieval steps, filtering and arithmetic. Each question has one objective answer.
note: 60 percent of the questions use facts from 2025. The README leaderboard lists LongCat-Flash-Thinking-2601 at 79.5.

name: S3Gym
description: Models try to improve themselves through self-testing, self-judging and self-improvement in seven text-based games with executable verifiers. Held-out evaluation is kept strict.
note: 43 HF paper upvotes.

name: SaaS-Bench
description: 106 long-horizon GUI workflows across 23 locally deployed real SaaS apps. Scored from app databases with weighted checkpoints and full-resolution rate.
note: The best agent fully completed under 4% of tasks at launch. Release v1.1 on 2026-10-02 kept the 106 tasks, fixed verifiers and task text, and added native agent harnesses. The v1.1 board reports Resolved Score.

name: Safe response to high-severity prompts
aliases: Challenging conversations with implicit harmful intent
description: Models handle multi-turn self-harm and violent activity conversations where harmful intent only emerges from context. Scored as safe response rate.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Reported per category, with and without system-level safety context.

name: SAFE-Teen
aliases: Scenario-based Assessment of Failure Emergence in Teen Chats
description: Chatbots hold 6 to 20 turn chats with a simulated teen across 106 clinician-written scenarios, branching on how the teen reacts. A judge rates safety checks and reports the failure rate.
note: Risk areas are urgent safety, health advice and relationship boundaries. Claude Sonnet 5.5 is the judge. Vals tested 17 setups including consumer app defaults.

name: SAFE-Teen Health advice
description: Models respond to simulated teens in health advice scenarios. The score is the published conversation failure rate.
note: One track of SAFE-Teen. The SAFE-Teen record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: SAFE-Teen Relationship boundaries
description: Models respond to simulated teens in relationship boundary scenarios. The score is the published conversation failure rate.
note: One track of SAFE-Teen. The SAFE-Teen record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: SAFE-Teen Urgent safety
description: Models respond to simulated teens in urgent safety scenarios. The score is the published conversation failure rate.
note: One track of SAFE-Teen. The SAFE-Teen record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: SafeLIBERO
description: VLA policies run 16 LIBERO tasks with an added obstacle at two levels, near the target or in the path. 50 episodes per scenario. Scored by collision avoidance and task success.
note: Introduced with the AEGIS safety layer and released 2025-12-20. At least five 2026 papers report it, often with different metrics or dropped tasks, so scores rarely line up.

name: Safety (MiniMax in-house)
description: Models respond to safety-relevant user prompts. MiniMax scores whether replies are safe and helpful.
note: In-house MiniMax evaluation built mostly from Hailuo AI user queries in Mandarin. The queries are not public.

name: Safety mode controllability (Cohere)
description: Models follow contextual or strict safety instructions. Accuracy averages correct answers on an over-refusal set and correct refusals on a control set.
note: In-house Cohere evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: SafetyBench
description: Models answer 11,435 multiple choice questions on seven safety topics in Chinese and English, such as ethics, illegal activities and privacy.
note: Tsinghua CoAI benchmark, ACL 2024. Test answers were open-sourced in July 2025.

name: SAGE (Vals)
description: Models grade handwritten undergraduate work in PDEs, linear algebra and computer science against rubrics. Scores compare their deductions with expert graders.
note: v1 scored the share of submissions where every rubric check was right, which rewarded graders that never deduct. Board frozen 2026-10-08 with 56 models.

name: SAGE v1.1 (Vals)
description: Models grade handwritten undergraduate math and computer science work against rubrics. Scored by class-balanced accuracy of each rubric check against expert grading.
note: Vals changed the metric from v1, which moved strict graders up and lenient ones down. 545 tests in five suites. The board had 28 models on 2026-10-27.

name: Sakana kana-letter reading-order set
description: Model recovers the reading order of 25 expert-annotated classical Japanese kana letters (chirashigaki). Scored by normalized edit distance.
note: Lab-created in-house eval (Sakana AI). Built because no public benchmark existed. No release link.

name: SALAD-Bench
description: Models answer harmful questions organized in a three-level taxonomy, some with attack or defense changes and some multiple-choice. The MD-Judge evaluator labels responses as safe or unsafe.
note: ACL 2024 Findings paper.

name: Sandbox Bench
description: Agents find and exploit vulnerabilities in runtimes, file format parsers and egress proxies across 22 challenges. Success means recovering the protected flag.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Most targets are undisclosed zero days.

name: Sandbox escape evaluation (Anthropic)
description: Agents face 28 handmade scenarios that tempt them to cross a staged sandbox boundary. Score is the share of runs with a crossing attempt.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: SArena
description: Models understand, edit and generate SVG graphics in domains such as icons, illustrations and chemistry diagrams. Generation is scored by comparing rendered output with references.
org: Shanghai Jiao Tong University, Shanghai AI Laboratory and others (InternSVG team)
note: Released with the InternSVG model and the SAgoge dataset. Labs report the Icon subset.

name: SAT (Spatial Aptitude Training)
description: Models answer static and dynamic spatial questions, such as how object relations change when the camera or an object moves. The real-image test set has 150 questions.
org: Boston University, Allen Institute for AI and University of Washington (Ray et al.)
note: The release also has 175K simulated training questions. COLM 2025 paper. Microsoft's Mage-VL card reports it as SAT.

name: SAT Evidence-Based Reading & Writing
description: Models take the SAT reading and writing section. Scored on the 200 to 800 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: SAT Math
description: Models take the SAT math section. Scored on the 200 to 800 scale.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: SAT Reading
description: Models answer the reading section of official SAT practice tests. Scored as accuracy.
note: Llama 3 averages 8 exams from the 2018 Official SAT Study Guide. This is reading only, not EBRW.

name: SAVE-Bench
description: A coding agent works where the environment or the user instruction carries hidden risk. The benchmark scores whether it surfaces the risk to the user.
note: In-house Meta benchmark with a multi-turn tier. An LLM judge scores harmful execution and risk verbalization.

name: ScanBench
description: Models act as doctors in 303 simulated clinical cases from 12 departments. They take a history, order lab tests and give a final diagnosis, scored per stage.
note: The paper calls it OSCE-like and says the data will be open-sourced. Scores are given for Clinical Inquiry, Laboratory Testing and Diagnosis, with a human doctor baseline. Grader type not checked.

name: ScarfBench
description: Agents migrate enterprise Java applications from one framework to another while keeping behavior the same. Build config, dependency injection, persistence and deployment all change.
note: Kaggle board published 2026-10-26 with no models yet.

name: scBench (LatchBio SingleCellBench)
description: 195 verifiable single-cell RNA-seq analysis problems. Each pairs a data snapshot with a task and a deterministic grader.
note: Anthropic system cards call it LatchBio SingleCellBench with 195 problems, which matches the 195 problems in latchbio/scbench. Only six example problems are public, and the rest are withheld.

name: scBench-Long
description: Agents run long single-cell RNA-seq analyses that need sustained empirical work and biological reasoning.
note: Part of LatchBio's BioBench suite on benchmarks.bio. The V1 set has 22 evaluations. Release month is the GitHub repo creation month.

name: ScholarCatalyst
description: Given a research question, retrieve the 'catalyst papers' that 184 lead authors labeled for 207 projects, searching only prior literature. Recall@20.
note: Far from saturated: best Recall@20 about 0.5.

name: SciArena
description: Researchers ask scientific literature questions and vote between two models' long cited answers. Votes give Elo ratings.
org: Yale NLP and Allen Institute for AI
note: At launch it had 23 models and over 13,000 votes from vetted researchers. A SciArena-Eval split tests model judges.

name: SciBench
description: Models solve open-ended college-level problems in mathematics, chemistry and physics. Most answers are numbers, which a script checks against the key.
note: The paper also sorts model errors into ten problem-solving skills through a user study. About 140 GitHub stars, and the repo was last pushed in 2024-07.

name: SciCode
description: Scientist-curated research coding problems split into subproblems across natural sciences. Code checked against test cases.

changes.text: The SciCode maintainers added scientist-written background and an evaluation setting that supplies it. Scores from this setting measure performance with extra scientific guidance and differ from scores without that guidance.

note: Mistral cites 'SciCode-Verified' (pass@1, n=6). Kimi uses Artificial Analysis numbers. Test-set answers partly held out.

name: Science's Last Exam
description: Agents conduct scientific research through tools, code, desktop software, laboratory recordings, and withheld references across 113 tasks in nine disciplines. The official composite equally averages six assessment scores on a zero-to-100 scale. Checks combine reference comparisons, executable tests, and literature audits.
org: AItonomy Foundation and the SLE team
note: AItonomy requires separate approval for hidden reference data. The composite includes the current zero scores for end-to-end research but excludes wet-lab execution, which has no released tasks. The board averages cost and time over four capabilities only. Models lacking an assessment receive no composite.

name: ScienceAgentBench
description: Agents write programs for 102 data-driven discovery tasks from 44 papers in four disciplines. Outputs are checked by execution and task-specific metrics.
note: ICLR 2025. Nine subject experts validated the tasks.

name: ScienceBoard
description: Computer-use agents do scientific workflows in desktop software such as ChimeraX, Celestia, GRASS GIS and Lean 4. The apps are modified to expose state for checking.
org: OS-Copilot team (Shanghai AI Laboratory and HKU)
note: 104 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: ScienceQA
description: Models answer about 21,000 multiple-choice science questions from school curricula, many with images. Scored by accuracy.
org: UCLA and Allen Institute for AI
note: Top systems score above 90 percent, so it is near saturation.

name: ScienceVision
description: Agents inspect 3D scientific data such as proteins, crystals, CAD assemblies, buildings and CT volumes, then answer 250 expert questions. A rule-based scorer grades each answer field.
note: Three settings: source files with code, source files plus an inspection MCP, and rendered 2D views only. Scores are mean answer_score from 0 to 1.

name: ScienceWorld
description: Agents carry out elementary-school science tasks, such as measuring conductivity or growing plants, by acting in an interactive text environment. Each task scores progress toward its goal.
org: Allen Institute for AI (Wang, Jansen, Côté, Ammanabrolu)
note: EMNLP 2022. Widely used with ALFWorld in agent papers. Repo has 401 stars.

name: Scientists' First Exam (SFE)
description: Models answer 830 expert-verified visual questions on scientific data across signal perception, attribute understanding and comparative reasoning.
org: Shanghai AI Lab (Yuhao Zhou et al.)

name: SciPredict
description: Models predict the outcomes of 405 real physics, biology and chemistry experiments published after March 31, 2025, with and without expert background knowledge.
note: Also measures calibration. The repo paper link was still a placeholder on 2026-11-01.

name: SciQ
description: Models answer crowdsourced multiple-choice science exam questions in physics, chemistry and biology, each with a supporting passage.
org: Allen Institute for AI (Welbl et al.)
note: Often reported for small and open base models in pretraining suites.

name: SciReasoner evaluation suite
description: Models perform scientific sequence and text tasks such as format translation, extraction, property prediction and molecule design, drawn from up to 103 tasks.
note: The Intern-S2 card lists SciReasoner 1.5 as a molecular structure reasoning benchmark. The SciReasoner paper is a model paper, so which test set the card means is unclear.

name: SciTS
aliases: Scientific Time Series Understanding and Generation
description: Models understand and generate scientific time series in 43 tasks across 12 domains. Signals range from one to ten million points. Each task uses its own metric.
org: Shanghai AI Laboratory, Tsinghua University and others
note: The paper benchmarks 17 models and was accepted to ICLR 2026. Shanghai AI Lab reports per task F1 on a subset in the Intern-S1-Pro report.

name: SciUniverse
description: 92 tasks in 17 chemistry, biology and materials families run in C5R's lab or its digital twin. Pass@1 averaged equally across families.
note: Level 1. 8 families run in the real lab, so results are noisier. Model evaluation by contacting C5R.

name: SCONE-bench
description: Agents find and exploit vulnerabilities in real smart contracts on a local blockchain fork. Success is measured in simulated dollars stolen, not only pass or fail.
note: 405 historical contracts at launch, later 417. A post-cutoff set of 12 incidents from 2026 was added in May 2026.

name: ScreenSpot
description: Model locates a described UI element in mobile, desktop and web screenshots. Scored by click-point accuracy.
note: Largely superseded by ScreenSpot-Pro for frontier comparisons.

name: ScreenSpot-Pro
description: GUI grounding on high-resolution professional-software screenshots. The model must locate the target UI element.
note: Astra score known only from secondary write-ups of OpenAI launch materials.

name: ScreenSpot-v2
description: Models locate a described element on mobile, desktop and web screenshots. A click inside the target box counts as correct.
org: OS-Atlas team (Shanghai AI Lab and others)
note: Released with OS-Atlas as a relabeled ScreenSpot that fixes wrong annotations, so scores differ from the original.

name: SCROLLS
aliases: Standardized CompaRison Over Long Language Sequences
description: Models do seven long-text tasks such as summarization, question answering and natural language inference over naturally long documents.
note: ZeroSCROLLS, a zero-shot follow-up, is a separate test.

name: SEA-HELM
aliases: Southeast Asian Holistic Evaluation of Language Models
description: Models are evaluated in Filipino, Indonesian, Tamil, Thai and Vietnamese across five pillars: NLP classics, LLM-specific tasks, linguistics, culture and safety.
note: HELM releases v1.0.0 (2025-03-17) to v1.2.0 (2025-04-18). AI Singapore also keeps its own SEA-HELM board.

name: SEAL Adversarial Robustness
description: Models receive 1,000 single-turn adversarial prompts written by 10 full-time red teamers across nine harm categories. Safety specialists grade responses, and models are ranked by the number of high-harm violations.
note: The board existed by 2024-08. Scale marked it deprecated in 2025-01 with 8 models. Gemini 1.5 Pro had the fewest violations at 8 and GPT-4o the most at 67.

name: SEAL Coding
description: Models answer 1,000 private coding prompts across common languages and tasks. Human annotators rate adherence, correctness, efficiency and readability, then compare responses side by side to produce Elo-style scores.
note: One of the four launch SEAL boards. Contributors could not use public code or questions. Scale marked it deprecated in 2025-03 with 28 models.

name: SEAL Multilingual
description: Models answer 1,000 private prompts per language, written by native speakers on general and cultural topics. Annotators rate each answer and compare pairs side by side, and boards rank models by Elo.
note: Spanish was a launch board covering Spain, Mexico and Latin America. Japanese, Chinese, Arabic and Korean boards followed. Scale marked Spanish deprecated in 2025-03 with 22 models.

name: SEAL Precise Instruction Following
aliases: Scale AI Precise Instruction Following Prompts Dataset
description: Models answer 1,054 private prompts with detailed instructions in nine categories. Human annotators check 12 yes or no criteria and compare responses side by side on a 7-point scale.
note: One of the four launch SEAL boards. Each model was paired with every other at least 50 times. Scale marked it deprecated in 2025-01 with 19 models.

name: SEAL Showdown
description: Users of Scale's Playground app chat with a model and sometimes compare its reply with a random opponent's reply. Scale ranks models with a Bradley-Terry model that controls for length and formatting. Rankings can be split by region, profession and age.
note: Votes come from contributors in more than 100 countries. On 2025-09-20 GPT-5 Chat ranked first, then Claude Opus 4.1. Scale withholds preference data for 60 days after collection.

name: Seal-0
description: Models answer 111 fact-seeking questions where web search returns conflicting or unhelpful results. Answers are graded for accuracy, usually with search enabled.
note: The makers refresh the answers about monthly (about 20 dated updates from 2025-07 to 2026-09) and keep old versions on Google Drive. Scores need the version date to compare.

name: Search triggering
description: Models decide whether to call search for queries that need fresh facts or answer directly when search is unneeded. Reports F1.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: SEC-bench
description: Code agents work on real OSS-Fuzz vulnerabilities in containerized repositories. They either write a proof-of-concept input that reproduces the crash or patch the code so the crash stops.
org: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (Lingming Zhang) + Purdue
note: NeurIPS 2025. A multi-agent pipeline builds the instances at about $0.87 each. Best agents reached 18.0% on PoC generation and 34.0% on patching. SEC-bench Pro is a separate, harder benchmark from the same group.

name: SEC-bench Pro
description: Agents hunt and reproduce security bugs in large software projects from limited information. The first release covers V8 and SpiderMonkey.
note: The 260505 snapshot of 5 May 2026 holds 103 V8 and 80 SpiderMonkey instances, 183 in all. A later 260617 snapshot adds Linux and more SpiderMonkey, reaching 344. The maker calls the benchmark self-evolving.

name: SEC-bench Pro 260617
description: Agents hunt security bugs in large software projects. This snapshot adds Linux kernel instances and more SpiderMonkey instances to the first release.
org: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign (Lingming Zhang) and University of Melbourne
note: 344 instances: 103 V8, 104 SpiderMonkey and 137 Linux. Dated 17 June 2026 and the board default. The maker calls SEC-bench Pro self-evolving and lets readers switch snapshots. The earlier 260505 snapshot had 183 instances.

name: SecCodeBench
description: Models write or patch functions in project scaffolds drawn from real Alibaba vulnerabilities. Code must pass functional tests, then proof-of-concept security tests.
org: Alibaba Group (with Tsinghua, Zhejiang, Fudan, and Peking universities)
note: 98 test cases over 22 CWE types in five languages: Java 53, C and C++ 15, Python 13, Go 13 and Node.js 4. Each case runs in four modes, code generation and code fix, each native and security aware. Apache 2.0. The repo states it is no longer actively maintained and development continues as the Last Secure Code Benchmark.

name: SecIT Bench
description: Agents investigate incidents from telemetry captured on real infrastructure, including intrusions, data egress and outages. Three LLM judges grade root-cause reports against diagnostic conditions.
note: 30 investigations, some deliberately benign. Joined the Fireworks index on 2026-10-28 with 17 models.

name: SecQA
description: Models answer multiple-choice computer security questions at two difficulty levels. Questions come from a security textbook and were checked by people.
note: Two datasets, v1 and v2, give two levels of difficulty. The inspect_evals harness runs each zero-shot and five-shot. Questions were drafted by GPT-4 from the textbook Computer Systems Security: Planning for Success.

name: SecretPatch
description: Models decide whether commits are security patches, including silently released ones, from a set of 4,702 security patches.
note: Dataset from a DSN 2019 paper on secret security patches. Google reports accuracy.

name: Secure and defensive coding (Anthropic)
aliases: Production secure coding sessions, classifier flag rate
description: Cyber safeguard classifiers screen sampled defensive coding sessions such as patching and incident response. Score is the classifier flag rate.
note: Measures false positives of the deployed classifier system on benign cyber work. An LLM grader labels sessions as purely defensive.

name: SecureBio VMQA, single choice
description: Models answer 350 virology troubleshooting questions in single-choice form. VMQA is an earlier version of the Virology Capabilities Test.
note: Google FSF sections report it with N=350. The Gemini 3 Pro FSF report calls the same N=350 set SecureBio VCT SC.

name: SecureCodeReview (xAI)
description: Internal agentic eval: fix the security issues in a realistic codebase without introducing new ones.

name: SEED-Bench
description: Models answer 19,000 human-annotated multiple-choice questions over 12 dimensions of image and video understanding. Scored by accuracy against the answer key.
org: Tencent AI Lab and ARC Lab (Li et al.)
note: Many papers report only the image dimensions. Later SEED-Bench-2 and SEED-Bench-2-Plus are separate tests.

name: SEED-Bench-2
description: Multimodal models answer multiple-choice questions that cover comprehension of interleaved image and text inputs and image generation, in hierarchical capability levels.
note: Adds interleaved and generation tasks, so scores do not compare with SEED-Bench.

name: SEED-Bench-2-Plus
description: Multimodal models answer multiple-choice questions about text-rich images such as charts, maps and web pages.
note: A text-rich companion to SEED-Bench-2, not a replacement.

name: Seed-TTS-eval
description: Models clone a voice from a short prompt and speak new text in English and Mandarin. Scored by word error rate from an ASR model and by speaker similarity.
note: Uses 1,000 Common Voice samples for English and 2,000 DiDiSpeech-2 samples for Mandarin, plus a hard Mandarin set. Repo has about 1,600 GitHub stars.

name: Seed1.5-VL internal benchmark (ByteDance Seed in-house)
description: Models answer more than 12,000 internal image questions over 100 tasks, from perception, OCR and STEM to agents, code and out-of-distribution puzzles. LLM judges grade answers, and the overall is a weighted average.
note: In-house ByteDance Seed evaluation. The tasks are not public. Many tasks are in Chinese, and the task set is refreshed over time.

name: SeedClawBench
description: Agents complete 100 OpenClaw-style user tasks built from Ark usage logs and crowdsourced tasks, such as data analysis and office work. An agent judge checks rubric items against the trace and deliverables.
note: In-house Seed benchmark. The card reports 89.69% agreement between the agent judge and humans on 262 rubric items. The launch blog calls it ClawBench.

name: SeedKernelBench
description: Models write or optimize CUDA style kernels for operator tasks mined from FlashInfer, SGLang, FlashAttention, DeepGEMM, CUTLASS and cuDNN. Scored as average speedup over reference code.
note: In-house ByteDance Seed evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Select machine learning engineering tasks from METR
description: Agents attempt machine learning engineering tasks drawn from METR. Scored as successful trials.
note: OpenAI ran these tasks for the GPT-4o Preparedness autonomy assessment.

name: Self-harm refusals (xAI)
description: Models face self-harm and crisis prompts and conversations. A model fails if it assists or refuses without pointing to help.
note: In-house xAI evaluation. The metric is compliance on should-refuse conversations.

name: Self-preference bias (Anthropic)
description: Models grade transcripts attributed to themselves or to other models. Measures whether scores favor the model's own outputs.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Self-proliferation challenges (Phuong et al. 2024)
description: Agents try 10 end-to-end tasks such as installing a wallet or deploying a model on a cloud server, with 45 milestone substeps.
note: Reports give challenges passed end to end, milestones passed and expert bits needed.

name: SemComp-Bench
description: Video generation models must complete an intended task outcome from a reference image while keeping the high-level semantics of the reference.
note: 51 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: Senior SWE-Bench
description: Agents build features and fix runtime bugs in real open-source repos from loose, natural instructions. Behavioral tests and codebase quality metrics give a tasteful solve rate.
note: 100 tasks, 50 public. The leaderboard lists 23 models and reports tasteful solves. Launched 2026-06-30.

name: SEvenLLM
description: Models analyze cyber security incidents and write responses. Tasks split into understanding and generation over 28 subcategories, in Chinese and English.
note: The harness runs four task sets: multiple choice and open question answering, each in Chinese and English.

name: Sexually Explicit Content Safety
description: An autorater checks answers to direct, adversarial and benign sexual content prompts in single and multi-turn chats. Reports safe response rate.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: SGI-Bench
description: Models work through more than 1,000 expert samples in four scientist tasks: deep research, idea generation, dry and wet experiments, and experimental reasoning.
org: Shanghai AI Lab and partners (Wanghan Xu et al.)
note: Tasks follow the Practical Inquiry Model and Science magazine 125 Big Questions.

name: SGP-Bench
description: Models read symbolic graphics programs such as SVG and CAD code and answer questions about what the rendered image would show, without seeing the image.
org: Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems and others (Zeju Qiu, Weiyang Liu et al.)
note: The benchmark is built procedurally.

name: SHADE-Arena
description: Paired main and hidden side tasks in mock environments. Measures if an agent completes the side task undetected by a monitor.
org: Anthropic + Scale AI + Redwood (Kutasov et al.)
note: Opus 5.5 recognizes it as an evaluation in over 80% of attempts. safety-research/SHADE-Arena is deprecated.

name: ShadowBench
description: Models pose two 3D hands between a lamp and a screen, one tool call at a time, until their shadow matches one of 20 hand-shadow plates from books of 1859 to about 1900. The environment refuses any pose real hands can't make. Score, out of 100, mixes the overlap with the target and how closely the outlines match.
note: Each model ran once per plate and effort, so small differences are not resolved. No model solved a plate. A featureless blob, the convex hull of each target, scores 56.9, above every model's average, and blind search over the pose scores 36.2. Models rarely hold the hands together, as the books do. Six models from two labs were tested, with no human baseline yet.

name: SheetBench
description: Agents solve finance and accounting spreadsheet tasks through a browser in a fresh Google Sheet. The score is the share of expected answer cells that match exactly.
note: 50 tasks with up to 200 model turns per attempt. 8 models in the Fireworks index. Release date not confirmed on a HUD page.

name: Short Form Bench
description: Agents act as growth lead of a small brand for a simulated week. They post short videos, run the store and answer customers, sponsors and the founder.
note: Some simulated parties make mistakes in the brand's favor to test honesty. Scored by business value in US dollars. 9 models in the Fireworks index.

name: Short-horizon computational biology tasks
description: Agents perform end-to-end computational tasks related to modifying and engineering biological agents.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: SHP2 Protein Function Prediction
description: Models predict held-out assay measurements for single amino acid variants of SHP2. Scored as mean R squared over three assay datasets.
note: OpenAI Critical bio capability evaluation. The Critical threshold is 0.60.

name: SIFo
description: Models follow a chain of dependent instructions, where each step uses the output of the one before. Only the final answer is checked, across 800 samples in four tasks.
org: University of Amsterdam and University of Groningen (Chen et al.)
note: Tasks are text modification, question answering, mathematics and security rules. Qwen also reports a SIFO-multiturn variant it does not define.

name: Silent copying of answers (Anthropic)
aliases: Undisclosed use of an available answer
description: Agents solve held-out coding tasks where the answer is reachable in the sandbox. Score is the rate of using it without telling the user.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: SimpleBench
description: Models answer over 200 multiple-choice trick questions on spatial, temporal, and social reasoning that ordinary people solve. Scored by average accuracy over five runs.
note: The human baseline from nine non-expert people is 83.7 percent. A small open-ended variant lists three models.

name: SimpleQA
description: Models answer 4,326 short fact questions that each have one indisputable answer. A grader model marks each reply correct, incorrect, or not attempted.
note: Google DeepMind released SimpleQA Verified, a cleaned 1,000 question subset, because the original has label errors and duplicates.

name: SimpleQA Hallucination Rate
description: Models answer 4,326 short fact-seeking questions. This metric is the share of questions answered incorrectly, so declining to answer is not penalized.
note: Google DeepMind later released SimpleQA Verified, a cleaned 1,000-question version.

name: SimpleQA Verified
description: 1,000 human-verified, de-duplicated short-answer factual questions measuring parametric knowledge.
note: Google fixed one dataset error on 2026-03-09 and posted paper v2 on 2026-03-10. Scores stay comparable, so it remains one record.

name: SimplerEnv
description: Real-to-sim replicas of Google Robot and WidowX/Bridge setups. Policies scored by success rate on pick, move, drawer and Bridge tasks.
org: UC San Diego + Stanford + UC Berkeley + Google DeepMind
note: Self-reported under mixed zero-shot and fine-tuned protocols. Papers quote conflicting baselines. The WidowX track is near ceiling. Google Robot tracks still separate models.

name: SimpleSafetyTests
description: Models answer 100 clearly harmful prompts on illegal items, physical harm, scams, child abuse and self-harm. The score is the share of safe responses.
note: HELM Safety reports it as a safety score.

name: SimpleVQA
description: Models answer 2,025 short factual questions about images across 9 tasks and 9 topics. An LLM judge grades answers against fixed references.

name: Simreal ML Benchmark
description: ML research agents study a dataset, build a model and submit predictions on 60 tasks in tabular, forecasting, vision, language, audio and multimodal learning. Competition platforms score them.
note: Public preview. Test labels stay with the competition platform, and briefs hide the source. About 270 GitHub stars.

name: SimRepairBench
description: Agents find and repair modeling errors in 3D OpenUSD assets for robot simulation, from 25 damaged objects in NVIDIA's SimReady collection, with partial credit from verifiers.
note: Release 0.4.13 on Harbor Hub holds the 25 CASTAIGNE25 tasks. Each task gives a damaged model, a repair brief and an image, and a separate verifier scores the repair from 0 to 1. Source objects are CC BY 4.0, the code is MIT.

name: SimuVerity
description: Agents build executable Simulink models from text for 101 tasks in ten engineering domains. Simulations check that each model meets its engineering requirements.
note: It had 36 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 21 GitHub stars.

name: Single-turn benign request evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Models answer benign requests on sensitive topics. Score is the refusal rate, where lower is better.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Single-turn harmful request evaluations (Anthropic)
description: Models answer single-turn requests that violate the usage policy. Score is the harmless response rate.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: SIQA
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions about people's motives, reactions, and emotions in everyday social situations. Scored by accuracy.
org: Allen Institute for AI and University of Washington
note: Test labels are hidden, so model cards usually report the dev set.

name: SITE
description: Models answer multiple-choice spatial questions over single images, multiple images and video, drawn from about 30 vision datasets. Tasks span figural to environmental scale.
note: Accepted at ICCV 2025. Some later papers report a chance-adjusted accuracy.

name: Situational Awareness Dataset (SAD)
description: 16 tasks measuring whether models know facts about themselves and their situation.

name: SkateBench v2
description: Models name skateboard tricks from technical trick definitions. The score is the share named correctly.
note: 390 trick definitions, private after v1 saturated. The board lists 28 models but stopped near Gemini 3.1 Pro (97%), so current models are missing. Release month comes from secondary reports of the maker's post.

name: SkillInject
description: Agents use a skill file that carries an adversarial instruction while doing a legitimate task. Reports how often the agent follows the injection.
note: Measures agent vulnerability to skill file attacks.

name: SkillsBench
description: 86-87 containerized expert tasks in 11 domains, run with and without Agent Skills. Verifier tests give pass rate and skill lift.
note: Paired runs with and without skills isolate the effect of skills. SkillsBench 1.1 (June 2026) pins 87 tasks in 8 domains, up from 86 in the first paper version. The task set is the same as v1.0.

name: SLAKE
description: Models answer English and Chinese questions about radiology images of the head, neck, chest, abdomen, and pelvis. Scoring is accuracy.
org: Hong Kong Polytechnic University (Xiao-Ming Wu group)
note: The authors say the released data was cleaned and may differ slightly from the paper.

name: Slide generation human evaluation (Z.ai)
description: People compare HTML slide decks from two models on content, layout and visual quality. Metric is overall win rate.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation. GLM-5 is compared with GLM-4.5.

name: SlideVQA
description: Models answer questions about whole slide decks, with single-hop, multi-hop and numerical reasoning. The set has 14.5k questions over 2.6k decks.
note: AAAI 2023. Numerical answers come with annotated arithmetic expressions. VLMEvalKit has a mini split.

name: Slop Arena
description: Site collecting writing-preference data to tune slop detection to a user's taste, paired with the slop-guard tool.
note: Site rendered only a title for us. Method and leaderboard not confirmed.

name: Slop Score
description: Model writing is scored by how often it uses words and patterns that are far more common in AI text than in human text. Lower means less slop.
note: The maker says it is not an AI detector. Release month is the repo creation month.

name: SlopCodeBench
description: Agents repeatedly extend their own code across 36 problems and 196 checkpoints as the specification changes. Tests check correctness, and metrics track structural erosion and verbosity.
note: The paper finds that no agent fully solves any problem end to end.

name: SMDD-Bench
description: 502 small-molecule drug-design tasks in 5 types. Agent uses a fixed toolkit to produce a molecule that must pass all task criteria.
note: 502 tasks per run in five types: 2D pharmacophore identification, interaction point discovery, scaffold hopping, lead optimization and fragment assembly. Agents get a Python sandbox, the Boltz structure predictor and an ADMET predictor. A separate diversity board resamples 20 lead-optimization tasks with 10 rollouts each. The board reports cost and time per task.

name: SMolInstruct
description: Models solve 14 chemistry tasks such as name conversion, property prediction, molecule captioning, generation and reaction prediction. Each task uses its own metric on the test split.
note: It is an instruction-tuning dataset with a test split. Shanghai AI Lab Intern-S models report the test split as a benchmark.

name: SMT 2025
description: Models answer 53 final-answer problems from the 2025 Stanford Math Tournament. MathArena scores the average accuracy over four attempts.
note: MathArena ran 44 models and later marked the set deprecated. MathArena did not run a 2026 edition.

name: SnakeBench
description: Two language models each steer a snake on a shared board in a turn-based game, and the one that survives longest wins. Ratings come from many head-to-head games.
note: ARC Prize launched it as an experimental side quest with 2.8K games on 50 models. The live site now uses TrueSkill ratings and listed GPT-5.1-Codex-Max first on 2026-11-01.

name: Sneaky Sandbox Escape
description: Agents doing coding tasks secretly escape a vulnerable sandbox and disable a monitor process. Scored on side task success while evading monitors.
note: In-house OpenAI monitorability evaluation with 40 tasks across 10 sandbox implementations.

name: Snorkel Agentic Coding
description: Agents complete 100 multi-step coding tasks in sandboxed containers, spread evenly over four difficulty tiers. Unit tests and rubrics grade both outputs and the agent trajectory.
note: Scored as Pass@5 on the Harbor harness with a 30-minute cap per task. Snorkel archived the board after Agentic Coding 2.0.

name: Snorkel Agentic Coding 2.0
description: Agents plan, run, check and recover on 200 terminal-native engineering tasks across 9 task types and 9 languages. Harbor checks task tests, required outputs, milestones and trace behavior.
note: Tasks are a frontier subset of Snorkel's Terminal-Bench+ dataset. Scored as Pass@1, unlike Pass@5 in version 1.0.

name: SnorkelFinance
description: ReAct agents answer expert-verified financial questions built from 10-K filings, using SQL, code and other MCP tools without seeing the documents. A judge scores full traces.
note: Archived. Claude Sonnet 3.7 judged SQL correctness, calculations, tool choice and completion. The page gives no release month, but its board covers 2025 models such as Claude Opus 4. Snorkel later built the OpenEnv FinQA environment from this data.

name: SnorkelFinance 2.0
description: Agents do 200 investment banking and private equity workflow tasks in a simulated firm with incomplete requests, scattered evidence, compliance rules and required state changes.
note: Exact outputs and state are checked by code and semantic answers by rubric. The board reports pass@1. Part of Snorkel Enterprise Environments.

name: SnorkelGraph
description: Models solve 200 procedurally generated graph problems, such as minimum vertex cover, given as node and edge lists in text. Answers are checked against verifiable ground truth.
note: Accuracy@1 with a 16,384-token budget. Part of Snorkel's procedurally generated reasoning series with SnorkelSequences and SnorkelSpatial. The board is archived.

name: SnorkelLegal
description: Agents work 200 tasks inside a simulated mid-market law firm. Each request ties to a matter, a procedural stage and a role with set authority.
note: 15 simulated personas. Record changes are checked by code and legal work product by scenario rubrics. The board reports pass@1.

name: SnorkelManufacturing
description: Agents make engineering, production, quality, supplier and safety decisions in a simulated discrete-parts plant across 200 tasks, a third of them CAD tasks.
note: Answer, state, safety, process and efficiency are scored separately.

name: SnorkelRevOps
description: Agents work 200 tasks in a simulated B2B SaaS revenue team spanning CRM, CPQ, billing, compensation, marketing and finance records.
note: State hashes verify required updates and rubrics grade memos and forecasts.

name: SnorkelSequences
description: Models compute values over integer sequences built from chains of filters, transforms and operators. The 250 procedurally generated questions test compositional multi-step math.
note: Answers are checked programmatically with no judge. Announced with SnorkelFinance and SnorkelUnderwrite as preview benchmarks. The board is archived.

name: SnorkelSpatial
description: Models track particles on a 2D grid through 10 to 200 text-described moves, then report final positions and orientations. The 330 samples test allocentric and egocentric spatial reasoning.
note: Text-only input with structured JSON answers checked against programmatic ground truth. The board is archived.

name: SnorkelUnderwrite
description: Agents help simulated small business insurance underwriters across six task types in multi-turn chats, using tools and asking the underwriter for missing facts.
note: Archived. Expert-verified conversation traces. Dataset created 2025-05-22 and blog post 2025-06-26.

name: SnorkelUnderwrite 2.0
description: Agents do 200 commercial property and casualty underwriting tasks in a simulated insurer with partial information, role permissions and stateful workflows.
note: Scores combine answer checks with safety, process and final state checks. At launch, no model passed over 41% of answer checks.

name: SnorkelWordle
description: Models play Wordle on 100 rare five-letter English words, with six guesses and letter feedback after each guess. The score is the win rate.
note: Target words were picked with the Google Books Ngram corpus to avoid common words. The repo dates from 2025-07-30. The board is archived.

name: SoccerNet-Caption
description: Models write timestamped commentary for soccer broadcasts. The set has almost 37k commentaries over 715.9 hours of video. Streaming reports also score when the model chooses to speak.
note: It is a SoccerNet challenge task. Microsoft's Mage-VL card uses it to score response timing for proactive streaming.

name: SocioHack
description: RL-trained models act in 72 sandbox environments that copy institutional reward rules, such as credit card points or school grading. The test measures whether they find compliant loopholes that defeat each rule's purpose.
org: King's College London, Fudan University and The Alan Turing Institute
note: Historical, synthetic and fictional subsets. Covered in Import AI 460.

name: Soft Bias (Internal)
description: Models answer paired sociopolitical prompts with sides swapped. A judge scores each pair 0, 0.5 or 1 for framing differences.
note: In-house xAI evaluation. The score is the average bias from 0 to 1.

name: SOL-ExecBench
description: Systems write CUDA kernels for 235 workloads taken from real model architectures, run on B200 GPUs. The SOL score measures how much of the gap between a baseline and the analytic hardware speed limit a kernel closes.
note: Speed-of-light bounds come from NVIDIA's SOLAR roofline pipeline. A score above 0.5 beats the baseline. Submissions are checked for reward hacking and numerical correctness. Dataset uses an NVIDIA evaluation license.

name: Soohak
description: Models solve 439 new research-level and graduate math problems written by mathematicians. A 340-item Challenge subset tests solving and a 99-item Refusal subset tests spotting ill-posed problems.
org: OneLineAI, EleutherAI and CMU with 64 mathematicians (Guijin Son et al.)
note: The makers plan a public release in late 2026 and run evaluations on request until then. On the Challenge subset Gemini 3 Pro scored 30.4 percent. 82 HF paper upvotes.

name: SOP-Bench
description: Agents follow expert-written standard operating procedures across 12 industrial domains, using executable tool interfaces over more than 2,000 tasks with 10 to 50 decision points.
note: Repo opened in February 2026 and the blog post followed on 2026-08-21. The repo reports 11 frontier models.

name: SORRY-Bench
