note: Microsoft Phi reports run it through Eureka ML Insights. Other labs use ToxiGen prompts to measure toxic generations instead.

name: TraceSpatial-Bench
description: Models plan an object-centric 3D trace, an ordered list of metric 3D waypoints, from language instructions in real cluttered indoor scenes with depth.
note: 100 test items. From the RoboRefer team, who call it a harder benchmark than RefSpatial-Bench. 37 Hugging Face paper upvotes.

name: TraceTrial-Bench
description: Agent harnesses, not only models, are tested on reliability across seven components, with traces used to attribute each failure to its cause.
note: 203 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: Trae Agent Bench
description: Coding agents complete tasks drawn from real use of the Trae coding product, such as web development, bug fixing, code generation, artifacts and environment setup.
note: In-house ByteDance Seed evaluation. The model card reports it as separate rows per task type with no overall score.

name: TRAIL
aliases: Trace Reasoning and Agentic Issue Localization
description: Models read long agent workflow traces and must find and classify the errors in them, using a formal taxonomy of agent error types. The set has 148 large human-annotated traces from established agent benchmarks.
note: It tests models as debuggers and judges of agent runs, not as agents. The dataset has 32 HF likes.

name: Training distribution hack rate (Anthropic)
aliases: Subset of training data classifier hack rate
description: Classifier monitors measure reward hacking on a subset of Anthropic's reinforcement learning training episodes.
note: Monitoring metric on training data, not a fixed public task set.

name: TRAIT
description: Models answer 8,000 forced-choice items on Big Five and Dark Triad traits. Reports a score per trait.
note: Psychometric inventory adapted for language models. There is no overall score. Meta cites Pellert et al. (2024), but the 8,000-item Big Five and Dark Triad TRAIT set is Lee et al. (arXiv 2406.14703).

name: Trajectory Labs cyber red teaming
description: Expert red teamers try to break safeguarded cyber endpoints across nine attack technique families on exploit reproduction tasks.
note: Run by Trajectory Labs for Google DeepMind. Results are counts of successful breaks.

name: Translated ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag and MMLU (Mistral)
description: Models answer French, German, Spanish and Italian versions of ARC-Challenge, HellaSwag and MMLU.
note: The Mixtral paper does not name the translation source and gives no average.

name: Translation Human Scoring (Z.ai)
description: People score model translations. The GLM-5 report does not describe the test set or the scale.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation shown only in a GLM-5 report chart.

name: TravelPlanner
description: Agents plan multi-day trips from a user request, using tools to search nearly four million records of flights, hotels, restaurants and attractions. Each plan must meet the user's hard constraints, such as budget, and commonsense rules. The headline final pass rate counts a plan only when it meets every constraint.
org: Ohio State University (OSU NLP Group) and Fudan University
note: The 1,225 queries split into validation and test sets, and test scores come from submissions to the leaderboard. A sole-planning mode hands the model the gathered information and tests planning alone, so its scores differ from the tool-use mode. About 570 GitHub stars and 36 HF paper upvotes.

name: TreeBench
description: Models answer 405 visual questions about small targets in dense SA-1B images and give bounding boxes as evidence. Scored by answer accuracy, with box overlap as a second measure.
note: At release no model reached 60% accuracy, and OpenAI o3 scored 54.87.

name: TritonBench
description: Models write Triton GPU operators in two channels, one from real GitHub kernels (G) and one matching PyTorch operators (T). Execution checks correctness and speedup.
note: Each channel comes with simple and complex instruction formats. The repo also ships crawled and synthetic training data.

name: TriviaQA
description: Trivia questions with evidence documents. Scored by exact match.
note: Saturated base-model metric.

name: TRLawBench
description: Models answer 297 questions on Turkish law in three stages: 97 questions from official ÖSYM legal exams and 200 harder questions across 14 branches of law. Answers are checked against the answer key. A judge model also grades the reasoning from 0 to 10.
org: Beta Space Studio (Said Sürücü), with attorney Esat Erbil Tavus
note: The authors say the Stage 2 and 3 questions come from print sources that were never online. Gemini 3.1 Pro grades the reasoning score, so only the correct count is free of judge bias. The board also scores models with YargıPro, which the page does not define. About 43 GitHub stars.

name: TroubleshootingBench
description: Models find and correct realistic experimental errors in expert-written wet lab protocols. Scored as pass@1.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: TrustLLM JailbreakTrigger
description: Models face 400 prompts that apply 13 jailbreak methods to questions about bad behavior and requests for toxic content. Scored by refusal rate.
org: TrustLLM team (Yue Huang, Lichao Sun and others)
note: TrustLLM lists it as the jailbreak part of its safety dimension. Ai2 reports it in its Tulu 3 and Olmo safety suites.

name: TruthfulQA
description: Models answer 817 questions across 38 categories that are written to elicit common misconceptions. Scoring checks for truthful answers, often in multiple-choice form.

changes.text: The maintainers added a recommended two-option multiple-choice format with randomized answer order. They retain the earlier formats and state that previous results remain valid.

note: In January 2025 the authors added a two-option multiple-choice format and now recommend it. They say MC1 and MC2 results stay valid, so it remains one record.

name: ts-bench
description: Coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex and Gemini CLI solve TypeScript tasks, and tests decide pass or fail. Version 1 uses 25 Exercism practice exercises. Version 2 uses real tasks from a large TypeScript monorepo, taken from SWE-Lancer.
note: The author calls the numbers directional, not lab-grade. Results are published as GitHub workflow runs and releases. Version 1 is frozen at the v1-final tag. About 243 GitHub stars.

name: ts-bench v1
description: Coding agents solve 25 self-contained TypeScript exercises from Exercism. The score is the percentage of exercises that pass their tests.
note: Version 1 is frozen at the v1-final tag. Version 2 uses five SWE-Lancer tasks.

name: TSP-Opt
description: Models find optimal tours for 960 traveling salesman instances across 8 difficulty levels. Answers are checked for optimality.
note: Microsoft released the dataset on Hugging Face as microsoft/tsp in June 2025, and the Eureka nphard_tsp config loads it.

name: TTS Arena
description: Users listen to two anonymous text-to-speech models read the same text and vote for the more natural one. Votes become Elo ratings.
note: The original space now points to TTS Arena V2, which has about 985 likes and was updated on 2026-10-31. Release month of the first arena not confirmed on a maker page.

name: TUA-Bench
description: Agents use a terminal for general computer tasks beyond coding, such as file, system and everyday productivity work.
note: 49 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: Tuesday Work Index
description: A composite score built from the Surge AI benchmark suite, such as DAYJOB, GDP.pdf, Riemann-bench and ComplexConstraints. It asks whether models get through an ordinary workday.
note: About 50 models on the board by 2026-10.

name: Tulu 3 Safety Eval
description: Models answer harmful, jailbreak and benign prompts from several safety benchmarks in Ai2's safety-eval suite. A WildGuard classifier judges the outputs, and the score is an average.
note: An aggregate used in the Tulu 3 release. The member benchmarks include WildGuardTest, HarmBench and XSTest. Released month taken from the Tulu 3 release.

name: TurkishMMLU
description: Models answer over 10,000 multiple choice questions that Turkish curriculum experts wrote for nine high-school subjects. Scoring is accuracy.

name: TurnBench
description: Turn-taking systems listen to two-person conversations and must detect when a speaker's turn ends and when the other speaker interrupts. The test set has 116 English conversations in six interaction styles, each labeled by three annotators. Systems rank by recall, and a system whose false-positive rate exceeds 0.15 ranks below every qualifying system. Latency after each event is also reported.
org: Sesame AI with Mundo AI, Carnegie Mellon University and others
note: Test labels are withheld, and submissions go by email with predictions and a public write-up. Systems must be causal, using audio only up to the current moment. Entries mix dedicated turn detectors with realtime voice models, and 12 of the 26 entries are outside submissions. About 60 GitHub stars.

name: TutorBench
description: Models act as tutors on three tasks: adaptive explanations for a confused student, feedback on student work, and hints. Graded against sample-specific rubrics.
note: Dataset card created 2025-10-07.

name: TVBench
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions on 10 temporal video tasks, such as action counting and ordering, that static frames cannot solve. Scored by accuracy.
org: University of Santiago de Compostela and University of Amsterdam et al.

name: TVQA
description: Models answer 152,545 multiple-choice questions about clips from 6 TV shows, using video frames and subtitles. Scoring is accuracy.

name: TxBench-Antibody-Discovery
description: Agents make antibody discovery and development decisions from real experimental data. A grader checks each decision.
note: Part of LatchBio's BioBench suite on benchmarks.bio. The V1 set has 100 evaluations. Release month is the GitHub repo creation month.

name: TxBench-Oligo-Discovery
description: Agents make oligonucleotide discovery decisions, such as ASO and siRNA design, from real data. A grader checks each decision.
note: Part of LatchBio's BioBench suite on benchmarks.bio. The V1 set has 113 evaluations. Release month is the GitHub repo creation month.

name: TxBench-Preclinical-Pharmacology
description: Agents analyze preclinical pharmacology data and make development decisions. A grader checks each decision.
note: Part of LatchBio's BioBench suite on benchmarks.bio. The V1 set has 100 evaluations. Release month is the GitHub repo creation month.

name: TydiQA
description: Models answer information-seeking questions from Wikipedia articles in 11 typologically diverse languages, across 204K question-answer pairs. Scored by F1.
note: Model cards usually report the gold passage (GoldP) task.

name: U-Artifacts
description: Models build interactive artifacts such as small apps and pages for 199 cases across 13 topics. A GUI agent simulates a non-expert user to grade interactivity, looks and fit to the need.
note: In-house Seed benchmark with four task families. It is a different test from Tencent ArtifactsBench.

name: U-MATH
description: Models solve 1,100 unpublished open-ended university math problems from teaching materials, balanced across six subjects. About 20% include images, and an LLM judge checks each solution.
note: The companion set mu-MATH tests how well LLMs judge math solutions. The paper has 20 HF upvotes.

name: U18 safety evaluations
description: Models answer challenging prompts in teen safety categories such as age-restricted goods, eating disorders and emotional reliance. Scored as safe completion rate per category.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report category scores with no overall number.

name: UGMathBench
description: Models solve 5,062 undergraduate math problems across 16 subjects. Each problem has three randomized versions, and effective accuracy counts problems solved in all versions.
org: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Department of Mathematics)
note: The paper was accepted to ICLR 2025. The authors plan more randomized versions as models saturate it. Ant Group reports it in the Ring-1T technical report.

name: Uhura ARC-Easy
description: Models answer ARC-Easy science questions translated into Amharic, Hausa, Northern Sotho, Swahili and Yoruba. Scoring is accuracy.
org: Masakhane with OpenAI and collaborators (Bayes et al.)
note: Human-translated by fluent speakers. Released on Hugging Face with the GPT-4o System Card.

name: Uhura TruthfulQA
description: Models answer TruthfulQA questions translated into Amharic, Hausa, Northern Sotho, Swahili and Yoruba. Scoring is accuracy.
org: Masakhane with OpenAI and collaborators (Bayes et al.)
note: Human-translated by fluent speakers. Released on Hugging Face with the GPT-4o System Card.

name: Uhura-Eval
description: Models answer new reading comprehension questions written in Amharic, Hausa and Yoruba. Scoring is accuracy.
org: Uhura collaborators (Adelani, Kgomo, Bayes and others)
note: Created with fluent speakers for the GPT-4o System Card.

name: UI-TARS 15 Games Collection
description: GUI agents play 15 browser games such as 2048, Infinity-Loop and Snake-solver from screenshots. Each game score is divided by a human score, and the mean is reported.
note: In-house suite from the UI-TARS-2 report. Human performance is 100 by construction.

name: UI-Vision
description: Computer use agents are tested offline on human desktop demonstrations from 83 applications. Three tasks go from element grounding to layout grounding to next-action prediction for clicks, drags and key presses.
note: The makers call it the first license-permissive desktop benchmark. The dataset has over 7,000 downloads and 22 likes. ServiceNow GroundCUA work reports results on it.

name: UI-Vision Action Prediction
description: Models predict the next desktop interface action. The score is the published step success rate.
note: One track of UI-Vision. The UI-Vision record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: UI-Vision Element Grounding
description: Models locate interface elements from instructions. The score is the published overall grounding accuracy.
note: One track of UI-Vision. The UI-Vision record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: UI-Vision Layout Grounding
description: Models identify interface layout regions. The score is the published intersection over union percentage.
note: One track of UI-Vision. The UI-Vision record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: UK AISI alignment and monitorability evaluations
description: UK AISI suites: Out-of-Scope Supply Chain Attack simulation, AI-safety-research sabotage in a simulated company, no-CoT time horizon, CoT legibility.

name: UK AISI and CAISI simulated enterprise network range
description: Agents attack a 32-step simulated enterprise network that takes a human expert about 20 hours. The score is steps completed.
org: UK AI Security Institute and NIST CAISI
note: Government pre-deployment evaluation. AISI names this range The Last Ones. The range is not public. Kimi K3 report cites the joint assessment.

name: UK AISI CoT Controllability
description: Models follow instructions that constrain the content of their chain of thought. Scored as the share of samples that follow the constraint.
note: External UK AISI evaluation. Low controllability is the safer direction for monitoring.

name: UK AISI cyber ranges
description: Agents attack multi-host simulated corporate and industrial networks end to end. Scored as the share of attempts that complete the range.
note: Third-party evaluation reported in OpenAI and Anthropic system cards. AISI describes two ranges, The Last Ones (32-step corporate network) and Cooling Tower (7-step industrial control attack). The ranges are not public.

name: UK AISI narrow cyber tasks
description: Agents solve UK AISI cyber tasks graded by difficulty, including expert-level tasks. Scored as pass@5 and pass@1.
note: Third-party evaluation reported in OpenAI system cards. The tasks are not public.

name: UK AISI Out of Scope Supply Chain Attack
description: Agents in simulated hard cyber challenges with incidental internet access may attack out-of-scope open source projects. Scored as rate of samples with such attacks.
note: External UK AISI evaluation. All tool calls are simulated by other models.

name: UK AISI sabotage continuation evaluation
description: Agents resume trajectories where sabotage of safety research already began. Scored on the share of trajectories where they actively continue the sabotage.
note: Third-party UK AISI evaluation reported in OpenAI and Anthropic system cards.

name: UK AISI unprompted sabotage evaluation
description: Agents act as AI research agents on AI safety research tasks. Scored on confirmed instances of sabotaging the safety research.
note: Third-party UK AISI evaluation reported in OpenAI and Anthropic system cards.

name: UltraText Bench
description: Image generators render dense bilingual text in many regions from 432 prompts. Scores check string accuracy, placement and legibility.
note: 42 upvotes on Hugging Face papers and 113 GitHub stars.

name: UMI-Bench
description: 10 real tabletop tasks trained from standardized UMI hand-held gripper demos. 50 rollouts per task. Progress score and success rate.
note: Best pi0.5 at 55.84 average progress. Two tasks have 0% full success for every model. No live leaderboard.

name: Unauthorized Code Execution Bench
description: A coding agent meets injected instructions to run or fetch malicious artifacts while doing a benign task. Reports attack success rate.
note: In-house Meta benchmark of 76 tasks over 40 malicious objectives.

name: Unauthorized voice generation
description: Speech models produce audio that may deviate from the approved system voice. Scored on how many meaningful deviations the output classifier catches.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation of the voice output classifier. Reports precision and recall by language.

name: Uncritically reporting flawed results (Anthropic)
description: Agents analyze data with code that silently mishandles broken values. Graders check whether the agent flags the flaw or reports the biased numbers.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. Cards report an overall score from 0 to 10 and a separate misreported rate.

name: Unexpected container or code states
description: Coding agents get impossible tasks, such as editing code that is missing from the container. Scored on correctly stating that the task could not be completed.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation built from synthetic samples. The tasks are not public.

name: Ungrounded inference and sensitive trait attribution
aliases: UGI and STA safe behavior accuracy
description: Speech models get requests to infer traits about a speaker from audio. Scored on refusing ungrounded inferences and hedging plausible ones.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Ungrounded Inference evaluation
description: Models receive requests for inferences about people that images or text cannot justify. Scored on refusal rate in non-adversarial and adversarial sets.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report two difficulty levels with no overall number.

name: UniClawBench
description: Agents act as proactive assistants on real-world tasks with live tools across many turns. Tasks are grouped by the capability they test, so failures can be traced to one skill.
org: The University of Hong Kong (HKU MMLab)
note: Qwen runs it with the OpenClaw harness and reports it as multimodal tool use.

name: Uniform Bar Exam (MBE+MEE+MPT)
description: Models take a simulated Uniform Bar Exam with multiple-choice, essay and performance test parts. Scored on the 400-point scale.
note: OpenAI collaborators at CaseText and Stanford CodeX ran it for the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: UniGenBench
description: Text-to-image models draw images for 600 prompts across 5 themes and 20 subthemes, in English and Chinese and in short and long forms. A multimodal model judge checks each image on 10 primary and 27 secondary semantic dimensions, such as attributes, actions, relationships, layout, text and logical reasoning.
org: Tencent Hunyuan, Fudan University and Shanghai AI Lab
note: It first appeared with the Pref-GRPO paper (arXiv 2508.20751), and UniGenBench++ (arXiv 2510.18701) extended it. Separate leaderboards cover English, Chinese and long prompts. The team also releases an offline judge model based on a 72B Qwen model, so scores from the two judges may differ. 68 HF paper upvotes and about 140 GitHub stars.

name: Unintended Engagement with External Agent Messages
description: Agents discover a message board with apparent peer agents during a task. Scored on engagement with peers and on carrying out a specified unauthorized action.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: UniREditBench
description: Image editing models carry out 2,700 edits that need reasoning, in real-world scenes and in game worlds with human-defined rules, across 8 primary and 18 secondary dimensions. A multimodal judge scores each edit against both a text reference and a ground-truth image.
note: The team also releases UniREdit-Data-100K, a synthetic training set made by the same pipeline. 32 HF paper upvotes and about 60 GitHub stars.

name: Unjustified refusals
description: An automated evaluation measures over-refusals on benign or borderline prompts that can be safely fulfilled.
note: In-house Google DeepMind evaluation. Model cards report only the change in percentage points against an earlier Gemini model.

name: UNO-Bench
description: Models answer 1,250 human-written omni-modal questions and 2,480 uni-modal questions across 44 task types and 5 modality mixes. Multiple choice and multi-step open questions are scored, the open ones by a scoring model.
note: Most samples are set in a Chinese context.

name: URO-Bench
description: Spoken dialogue models answer speech with speech across Understanding, Reasoning and Oral conversation. It has a basic track of 16 datasets and a pro track of 20.
note: Covers multilingual, multi-round and paralinguistic tests. Labs report U, R and O scores separately.

name: US-DermMCQA (Google)
description: Models pick the skin condition in a teledermatology image from 4 options. The set has one image per patient from 1,996 patients and 136 conditions.
note: Internal dataset described in Liu et al. (2020, Nature Medicine). Google added random distractors to make the questions.

name: USABO Semifinal Exam 2020
description: Models take the 2020 USA Biology Olympiad semifinal exam. Scored out of 150 points.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: USACO
description: Models solve 307 USA Computing Olympiad problems. Hidden unit tests check correctness and efficiency, scored as pass@1.
note: Princeton's Holistic Agent Leaderboard runs it.

name: USAMO 2024
description: Models write full proofs for problems from the 2024 USA Mathematical Olympiad, graded by human experts.
note: The MathArena dataset holds only the first three of the six problems.

name: USAMO 2025
description: Models write full proofs for the 6 problems of the 2025 USA Mathematical Olympiad. Expert human graders score each proof.
note: In the first evaluation only Gemini 2.5 Pro reached a non-trivial score, at 25 percent.

name: USAMO 2026
description: Models write full proofs for the six problems of the 2026 USA Mathematical Olympiad. Judges grade each proof from 0 to 7 against rubrics.
note: MathArena reports GPT-5.4 at 95.2% and says it essentially saturates the benchmark.

name: User Confirmations During Computer Use
description: Agents doing computer use tasks reach financial, high-stakes communication and other actions. Scored on asking the user for confirmation when policy requires it.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards report category scores with no overall number.

name: UserBench
description: Agents help simulated users who start with vague goals and reveal preferences bit by bit. Agents must ask clarifying questions and use tools to reach choices that fit the user.
note: The paper finds a gap between task completion and alignment with user preferences.

name: USMLE Step 1 (sample questions)
description: Models answer the official USMLE Step 1 multiple choice sample questions. Scored by accuracy.
note: Uses the official USMLE practice questions, not the MedQA question bank.

name: USMLE Step 2 (sample questions)
description: Models answer the official USMLE Step 2 multiple choice sample questions. Scored by accuracy.
note: Uses the official USMLE practice questions, not the MedQA question bank.

name: USMLE Step 3 (sample questions)
description: Models answer the official USMLE Step 3 multiple choice sample questions. Scored by accuracy.
note: Uses the official USMLE practice questions, not the MedQA question bank. Only the multiple choice section is included.

name: USNCO Local Section Exam 2022
description: Models take the 2022 US National Chemistry Olympiad local section exam. Scored out of 60 questions.
note: OpenAI ran this as a simulated exam in the GPT-4 Technical Report.

name: V*
description: Models answer 191 multiple choice questions about small details in high-resolution images, such as an object's color or relative position.
note: Some model cards report runs with Python image tools, which are not comparable with plain runs.

name: VAKRA
aliases: eValuating API and Knowledge Retrieval Agents
description: Agents answer multi-step questions by calling more than 8,000 locally hosted APIs over real databases in 62 domains, along with matching document collections. Tasks need chains of 3 to 7 steps across APIs and documents. A deterministic evaluator replays tools and checks the full trajectory.
note: The score averages four parts: API chaining, tool selection, multi-hop and multi-turn. IBM ran five models with a ReAct agent, and one outside submission had entries only for tool selection. About 77 GitHub stars.

name: Vals Finance Agent
description: Agents answer 537 financial analyst questions on public company SEC filings with search and filing tools. A three-vote GPT-5.2 judge grades each final answer.
note: Vals refreshed v1 in early 2026. AfterQuery checked the data, the judge moved to GPT-5.2 with a mode of three votes, and every model was rerun. Board frozen on 2026-06-04.

name: Vals Finance Agent v1
description: Agents answer 537 financial analyst questions on public company SEC filings using search and filing tools. An LLM judge grades each final answer.
org: Vals AI (with Stanford researchers and a global systemically important bank)
note: Splits are 50 public, 150 licensable validation and 337 private test questions. Vals froze the v1 board on 2026-02-10 when v1.1 replaced it.

name: Vals Finance Agent v2
description: 927 expert-reviewed research questions on public-company filings. Partial credit only after required checks pass. Private test split.
note: Rebuilt with 927 harder questions in nine workflow categories, scored with partial credit. Scores do not compare with v1.1.

name: Vals Finance Agent v2.1
description: Agents answer analyst-grade questions on public company filings, scored with dealbreaker-gated partial credit. A three-model jury grades answers and fails hedged ones.
note: Revises v2 with question and rubric fixes and a jury of GPT-6.1 Sol, Gemini 3.8 Flash and Claude Sonnet 5.5. Vals says scores are not comparable with v2. Part of Vals Index v2.2 from 2026-10-19.

name: Vals Finance Index
description: Agents are scored on Finance Agent v2.1, Excel Modeling Benchmark v1.1 and Tax Agent Bench, combined with weights from each sub-sector share of US GDP.
note: Securities work (1.6% of GDP) averages Finance Agent and EMB. Tax work (0.5%) uses Tax Agent Bench all-pass accuracy. 35 models on 2026-10-29.

name: Vals Index v1
description: Vals AI's first index of agentic work in finance, law and coding, with each sector weighted by its share of U.S. GDP.
note: Versions 1.0 to 1.2 ran from October 2025 to 12 August 2026. Until May 2026 it combined CorpFin, Finance Agent, CaseLaw, SWE-bench Verified and Terminal-Bench 2.0. In May 2026 Vals dropped the law sector, added Vibe Code Bench, moved to Finance Agent v2 and to Terminal-Bench 2.1. The archived v1.2 is (2.0 × finance + 1.4 × coding) / 3.4.

name: Vals Index v2
description: Version 2 of Vals AI's GDP-weighted index, which brought back a legal sector and added financial modeling in Excel and code migration.
note: Released 13 August 2026. EMB replaced CorpFin, Code Migration joined coding, Legal Research Bench and HLAB formed the legal sector, and SWE-bench Verified left as saturated. Coding averages Terminal-Bench 2.1, Vibe Code Bench and Code Migration.

name: Vals Index v2.1
description: Version 2.1 of Vals AI's GDP-weighted index, which moved coding to Terminal-Bench 4.0 and added a tax sector.
note: Released 25 September 2026. Terminal-Bench 4.0 replaced 2.1, and Tax Agent Bench entered at weight 0.5, so the denominator rose from 14.8 to 15.3. Finance and legal were unchanged.

name: Vals Index v2.2
description: Agents are scored on eight finance, coding, legal, and tax benchmarks, combined with weights from each sector's share of US GDP.
note: Version 2.2 from 19 October 2026: (8.0 × finance + 5.6 × coding + 1.2 × legal + 0.5 × tax) / 15.3. Finance averages Finance Agent v2.1 and EMB v1.1. Coding averages Terminal-Bench 4, Vibe Code Bench v1.1 and Code Migration v1.1. Legal averages Legal Research and HLAB-Vals-1.1. Tax is Tax Agent Bench (all-pass accuracy). Six of the eight components are private. Earlier versions have their own records.

name: Vals Legal Index
description: Agents are scored on Legal Research Bench, HLAB-Vals-1.1 and Tax Agent Bench, mapped to practice areas weighted by share of US law-office revenue.
note: Practice areas without a covering benchmark (7% of revenue) are not scored. The board had 33 models on 2026-10-29.

name: Vals Multimodal Index
description: Models are scored on a GDP-weighted mix of seven Vals finance, coding and education benchmarks, including MortgageTax and SAGE, which grades handwritten math work.
note: Finance (weight 2.0) averages CorpFin, Finance Agent v2 and MortgageTax. Coding (1.4) mixes SWE-bench Verified, Terminal-Bench 2.1 and Vibe Code Bench. Introduced 2025-10-29, version 1.2 by 2026-08-11.

name: Vals Router Index
description: Model routers run all eight Vals Index v2.2 benchmarks through the same agents as single models and are scored with the Index weights.
note: The board had five routers on 2026-10-28. It compares them with single-model Index runs.

name: Vals RSI Index
description: Agents work four open AI R&D problems under fixed compute and time budgets: compression, LM training, judge harness work and post-training. Each runs in its vendor harness.
note: Each task maps a measured result, such as bits per byte on enwik8, onto a score between a baseline and a theoretical best. 25 models on 2026-10-15.

name: Vals Science Index
description: Agents are scored on the equal average of BioMysteryBench, MysteryMechanism and Terminal-Bench-Science.
note: Version 1.0 released 2026-10-16. The board had 23 models on 2026-10-25.

name: Vals Web Search Index
description: Agents work Finance Agent v2 and Legal Research Bench tasks with one web search tool as their only outside source. It compares native provider search with Exa and Keenable.
note: Domain tools such as SEC EDGAR and CourtListener are removed. The board had nine model and tool pairs on 2026-10-21.

name: VariantBench
description: Agents discover and interpret genetic variants from real sequencing analyses. A deterministic grader checks the result.
note: Part of LatchBio's BioBench suite on benchmarks.bio. The V1 set has 118 evaluations. Release month is the GitHub repo creation month.

name: VATEX
description: Models write English or Chinese captions for short video clips from a set of over 41,000 videos. Scored by CIDEr.
org: UC Santa Barbara and ByteDance AI Lab

name: VATEX ZH
description: Models write Chinese captions for short videos of human activities from the VATEX dataset. Captions are scored with CIDEr against human references.

name: VBench
description: Video generation models make clips from prompts, and automatic checks score 16 dimensions of quality and prompt adherence.
org: NTU S-Lab and Shanghai AI Laboratory (Vchitect)
note: Results give Quality, Semantic and Total scores. VBench++ (TPAMI 2025) extends it to image-to-video and trustworthiness. VBench-2.0 (2025-03) tests intrinsic faithfulness with new dimensions. VBench and V*Bench are different tests.

name: VBench image-to-video
description: Models animate input images. Automatic checks score image conditioning and video quality across the complete image-to-video suite.
org: NTU S-Lab and Shanghai AI Laboratory (Vchitect)
note: The official Gradio board provides a separate image-to-video table. Total Score is the headline, with I2V and Quality scores retained separately.

name: VBench-2.0
description: Video generation models are scored on intrinsic faithfulness, such as human fidelity, controllability, creativity, physics and commonsense, beyond pixel quality and basic prompt match.
org: NTU S-Lab and Shanghai AI Laboratory (Vchitect)
note: A VBench-2.0 Video Arena on Hugging Face shows the generated videos. 33 HF paper upvotes.

name: VBVR-Bench
description: Video generation models solve visual reasoning tasks by generating a video from a starting image and instruction. Rule-based scorers check the result instead of a judge model. Tasks cover abstraction, knowledge, perception, spatial reasoning and transformation, with in-domain and out-of-domain splits.
org: Video-Reason (Maijunxian Wang, Ruisi Wang and others)
note: The existing importer reads VBVR-Pro. Move those rows to proposed vbvr-pro and restore original VBVR scope independently.

name: VBVR-Pro
description: The current official results table evaluates the Pro release. Original VBVR results must remain separate.
org: Video-Reason (Maijunxian Wang, Ruisi Wang and others)
note: The current official results table evaluates the Pro release. Original VBVR results must remain separate.

name: VCR (Visual Caption Restoration)
description: Models restore caption text that is partly covered in an image, using only the visible pixel fragments. Scored by exact match and Jaccard similarity of the words.
note: English and Chinese splits in easy and hard settings. Not the older Visual Commonsense Reasoning dataset with the same short name. OpenVLM lists it for 56 models.

name: VCR-Bench
description: Video models answer 1,034 questions on 859 videos, and graders score both the final answer and each tagged chain-of-thought step against human rationales.
note: At release o1 scored a 62.8% CoT score and 56.7% accuracy.

name: VCSUM
description: Models summarize transcripts of 239 real Chinese meetings that total over 230 hours. Scored with ROUGE against human-written summaries.
org: Han Wu, Mingjie Zhan, Linqi Song, and colleagues

name: VCT-v2
description: Models answer an updated set of expert virology troubleshooting questions from SecureBio. Scored as refusal-corrected accuracy.
note: 279 text and image questions with a private holdout. 35 PhD virologists give the expert baseline, reusing 216 original VCT expert answers rescored.

name: vCX Benchmark
description: Models run inside a Retell voice agent on pass or fail checks for business rules, grounding, tool calls and speech-ready replies. Each suite reports its own pass rate.
note: Retell's board also compares latency and reliability across providers. 15 models in the Fireworks index.

name: VDEBench
description: Image editing models make local text and table edits to 3,506 Chinese and English document images. Scores check the edit and that the rest of the page is preserved.
note: Added to Hugging Face's official benchmark list in October 2026.

name: Vectara Hallucination Leaderboard (2025 dataset)
description: Models summarize over 7,700 private articles of up to 32K tokens using only facts in the text. Vectara's commercial HHEM model flags hallucinated summaries.
note: Vectara calls it a new baseline. The articles grew from 1,000 to over 7,700 and the prompt changed, so rates are much higher than on the old board.

name: Vectara Hallucination Leaderboard (HHEM)
description: Models summarize short documents. The HHEM-2.1-Open classifier flags summaries that add unsupported facts, giving a hallucination rate.
note: Labs often report one minus the hallucination rate so that higher is better. The judge moved from HHEM-1.0 to HHEM-2.x in 2024-08. Vectara replaced the 1,000 article set in 2025-11.

name: Vending-Bench
description: Agents run a simulated vending machine business over long horizons, ordering stock, setting prices, and paying daily fees. Scoring is final net worth in dollars.
note: Andon Labs deprecated it in November 2025 in favor of Vending-Bench 2.

name: Vending-Bench 2
description: Agent runs a simulated vending-machine business for one year starting with $500. Score is the final bank balance, averaged over runs.
note: Paper covers the original Vending-Bench. The v2 environment is not released. Theoretical optimum is ~$63k, so headroom remains.

name: Vending-Bench Arena
description: Several agents each run a vending machine at the same location in the Vending-Bench 2 environment. They can email, pay and trade with each other, but each is scored on its own money balance.
note: Andon Labs first multi-agent eval. A round is usually four runs with the same models, and 14 rounds had run by 2026-10. Gemini 4 Carbon set the record average of about 16.0k US dollars.

name: Verbalized grader awareness (Anthropic)
description: Models work on tasks where grading is disclosed clearly, ambiguously or barely. An autorater flags transcripts that reason about the grader.
note: Reported separately for three disclosure levels with no overall rate.

name: Verbalized metagaming
description: A prompted monitor reads chains of thought on alignment evaluations and deployment simulations. Scored as the share of samples reasoning about grading or monitoring.
note: In-house OpenAI measurement. Cards report rates per evaluation suite with no overall number.

name: Verifiable Browsing Task (Meta)
description: Agents answer list-style information-seeking questions, written as realistic user requests, using browser search, open and find tools.
note: Meta in-house eval reported in the Muse Wonder model card. The name says verifiable, but the card does not describe the grader. Part of Meta's PSI composite.

name: Verifying the Verifiers (Project APE CRED benchmark)
aliases: Verifying the Verifiers: Towards Autonomous Policy Evaluation
description: Verifier LLMs must find planted errors (prose-table, paper-code, execution, data) in AI-generated economics papers. Credit needs a verbatim quote of the edit.
org: Project APE, University of Zurich (Willner, Yanagizawa-Drott)
note: Mutation testing on 100 reproducible host papers with deterministic scoring and no LLM judge. Best single config 99% recall (Codex 5.6 Sol high). Instances and answer key withheld against contamination. Up to 28% of per-error outcomes flip between identical runs. Repo holds the APE papers, not the CRED code.

name: VGI-Bench
description: Video generation models solve 27 visual reasoning tasks with 810 instances through generated frames. Scoring checks that the process is valid, not only the final frame.
note: 77 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: VHELM
aliases: Holistic Evaluation of Vision Language Models
description: Vision-language models are scored across nine aspects, including perception, reasoning, knowledge, bias, fairness, multilinguality, robustness, toxicity and safety, from many existing datasets.
note: Releases run from v1.0.0 to v2.1.2.

name: VIALS
aliases: Visual Interpretation of Artifacts in the Life Sciences
description: Vision models answer 161 questions about lab images such as gel blots, plasmid maps, microscopy and flow cytometry plots. An LLM judge grades each answer against a key.
note: Images come from everyday biotech work, not published figures. Judge is GPT-5 mini. Version 2.0.0 on 2026-10-30 revised 3 of 161 tasks after expert review, so scores stay close to version 1.0.0.

name: VIALS 2
description: Models interpret 161 professional life-science visual artifacts. The score is judged accuracy averaged across three rollouts.
note: The official changelog requires reruns after three task changes. Values are transcribed from the current chart and hash-checked. Unlabeled confidence intervals are not digitized.

name: VIBE (MiniMax)
aliases: VIBE: Visual & Interactive Benchmark for Execution
description: Agent builds complete web, simulation, Android, iOS or backend apps from scratch. Agent verifiers check execution, interaction and visuals.
note: VIBE v1 is open on Hugging Face (December 2025). MiniMax then reported harder internal versions, VIBE-Pro with M2.5 and VIBE-V2 with M3, which have their own records.

name: Vibe Code Bench
description: End-to-end web application development from natural-language specs. Built apps are tested against functional requirements.
note: Official scaffold fork at github.com/vals-ai/VibeCodeBench-Openhands-Scaffold. Results come from the Vals AI leaderboard.

name: Vibe Code Bench 1-100
description: Agents start from a working web app built for Vibe Code Bench v1.1. They extend it through up to ten dependent plain-English product requests without breaking it.
note: Later turns keep the code, data and conversation from earlier work. The board had 26 models on 2026-10-29.

name: Vibe Code Bench v1
description: Agents build web applications from scratch from a natural-language spec in OpenHands. The built apps are tested against functional requirements.
note: Vals froze the board on 2026-02-20. Vals moved to v1.1 on 2026-03-02.

name: Vibe-Eval
description: Models answer 269 image-based prompts, 100 of them hard, that have expert gold responses. A Reka Core judge rates each answer.

name: VIBE-Pro (MiniMax)
description: Agents build full-stack projects for Web, Android, iOS and Windows, including server APIs and databases. Claude Code based verifiers check interaction logic and visual output.
note: MiniMax introduced it with M2.5 as a harder upgrade of VIBE and reports Web, Simulation, Android and iOS subsets. Internal, so only MiniMax reports it.

name: VIBE-V2 (MiniMax)
description: Agents build front-end and full-stack Web, Android and iOS projects from scratch in Claude Code. An agent-as-verifier pipeline checks interaction logic and visual output.
note: MiniMax first reported it with M3 and calls it internal.

name: ViBench 2.0
description: Agents build 17 real web apps from empty projects one feature at a time from short specs. A grading agent uses each app in a browser and follows test plans.
note: 8 apps are public and 9 held out, with 241 feature stages and 544 test plans. The paper (ACM CAIS 2026) describes the first version.

name: VibeVideoBench
description: Agents write code to render a finished video with sound, with no image or video generation model, in their native harness within one hour. Program checks, task rubrics and a judge panel score the result.
org: BUPT + Zhongguancun Academy + Peking University + Jilin University + Kling AI
note: 239 tasks in English and Chinese across 12 content types. Headline is the mean of five 1 to 5 quality scores, with a missing video counted as 0. Nine agent systems in the first release.

name: Video Reality Test
description: Vision-language models and humans judge whether ASMR videos with tight audio and visual coupling are real or AI-generated. It tests perceptual realism detection.
note: 65 HF paper upvotes. Also used to see whether generated videos can fool the models.

name: Video SimpleQA
description: Video models answer multi-hop fact-seeking questions that need knowledge beyond the video and evidence from its time segments. Short definitive answers are graded for factual correctness.
note: The paper evaluates 33 video language models. Each question also has single-fact sub-questions for step-by-step grading.

name: Video-Holmes
description: Models answer 1,837 questions about 270 suspense short films across seven reasoning tasks. Each question needs several visual clues from different parts of the film.
org: Tencent ARC Lab and City University of Hong Kong
note: Films were annotated by hand for key events and causal links before questions were written.

name: Video-MME
description: Models answer 2,700 multiple-choice questions about 900 videos from 11 seconds to 1 hour long, with and without subtitles. Scored by accuracy.

changes.text: The maintainers replaced videos with broken or potentially broken links and annotated the replacements again. Evaluations before and after this update use different video content and annotations.

note: Video-MME-v2 (2026-04) is a harder successor. MiniMax HF metadata maps its score to v2 though the card says Video-MME.

name: Video-MMMU
description: 300 expert-level lecture videos with questions testing perception, comprehension and adaptation of knowledge. Accuracy.
note: Frame sampling differs across labs.

name: Video-Oasis
description: A diagnostic suite that audits video understanding benchmarks and keeps only samples that need visual and temporal input. Models are tested on the remaining video-native questions.
note: The audit found 55% of existing benchmark samples solvable without the video or its timing. 65 HF paper upvotes.

name: Video-SafetyBench
description: Video-language models receive 2,264 synthesized videos paired with a harmful or a benign-looking query across 13 unsafe categories and 48 subcategories. An LLM judge scores harm with a confidence-weighted metric called RJScore.
note: Accepted to the NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks track. Benign queries look harmless but become harmful when read with the video.

name: VideoDR (with search)
description: Agents watch a video, gather clues across frames, and search the web to answer multi-hop questions. Scored by answer accuracy.
note: The first release and the official leaderboard use 100 questions. A 500-question set followed on 2026-05-19 at huggingface.co/datasets/strike20023/VideoDR. Scores on the two sets are not comparable.

name: VideoEval-Pro
description: Video models give open-ended short answers to questions that need the whole long video, which removes the guessing that multiple choice allows.
note: The scoring field assumes a model judge grades the open answers.

name: VideoFDB
description: Multimodal agents are evaluated on two-person video conference recordings. They cover 11 conversational dynamics across verbal, nonverbal and mixed behavior, annotated by people in three passes.
note: Gated Hugging Face dataset. A launch post on r/singularity (1,387 points) said a human interaction model ranked first on it. Scoring method needs a check.

name: VideoGameBench
description: Vision-language models play 10 popular 1990s Game Boy and MS-DOS games in real time from raw frames. Scored by the share of each game completed.
org: Alex Zhang, Ofir Press and collaborators
note: Three games are kept secret. VideoGameBench Lite pauses the game while the model thinks. Users supply their own game ROMs, and the repo has had no commits since 2025-05.

name: VideoGameBench Lite
description: Agents play video games while the environment pauses during inference. The headline is the official Overall Score.
org: Alex Zhang, Ofir Press and collaborators
note: Agents play video games while the environment pauses during inference. The headline is the official Overall Score.

name: VideoHallucer
description: Paired basic and hallucinated questions about videos detect intrinsic and extrinsic hallucinations. Scored by pair accuracy.
note: In 2025-10 the makers removed some duplicate questions from the temporal hallucination task. They treat it as a fix, so it stays one record.

name: VideoMME v2 (with subtitles)
description: Models answer multiple choice questions about videos with subtitles or audio added. Related questions are scored as groups to penalize guessing.
note: This is the with-subtitles setting, which scores higher for reasoning models than the frames-only setting.

name: VideoPhy
description: Text-to-video models generate clips from captions of physical interactions between solids and fluids. Human raters judge caption match and physical commonsense.
org: UCLA and Google Research (Hritik Bansal et al.)
note: ICLR 2025 paper. The headline score is the share of prompts whose videos both follow the caption and obey physics, with CogVideoX-5B best at 39.6%. The paper also releases an auto-evaluator, VideoCon-Physics.

name: VideoPhy-2
description: 200 action-centric prompts. Generated videos human-rated for semantic adherence, physical commonsense and physical-rule grounding.
note: Hard: best model reached only 22% joint performance on the hard subset at release. Conservation laws are a common failure.

name: VideoReasonBench
description: Video models watch a sequence of fine-grained operations on a partly hidden state and answer questions that recall, infer or predict that state.
note: Questions come in three levels of reasoning skill.

name: ViDoRe v2
description: Models retrieve relevant documents from multimodal document collections.

name: ViDoRe V3
description: Retrieval and RAG pipelines answer queries over visually rich documents, such as reports with tables, charts and images. The benchmark has 10 datasets from professional domains, about 26,000 pages and 3,099 human-verified queries, each in 6 languages. It scores retrieval relevance, bounding-box grounding and the final answers.
note: Earlier versions, ViDoRe V1 from the ColPali paper and V2, use different datasets and are separate tests. The 278 GitHub stars belong to the repository for all versions. 12 HF paper upvotes.

name: ViewSpatial-Bench
description: Models answer 5,712 questions that locate objects from the camera view and from the view of people in the scene. Five task types test egocentric and allocentric reasoning.
org: Dingming Li, Yueting Zhuang et al.
note: Questions were made by automatic generation plus human annotation.

name: VIMA-Bench
description: Robot policies carry out tabletop manipulation tasks given as multimodal prompts that mix text with images of objects or goal scenes. Thousands of tasks are generated procedurally, with over 600,000 expert trajectories for imitation learning. A four-level protocol tests generalization from new object placements up to unseen tasks, and scores are success rates.
org: Stanford University and NVIDIA with collaborators
note: It shipped with the authors' VIMA agent. About 330 GitHub stars on VIMABench and 860 on the VIMA repository, and the benchmark repo was last pushed in 2023-09.

name: Virology Capabilities Test (text-only)
description: Models answer the text-only questions of the SecureBio Virology Capabilities Test. Scored as accuracy.
note: Third-party SecureBio evaluation reported in OpenAI system cards.

name: Virology Capabilities Test (VCT)
description: Models answer 322 multimodal virology troubleshooting questions written by expert virologists. Multiple-select variant requires all correct options.
org: SecureBio and Center for AI Safety
note: Anthropic cards call it Multimodal virology and use the multiple-select variant.

name: VisFactor
description: Models take 20 vision-centric subtests adapted from a human cognitive psychology test battery, covering perception primitives and visual memory. Scored by accuracy.

name: Vision Arena
description: People send an image with a prompt, compare answers from two anonymous vision-language models, and vote for the better one. Votes become Bradley-Terry ratings.
note: Launched as the Multimodal Arena on 2024-06-27 with 17,429 votes. Since September 2025 an LLM filter drops image-generation prompts.

name: Vision2Web
description: Agents build websites from 918 prototype images across 193 tasks, from static pages to full-stack apps. A GUI agent and a VLM judge score them.

name: Vision2Web S1-2026
description: Agents build websites from 918 prototype images across 193 tasks, from static pages to full-stack apps. A GUI agent and a VLM judge score them.
note: This season uses Gemini-3-pro-preview as its visual judge. Scores from other seasons use different judge or agent configurations.

name: Vision2Web S2-2026
description: Agents build websites from 918 prototype images across 193 tasks, from static pages to full-stack apps. A GUI agent and a VLM judge score them.
note: This season uses Gemini-3.1-pro-preview as its visual judge. Scores from other seasons use different judge or agent configurations.

name: Vision2Web S3-2026
description: Agents build websites from 918 prototype images across 193 tasks, from static pages to full-stack apps. A GUI agent and a VLM judge score them.
note: This season uses Gemini-3.5-flash as its visual judge. Scores from other seasons use different judge or agent configurations.

name: ViSpeak-Bench
description: Streaming video models must notice instructions given visually, such as a hand wave, and respond in seven subtasks of visual instruction feedback.
note: Released with the ViSpeak-Instruct training set and the ViSpeak model. The scoring field is a guess.

name: VISTA
description: Models answer 758 single-turn prompts about one image each, covering perception and reasoning. Three LLM judges grade answers with yes/no rubric questions. The main score is average task accuracy.
note: Scale keeps the data private until models improve a lot. Judges were Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o and Gemini 1.5 Pro, with three runs per evaluation. The board ranked 63 models on 2026-11-01.

name: Vistra
description: Systems translate text in natural images across multiple language directions.

name: Visual Aesthetic Benchmark
description: Models see a set of images with the same subject and intent and must pick the best one, and in a harder setting both the best and the worst. The 400 sets hold 1,195 commissioned works across fine art, photography and illustration. Labels come from expert judgments, and only sets where experts largely agreed are kept.
org: BakeLab with University of Washington, UC Santa Barbara, Stanford, Notre Dame and IBM Research
note: Expert annotators reach 77.7 Top-1 and random guessing 6.6. Each model answers three times with shuffled options, and PASS^3 and AP@1 summarize the runs. The leaderboard lists 20 models and was last updated in 2026-02. Its short name VAB is also used by VisualAgentBench, a different test. About 40 GitHub stars and 9 HF paper upvotes.

name: VisualAgentBench
description: Large multimodal models act as agents in embodied, GUI and visual design environments, including mobile, WebArena-based web and Minecraft tasks.
note: ICLR 2025. 279 GitHub stars at 2026-11-01.

name: VisualProbe
description: Models search high-resolution images for small targets to answer questions, often over many crop and zoom turns. Answers are checked against a key.
note: Released with the Mini-o3 paper as the Visual Probe Dataset, with train and test splits.

name: VisualPuzzles
description: Models solve visual puzzles that need algorithmic, analogical, deductive, inductive and spatial reasoning but little domain knowledge. Scored by accuracy.
note: Many puzzles come from translated Chinese civil service exam questions.

name: VisualToolBench
description: Vision-language models solve 1,204 image tasks with tools, half single-turn and half multi-turn, graded per turn against weighted rubrics.
note: Categories include medical, scientific and general prompts. Dataset created 2025-10-17. No paper link on the card.

name: VisualWebArena
description: Multimodal web agents complete 910 visually grounded tasks on self-hosted classifieds, shopping and Reddit-style sites. Execution-based checks score each task.
note: Built on the WebArena environments by the same group. Many 2024 and 2025 agent papers report it.

name: VisualWebBench
description: Models answer questions about web page screenshots across seven tasks, such as captioning, OCR, element grounding and action prediction.
org: Junpeng Liu, Yifan Song et al.

name: VisuLogic
description: Models answer 1,000 visual reasoning puzzles in six categories that cannot be solved by describing the image in words. Scored by accuracy.
org: Shanghai AI Laboratory with several universities
note: The paper reports human accuracy near 51 percent and most models near the 25 percent chance level.

name: VITA-Bench
description: Agents handle multi-turn requests in simulated food delivery, in-store, and travel services with 66 tools. A rubric-based judge scores task success.
note: An updated version in January 2026 fixed data and the evaluator, so older scores differ.

name: VitaBench 2.0
description: Agents serve one simulated user across a sequence of life-service subtasks over days or months. They must infer, use and update the user's preferences, judged by rubrics.
note: Reuses the three VitaBench domains and adds a memory interface with full-context, agentic and RAG memory settings. The board reports Avg@4.

name: VitaBench-Noise (LongCat)
description: Agents run VitaBench life-service tasks after a pipeline injects instruction noise and tool failures into the environment. The score is the average over several noisy copies.
note: In-house robustness variant of VITA-Bench. Meituan says it will release the noise injection pipeline.

name: ViVerBench
description: Models judge whether visual outcomes in multimodal reasoning are correct, across 16 task categories such as boxes, points, counts, mazes, GUIs, charts and LaTeX.
note: Scoring is rule-based, with an optional GPT-4.1 judge. The project page lists humans at 93.2 and random choice at 50.

name: VizWiz
description: Models answer over 31,000 spoken questions that blind people asked about photos they took with phones. Some questions are unanswerable from the image.
org: University of Texas at Austin and collaborators (Gurari et al.)
note: Each question has 10 crowdsourced answers and uses VQA accuracy.

name: VL-RewardBench
description: Vision-language reward models pick the better of two responses on general queries, hallucination detection and reasoning tasks.
note: Multimodal reward model cards often report it.

name: VLA-Arena
description: VLAs fine-tuned on level-0 tabletop tasks, tested on 170 tasks in 11 suites at harder unseen levels L1/L2. Success rate.
note: L0 (the fine-tuning level and page default) median 0.73. L2 best 0.56 and median 0.14, so compare on L1/L2. Benchmark team fine-tuned most entries. Five came from outside users.

name: VLABench
description: 100 language-conditioned manipulation task categories needing world knowledge, implicit intent and long-horizon reasoning. Evaluates VLAs and VLMs.
note: Site says the complete leaderboard 'will be released soon'.

name: VLADBench
description: Models answer closed-form questions about driving scenes, from static traffic knowledge to reasoning about dynamic road situations.
note: Qwen reports it under autonomous driving.

name: VLGuard
description: Vision language models answer safe and unsafe image and text pairs from the VLGuard test set. Responses are judged for harmfulness and refusal.
org: Zong et al. (University of Edinburgh and others)
note: Built as a safety fine-tuning dataset with a held-out test set. The Phi-3 report gives a judged score from 0 to 10.

name: VLMs Are Blind
description: Models answer seven simple visual tasks such as counting line crossings or overlapping circles, which young children solve easily. Scored by accuracy.
org: Auburn University and University of Alberta
note: VLMsAreBiased is a separate test by an overlapping team.

name: VLMsAreBiased
description: Models count or identify features in altered images of famous subjects, such as a logo with an added stripe, across 7 domains. Scoring is accuracy.

name: Voice Arena Arabic MSA
description: Models generate speech in Arabic MSA. Listeners compare anonymous clips, and preference votes determine independent language Elo ratings.
note: Each language has an independent leaderboard. Topic filters stay within its vote pool.

name: Voice Arena Bahasa
description: Models generate speech in Bahasa. Listeners compare anonymous clips, and preference votes determine independent language Elo ratings.
note: Each language has an independent leaderboard. Topic filters stay within its vote pool.

name: Voice Arena Brazilian Portuguese
description: Models generate speech in Brazilian Portuguese. Listeners compare anonymous clips, and preference votes determine independent language Elo ratings.
note: Each language has an independent leaderboard. Topic filters stay within its vote pool.

name: Voice Arena French
description: Models generate speech in French. Listeners compare anonymous clips, and preference votes determine independent language Elo ratings.
note: Each language has an independent leaderboard. Topic filters stay within its vote pool.

name: Voice Arena German
description: Models generate speech in German. Listeners compare anonymous clips, and preference votes determine independent language Elo ratings.
note: Each language has an independent leaderboard. Topic filters stay within its vote pool.

name: Voice Arena Hindi
description: Models generate speech in Hindi. Listeners compare anonymous clips, and preference votes determine independent language Elo ratings.
note: Each language has an independent leaderboard. Topic filters stay within its vote pool.

name: Voice Arena Indian English
description: Models generate speech in Indian English. Listeners compare anonymous clips, and preference votes determine independent language Elo ratings.
note: Each language has an independent leaderboard. Topic filters stay within its vote pool.

name: Voice Arena Japanese
description: Models generate speech in Japanese. Listeners compare anonymous clips, and preference votes determine independent language Elo ratings.
note: Each language has an independent leaderboard. Topic filters stay within its vote pool.

name: Voice Arena Mexican Spanish
description: Models generate speech in Mexican Spanish. Listeners compare anonymous clips, and preference votes determine independent language Elo ratings.
note: Each language has an independent leaderboard. Topic filters stay within its vote pool.

name: Voice Arena Tagalog
description: Models generate speech in Tagalog. Listeners compare anonymous clips, and preference votes determine independent language Elo ratings.
note: Each language has an independent leaderboard. Topic filters stay within its vote pool.

name: Voice Arena US English
description: Models generate speech in US English. Listeners compare anonymous clips, and preference votes determine independent language Elo ratings.
note: Each language has an independent leaderboard. Topic filters stay within its vote pool.

name: Voice Arena Vietnamese
description: Models generate speech in Vietnamese. Listeners compare anonymous clips, and preference votes determine independent language Elo ratings.
note: Each language has an independent leaderboard. Topic filters stay within its vote pool.

name: Voice persuasion study on party preferences
description: Participants hear model-voiced audio clips or talk with a voiced model. Scored on shifts in hypothetical party preference against human baselines.
note: Human participant study with over 3,800 respondents and a one-week follow-up.

name: VoiceBench
description: Spoken instructions with speaker, environment and content variation. Voice assistant responses scored by GPT judge or rules.
note: The suite grew after release: mmsu joined the leaderboard in 2024-12, and bbh and wildvoice in 2025-04. The Overall score now averages nine subsets, so early Overall scores are not comparable.

name: VoiceCodeBench
description: Speech-to-text models transcribe 300 English workplace recordings. They are scored on whether every target entity, such as an address or email, survives exactly.
note: 5.6 hours of audio with 1,482 audited entities across 26 types and 8 workflow domains. Metrics are task success rate, CTEM and WER. 20 systems on 2026-09-24.

name: VoxelBench
description: Language models turn text or image prompts into voxel structures. Voters compare anonymous builds from the same prompt, and Glicko-2 ratings rank the models.
note: Separate text-prompt and image-prompt boards. A model needs 50 votes to appear. Different from MineBench.

name: VoxelBench Image
description: Models turn image prompts into voxel structures. Human comparisons determine Glicko-2 ratings in a separate image-prompt vote pool.
note: The site requires at least 50 votes. Text-prompt ratings belong to the separate VoxelBench Text board.

name: VoxMem
description: Audio language models answer questions that need memory of earlier spoken sessions. Questions cover what was said, who said it, how it was spoken and what was audible.
note: It had 64 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 10 GitHub stars.

name: VPCT
description: Models view an image of a ball, ramps, and three buckets and predict which bucket the ball falls into. Scored by accuracy on 100 problems.

name: VQA-RAD
description: Vision-language models answer clinicians' questions about 315 radiology images, including head CTs, MRIs and chest X-rays. Questions are closed yes or no, or open free text.
note: Published in Scientific Data. Medical model reports often cite it next to SLAKE and PathVQA.

name: VQAv2
description: Open-ended questions about COCO images, balanced to reduce language priors. Scored by consensus accuracy against 10 human answers.
note: Saturated legacy benchmark.

name: VRBench
description: Models answer multi-step reasoning questions about long narrative videos, which average 1.6 hours. The 1,010 videos come with 9,468 human-labeled question and answer pairs and 30,292 timestamped reasoning steps across seven reasoning types. Multiple-choice answers score the outcome, and a model judge scores the reasoning steps.
note: Sources may report the outcome score, the process score or both. 30 HF paper upvotes and about 30 GitHub stars.

name: VSI-Bench
description: Models watch egocentric videos of 288 indoor scenes and answer over 5,000 questions on object counts, distances, sizes, room layout and route planning.
org: New York University (VisionX, Saining Xie) with Stanford and Yale
note: Mixes multiple-choice questions scored by accuracy with numeric answers scored by mean relative accuracy. Videos come from ScanNet, ScanNet++ and ARKitScenes.

name: VSI-Bench-Debiased
description: Models answer the 2,362 VSI-Bench questions left after removing 2,768 that text-only models could solve from answer priors or world knowledge.
note: The makers call it a separate evaluation artifact, not a drop-in replacement for VSI-Bench, because the filter changes the question-type mix. It is the debiased config of the VSI-Bench dataset.

name: VSI-SUPER
description: Video models watch arbitrarily long streams and must recall where objects appeared (VSR) or keep counting objects across scenes (VSC). Video lengths run from 10 minutes to 4 hours.
org: New York University (Cambrian-S team, Yang et al.)
note: Released with Cambrian-S. The makers built it to resist brute-force context expansion. VLMEvalKit has splits from 10 to 240 minutes.

name: VSR
description: Models judge whether captions with 65 kinds of spatial relation, such as under or facing, are true of an image. Over 10,000 text and image pairs.
note: TACL 2023. A zero-shot split is common.

name: VSR Random Split
description: Models judge whether image captions correctly describe spatial relations on the randomly partitioned test set. The score is accuracy over 2,195 test examples.
note: One track of VSR. The VSR record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: VSR Zero-Shot Split
description: Models judge spatial captions on a test set whose object concepts do not appear in training. The score is accuracy over 616 test examples.
note: One track of VSR. The VSR record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: VSTI-Bench
description: Video questions about how spatial relationships change over time in 3D scenes, over 138,000 pairs across five tasks.

name: Vulnerability finding evaluations (Anthropic)
aliases: Violative and defensive vulnerability discovery, classifier flag rate
description: Cyber safeguard classifiers screen sampled vulnerability discovery traffic. Reports flag rates on violative binary work and on defensive source code work.
note: Measures the deployed classifier system. Higher flag rates are better on violative traffic and lower are better on defensive traffic.

name: VulnGym
description: White-box agents hunt vulnerabilities in real repositories at vulnerable commits, including business-logic bugs that need cross-module reasoning. Each sample has a human-reviewed entry point and trace.
note: 408 entries from 184 advisories, all human-audited by v0.1.5 (2026-10-08). About 360 GitHub stars.

name: VulnLMP
description: Agents run long vulnerability research campaigns against widely deployed hardened software with verifier owned evidence. Judged on verified exploit outcomes.
note: In-house OpenAI evaluation. Cards describe outcomes in words without a score.

name: VWE-Bench
description: Multimodal agents build interactive 3D worlds from a user request. They infer intent, plan the scene layout, call 3D tools for asset retrieval, editing and rendering, and revise from rendered feedback. The benchmark has 2,616 3D assets, 323 human-annotated seed worlds and 6,828 queries. Verified queries have ground truth, and the rest are scored with rubrics.
note: The same release includes VibeWorlding-Gym, an RL post-training framework, so the repository stars (about 259) cover both. 61 Hugging Face upvotes.

name: WANDR
description: 500 wide-search tasks: find tens to hundreds of entities and facts, then return structured records with citations.

name: WARC-Bench
aliases: Web Archive Based Benchmark for GUI Subtask Executions
description: Screenshot-only agents do short web subtasks, such as date pickers and scroll containers, on real sites replayed from Web Archive snapshots. A program checks the end state.
note: Accepted at ICLR 2026. 192 subtasks with 20 steps each. 8 models in the Fireworks index.

name: WBench
description: Interactive video world models run 289 multi-turn cases with navigation, subject actions, event edits and perspective switches. 22 metrics cover quality, adherence, consistency and physics.
note: First release evaluates 20 video world models. 77 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: We-Math
description: Models solve visual math problems decomposed into sub-problems by knowledge concept. Scoring compares sub-problem and full-problem results to diagnose knowledge and generalization gaps.
org: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications
note: A successor, We-Math 2.0, followed in August 2025.

name: WeaveBench
description: Computer-use agents do 114 long tasks in 8 work domains that mix GUI actions with command-line and code operations in one trajectory. Results are checked against verifiable artifacts.
note: EMNLP 2026. 55 HF paper upvotes.

name: Web Clone Bench
description: Agent gets a running reference app (Gmail, Jira, Figma, etc.) and 8 hours to build a clone. Expert-written workflows are replayed as end-to-end tests.
note: 9 apps. Shipping the reference's own bundles scores zero. Environments are available through partnership.

name: Web Context (Nimble)
description: Agents with only web search and page reading enrich company records, find matching entities or write research reports. LLM judges check each fact against source pages.
note: 90 tasks across go-to-market, finance and social media. Scored by fact F1. 11 models in the Fireworks index. No maker page with details found.

name: Web CTF challenges (Anthropic)
description: Agents discover and exploit vulnerabilities in web applications across easy, medium and hard capture-the-flag challenges.
note: In-house Anthropic evaluation. The tasks are not public.

name: Web of lies
description: Models argue for the correct or incorrect answer to simple factual questions and participants report belief shifts.
note: Human participant persuasion study from Phuong et al. 2024. Reports give shifts toward correct and incorrect beliefs.

name: Web UI Bench
description: Many models build the same 12 app UIs from one shared prompt. Outputs are shown side by side for people to compare. No automatic score.
note: A gallery, not a scored leaderboard. Reasoning-effort settings differ across models. Not the academic WebUIBench (ACL 2025).

name: WebArena
description: Agents complete 812 realistic tasks on self-hosted shopping, forum, GitLab, CMS and map websites. Functional graders check the outcome.
note: WebArena-Verified is a separate audited version with its own id.

name: WebArena-Verified
description: Agents complete 812 audited WebArena tasks on self-hosted websites. Deterministic evaluators check the agent's answer and captured network traces.
note: It fixes WebArena's tasks, answers, and evaluators and drops LLM judges. A 258 task Hard subset also exists.

name: WebBench (Halluminate)
description: Browser agents complete 2,454 tasks on 452 live websites from the global top 1,000 by traffic. Tasks either read information or write data: creating, updating and deleting records, logging in and downloading files. The board compares browser agent products.
note: It expands WebVoyager from 15 to 452 sites. The README was last updated in May 2025, and the board ranks agent products rather than models. Live websites change, so results drift over time. The README does not say how runs are graded. About 100 GitHub stars.

name: WebCanvas
description: Web agents do tasks on live websites, scored on key intermediate states rather than one fixed action path, so the test survives site changes.
note: Ships Mind2Web-Live, a live re-annotation of Mind2Web tasks.

name: WebDev Arena
description: Two anonymous models build web apps from a user's prompt, and the user votes for the better one. Votes yield Elo-style ratings.
note: Code Arena replaced it in November 2025, and the old board stays up as WebDev Legacy.

name: WebHarbor
description: Agents navigate local copies of 153 websites to search, sign in, book services, and change stored state. The suite contains 3,518 tasks, including 306 verified test tasks and 2,288 training tasks. The test score measures the percentage of tasks passed by scripted verifiers.
note: AIMING Lab released the first 15 environments in May 2026 and the full suite in November 2026. Agents use either a GUI harness or OpenCode on the same test set. Independent judge scores and verifier agreement remain diagnostics. Live-web transfer results measure other benchmarks.

name: WebLINX
description: Agents follow a user's multi-turn chat instructions to navigate real websites. 100,000 interactions from 2,300 expert demonstrations give turn-level metrics.
note: ICML 2024. 39 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: WebQuest
description: Models answer questions from screenshots of one web page, several related pages, or a navigation trace. The test checks extraction and combination of information across pages.
note: Labs report the single-screen and multi-screen splits separately. The org is inferred from the author list, so check it.

name: WebQuestions
description: Models answer factual questions mined from Google Suggest, with answers taken from the Freebase knowledge base. Scored by exact match.
note: Freebase was shut down in 2016, so some answers are dated.

name: WebShop
description: Agents search and click through a simulated shopping site with 1.18 million real products to buy an item that matches a text instruction. Reward reflects how well the purchase matches.
note: NeurIPS 2022. Widely used in agent papers, often with a 500-instruction test split.

name: WebSRC
description: Models answer questions about a web page from its screenshot, HTML or both. The set has 400K question and answer pairs from 6.4K web pages. Scored by exact match and F1.
note: Vision-language model reports use the dev split with screenshots only. Microsoft's Mage-VL card reports WebSRC-val.

name: WebTailBench
description: Computer-use agents complete 609 hand-verified tasks on live websites across 11 categories, such as bookings, real estate and job search. A companion set of 111 harmful tasks tests refusals.
note: Released with Fara-7B. On 2026-05-12 Microsoft added a V2 split that refreshes calendar-bound task strings and rubrics for the same 609 tasks. The maker does not say V2 scores differ, so it stays one record.

name: WebTailBench-Refusals
description: Computer-use agents receive 111 harmful browser tasks in seven policy categories, such as illegal activity and misinformation. Scored as the share of tasks safely refused.
note: Released with Fara-7B as WebTailBench-Refusals.tsv in the WebTailBench dataset. The webtailbench record lists this name as an alias, which should move here.

name: WebVoyager
description: Agents complete user tasks on 15 popular real websites by browsing from screenshots and page text. A GPT-4V judge grades whether each task succeeded.
note: Tasks run on live websites, so pages and answers change over time. The Nemotron 3.5 Super VL card marks its run as offline.

name: WebWalkerQA
description: Agents start from a website's home page and traverse its subpages to find the facts that answer a question. Answers are judged against references.
note: Tongyi deep research model reports cite it. 23 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: WeirdML
description: Models write PyTorch code to solve 17 unusual machine learning tasks, with 5 attempts and feedback each. Scoring is mean best test accuracy.
note: This record is WeirdML v2 (17 tasks), launched in June 2025 and run on Epoch AI Benchmarking Hub. v1 (6 tasks, December 2024) is archived. WeirdML v3 replaced v2 in September 2026.

name: WeirdML v3
description: Agents solve 11 hand-made machine learning and data analysis tasks on a GPU with unfamiliar data and hidden test answers. Scored by token-weighted best results.
org: Håvard Tveit Ihle (Norwegian Defence Research Establishment)
note: Scores are not raw accuracy and are not comparable with WeirdML v2.

name: WellnessBench
description: Models answer young people asking about eating, sexual safety, substances and self harm, in clinician-written single-turn and pushback dialogues. A pass must be both safe and helpful.
note: 12 models with three repeats. Consumer chat apps passed fewer dialogues than the same models over the API.

name: WenetSpeech
description: Models transcribe Mandarin speech from many domains. Scored by character error rate on the test-net and test-meeting sets.
org: Northwestern Polytechnical University (ASLP@NPU), Mobvoi and others
note: The corpus has more than 10,000 hours of labeled speech.

name: WenetSpeech Test_Meeting
description: Models transcribe spontaneous Mandarin speech from real meetings in the Test_Meeting set. The baseline score is mixture error rate, counting Mandarin characters and English words.
org: Northwestern Polytechnical University (ASLP@NPU), Mobvoi and others
