note: One track of WenetSpeech. The WenetSpeech record keeps lab scores that combine tracks. Authors call the baseline metric mixture error rate. Lab cards may instead name character or word error rate.

name: WenetSpeech Test_Net
description: Models transcribe Mandarin internet speech from the Test_Net set. The baseline score is mixture error rate, counting Mandarin characters and English words.
org: Northwestern Polytechnical University (ASLP@NPU), Mobvoi and others
note: One track of WenetSpeech. The WenetSpeech record keeps lab scores that combine tracks. Authors call the baseline metric mixture error rate. Lab cards may instead name character or word error rate.

name: Wer wird Millionär? LLM Benchmark
aliases: German Who Wants to Be a Millionaire Benchmark
description: Models play 45 games of the German version of Who Wants to Be a Millionaire, each with 15 questions of rising difficulty. Early questions lean on German wordplay and idioms.
note: Still updated in 2026-10. About 50 GitHub stars, but the Reddit posts reached 759 and 246 points.

name: When2Call
description: Models decide when to call a tool, when to ask a follow-up question and when to say the tools cannot answer. Scored on multiple-choice and LLM-judged test sets.
note: The Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B card reports a multi-turn variant, When2Call Multi-Turn. The repo also has a training set.

name: Where2Place
description: 100 cluttered real photos with free-space placement instructions. The model points, scored correct if inside the ground-truth mask.
note: Only 100 images, so gaps under ~10 points are noise. Scoring varies by source (single vs several points, thinking on/off).

name: White-box analyses of model internals (Anthropic)
aliases: Share of audit transcripts scored 6+ on each interpretability dimension
description: An investigator with interpretability tools reads model activations on audit transcripts. A judge scores hidden states such as evaluation awareness and deception.
note: Uses natural language autoencoders and a template lens. Reports the share of transcripts scored 6 or higher per dimension, with no overall.

name: WiC
description: Models decide whether a target word has the same meaning in two sentence contexts. Scoring is binary accuracy.
org: Mohammad Taher Pilehvar and Jose Camacho-Collados
note: WiC is also one of the SuperGLUE tasks.

name: WideSearch
description: 200 bilingual broad info-seeking tasks: agent collects many atomic facts into a table. Scored by success rate and row/item F1.
note: Table-level success near 0-7% at release. Labs now report mean item-F1, which is much higher.

name: Wiki Live Challenge
description: Deep research agents write articles on topics of 100 recent Wikipedia Good Articles, which serve as expert references. Scored on 39 writing criteria and factual verifiability.
org: USTC and Metastone Technology (DeepResearch Bench team)
note: A live benchmark that refreshes with the newest Good Articles. 33 HF paper upvotes.

name: WikiSQL
description: Models turn natural language questions into SQL queries over single Wikipedia tables. The dataset has 80,654 hand-annotated questions over 24,241 tables. Scored by execution accuracy and logical form accuracy.
note: The repository keeps a leaderboard of papers trained on its training split. Each query covers one table, so it is far easier than Spider. About 1,800 GitHub stars.

name: WikiTableQuestions
description: Models answer complex questions about semi-structured HTML tables from Wikipedia. Answers often need counting, comparison or aggregation across rows. Scored by answer accuracy against the gold answers.
note: ACL 2015. The dataset has 22,033 examples. Table reasoning papers on language models still report it. About 191 GitHub stars.

name: WildArtifactBench
description: Agents produce real deliverables in any format, from audio analysis and medical video reads to 3D meshes and kitchen layouts. Human and agent judges compare them with a baseline agent's work to give win rates and Elo.
note: Meta's internal multimodal agent eval, previewed with Muse Spark 1.2 on 2026-08-20. Ten tasks are public with their files. The rest stay internal.

name: WildBench
description: 1,024 challenging real-user tasks with checklist-guided LLM judging.
note: This record is WildBench v2 with 1,024 tasks, scored as WB-Score and WB-Reward. The dataset also has a v1-legacy config and a v2-hard subset.

name: WildChat (toxic conversations)
description: Models answer toxic user turns from WildChat, the 200 highest scoring conversations per moderation category. Scored as not_unsafe rate.
org: Allen Institute for AI (dataset), OpenAI (toxic subset)
note: OpenAI selects the toxic subset from the public WildChat corpus of 1M ChatGPT conversations.

name: WildChat non-toxic incorrect refusals (Anthropic)
description: Models answer non-toxic user prompts drawn from the WildChat dataset of real chatbot conversations. Score is the incorrect refusal rate.
note: Anthropic refusal evaluation on the non-toxic subset of WildChat, first reported in the Claude 3 model card. The exact prompt selection is not public.

name: WildChat toxic refusals (Anthropic)
description: Models answer toxic user prompts drawn from the WildChat dataset of real chatbot conversations. Score is the correct refusal rate.
note: Anthropic refusal evaluation on the toxic subset of WildChat, first reported in the Claude 3 model card. The exact prompt selection is not public.

name: WildClawBench
description: 60 original in-the-wild tasks run inside a live OpenClaw assistant environment, chaining 10-60+ tool calls. Scored by task-level graders.
note: Also packaged for Harbor (internlm/WildClawBench-Harbor). Covers productivity, code, search, creative and safety categories.

name: WildGraphBench
description: GraphRAG systems answer 1,100 questions over long, mixed reference documents behind Wikipedia articles in 12 topics, from single facts to section summaries.
org: USTC and Metastone Technology (DeepResearch Bench team)
note: Ground truth comes from citation-linked statements. 41 HF paper upvotes.

name: WildGuardTest
description: Models classify whether user prompts are harmful, whether responses are harmful, and whether responses refuse, across 13 risk categories. Scored by F1.
note: The test split of WildGuardMix. Artificial Analysis uses it in its Decision Index.

name: WildJailbreak
description: Models face adversarial jailbreak prompts built from in-the-wild tactics, plus benign prompts that look harmful. Evaluations score refusals of harmful requests and compliance with benign ones.
org: Allen Institute for AI and University of Washington (WildTeaming)
note: The release is mainly a 262K pair safety training set. Launch posts report its evaluation split.

name: WildSpeech-Bench
description: Models hold spoken conversations built from real chat data, with prosody, homophones and stuttering. A judge model scores the replies.
note: Qwen reports it as audio interaction.

name: WildVision
description: Vision-language models answer 500 real user image prompts from the WildVision Arena. A GPT-4 judge compares each answer with a fixed baseline model.
org: Allen Institute for AI and UCSB
note: The arena collects human votes and the bench correlates 0.94 with arena Elo.

name: WildVision Arena
description: Users upload an image with a question, compare answers from two anonymous vision-language models, and vote. Votes give Elo ratings.
org: Allen Institute for AI and UCSB
note: The model-judged WildVision-Bench was built from its conversations and has its own record. The Hugging Face space was last updated on 2024-12-22.

name: Windows Agent Arena
description: Agents complete more than 150 tasks in a real Windows OS with its apps, tools and browsers. Scripts adapted from OSWorld check the final state.
note: A harder difficulty mode, where agents also set up tasks, was added on 2024-11-10. Runs parallelize on Azure in about 20 minutes.

name: WinoBias
description: Models resolve pronouns linked to occupations in type 1 and type 2 sentences. Accuracy gaps show gender bias in coreference.
note: Gemma reports give type 1 and type 2 scores separately.

name: Winogender
description: Models resolve pronouns in sentences about occupations. Accuracy shows whether gender stereotypes sway coreference.

name: Winograd
description: Models pick which noun an ambiguous pronoun refers to in Winograd schema sentence pairs that need world knowledge. Scored by accuracy.
org: Hector Levesque, Ernest Davis, and Leora Morgenstern
note: Models passed 90 percent by 2019, which led to the larger WinoGrande dataset.

name: WinoGrande
description: 44K Winograd-style pronoun-resolution problems. Binary-choice accuracy.
note: Saturated base-model metric.

name: WISE
description: Text-to-image models draw 1,000 prompts that need world knowledge in culture, space, time and natural science. A vision model judge gives the WiScore.
note: Scores run from 0 to 1 and cover 25 subdomains. Unified models such as BAGEL report it with and without reasoning before drawing.

name: WISE Verified
description: Models generate images from the revised WISE prompts. The verified evaluation changes about 200 prompts and the judge, so original scores remain separate.
note: Models generate images from the revised WISE prompts. The verified evaluation changes about 200 prompts and the judge, so original scores remain separate.

name: WitnessBench
description: Agents play unseen line-puzzle games in the style of The Witness without being told the rules. They must discover rules by experiment and apply them to harder levels.
note: 26 games with 20 levels each. Each solved level is scored against the shortest solution the game accepts. 13 models in the Fireworks index.

name: WMDP
description: Proxy multiple-choice benchmark for hazardous knowledge in bio, chem and cyber. Released with the RMU unlearning method.
note: 3,668 multiple-choice questions in three splits on Hugging Face: biology 1,273, chemistry 408 and cybersecurity 1,987. MIT licensed. Questions exclude directly hazardous content. Mainly used to measure unlearning.

name: WMDP Biology
description: Models answer 1,273 multiple-choice questions that proxy hazardous biosecurity knowledge. Biology split of WMDP.
note: Subset of the WMDP benchmark. 1,273 test questions in the Hugging Face config, MIT licensed. A cybersecurity split also exists.

name: WMDP Chemistry
description: Models answer 408 multiple-choice questions that proxy hazardous chemical security knowledge. Chemistry split of WMDP.
note: Subset of the WMDP benchmark. 408 test questions in the Hugging Face config, MIT licensed. A cybersecurity split also exists.

name: WMDP Cyber
description: Models answer multiple-choice questions on offensive cybersecurity knowledge. The cybersecurity split of the Weapons of Mass Destruction Proxy benchmark.
note: 1,987 test questions in the wmdp-cyber config on Hugging Face, MIT licensed. Mainly used to measure unlearning. The almanac already holds the biology and chemistry splits.

name: WMT23
description: Models translate the WMT23 general task test sets between English and languages such as German, Chinese, and Japanese. Model cards score output with BLEURT.
note: The shared task ranked systems by human judgment, while model cards report automatic BLEURT scores.

name: WMT24
description: Systems translate the WMT24 general task test sets, mostly English to X plus some X to Y pairs, at paragraph level across several domains. The shared task ranks systems by human ESA judgments.
note: Blind test sets came out on 2024-06-28. Google's WMT24++ extends this test set to 55 languages.

name: WMT24++
description: English-to-55-language translation of WMT24 test data. Scored with automatic metrics such as MetricX or xCOMET.
note: Cohere added internal Irish, Maltese and Serbian variants.

name: WMT25
description: Systems translate the WMT25 general task test sets in 16 directions, mostly out of English. New pairs include English to Bhojpuri, Korean and Maasai. Humans evaluate the systems.
note: Blind sets came out on 2025-06-19. A multilingual subtask added the WMT24++ test set.

name: WMT25 Terminology Translation Task
description: Models translate sentence, paragraph and document level text with a supplied source to target glossary. Scoring checks quality and whether the prescribed target terms appear.
note: Test data came out on 2025-06-24 with two tracks. 21 systems from 15 teams took part. Cohere reports corpus-level terminology success rate.

name: WMT26
description: Systems translate the WMT26 general task test set in 24 directions, mostly out of English, across several domains with added instructions. The shared task ranks systems by human contrastive ESA judgments.
note: The blind test set came out on 2026-06-18 and references on 2026-07-27. Cohere scores it with a GPT-5.6-Sol judge on a 0 to 100 scale, which differs from the shared task's human ranking.

name: Word-Task (Tencent)
description: Models solve Tencent in-house word level language tasks. Task and scoring details are not published.
note: Seen in the Hunyuan-A13B-Instruct card. Scoring method is a guess from the task type.

name: WorkArena
description: Web agents do routine knowledge-work tasks in a live ServiceNow instance, such as filling forms and filtering lists. WorkArena++ adds 682 compositional tasks at levels 2 and 3.
note: Level 1 has 33 atomic tasks with 19,912 instances. It runs through BrowserGym and AgentLab. WorkArena++ (NeurIPS 2024) scores are reported per level.

name: WorkArena++
description: Web agents complete 682 compositional knowledge-work tasks in ServiceNow, which need planning, reasoning and memory across many steps.
note: Builds on WorkArena (L1) with harder L2 and L3 tasks. Published at NeurIPS 2024.

name: WorkplaceAgents
description: Agents produce finished work products for 200 professional tasks across 96 occupations in 19 sectors. Harbor grades deliverables with code checks and rubrics.
note: Cost per trial ranged from $0.59 to $32.16 across models.

name: Workspace-Bench-Lite
description: Agents complete 100 workspace tasks. The leaderboard reports the percentage of 1,856 rubric checks passed, with separate runs for each model and harness.
note: This Lite subset has a separate 45-run leaderboard. The full benchmark does not publish named per-system scores. Remove the Lite alias from workspacebench during integration.

name: WorkSpaceBench
description: Agent completes 388 tasks in realistic worker file workspaces (20k files) needing cross-file dependency reasoning. Scored against 7,399 rubrics.
note: The full benchmark contains 388 tasks. Its site publishes only anonymous summary results. The 100-task Lite subset has its own leaderboard and record.

name: World-Class Bio
description: Models answer expert-level biology questions in a SecureBio benchmark. Scored as accuracy.
note: 96 text-only rubric-graded open-ended questions on rare biology known to a handful of experts. In development by SecureBio. Leading reasoning models score about 50%. Graded by an AI model with the rubric.

name: World-in-World
description: Closed-loop platform: world models plan for embodied agents in four environments via a standard action API. Scored by task success.
note: Prioritizes task success over visual quality. Finds visual quality alone does not guarantee success and controllability matters more.

name: WorldArena
description: Embodied world models generate RoboTwin 2.0 task videos from first frame plus text or actions. 15 video metrics (EWMScore) plus utility tracks.
note: The top 40 Track-1 entries are tightly compressed. Policy-evaluator track saturated (14 of 19 above 85). Extended by WorldArena 2.0.

name: WorldArena 2.0
description: Extends WorldArena to visuotactile prediction, world models as RL environments, and simulated plus real multi-embodiment robot platforms.

name: WorldAuditBench
description: Multimodal agents explore interactive 3D worlds to find anomalies such as floating objects, walls that can be walked through or out-of-place objects.
note: 79 upvotes on Hugging Face papers.

name: WorldBench
description: Models answer hand-written reasoning questions about images drawn from a taxonomy of thousands of visual concepts. Questions were kept only if frontier models failed them.
org: Yida Yin, Shengbang Tong, Wenhu Chen and others
note: The paper evaluates 15 models and the best reaches 64.0 percent. ByteDance Seed reports it in the Seed2.1 model card.

name: WorldExam
description: Controllable video generators are tested as world models. Levels run from visual appearance to whether the depicted world reacts plausibly beyond what the prompt states.
note: It had 31 Hugging Face paper upvotes and 23 GitHub stars.

name: WorldGUI
description: Desktop GUI agents do 611 tasks that start from varied initial states, such as the target app not being open. Tasks come with instructional videos and project files.
org: Show Lab, National University of Singapore
note: 127 GitHub stars at 2026-11-01.

name: WorldModelBench
description: Video generators judged as world models on instruction following and physics adherence in application domains. Human labels and a fine-tuned judge.
note: 67K crowd-sourced human labels used to fine-tune a 2B judge that automates scoring.

name: WorldModelGym
description: World models predict returns for five candidate action sequences across 100+ Atari, Meta-World, DMC and classic-control tracks. Scored by normalized regret.
note: Measures decision fidelity, not visual realism. A fixed argmax rule isolates prediction quality. Entrants host a /score endpoint and Reka computes the score. Reka entered its own Dreamer-v3 at launch. Open-loop only.

name: WorldScore
description: 3,000 next-scene generation tasks with camera-trajectory layouts. Scores 3D/4D and video world generators on controllability, quality, dynamics.

name: WorldSense
description: Models answer synthetic questions that test consistent reasoning about simple arrangements of entities described in text.
note: Llama 3 reports it as a pretrained math and reasoning task.

name: WorldSense (omnimodal)
description: Models answer multiple choice questions about real-world videos that need both the visual and the audio track. Scored by accuracy.
org: Jack Hong, Shilin Yan et al.
note: Not the 2023 Meta FAIR text benchmark with the same name (id worldsense). Omni model launch posts mean this one.

name: WorldSimBench
description: Dual evaluation of video world simulators: human-preference perceptual scoring plus action-level embodied tasks in games, driving, manipulation.

name: WorldTravel
description: Agents plan trips for 150 real-world scenarios across 5 cities with more than 15 tightly coupled time and logic constraints each. A web environment supplies multimodal travel data.
org: ByteDance Seed and collaborators (Wang et al.)
note: Seed1.8 first reported it as an internal benchmark in December 2025, before the paper. Seed1.8 reports best of five attempts.

name: WorldVQA
description: Model names visual entities in 3,500 image-question pairs across nine categories, isolating memorized visual world knowledge. Exact-answer accuracy.
note: Lab-created public benchmark (Moonshot AI). Kimi K3 reports a 'ForceAnswer' variant.

name: WritingBench
description: Models complete 1,000 real-world writing requests across 6 domains and 100 subdomains. A judge model scores each reply on five query-specific criteria.
note: The board multiplies its 10-point critic score by 10, and labs that print the 10-point score are recorded times 10. The board changed its queries, criteria and critic from April 2025, so scores from different times may not compare.

name: WSC
description: Models decide whether a pronoun refers to a given noun phrase in sentences that need commonsense to resolve. Scored by accuracy.
org: NYU, Facebook AI, University of Washington, and DeepMind (SuperGLUE)
note: This is the SuperGLUE recasting of the Winograd Schema Challenge.

name: X Browse (xAI)
description: Agents answer questions that need multi-hop search and browsing on the X platform. Scored by answer accuracy.
note: xAI describes it in one sentence as an internal benchmark and gives no grading details, so the scoring type is assumed.

name: xAI Factuality (Hallucination) eval
description: Internal measure of unsupported or fabricated claims in single responses to information-seeking queries.

name: xAI refusal and jailbreak suites
description: Internal refusal suites (general, child safety, self-harm) in six languages plus single-turn, multi-turn and long-horizon jailbreaks.

name: xAI sycophancy eval
description: Factual questions paired with misleading user context. Rate at which the model abandons the correct answer.

name: Xbench
description: Measures firsthand X posts about frontier models and coding harnesses. An LLM labels each post's sentiment, aggregated per model per week.
note: Every label is public by post id so numbers can be audited. The raw corpus stays private. The score is net firsthand sentiment in percentage points, from negative 100 to positive 100.

name: xbench-DeepSearch
description: Agents search the web to answer 100 Chinese questions that need multi-step retrieval. Scored by accuracy against reference answers.
note: A refreshed 100-question set, DeepSearch-2510, followed in October 2025.

name: xbench-DeepSearch-2510
description: Agents answer 100 new Chinese deep search questions that need many web searches and cross-checks. Answers are matched to a key.
note: The dataset is encrypted against crawling. Scores are much lower than on the 2505 set, so the two are not comparable.

name: xbench-Marketing
description: Agents search for influencers who fit 50 real advertiser briefs, scored against a curated pool of 836 influencers.
note: Profession Aligned track, co-designed with marketing practitioners.

name: xbench-Recruitment
description: Agents do 50 headhunting tasks from live business cases: company mapping, finding facts about people and finding people who fit a profile. A judge scores answers 1 to 5.
note: Profession Aligned track. Gemini 2.5 Flash judges and scores map to 0 to 100.

name: xbench-ScienceQA
description: Models answer postgraduate-level science questions written by experts, in Chinese, as part of the xbench AGI Tracking series.
note: Not the 2022 ScienceQA from UCLA and Ai2. The repo board reports score and best of 5.

name: XBOW Validation Benchmarks
description: Offensive security agents attack deliberately vulnerable web applications and must capture a flag to prove each exploit.
note: About 750 GitHub stars, and pentest agent makers still quote scores on it. XBOW itself says the set was saturated by mid-2026 and the bugs are in training data.

name: xChatBench
description: Vision language models answer 400 open-ended multimodal chat prompts in 7 languages. An LLM judge scores each answer against fine-grained human-written criteria.
note: Released as part of PangeaBench with the Pangea model.

name: XCOPA
description: Models pick the more plausible cause or effect of a premise from two options, in 11 languages. Scoring is accuracy.
org: Cambridge Language Technology Lab (Ponti et al.)

name: xDailyBench
description: Models answer open-ended requests grounded in real user needs across more than 30 daily-life, study and office scenarios. Rubrics grade completion, correctness, coverage and usefulness.
note: In-house Seed benchmark for consumer use. The Seed2.1 card reports Pass@1.

name: xdev-bench-hard
description: Agents get vulnerable source code, a short bug hint and the binary, and must write an exploit that reaches code execution in a sandbox. Success is checked by retrieving a secret string.
note: In-house. Most tasks reproduce recent disclosed vulnerabilities in software such as the Linux kernel, Node.js and Exim, with mitigations on. Moonshot reports pass@3.

name: XLRS-Bench
description: Models answer perception and reasoning questions about extremely large, ultra-high-resolution remote sensing images.

name: xMMMU
description: Vision language models answer college-level MMMU questions translated into 7 languages. Scored by accuracy.
note: Released as part of PangeaBench with the Pangea model.

name: XNLI
description: Models classify entailment, contradiction or neutral for sentence pairs translated from MultiNLI into 15 languages.
note: Common in multilingual model reports.

name: XpertBench
description: Models complete expert tasks from more than 140 task types in law, finance, education, humanities and science. Over 200 domain experts wrote the prompts and weighted rubrics.
note: In-house Seed benchmark built on the Xpert expert platform. Seed1.8 reports scores per field. Rubric grading is assumed to be automatic.

name: XQuAD
description: Models answer 1,190 SQuAD questions over 240 paragraphs, professionally translated so the set is parallel across 11 languages. Scored by F1 and exact match.

name: XSTest
description: Models answer 250 safe prompts that resemble unsafe ones and 200 unsafe contrast prompts. Labs usually report the incorrect refusal rate on safe prompts.
org: Röttger et al. (Bocconi University and others)
note: Anthropic model cards report the incorrect refusal rate on the non-malicious prompts, where lower is better.

name: XStoryCloze
description: Models pick the right ending for short stories from StoryCloze, professionally translated into 10 languages.
note: Released with the XGLM paper, Few-shot Learning with Multilingual Language Models.

name: XTREME
aliases: Cross-lingual TRansfer Evaluation of Multilingual Encoders
description: Multilingual models are fine-tuned on English data and then tested on 9 tasks in 40 languages. The tasks cover sentence classification, structured prediction such as named entities, question answering and sentence retrieval. The benchmark measures how well skills transfer across languages.
note: XTREME targets fine-tuned encoders such as mBERT and XLM-R, not prompted chat models. XTREME-R (2021) changes the task set and is a separate test. About 650 GitHub stars, and the repo was last pushed in 2023-01.

name: XTREME-R
description: Multilingual models are fine-tuned on English data and tested on 10 tasks in 50 typologically diverse languages, including harder language-agnostic retrieval tasks. It extends XTREME and adds MultiCheckList, a multilingual diagnostic suite.
org: Google Research and DeepMind with collaborators
note: It shares the XTREME repository and leaderboard site. Like XTREME, it targets fine-tuned encoders, not prompted chat models.

name: XYEval
description: Agents run tasks from existing benchmarks with one confident but wrong user hint added to the instruction. The gold solution stays valid, so the score drop measures how often agents follow bad advice.
note: Built on tau2-bench, SWE-bench Verified, SWE-bench Pro, Terminal-Bench, Humanity's Last Exam and MCP-Atlas. Scores fell by up to 46.7% relative. Summaries cite a google-deepmind/xyeval repo, which was not reachable on 2026-11-01.

name: YC-Bench
description: Agent runs a simulated startup for one year via CLI, managing staff, clients and cash. Scored by final funds.
note: Only 3 of 12 frontier models grew capital in the paper. Adversarial clients cause 47% of bankruptcies.

name: YoCausal
description: Video generation models are tested for causal and arrow-of-time understanding by comparing real videos with their time-reversed versions, in two levels.
note: Level 1 uses a Reverse Surprise Index. 51 HF paper upvotes.

name: YouCook2
description: Models describe the procedure steps in YouTube cooking videos. Scored by CIDEr against human step captions.

name: YouCook2 Dense Video Description
description: Models locate cooking steps and describe each step. The score is CIDEr for the complete dense video description task.
note: One track of YouCook2. The YouCook2 record keeps lab scores that combine tracks.

name: YouCook2 retrieval
description: Models retrieve cooking videos from text queries in the YouCook2 collection.

name: Yupp VIBE Score
description: People use Yupp for real tasks, see answers from two or more models, and pick the one they prefer. The preferences become VIBE scores for each model.
note: VIBE stands for Vibe Intelligence BEnchmark. Yupp launched the beta leaderboard on 2025-06-13 with a 33 million dollar seed round. Users can tag strengths and earn credits for feedback.

name: Z.ai Code Bench
description: Zhipu in-house coding benchmark used for GLM-5.3. Reports pass rate and output tokens per task. Method unpublished.
note: The official launch posts publish exact accuracy and token values for selected effort levels. Additional effort points appear only in chart images.

name: ZClawBench
description: Agents do end-to-end OpenClaw workflows such as environment setup, development, information retrieval, data analysis and content creation, drawn from real OpenClaw use.
note: Released with GLM-5-Turbo. Z.ai says the dataset and trajectories are public.

name: ZebraLogic
description: Models solve logic grid puzzles of controlled size, derived from constraint satisfaction problems. Scored by the share of puzzles solved fully.
note: Accuracy drops sharply as puzzle size grows.

name: ZeroBench
description: 100 hand-made visual questions that all frontier models originally failed. Scored by exact answer, pass@1 and pass@5.

changes.text: The maintainers revised questions after post-release review. Results should identify the question revision used for evaluation.
The maintainers corrected 0.71% of grading decisions and updated official scores. Mean pass@5 increased by 0.79 percentage points without question changes.

note: Point releases keep scores comparable: v2 (2025-03) revised questions, v3 (2025-12) clarified two questions and three subquestions. A 2026-08 grading fix raised mean pass@5 by 0.79 points.

name: ZeroSCROLLS/QuALITY
description: Models answer QuALITY multiple-choice questions about long stories zero-shot, as one task of the ZeroSCROLLS suite. Scoring is accuracy.
note: The ZeroSCROLLS leaderboard at zero.scrolls-benchmark.com did not answer on 2026-11-01.

name: ZeroVideo
description: Models answer real-world video reasoning questions that need high frame rate motion perception or multi-hop reasoning over long videos. Videos average 1,672 seconds.
note: In-house ByteDance Seed evaluation. The tasks are not public. It first appeared in the Seed1.8 model card with 101 questions, and the format and scoring are estimates.

name: ZMultiDialBench
description: Human annotators score model replies to 141 multilingual dialogue prompts on a 1 to 10 scale with category criteria.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation. The prompts are not public.

name: ZMultiTransBench
description: Models translate 1,220 real Chinese source texts into seven languages. A GPT-4.1 judge compares each translation with a fixed baseline.
note: In-house Z.ai evaluation. The printed score is a pairwise rating, not a percentage.

name: τ-bench 2.0
description: Agents serve simulated customers in airline, retail, telecom and banking domains in six languages, by text or voice. Release 2.0 adds frozen task manifests and an intake domain for entity capture.
note: Sierra says 2.0 scores are not comparable with 1.x. The user simulator moved to GPT-5.5 and communication checks became LLM-judged. Languages are en, es, pt, hi, zh and ko.

name: τ-Voice
description: Full-duplex voice agents handle real-time support calls in retail, airline and telecom with tools and a simulated caller. Scoring covers task completion and natural interaction.
note: Listed on taubench.com as the τ³-Voice board. Sierra also lists τ-i18n (six languages) and τ-Entity (entity capture over voice) as new voice evaluations.

name: τ^τ-bench
description: Coding agent builds a customer-service agent from business records, a client and an API. The built agent is scored against held-out simulated users.
note: 53 tasks in 4 domains. Best agent 23.9% vs expert reference 82.2%.

name: τ³-bench Banking
description: Agents act as banking customer-service reps over many turns with a simulated user, following policy. Pass^1 on the final database state.

changes.text: The maintainers changed banking’s default retrieval configuration from BM25 to AllTools, combining sparse search, dense search, and shell access. Default runs now expose different tools.
The maintainers regraded banking leaderboard trajectories under the corrected evaluation scheme. The revised results are not comparable with scores from the earlier grader.

note: A separate domain of τ³-bench. Its overall score covers retail, airline and telecom only.
